News.title: Sick nude pictures of dead college student, 19, ‘sent in texts by man who drugged and raped her’ instead of calling 911
News.content:
Next

HORRIFYING new details have emerged about the death of a fashion student who was allegedly drugged and raped in her dorm room.

Annabel Richter, 19, from Brazil, was studying at the Fashion Institute of Technology in New York when she fell into a coma and died following the alleged attack.



Moises Freire, 19, has now been charged with distributing fentanyl disguised as cocaine with the intent to commit rape following the March 18 incident.

Federal prosecutors say the Bronx teen, who was not a student at the college, tricked Richter and her friend into taking the deadly drug by claiming it was pure cocaine from Mexico.





The pair both immediately lost consciousness inside their dorm room and Freire then raped Richter who died in hospital three days later, according to the Manhattan US Attorney’s Office.

As her family pay tribute to the “bright and beautiful young woman,” officials say Freire texted nude pictures of his victims to pals rather than call 911.

Images allegedly sent during this sickening 45-minute delay before calling for campus security include a picture of Richter naked from the waist down, newly unsealed court docs state.

Prosecutors claimed Freire lied to campus security saying that both women drank too much and lost consciousness.



They further claim he told security that he failed to realize Richter had passed out until after he finished having sex with her.

“It is truly hard to believe that the defendant, who seemed entirely coherent and sober at the time, who didn’t have any of the substance, who is captured on the security guard’s body-worn camera seeming coherent and sober, didn’t know what was going on when he was having sex with the victim who was completely unconscious,” prosecutor Ariana Bloom said at hearing in April.

Both women were given Narcan by emergency services before being rushed to hospital.

“Annabel was full of life,” her mom Flavia Rocha, told The New York Post.

“She knew loads about music and art and had a contagious laughter. Her presence filled the room.



“For us, her family and her friends, she was and always will be, our beloved Bel.”

Despite her parents’ mad dash to get to New York after learning what happened, they never got to say goodbye to their daughter, one student told the Daily Mail.

Her surviving roommate has withdrawn from the fashion college and has not been identified.

Brian Peralta Cabrera, 18, of Queens, has also been charged with conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance resulting in death and serious bodily injury after allegedly helping supply Freire with the drugs.

Court documents allege he told Cabrera that he wanted substances that “would last the entire night”.



The pair were initially arrested in March and pleaded not guilty to earlier charges that did not include the rape allegation against Freire.

Freire is due back in court on October 28 for arraignment on the upgraded charge of distributing a controlled substance with the intent to commit rape.

He is being held without bail pending a March 2027 trial.

His attorney, Mitchell Schwartz, previously described Richter’s death as a tragedy but disputed suggestions that his client had deliberately drugged the students.

He argued that the events leading up to the overdoses amounted to “a story of teenagers doing what I would call ‘dumb teenager things.’”



His attorney previously told the court that he and Richter had a consensual “sexual relationship” in the year before she died.

New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch branded the defendants’ alleged actions “truly unconscionable.”

“As alleged in the indictment, the two defendants supplied the fentanyl that killed one young woman and nearly killed another,” Tisch said.

“Rather than immediately seek help, Freire allegedly first raped the incapacitated victim who died and then lied to first responders.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“These actions are as sick and twisted as they come.”



If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call RAINN (Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network) at 800-656-HOPE (4673).

News.title: Dystopian scenes as woman, 78, arrested for blocking delivery robot while leaving flu shot appointment
News.content:
NEW AGE Dystopian scenes as woman, 78, arrested for blocking delivery robot while leaving flu shot appointment







Next

AN elderly woman was shockingly led away in cuffs after blocking a delivery robot in the street.

Carolyn Marvin, 78, was leaving her flu shot appointment in Philadelphia when she was confronted by the new-age machine.



Bystanders filmed the interaction after the senior stood in front of the Uber delivery bot which prompted a response from police officers.

She allegedly refused to move out of the way of the machine, preventing it from completing its delivery.



Philly police responded to reports of a disturbance around 1.16pm on Wednesday and they said Marvin refused to move despite being asked multiple times.

The University of Pennsylvania professor emeritus was then surrounded and arrested by three police officers under the charge of disorderly conduct.

Speaking about the dystopian scenes filmed by witnesses, Marvin told ABC’s Action News that she was executing her First Amendment rights.

“I think it’s my First Amendment right to publicly demonstrate on a sidewalk to protest against delivery robots,” she said.

The senior said her protest stems from fears that robots are “taking the jobs of human delivery workers.”

She revealed that it is not her first time blocking such deliveries.



“I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front of them and preventing them from going forward,” she said.

Marvin was issued a criminal violation notice for the offense, cops confirmed.

Such robots have been dubbed “the future of delivery” by Uber Eats and thousands of the machines are already in operation across the US for various companies and are set to rise.

News.title: Bizarre moment driver runs along motorway NAKED after ‘stripping off and fleeing three-car pile-up’ in Moscow
News.content:
Next

THIS is the bizarre moment a driver is seen running butt naked along a busy motorway after reportedly causing a three-car pile-up in Moscow.

The shameless motorist stripped off and fled the scene following a collision involving his Audi, a Mercedes and a Volkswagen on the Russian capital’s Third Transport Ring.



Baffling footage shows the man jogging completely naked along the busy highway as stunned motorists pass by.

At one point, the bare-bottomed driver appears to run out of breath, slowing down before continuing his bizarre escape.



But he soon seems to regain his energy, leaping into the air and throwing his arms up in an apparent display of joy.

The strange scenes unfolded on Moscow’s 22-mile orbital motorway.



Unfazed by the streaming traffic, he continues his run along the motorway without a stitch of clothing.

The driver was accused of causing a crash involving the two other German-made cars.

Rather than remain at the scene, the Audi driver reportedly removed all his clothes before making a naked dash along the road.

Local reports described the stunt as an “epic escape from the scene of the accident”.



A friend reportedly gave chase on foot in an attempt to catch up with the fleeing motorist.

The naked driver was eventually apprehended and sent for a medical examination.

Police were today questioning him as they attempted to establish the circumstances surrounding the collision and his extraordinary reaction.



The Volkswagen driver reportedly suffered a concussion and spinal injury in the three-car smash.

It remains unclear whether anyone else was injured in the collision.

The Audi driver’s identity and age have not been made public.

Investigators have also yet to establish what prompted him to strip naked and flee the scene rather than remain with the damaged vehicles.

Temperatures in Moscow were hovering around 16C at the time of his impromptu striptease.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It has also emerged that the motorist was involved in another road accident two years ago.

Moscow traffic police are continuing their investigation into the pile-up and the driver’s bizarre motorway escape.

News.title: ‘They saw things you pray you never see’: Blast during live-fire drill kills ‘at least 7’ as troops parachute into base
News.content:
Next

A MAYOR has revealed the horror witnessed by troops after a devastating explosion during a live-fire military drill reportedly killed seven.

The deadly blast erupted at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta on Saturday after a training exercise reportedly struck a gas line or well.



The exact number of victims remains unknown with local media reporting at least seven deaths.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has only confirmed four fatalities so far.



He said in a public address this afternoon that “four service members lost their lives” and that “dozens more are seriously wounded”.

The casualties were rushed to hospital as fierce 62mph winds fanned flames beyond the base, leaving emergency crews battling to contain the blaze.

Wainwright mayor Bruce Pugh has now spoken of the harrowing scenes witnessed by soldiers caught up in the disaster.

He told CBC: “They were witness to things that you would pray that you never see, or that if you do it would be a once-in-a-lifetime experience of service.”

The mayor became emotional as he described the devastating impact on military personnel caught up in the disaster.

He said: “What I’m feeling is nothing compared to what they are.



“Our hearts just go to them.”

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called it a “significant and tragic fire” – with the Canadian military forced to parachute troops into one of the country’s busiest bases.

Pugh revealed that military personnel had been conducting live-fire exercises at the base throughout the past week.



He said locals were accustomed to hearing the thunder of cannons from the sprawling training facility.

But on Saturday, the familiar sound of artillery fire suddenly fell silent.

Reports soon emerged that emergency crews had been scrambled to an “all hands on deck” incident at the base.

Pugh told the BBC that nothing of this scale had ever happened at the military facility before.

“This kind of tragedy is unheard of,” he said, stressing that Canadian Armed Forces personnel were exceptionally professional and well trained.



The mayor described the explosion as “the largest mass casualty event the community has ever seen”.

The scale of the disaster left nearby medical facilities overwhelmed, with casualties transferred to hospitals in Edmonton, around 120 miles away.

Dr Warren Thirsk, an emergency doctor at Royal Alexandra Hospital, described the situation as a major medical emergency.



He told CBC: “It is more patients than any of us want to count right now.

“It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster.”

The hospital declared a code orange, triggering emergency procedures for a mass casualty incident.

Defence Minister David McGuinty described the situation as “very, very active and delicate” as authorities worked to establish what caused the blast.

He said: “I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory”.



Canadian military officials said there was no indication the explosion was linked to terrorism.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the incident, while the Armed Forces have withheld official casualty figures until victims’ families have been notified.

CFB Wainwright is one of Canada’s busiest military training facilities and serves as a major centre for preparing soldiers for combat operations.

It houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, where troops undergo realistic battlefield exercises, alongside the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith described the incident as a “significant and tragic fire”, with the military forced to parachute troops into the base.



Prime Minister Mark Carney said: “Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

General Jennie Carignan, Canada’s chief of the defence staff, called the tragedy “a profoundly difficult moment for the entire Canadian Armed Forces”.

She added: “I extend my deepest condolences to the loved ones of those who have lost their lives.”

News.title: Inside the VERY surprising new sex tourism hotspot with £60 romps, ‘all-inclusive’ offers & even raunchy airport pickups
News.content:
Next

IT’S HARD to picture a woman living in a strict Islamic state openly posting selfies in black lingerie and knee-high boots while offering romps for as little as £60.

But scores of sex workers are now openly available in a rising Gulf hotspot with its surging tourist population including randy Brits looking to secretly score big on the cheap.



Oman has strictly conservative legal rules that are deeply rooted in Islamic culture thanks to Sharia-influenced laws.

This includes women having to wear modest outfits in public that cover both the top of the arms and anything below the knee.

Even bikinis are forbidden unless at a private beach or swimming pool.



It is also illegal to live with or share a hotel room with someone of the opposite sex if you’re not married or closely related.

Like almost all nations in the Middle East, getting involved in sex work is a dangerous game.

In 2018, more than 240 expats were arrested in the country on charges of prostitution and human trafficking.

Then last year, reports emerged saying that the government has issued new punishments for certain sex crimes. Those convicted of prostitution or trafficking would face just three years in jail.

This is feared to have sparked a sharp rise in the number of locals exploiting the industry and helping it grow.



The Sun has tested out these new laws using Tinder Passport, which allowed us to pose as a customer from the capital Muscat. We found the sex trade was rife and open.

Almost immediately swarms of sex workers made offers to move the conversation to WhatsApp, likely because of its promise of encrypted conversations.

One Asian woman, whose profile picture proudly displayed her bum and breasts, quickly moved over to the messaging service and wrote: “Anything you want is possible.”



She sent an image of her room and its location in a palm-lined residential area with seafood restaurants, cafes and access to a popular beach.

It’s also an area of the capital that one real estate company bills as a diverse mix of locals and expats.

The eager lady offers “professional massages” and sex, protected or unprotected, for sessions lasting up to an hour. It costs 40 Omani Rials or just £79.

The sex worker also offers upgrades for group sex with prices starting at 100 Rials (£196).

Remarkably, she even offers to pick up customers from Muscat International Airport and allows them to stay at her apartment as part of an “all-inclusive” package for 150 Rials (£295).



Alcoholic drinks, which are legal in Oman but strictly regulated, can be added as an extra.

She even extended her offer to accommodate our reporter for the pretend stay of five nights for 800 Rials (£1,571).

When quizzed about what the police would do if her promises were ever uncovered, she said: “Oman is easy, believe me.

“I have stayed in Oman for 15 years and never had a problem. I have a friend in the police.”

Another woman, listing herself as a massage therapist on dating apps, offers similar services for even less, starting at 30 Rials (£59) for sex.



Another woman posing as a massage therapist – a common cover job – offers a mysterious “one shot” service for just 25 Rials (£49).

A telling sign of sex work on the dating app was the sheer volume of women sending their real phone numbers without even exchanging a hello first.

Pardis Mahdavi, an expert in human trafficking who previously examined the issue in the Gulf, told The Sun: “I think the countries in the Gulf are very invested in their reputation and their image.”



Mahdavi, who authored the book Gridlock: Labor, Migration And Human Trafficking In Dubai, added: “Women are vulnerable to exploitation in the Middle East and around the world.

“Trafficking is a heinous crime and women are vulnerable particularly for political and economic reasons because women have to make a very difficult choice between watching their families starve and trying to make ends meet.

“So this is a really tough spot for them to be in, and they rely on unscrupulous middle men recruiters because they are not able to get jobs at home.”

Naomi McAuliffe, Head of Policy and Research at Amnesty International UK, said: “Sex trafficking is a profound human rights abuse.

“It robs people of their freedom, dignity and bodily autonomy, and most of those targeted are women and girls.



“Too often, the systems meant to protect them fail them instead. Governments must confront trafficking as a systemic problem rooted in inequality, impunity and the mistrust of victims.

“Exploitation thrives on silence and indifference, and it will only end when governments protect victims and hold perpetrators to account.”

The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office estimates that there are up to 300,000 British citizens living across the Gulf region.

The majority live in the United Arab Emirates or Saudi Arabia with other nations like Qatar, Bahrain and Oman quickly growing.

Up to 7,800 British expats currently live in Oman, according to regional census datasets.



The vast majority move to the capital of Muscat or along the Batinah coastal region with the promise of a high paying job and year-long sunshine.

The Sun has approached Tinder and the Omani government for a response.

Oman’s underground sex industry is still a long way off rivalling some of the world’s raunchiest cities.

In Marmaris, Turkey, almost every beach bar showcases buff, young male staff who are topless, oiled up and putting on sexy performances for pleasure-seekers, including thousands of Brits.

The holiday hotspot has surged in popularity among British women, many from the younger crowd, with throngs jetting out each summer in search of a steamy beach romance.



A place dubbed “Disneyland for swingers” has also emerged as a sex hotspot where Brits romp on sunbeds and are gifted X-rated “swag bags”.

Known as Spicy Island, the top secret location sits off the coast of Croatia and is a far cry from your budget all-inclusive package holiday.

Hundreds of people flock there to experience two weeks of blistering sun and plenty of sex making it a swingers paradise.

News.title: Road rage killer Tracie Andrews gets behind the wheel of car 30 years after she stabbed her fiancé 42 times to death
News.content:
Next

ROAD rage killer Tracie Andrews has been spotted behind the wheel of a car again as she runs errands in a British seaside town.

Andrews savagely stabbed her fiance, Lee Harvey, 25, more than 40 times in Worcestershire in 1996.



The convicted murderer, who was released from prison in 2011, went on to appear on television just days after the killing.

Andrews, then 29, told police and witnesses they were victims of road rage after she was found in the car covered in blood.



She explained that their car had been chased by another motorist who went on to attack them.

Appearing before cameras at a press conference a couple of days after the murder in 1996, Andrews appeared bruised, tearful and distraught.

She held the hand of Lee’s mother spinning a web of lies that would eventually expose her as the killer.

Andrews, now 57, lives under a new name in a south west seaside town.



She was spotted running errands – at a McDonald’s drive-thru and visiting a Post Office – behind the wheel of a blue motor.

Andrews has returned to her dyed blonde hair after going brunette on her release from prison.

She spent 14 years in prison and was released in 2012, changing her name and undergoing surgery, and even marrying bouncer boyfriend Phil Goldsworthy in 2017.

At trial she pleaded self-defence but was found guilty of the murder and sentenced to life behind bars.

Aspiring model Andrews worked in Worcestershire as a barmaid, and already had a young daughter when she met Lee in a nightclub and started a relationship.



Three months after meeting the pair moved in together and quickly got engaged.

But Andrews was a jealous partner and would often burst into a rage if she didn’t feel she was getting the treatment she deserved from her partner.

Their arguments began to escalate, frequently turning violent, including incidents where Andrews hit Lee with a bottle.



After a fierce day of fighting on Sunday 1 December, the pair headed to a local pub to smooth things out then got into his white Ford Escort to head home.

The next that anyone saw of the couple was when a local resident, hearing a commotion, went outside to the country lane where their car was parked and found Lee brutally murdered.

During the now infamous press conference that followed Andrews lied about what had happened.

She said at the time: “They overtook us and pulled in and Lee got out of the car,” Tracy said at the time. There was some sort of argument going on.

“The passenger called me a slut and punched me in the face. Afterwards I went to Lee, I don’t know whether he was alive.



“I held him, I cradled his head and was just thinking of anything I could do for him.”

During the press conference, concern was raised about her story, which differed from what she had told police.

Officers at the press conference had to stop her answering questions from journalists.

When she was brought to court for sentencing after being found out, judge Mr Justice Buckley said: “The jury has found you guilty on very strong evidence of murder.

“Only you know precisely what went on that night but we have all seen the awful consequences.



“Certainly it has been a tragedy for all concerned and I feel deeply for the families on both sides.”

It would be two years before Andrews wrote a letter from her cell confessing to the murder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andrews would later go on to change her name to Jenna and spent £5,000 of taxpayers’ money on surgery to change the shape of her jaw, before being released after serving 14 years.

Her current husband Paul Goldsworthy allegedly left his wife and kids to be with her.

News.title: How Scott Peterson guilty of killing pregnant wife could be INNOCENT as witnesses claim she was alive on ‘day of murder’
News.content:
Next

ON CHRISTMAS Eve 2002, 27-year-old Laci Peterson vanished from her home in Modesto, California, while eight months pregnant.

Her husband Scott told police he had last seen her that morning when he left the house to go fishing.



When he returned that evening, the house was empty, apart from their dog in the yard.

At 6pm, when there was still no sign of Laci, he called police.



The disappearance sparked a huge search from friends, family and locals Peterson appeared unusually calm and nonchalant instantly sparking suspicion among police.

But it wasn’t until a woman named Amber Frey came forward that he became a prime suspect.



Amber, who worked as a massage therapist, informed detectives she had met Peterson on 20 November 2002 and they had begun a romantic relationship.

She said that he had told her he was a widower and that coming Christmas would be his first without his wife leading police to believe he had already been plotting to kill her.



On 13 April, 2003, two people out walking their dog found the body of a male foetus on a tidal flat of the San Francisco Bay.

The following day, a jogger spotted a human torso about a mile away.

DNA tests confirmed the bodies were Laci and her unborn son, Conner.

Laci’s body was severely decomposed, and missing its head, arms, lower legs, and internal organs.

Scott was arrested and charged with two counts of murder.



At his trial in 2004, prosecutors claimed Peterson had had killed his wife because he was having an affair with Amber Frey and claimed that on the night of 23 December, 2002, he strangled Laci in her sleep and dumped her in the water at San Francisco Bay in the early hours of Christmas Eve.

He was convicted of the first-degree murder of Laci and the second-degree murder of their unborn son and is currently serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole.

But more than 20 years later, the LA Innocence Project – a nonprofit legal advocacy organisation – took on Peterson’s case saying it had new evidence that supported his claims of innocence and listing several factors suggesting he did not get a fair trial.



The key points are:

Vital evidence destroyed by police

Multiple witnesses who said they saw Laci after her supposed death but were ignored

New biometric and tidal science suggesting that Laci died much later than 24 December and that her body would not have ended up where it was found if it had been dumped where Scott was fishing.

A lack of any forensic evidence

In the three-part TV documentary, Scott Peterson: The New Evidence, attorney Chris Pixley goes back over the case, detailing the anomalies and irregularities with which both he and the LAIP say, proves that his conviction was not viable and that he was wrongfully prosecuted.

“If you ask people about this case, they’ll just tell you that Scott did it,” says Chris.

“But what if everything we knew was just wrong?

“Firstly, the LAIP argues that new foetal biometric science suggests that Laci Peterson didn’t die on 24 December and that she may not have died for many days or even weeks later.



“If they’re right, it means that Scott Peterson is innocent.

“Secondly, new computational hydrodynamic modelling suggests that if Laci Peterson’s body had been placed in the bay in the location where Scott was fishing, her body and Conner’s body would not have been recovered where they were.”

Chris described that new science has been a ‘game changer’ in the case.

He adds, “They are also challenging the integrity of the criminal investigation, arguing that not only did the Modesto police not investigate the many witnesses that came forward with sightings of Laci on the morning of December 24th, they also destroyed evidence in the case.

“The state’s theory is that Scott murdered his wife, wrapped her body in blue tarpaulin, loaded it into the back of his truck and covered it with some umbrellas.



“Then he drove to his warehouse, put the body into his fishing boat, drove that on its trailer to Berkeley Marina and dumped the body into the water.

“What is the likelihood that you’re going to be able to move the body multiple times, all without leaving any forensic evidence of Laci behind?

“None of her DNA, her hair, her blood, her bodily fluids, wound up anywhere on the cover or in the boat.



“Another part of the prosecution’s theory is that he didn’t just clean up one crime scene, but four.

“After Laci Peterson was reported missing, one of the first investigators to come to the Peterson home was Detective Brocchini.”

Chris also says that he has become interested in how cooperative Peterson was.

“He agreed to searches of his home, of his place of business, the warehouse where he worked and handed over his phone,” he explains.

“Not only did Brocchini focus on Scott Peterson from day one, but he did some highly unusual things in his investigation.



“One of them is that the notes he took on 24 and 25 December went missing.

“He testified in court that he had destroyed them. Why?”

Scott’s demeanour in a filmed police interview, sitting with his hands in his pockets, answering questions that might be considered to be nonchalant, added to suspicion about him.

PROSECUTION’S TIMELINE 24 Dec 9.30am. Scott tells police that he last saw his wife at about 9:30 a.m. when he left to go fishing off the Berkeley Marina, California. The prosecution contends that he drove Laci’s body to the bay and dumped her. Conner Peterson dies. 10.18am Karen Servas, a neighbour says she saw their dog alone, outside, and returned him to the Peterson’s back yard. 10.30am (approx.) Their neighbours, the Medina’s, leave for a festive break in LA. 26 Dec 4.00am – 6.30am Some time between these hours police say the Medina’s home was burgled. 4.20pm (approx.) The Medina’s return home to find their house has been burgled. 30 Dec Amber Frey reveals to police her affair with Scott. 13 April The foetus of Conner is found washed ashore near Marina Bay, Richmond. 14 April Laci’s body is found not far away from Conner, at Point Isabel, Richmond.

“The state argued that the portions of that tape they showed suggested that this was not a grieving husband who was concerned at the disappearance of his wife, but instead that it was a man who lacked any emotion,” says Chris.

“But they rolled out very limited pieces of Scott’s on-camera interview so that his answers and responses just seemed out of line with the gravity of the circumstances.



“They are leaving out important facts about the number of hours that this man spent answering questions before he actually went on camera.

“Peterson reports that on the day of Laci’s disappearance, he was interrogated four separate times and it was only the fourth time, at the station, on camera, that the rest of us have been able to see.

“He was peppered with questions to the point of exhaustion.”

Chris says that further evidence about a Christmas gift could point to Peterson’s innocence.

“About two weeks before Laci went missing, Scott purchased a 14-foot aluminium fishing boat,” he says.



“The prosecution state that he bought it with the express purpose of murdering his wife and using it to deposit her body.

“But he says he was taking the boat out to test it, because he had purchased it for his father-in-law as a Christmas gift.

“The prosecution, throughout the trial, argued that the purchase of the boat was not known to Laci.

“But in 2024, the LAIP found handwritten notes that were in the Peterson’s home that were not turned over to the defence.

“The notes have the phone numbers of local marine supply stores written on them.



“A handwriting expert that the LAIP used and one I went to, both believe that it is Laci’s writing.

“That means that she was not only aware of the boat, but that she participated in the purchase of accessories for it.

“Prosecution has a theory that Laci Peterson was calling marine supply stores to buy items of a nautical theme that she had for Conner’s nursery room.



“But these are not notes where she wanted to buy some small rubber ducks.

“She’s pricing an anchor, and that’s not something that you’re going to hang over the baby’s crib.”

Nearly four months after Laci disappeared, her torso and the foetus of her son were washed ashore.

“The state presented testimony at Scott Peterson’s trial through a Doctor Cheng, who was a tidal expert,” Chris says.

“He said that for the bodies to have washed up on the Richmond shoreline, the most likely launch point would have been exactly where Scott Peterson was fishing.



“But new science is challenging the viability of that narrative.

“Doctor Feagin, the LAIP’s expert, has done something called computational hydrodynamic modelling using the Delft 3-D modelling system.

“He ran various simulations, including trajectory and wind simulations, and concluded that the bodies were likely to have been put in the water at Albany Bulb.”

Karen Servas, a neighbour of the Peterson’s, said that she found their dog alone outside their home at 10.18am on Christmas Eve and returned him to the Peterson’s back yard.

“This is a timeline case and the state established their entire timeline on the basis of the testimony of one person, Karen Servas,” says Chris.



“But was her testimony as critical as prosecutors made it out to be?

“At trial, her testimony was presented on the premise that Laci Peterson had already been murdered by the morning of December 24th, and therefore didn’t take her dog, McKenzie, out for her normal morning walk.

“The state never addressed how McKenzie got a leash on in the first place, why she was out in the front yard, or any alternative timeline that would have involved Laci preparing to go for a walk and being called back into the house.

“Possibility exists that because Karen Servas didn’t knock on the door and give the dog back to Laci, that she was alive and well and inside the house.”

Chris says Karen was not the only eyewitness that morning.



“Central to the LAIP’s case is that there were 15 eyewitnesses who said they saw Laci walking her dog that morning, after Scott had already left for the San Francisco Bay,” he explains.

“These people came forward immediately but according to the LAIP, most of their statements were never followed up by the Modesto Police.”

“Another cause for concern, which the police discounted, is that the Peterson’s neighbours, the Medina’s, who left home to stay with their family in LA on 24 December, found their home had been burgled when they returned at 4.20pm on 26 December.

“Two other neighbours reported to police that they believed that on 23 December, their homes were being cased by burglars,” says Chris.

“A man had knocked on their doors with some story about a missing dog, which they didn’t believe and thought was suspicious.



LAIP’S ALTERNATIVE TIMELINE 24 Dec A suspicious van is seen in the area that morning. Laci’s body is deposited in the water not at Berkeley Marina, where Scott was fishing, but at Albany Bulb. The Medina’s home is burgled – the same day as Laci vanished. 25 Dec The white van is found burning a mile and a half away from the Peterson home. It is arson. 28 Dec to early January The time range that Connor Peterson is believed to have died.

“So, maybe they were trying to figure out who’s going to be around for the holidays and who’s not.”

There were also seven witnesses who said they saw a suspicious van in the area before Laci was murdered.

The thieves – Steven Wayne Todd and Donald Glenn Pearce – were soon caught and admitted to the robbery which included a safe.

“The police say the burglary occurred between four and six thirty on the morning of 26 December,” says Chris.

“The problem with that story is that when Laci Peterson went missing, it immediately became huge news.



“There were television crews and vans up and down the street by the 26th and none of them saw a heavy safe being hauled out of the Medina’s house into the street.

“If, instead, the burglary occurred the same day Laci went missing, that means there’s an entirely plausible explanation for her disappearance that has nothing to do with Scott Peterson.

“Laci was a member of the neighbourhood watch and she was known as being very vigilant.”

Chris argues that there is an alternative timeline on Christmas Eve.

He says: “An alternative timeline is that on 24 December, the thieves turned up in their van to burgle the Medina’s house across the street from the Peterson’s and Laci went out to confront them and they took possession of her.



“The van was found burning on Christmas Day, after an arson attack at the airport district of Modesto a mile and a half away.

“It was investigated and ultimately closed without being connected in any way to the Peterson case.

“The defence never received any information about the van being set alight.

“That came out only years after Scott was convicted.

“In the back of that van was a mattress.



“And while the mattress and the van burned, parts of that mattress remained intact and appeared to have blood on it.

“The state says that in testing the mattress, they determined it was not blood.

“But to this day, there is no consensus about whether or not this was, in fact, a blood stained mattress.

“Throughout the petition, the LAIP is claiming that the Modesto Police Department and the Stanislaus County DA’s office destroyed and suppressed evidence related to the burglary and the van fire to keep Peterson’s defence team from having it.

“At the trial, the state’s expert, Doctor DeVore, testified that Conner Peterson died around 24 December, the day Laci went missing.



“He was relying upon studies from 1984 to determine Conner Peterson’s gestational age at the time of death.

“Doctor Doubilet, the LA Innocence Project’s expert, used more recent studies and was able to identify Conner’s likely date of death as sometime between December 28th and as late as January of 2003.

“That range completely contradicts the state’s timeline.”

On 27 April, 2026, the Superior Court of California, county of San Mateo, denied the LAIP’s petition for habeas corpus – a legal procedure to determine whether the imprisonment of a convicted person is legal.

“The judge’s decision was that the new evidence presented was inadmissible.



“We’re talking about new scientific evidence, science that did not exist 24 years ago.

“This is a case that demands review. It’s not closed.

“The LAIP will appeal to the California Supreme Court, and if they have to, they can take it all the way to the federal appeals courts, which of course includes the U.S. Supreme Court.”

No members of law enforcement involved in the Laci Peterson investigation or the Medina burglary investigation agreed to requests for an interview for the documentary.

Scott Peterson: The New Evidence can be seen on Crime+Investigation this Sunday

News.title: Innocent man, 53, shot dead by stray bullet while cycling through Spanish holiday resort
News.content:
GUNNED DOWN Innocent man, 53, shot dead by stray bullet while cycling through Spanish holiday resort







Next

AN INNOCENT cyclist has been shot dead by a stray bullet as a terrifying wave of gun violence grips Spain’s Costa holiday hotspots.

The 53-year-old man was caught in the crossfire of a violent altercation in La Linea, a short drive from the popular British resort of Estepona.

The victim, identified only as Alonso S.C., was reportedly cycling through a residential neighbourhood when he was struck by a bullet.

Police believe he was shot by accident and have confirmed he had no criminal record.





One local described Alonso as a “good man”, while an unconfirmed report suggested he may have been trying to break up a street fight when he was killed.

The horror shooting unfolded in the early hours of yesterday morning, with police launching an investigation.

No arrests have yet been made.

It comes as cops investigate another suspected murder after a man’s decomposing body was discovered floating in the sea with a gunshot wound to his head.

The unidentified victim, described as a white male, was found near the secluded Zacatin Cove on Spain’s Costa Tropical in Granada province.

The beauty spot, west of Castell de Ferro, is popular with divers, kayakers and nature enthusiasts.

Police confirmed the man had both an entry and exit wound to his head.

Detectives are treating the death as a probable murder but have not ruled out other possibilities.



They have yet to establish how long the body had been in the water, and no weapon has been reported found.

The grim discovery follows two separate murders in just three days in Almeria, around an hour’s drive east along the coast.

The first victim, recycling plant worker Antonio Santiago, was gunned down in the early hours of Wednesday as he headed to his car after finishing a night shift.

Antonio was the brother of Juana Santiago, who was recently released from prison after serving a 23-year sentence for the March 2002 murder of a seven-year-old girl.

Another man was shot dead on Friday morning in a suspected drugs-related killing.



The fatal bullet severed his aorta, with one of the two suspected gunmen already arrested.

Hours later, around 6pm, another man was gunned down at a tattoo parlour in Badalona, near Barcelona.

Police are hunting two suspects believed to be Colombian nationals.

The latest bloodshed comes as detectives continue investigating the assassination of UK-trained plastic surgeon Alexander Aslani in Marbella.

The 57-year-old father-of-two was shot dead in front of horrified customers at his Cirumed Clinic on October 7.



An 18-year-old Swedish national suspected of fleeing the scene on a Yamaha maxi-scooter was arrested the following day and remanded in custody.

But investigators believe he may have been a hired hitman and are now examining the surgeon’s patient files to identify who could have ordered the killing.

Police are understood to be focusing on a potentially disgruntled former patient following reports of threats against the surgeon.

Last weekend, it emerged that a woman who allegedly threatened Mr Aslani after he refused to refund her Brazilian butt lift had left Spain.

The woman, described locally as being of “Arabic origin”, reportedly demanded her money back after becoming unhappy with the results of her surgery.



Her husband is also said to have visited the clinic before the killing to “issue warnings to staff”.

Mr Aslani, whose celebrity clients included former Towie star Chloe Sims and Big Brother contestant Aisleyne Horgan-Wallace, had complained to police in April about receiving “work-related” threats.

It remains unclear whether he named any suspects in his statement.

Amid the mounting violence, police are also investigating a terrifying attempted kidnapping in an upmarket Marbella neighbourhood.

A 25-year-old man narrowly escaped after four masked men allegedly tried to abduct him at gunpoint in Alto de los Monteros.



The hillside residential area lies around three miles north-east of the clinic where Mr Aslani was murdered.

The victim told police that three attackers armed with a pistol and iron bars tried to force him out of his car and into another vehicle during the early-hours ambush.

But he managed to escape by reacting quickly and speeding away before they could seize him.

His nationality has not been made public, and police are continuing to investigate the attempted abduction.

The Spanish government has responded to growing fears over gang violence by announcing additional police reinforcements for Malaga.



Officials have also sought to reassure holidaymakers, insisting tourists visiting the popular British destination can have “complete peace of mind”.

More to follow… For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Sun Online

News.title: CFB Wainwright fire - latest: Four dead and dozens injured in Alberta military base disaster
News.content:
At least seven people are dead and dozens more have been left injured after an explosion and fire at CFB Wainwright, after what sources have said was an accident during a live-fire training exercise

Major fire at Canada military base: What we know so far

Four service members have been killed with dozens more seriously injured following a major fire at the Alberta military base, the Prime Minister Mark Carney has confirmed

Speaking from Ottowa on Sunday night, he said the situation is "evolving rapidly" with a formal briefing scheduled later today.

"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces who we have lost," he said and confirmed flags will be flown at half-mast.

The blaze started near the CFB Wainwright Canadian Forces Base in Alberta at around 4pm local time yesterday (Saturday) and "spread rapidly due to high winds".

Canadian TV network Global News reported that the incident happened when a gas line or gas well was hit during a live-fire training exercise, citing unnamed military sources.

Dr Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at the Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, said: "This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton and that is why we are clearing our decks and mobilizing to respond as if it was our own city.

"It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster. It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster."

Prime Minister of Canada Mark Carney said in a post on X: "Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected.

"We are working closely with the Government of Alberta and local authorities. Premier Smith and I are in close contact as are our relevant ministers and officials."

News.title: John Healey faces Budget pressure to help '372,000 renters living on £7 or less a day'
News.content:
John Healey faces Budget pressure to help '372,000 renters living on £7 or less a day'

EXCLUSIVE: England’s poorest private renters are struggling to afford a weekly food shop, with households left with just £7 or less a day after rent and basic bills, grim research shows

View 3 Images Shelter is urging Chancellor John Healey to accelerate the Government's social housebuilding programme (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

England’s poorest private renters are struggling to afford a weekly food shop, with households left with just £7 or less a day after rent and basic bills, grim research shows.

‌



‌



An estimated 372,652 private renting households have less than £50 a week to spend after paying for rent, council tax, water and energy bills – this is just £7 or less a day, according to analysis by Shelter.

‌



The homelessness charity warned this means the poorest renters cannot afford the average cost of a weekly food shop at £50.60, let alone the extra cost of basic daily necessities such as food, clothing, internet and travel costs, including commuting to work or taking children to school. Polling released alongside the study shows nearly a quarter (23%) of working private renters say they have no savings and would be immediately unable to pay their rent if they lost their job.

‌



Shelter said the situation is worsening, with the number of households with less than £50 a week left after paying their rent and essential bills having increased by nearly a third (31%), or 87,358 households since 2021/22.

View 3 Images Jane said she fears being evicted if her rent payments fall into arrears (Image: Supplied)

Self-employed hairdresser Jane, 53, who currently lives in a private rental in Romford with her two daughters, 11 and 19, said her family have endured appalling conditions since moving into the property in 2019.

‌



The mum, who has to wipe mould off the walls every day, f ears she won’t be able to cover the cost of food after her landlord slapped her with a £400 rent increase from next month.

Jane said she fears being evicted if her rent payments fall into arrears. “There’s not much money left after rent and bills," she said. "We can barely afford essentials, let alone anything else. I have to budget just to afford food, and I’m already cutting back. We don’t have days out anymore and we’ve been walking instead of driving. I’m worried I won’t be able to put the heating on when it gets cold. I’m not sleeping at night - I’m worried all the time about becoming homeless as a result of the rent increase.

“A social home would change everything. It would be a home for life, and I wouldn’t have the fear of being evicted and having to move or a landlord increasing the rent suddenly. Plus, it’s genuinely affordable. I would be able to afford the rent, bills, food and heating instead of worrying and being left penniless. It would be like winning the lottery.”

‌



Ahead of this month's Budget, Shelter is urging Chancellor John Healey to accelerate the Government's social housebuilding programme and provide more people with a long-term alternative to costly private renting. The charity argues that increasing the supply of social homes, where rents are linked to local incomes and are on average 67% lower than private rents, would reduce the number of families struggling.

It says one of the "biggest" barriers to preventing councils from building at scale is £31.8billion worth of housing debt that was transferred in 2012 as part of a council house financing agreement. Research carried out by Savills for Shelter shows that removing this "unfair debt burden" at the Budget on October 28 could unlock 284,000 social rent homes, with every £1bn of debt removed enabling 8,900 new homes to be delivered.

View 3 Images Homelessness charity Shelter warned this means the poorest renters cannot afford the average cost of a weekly food shop (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Mairi MacRae, acting chief executive at Shelter, said: “It is clear our housing system is on its knees when hundreds of thousands of private renters have £7 a day or less to feed and clothe themselves, after paying their rent and basic bills.

“Decades of poor political choices have driven down the supply of genuinely affordable social homes and pushed millions into expensive private renting. As their housing costs soar, more families are locked in survival mode scraping around for every penny to pay for life’s essentials. Those who constantly find themselves in the red face homelessness and destitution.

“If the government wants families to thrive, instead of barely survive, it must accelerate social housebuilding and provide an alternative to private renting. The Prime Minister should use his first Budget to remove the historic housing debt burden that’s holding councils back from building social homes.”

Article continues below

An MHCLG spokesman said: “We know that far too many people are struggling with their rent, which is why we are supporting delivery of the homes the country needs and investing £39 billion to give the biggest boost to social and affordable housing in a generation.”

Savanta surveyed 3,337 adults (18+), including 1,461 private renters who are employed, between April 21 and May 8.

News.title: Man dead after being hit on M56 as he ran across motorway away from police
News.content:
Man dead after being hit on M56 as he ran across motorway away from police

The incident saw the motorway closed in both directions for hours on Saturday night

View Image The motorway was closed for hours (Image: Submitted)

A man who was being pursued by police after driving 'dangerously' on the M56 was struck and killed by another driver who was allegedly under the influence of alcohol or drugs, police have said.

‌



‌



The M56 in Greater Manchester was closed in both directions on Saturday (October 17) after a horror crash between a pedestrian and a vehicle.

‌



Greater Manchester Police has said officers were initially pursuing a man on a red motorbike after noticing he was driving in "a dangerous manner" on the M60 around Stockport Pyramid at around 7.30pm.

‌



After officers pursued and brought the bike to a stop between junctions 3 and 4 on the M56, the bike rider made off on foot across the motorway where he was then struck by another vehicle.

Despite the best efforts of paramedics, the driver of the bike was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

The force said the driver of the car that struck the man, who was not involved in the initial pursuit, was arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing death by careless driving when under the influence of drink or drugs and causing death by driving uninsured.

‌



GMP said the motorbike had been posing a "significant risk to members of the public" on the motorway and made "tactical contact at low speed" with the bike on the hard shoulder near junction 5.

As per procedures following a fatality after police contact, GMP has referred the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC). It has been decided an independent investigation is required to establish the full circumstances of the incident.

The force said it is now awaiting the conclusion of that investigation.

Article continues below

Meanwhile the Serious Collisions Investigation Unit is appealing for information regarding the incident to assist with the investigation.

Anyone with information, Dash Cam, or CCTV footage is urged to contact Greater Manchester Police on 101 and quote log 2974-17/10/26. Reports can also be made via the LiveChat function at gmp.police.uk

Alternatively, contact Crimestoppers, anonymously, on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Nigel Farage's asylum plan 'betrays Britain's proud history' says senior Bishop
News.content:
Nigel Farage's asylum plan 'betrays Britain's proud history' says senior Bishop

EXCLUSIVE: The Right Reverend Dr Guli Francis-Dehqani, Bishop of Chelmsford - who sits in the House of Lords - told The Mirror that Reform UK's policy goes against Christian values

View 2 Images Nigel Farage has previously spoken about Reform UK's Christian values (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

One of the UK's most senior Bishops has warned that Nigel Farage's proposed asylum ban "betrays Britain's proud history".

‌



‌



The Right Reverend Dr Guli Francis-Dehqani, Bishop of Chelmsford, told The Mirror that a plan to shut down the asylum system for five years, as proposed by the Reform leader, flies in the face of Christian teachings. Mr Farage has repeatedly spoken about Judeo-Christian values - saying these are the heart of what makes Britain great.

‌



But he has faced heavy criticism from Christian leaders. The latest intervention comes just days after the Catholic Church of England and Wales voiced its opposition to Mr Farage's draconian plan. Dr Francis-Dehqani, one of 25 Church of England Bishops who sit in the House of Lords, told The Mirror: "Christians are called to love our neighbours and show hospitality to the stranger, a tradition deeply embedded in Britain's long-standing history of protecting those fleeing danger and persecution.

‌



View 2 Images Dr Guli Francis-Dehqani, Bishop of Chelmsford, has criticised proposals to shut down Britain's asylum system (Image: PA Media)

"A policy that dismantles our asylum system and slams the door on all those seeking sanctuary, including children and those who have come through established routes, betrays Britain's proud history of helping those most in need. Instead of locking out the vulnerable, politicians should develop proposals for building a fair, efficient and humane asylum system that honours the inherent dignity of those seeking sanctuary here.”

Last week Mr Farage announced he would bring in a five-year asylum pause if he becomes PM. This would mean Britain would not process any new asylum claims, regardless of their merit - which has sparked outrage among religious leaders.

‌



James Tullett, chief executive at Refugee and Migrant Justice, told The Mirror: "We see every day how faith groups support people in their hour of need. Unlike many politicians who seek to exploit and divide us, bishops, imams, priests, rabbis and other religious leaders regularly preach a message of love, tolerance, acceptance and welcoming thy neighbour.

"This is the UK at its best, a place that does not shirk its responsibilities towards those seeking sanctuary and recognises its moral and legal obligations under international law. We would be a much more united society if our political leaders practised these same values.”

On Wednesday The Mirror reported that the Catholic Church had come out against Mr Farage's latest proposals. It pointed to Pope Leo’s warnings about hatred and division when asked for its position on Mr Farage’s announcement.

‌



In a statement a Church spokesperson said: “The Gospel calls us to welcome the stranger, and that call must shape how we speak about and respond to people seeking safety. In 2023, The Bishops’ of England and Wales published a document called Love The Stranger reminding us that every migrant has a name, a face and a story.

"As Pope Leo recently commented after his Apostolic Journey to France: ‘We can go back to the values of the Gospel, which are not about hatred and division, they are about understanding, compassion and accompaniment.

"'I hope deeply, and the Church can be part of this, that we can find ways of reaching out to a majority of people of goodwill who will understand how important their commitment is, even in terms of participating in political processes, to make clear choices for the common good and not for extremist ideas (that perhaps will do much more damage than we are even aware of now).

‌



"For our part, we [promote] the social doctrine of the Church, talking about, teaching about, preaching about what we believe. These are life-giving values and not about destruction, division, and hatred."’

Last Monday Reform confirmed its plan would involve removing women and children from countries like Sudan and Afghanistan - but it is not clear where they would be sent.

Mr Farage said: "All of the Tories' and Labour's immigration schemes - Afghanistan, Palestine - will immediately be closed. Every asylum grant given in the prior five years will be reviewed.

‌



"Those who came illegally, or from a safe country, will have their asylum grant revoked and be deported. Countries that refuse to take back their illegal migrants and criminals will face visa bans, sanctions, and tariffs."

The Reform chief has previously come under fire from religious leaders over his party's draconian migration plans. Last year the Archbishop of York, Stephen Cottrell - who was the top Church of England bishop at the time - said Reform's deportation proposals were "beneath us as a nation".

Mr Farage hit back by claiming the Church of England had "gone to the dogs". Former Lib Dem leader Tim Farron, who chairs the Christians in Parliament group, said it is "inexcusable" to make such claims about Christian values.

‌



He told The Mirror: "Nigel Farage has said that he believes Christian values are what has made Britain great – I don’t disagree, in fact the values of western liberal democracies are fundamentally shaped by the gospel.

"One of those Christian values is that each human being is made in God’s image and loved by God. It’s a massive contradiction to say that we should be a Christian country but then to say things which are diametrically opposed to Christianity, such as denying people any basic human dignity.

"Nigel Farage does not claim to be a Christian and I applaud his honesty on that. But he then says he wants Britain to be run on Christian values whilst clearly not understanding them. And that is what’s inexcusable."

‌



Mr Farage - who makes no claims to be a devout Christian himself - has previously spoken about advancing Christian values. He told a press conference in February: "I can see that so much of what makes Britain such a great country is associated and irrevocably derived from Christian heritage."

And in an Easter message earlier this year he said: "The Christian values on which our country is built are something to be proud of."

Other prominent critics have included the Bishop of Oxford, who said it was "deeply disturbing" that Reform had attempted to "stoke division for political advantage".

Article continues below

Challenged about the comments by senior Bishops, Mr Farage said: "You've just encapsulated beautifully, I couldn't have done it better myself, why the Church of England has gone to the dogs.

"I think they've got a rather twisted view of what their flock in this country actually want them to do."

News.title: Apprentice, 20, died after room on board trawler filled with 'toxic gasses'
News.content:
Apprentice, 20, died after room on board trawler filled with 'toxic gasses'

Apprentice engineer Connor Moseley, 20, died after a fire suppression system unexpectedly activated and released aerosol inside a crowded engine room on a trawler boat

View 2 Images Connor Moseley, 20, tragically died after inhaling aerosol (Image: HSE / SWNS)

A fishing company apprentice died after a room on board a trawler filled with toxic gasses.

‌



‌



Connor Moseley, 20, was an apprentice engineer when he died on board the Resurgam in November 2019 while it was moored in Newlyn harbour in Cornwall. He inhaled aerosol from the fire suppression system that unexpectedly activated in the crowded engine room.

‌



Conor and three other workers were carrying out work on the Resurgam, a fishing vessel owned and operated by W. Stevenson & Sons Limited, on November 15, 2019. Steven & Sons was fined £100,000 with an additional £27,906 in costs following the hearing on Thursday.

‌



The Health and Safety Executive said the fire suppression system which was being installed by Ocean Engineering (Fire) Ltd unexpectedly activated and filled the engine room with hot, toxic gases, creating dangerous conditions and making it difficult to see.

View 2 Images Toxic gasses filled up in the crowded engine room (Image: HSE / SWNS)

Warning update for sertraline, citalopram and fluoxetine after number of deaths READ MORE :

The small, enclosed engine room had only one way in and out. Workers had to climb a ladder and pass through a hatch one at a time, passing through a gas jet in excess of 75C.

‌



The other workers managed to climb out, but Conor was overcome by carbon monoxide and other substances, leaving him unable to escape. Conor's colleagues tried to rescue him but they were unable to reach him.

Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service later rescued Conor from the engine room, but he could not be revived. Truro Crown Court heard that health and safety failings included no evacuation plan or sufficient leadership.

Conor's mother Tracy Moseley said she was not allowed to hold her son as he lay dying on the ship and his death has left a hole in their lives which will never be filled. Speaking after the case, she also reflected on her son's life and the impact his death has had on them.

‌



She added: "Growing up Conor loved nothing better than helping out on his dad's boat.

"Conor always made himself available to help his father when he came in from sea and would be ready to help him land his catch even after a full day's work. Now for Steve, my husband, there is just an empty place that cannot be filled.

"All we have now are his ashes which are kept in his bedroom. Every morning I go in and say, 'morning little man I love you' and blow him a kiss. I never say 'good morning' as it can never be a good morning without him.

Article continues below

"At night I blow him a kiss and say 'night night little man, I love you'." An investigation by the HSE found that the risks created by several contractors working in the cramped engine room had not been properly considered.

One contractor described the room as a mess, with poor lighting and trip hazards, and said that at one point six or seven people were working in the space. One witness described it as chaos. There was no safe system of work for installing the fire suppression system and no effective emergency plan.

The HSE said a permit-to-work system could have been used to coordinate the different activities and ensure they were carried out safely. It said its code of practice also highlights the need for parties to work together and have an overall written plan covering responsibilities, shared risks and emergency arrangements.

News.title: France riots: Paris stores looted and Limoges town hall burns - cops arrest 2,000
News.content:
France riots: Paris stores looted and Limoges town hall burns - cops arrest 2,000

Organisers said around 800,000 people took to the streets of France in hundreds of marches, many of which turned violent with looting, arson and violent clashes with the police

Paris violence: Masked protesters dance as disorder breaks out

The French president Emmanuel Macron is set to address the nation following ongoing unrest where 2,000 people have now been arrested.

Chaos hit the streets of France yesterday as rallies held to protest the cost of living, education standards and the state of public services turned violent with police admitting they "lost control".

The president is now set to hold an emergency meeting with top government officials on Sunday afternoon, before addressing the nation at 8pm, according to reports.

Students were joined by unions and the gilets jaunes (yellow vests) as more than half a million people took to the streets.

While many protested peacefully, violence erupted across France, with horror images showing looting, burning buildings and vehicles and confrontations with cops. The city hall in Limoges was burned down with its 143-year-old spire collapsing, while a tourist office in Lyon also went up in flames. Crowds fought running battles with police in Paris, Lyon, and Marseille.

Several videos posted on social media show shop owners outside their businesses pleading with balaclava-clad looters to spare their stores. In one, a distraught woman is seen begging rioters in Paris not to loot a supermarket.

She is heard asking "why are you doing this" and screaming "this is not the cause" as a group of young male rioters push past her into the smashed shop.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

French police arrested more than 2,000 people across the country, as the force admitted it was unable to cope with disorder on such a massive scale.

"It was apocalyptic," a senior commander told Sunday's Le Parisien newspaper. "Law enforcement was unable to contain the multitude of simultaneous attacks occurring across the country, and was quickly overwhelmed by determined protesters."

In Paris, demonstrators erected flaming barricades and hurled missiles at riot police, who responded with tear gas grenades and water cannons. In the southern city of Marseille protesters managed to storm the city hall.

View 2 Images Protestors next to a car on fire near the Porte Saint-Denis (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

About 1,500 shops and retailers were damaged in yesterday’s protests according to Alexandre Bompard, president of the Retail and Trade Federation.

Authorities said that around 550,000 people took part in the protests yesterday, but organisers claim the figure is closer to 800,000. Thirteen police and gendarmerie officers and two firefighters were injured, according to Associated Press. One protestor died of a heart attack, according to French police.

View 2 Images A protester waving a French national flag in Marseille, southern France (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

France's interior minister Laurent Nunez said more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have been injured in the demonstrations. “The material damage is considerable,” he added, pointing to damaged shops.

In a post on X the minister blamed thousands of "far-left" protesters along with "criminals who looted and ransacked" civic and private buildings across France yesterday.

Meanwhile French President Emmanuel Macron is holding a crisis meeting with ministers today in the aftermath of the protests. He is due to give a televised address to the French nation this evening.

Article continues below

The mayors of France’s three largest cities, Paris, Marseille and Lyon have asked to meet with French prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, in the coming days.

News.title: More couples getting divorced after over 20 years of marriage, new figures show
News.content:
More couples getting divorced after over 20 years of marriage, new figures show

More divorces are happening after decades of marriage as the couples get through the 'seven year itch' but face hefty costs if they do want to end their marriage

View 4 Images More couples are getting divorced later. Stock photo. (Image: Getty Images)

Forget the notorious “seven year itch” more couples are now divorcing after spending over 20 years together. The infamous affairs and splits around seven years of marriage are no longer as common as those that come after two decades, as new official figures show the rise in later divorce rates. More than a quarter of all divorces between couples of the opposite sex last year were between those who had been together for 20 years or longer, according to the Office for National Statistics.

‌



‌



Professor Emma Hitchings of Bristol University, who led a national study into the financial arrangements of divorcing couples, said: "We are moving away from the seven-year itch to the longer itch."

‌



View 4 Images Marriages lasting longer - new figures show (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



One factor "may be the cost of getting a divorce itself ". This trend has also been seen in America and Japan, where it has been dubbed the "grey divorce". In Japan, the Mainichi Shimbun newspaper reported that 24 per cent of divorces last year were between couples of at least 20 years' standing.

Lisa Pepper, a divorce lawyer at Osbornes Law, told The Sunday Times: "The largest percentage of cases I see are after a long marriage. Staying together for the sake of the children is true."

Since its records on marriage duration began in 1963, the largest proportion of divorces each year has almost always been among couples who had bene married for five to nine years proving the truth of the popular perception of a seven-year itch. Of the 102,879 heterosexual divorces in England and Wales last year, 26 per cent were between couples who had been married for 20 years or more (27,180 couples).

‌



View 4 Images Marriages lasting longer - new figures show (Image: Liverpool Echo)

23 per cent were between five and nine (24,052 couples) and 22 per cent between ten and 14 (22,197 couples). Because same-sex marriage was only legalised in 2013, there is no comparable data on couples of more than 20 years.

‌



It was only in the mid-1980s when the five-to-nine years category was briefly relegated to second place, after a new law cut the minimum term of a marriage from three years to one. It is still impossible to get divorced before your first wedding anniversary. Legal aid for family matters, except domestic abuse, was cut in 2013, making divorce an expensive proposition.

Ms Pepper added: "It's also about affordability: being at a stage in life where sufficient wealth has been accumulated to have two homes and small or no mortgages, and pension funds large enough to be able to share them fairly and both have a good standard of living."

View 4 Images Couples staying together longer before divorcing (Image: Shared Content Unit)

‌



In May, Tess Daly, the former Strictly Come Dancing presenter, announced she was separating from Vernon Kay after 22 years of marriage, and that there were "no other parties involved". Last week the newsreader Natasha Kaplinsky announced she had separated from her husband of 20 years.

In 2023 Downton Abbey star Hugh Bonneville announced he and his wife, Lulu Williams, had split after 25 years. In 2019 Colin Firth announced he was splitting from his wife, Livia Giuggioli, after 22.

Jeremy Todd, head of Coram Family Lives, a national free helpline for families in crisis, said: "Parents stay together for the sake of the children. Often empty-nest syndrome is the big reveal that there's nothing really that's keeping the couple together once their shared parenting has gone."

Article continues below

Over his 18 years at the helpline, he said the reason couples break up after so long together has consistently been poor communication and unresolved tensions. "Obviously, if all you're left with is the tumbleweed of all the issues that remain unresolved, then it's unlikely that over time that's going to sustain you," he said.

The average length of an opposite-sex relationship ending in divorce has risen from 10.7 years in 2000 to 13 years last year, the longest since records began.

News.title: Dad spots mysterious face in family lake photo – then gets chilling Facebook reply
News.content:
Dad spots mysterious face in family lake photo – then gets chilling Facebook reply

Stephanie Renaud thought she had captured a simple family moment until she spotted what appeared to be a woman's face in the background – prompting a Facebook appeal and an unexpected response

View 3 Images Kristopher Levasseur and his daughter (Image: Kristopher Levasseur/Facebook)

A family photograph taken beside a lake sparked an unsettling mystery after a spooked mum and dad spotted what appeared to be a woman's face in the background.

‌



‌



Stephanie Renaud had been photographing her partner, Kristopher Levasseur, and their young daughter at Lake Auburn in Maine. It was only when she looked at the image that evening that she noticed something neither parent could explain. Days later, Kristopher shared the picture on Facebook, asking: "Does anyone notice anything else weird about this picture? Creeping me out."

‌



Among the responses was a message from Jennifer Gallant, whose daughter Jessica had been found dead near the lake two years earlier. She wrote: "That's my daughter."

‌



The photograph was taken on September 7, 2020, during a family outing after the couple had grown tired of spending so much time indoors under Covid-19 restrictions. Kristopher, from Lewiston, Maine, was offering their daughter some snacks when Stephanie captured the moment by the water.

Nothing interrupted their day out. But that evening, as Kristopher watched television, Stephanie sat beside him studying the photograph on his phone with what was described as an almost "frightened" expression. At first, he could see nothing unusual. Then she pointed towards the top-left corner of the image, where they could make out what looked like a woman's face.

View 3 Images They supposedly captured a ghost on camera (Image: Kristopher Levasseur/Facebook)

‌



The couple spent the following week discussing the picture without finding an explanation. Their experience was later recounted by YouTuber MrBallen, known for sharing "strange, dark and mysterious stories".

He said: "Like, they didn't understand how that thing could be in frame. It really made no sense at all. And so Kristopher is like obsessing over it. So is Stephanie. And they've got no answers. None of their friends have any idea what it is."

On September 16, Kristopher uploaded the image to Facebook. In comments beneath his post, he insisted "nobody else was there" and said the photograph was giving him "goosebumps". As people shared their reactions, some suggested a connection to Jessica Gallant. Fishermen had discovered her body in a pond at the northern tip of Lake Auburn in July 2018. Her cause of death was undetermined, and an autopsy found several drugs in her system.

‌



View 3 Images Jessica Gallant was found at the lake two years before the viral photo (Image: Supplied)

Jessica's friend April Collins later told CBS she had been in recovery and was trying to build a better life for her son. April said she hoped answers would be found and expressed her belief that somebody had harmed Jessica.

One person commenting on Kristopher's photograph asked: "Could it be the person they found floating a couple years ago in the lake?" Another wrote: "Wow I just got the worst goosebumps ever after reading the comments then looking at the face." A third added: "That's just messed up."

Article continues below
