MrBallen said Jennifer believed the face in the photograph belonged to her daughter. He described her reaction: "It was her daughter's face, undeniably so, at least to Jennifer. And she's thinking, you know, the picture was taken right near Lake Auburn. That's my daughter's ghost."

He went on to say Jennifer believed her daughter's spirit was haunting the lake until her case was closed.

News.title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
News.content:
Zack Polanski has said he will not overturn a motion passed by Green Party members that declared Zionism a form of racism.

The Green leader told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, it would be party policy until 2028.

The motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month, described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It divided the party and sparked a major backlash from MPs, Jewish campaigners, the government and the European Green movement, with the equality watchdog writing to the party for more information on it.

The fallout from the motion overshadowed the final days of Polanski's campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, in which he came second to Labour, and threatened his leadership.

He came under criticism for not voting on the motion which was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 - a small fraction of the party's 230,000 members - in Brighton earlier this month.

The motion also asserted the party's backing for "a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine", a full arms embargo on Israel and a commitment to Palestinian liberation.

Asked if he would now step in as leader to overturn it, Polanski said: "I'm not going to try to overturn it.

"At the first available opportunity, I do want to amend it - I want to move away from one state, towards saying that Israelis and Palestinians should decide that future for themselves."

He said this would not be until 2028 as "you can't [amend it] within the rules, so when you vote on something in our party conference that's then policy for two years".

Kuenssberg asked if he would therefore change the rules as leader, but Polanski said: "I think if members have made a decision, then I respect the democratic will of our members."

Former Green Party co-leader and current MP Adrian Ramsay responded by calling for action to be taken sooner.

"I don't think it's tenable for us to continue the next two years with this policy that's been adopted given the huge political distraction that it's been for our councillors across the country," he told the BBC News Channel.

"One way forward could be to have a ballot of all party members to establish very clearly where does the party as a whole stand - my view is we would see a different answer."

Polanski had previously said he would not have voted for the motion without two amendments.

The first of these would have avoided "determining there was a single democratic state", and the other would have specified that the motion should not be used to discipline Jewish Green members who attend synagogues that consider themselves Zionist.

Both of these amendments were voted down by members at the party's conference.

Green MPs, including Ellie Chowns, have called for the party's member-led decision-making procedures to be reviewed given how few people took part in the vote.

News.title: Watch: Police hunt for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail
News.content:
Chicago's largest jail, and the largest single use jail in America, is Cook County.

In 2023 it saw a spike in overdose deaths. The facility, which averages one or two overdose deaths a year, lost eight inmates that year to fatal seizures. Security footage shows prisoners spasming and collapsing.

Traditional drugs were usually brought into the jail in body cavities, so the jail had the same body scanners you find at airports to prevent that happening. However, a new way of drugs entering the prison was uncovered. Drugs were being mailed into the jail soaked in the paper of the pages of books and in letters.

The BBC's Quentin Sommerville joined corrections officers at Cook County as they prepared for an early morning raid on the jail's high security D block.

To understand the challenge that authorities face in tackling the problem the BBC interviewed a former inmate and dealer, who explained how synthetic drugs can be made in the US using household ingredients and how this could change the demand for drugs from outside of the country.

Read more here.

News.title: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary
News.content:
The health secretary has asked the NHS to draw up urgent plans to speed up ending hospital "corridor care" for children.

Yvette Cooper told the BBC there would be new standards for caring for children in A&E in England, with figures collected on corridor care by age for the first time.

She was speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg where the programme highlighted the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts who died in a hospital corridor in 2024.

The health secretary has announced Â£140m to improve urgent care in England ahead of what she said would be a "more difficult" winter than usual.

The government has already pledged to end corridor care for all patients by the end of this parliament, and now Cooper has said eradicating it for children would be prioritised.

Corridor care refers to patients receiving treatment or waiting in corridors, waiting rooms or other hospital areas due to a lack of appropriate space.

The health secretary was also asked if the government would meet a key manifesto pledge that 92% of patients would start treatment within 18 weeks of booking a hospital appointment by 2029.

"That remains our manifesto commitment and of course we're going to keep working towards it," Cooper said.

Pushed further on whether the target was achievable, she replied: "The whole point about having the targets is about having something stretching that we work towards."

The 18-week target has consistently not been met for more than a decade.

Cooper said that the NHS was dealing with a number of challenges after record A&E admissions following heatwaves over the summer.

According to the latest figures for England, an estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.

On the programme the story of Finlay Roberts, who died in 2024 after spending the final hours of his life in an A&E corridor in north London was highlighted.

Finlay's father David told the BBC the situation was a "terrible mess", with the family moved into a room with a bed before being moved back into the corridor.

"He just clung to me, as we now know, slowly dying," he said.

Liz Roberts, Finlay's mother, said corridor care "robs people of their dignity when they are at their most vulnerable". She recalled being told to administer a suppository to her son in the corridor.

Cooper apologised to Finlay's parents on behalf of the NHS, saying: "No child should be treated in a corridor. No patient should be treated in a corridor."

News.title: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting
News.content:
Detectives are searching for two suspects who fled after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.

Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.

The officer is in a stable condition in hospital, where he is receiving treatment for a wound to his foot, the force added.

Detectives said a man and a woman had fled the scene and that a firearm, which could be seen within the cordon, had been found.

Angel Row is currently closed and a large police scene remains in place.

Police cars are parked along the road, which is lined by fast food stores and shops, and orange traffic cones have been laid out alongside items left on the road.

The cordon has also been extended to St James's Street, where an officer is standing guard.

The force said there would be a heightened police presence as the investigation continued.

News.title: Man, 80, who died in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond named
News.content:
An 80-year-old man who died in a light aircraft crash is understood to be flying instructor Ian Haggis.

He and a 16-year-old boy died when their plane came down near Loch Lomond. The teenager's identity has not been released.

The pair had flown out from Glasgow Airport at 16:17 and stopped transmitting at 16:37, a few miles north east of the village of Drymen near Stirling.

Emergency services were called to the crash at about 16:45 on Friday.

Both of them were pronounced dead at the scene.

Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) carries out its inquiries.

Old Drymen Road, near the scene of the crash, remains closed with vehicles being turned around and hillwalkers rerouted.

News.title: Watch: Pope thanks well-wishers in first event after cancer surgery
News.content:
Pope Leo XIV held his first public engagement since his lung cancer surgery on Sunday, as he recited the Angelus prayer from the window of Vatican's Apostolic Palace.

The surgery had taken place just a few days before, after Pope Leo had been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

After the prayer, he thanked the people who have prayed for him in recent days and said he appreciated the support. He added he will now gradually return to his commitments as he recovers.

Read more about the Pope's cancer diagnosis.

News.title: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
News.content:
An 80m (263ft) luxury vessel has been repeatedly spotted in satellite images off North Korea's Wonsan coast from July to mid-October this year.

What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end.

After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula.

This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family.

It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC.

The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size.

News.title: There's a crackdown on sports piracy but is it already out of control?
News.content:
"Football's Gone Round the Spend!" screamed The People newspaper one Sunday in July 1995. It reported breathlessly that three clubs between them were set to pay out more than Â£20m on new players.

The highlight that summer was the transfer of Stan Collymore from Nottingham Forest to Liverpool for a British record fee of Â£8.5m.

That number might not seem too impressive today, in an age when Â£100m transfers are almost commonplace. But at the time it was seismic stuff, and it symbolised the conversion of football from sport into big business.

All of this had been made possible in the early 1990s by the creation of the Premier League, and its initial TV deal with the broadcaster Sky, which paid more than Â£300m for five years of rights. The agreement put live top-tier football behind a TV paywall for the first time.

It was a lucrative model, one that other leading championships in motorsport, rugby, golf and cricket would later seek to replicate.

But now, that model is coming under pressure. Piracy has become endemic in British sports: around half of sports fans now admit to using what they might euphemistically call "alternative" means to watch paywalled material, according to the consultancy Ampere Analysis.

News.title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says
News.content:
NHS staff accessing the medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims and possible breaches over a man killed by a tiger is a "disgrace", the health secretary has said.

Speaking to the BBC, Yvette Cooper said she expected action to be taken against staff who had breached NHS data and privacy standards.

Her comments came after Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust confirmed it had sacked a total of 15 members of staff and Yorkshire Ambulance Service said William Chapman's medical records may have been accessed illegitimately.

Dr Manjeet Shehmar, NUH medical director, previously said there was "simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason".

Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper said "there's got to be proper respect for patients" from NHS staff.

"Let me be really clear about this," she said. "There are proper data and privacy standards across the NHS."

Students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020.

NUH said in May that it had sacked 11 members of staff for inappropriately accessing the victims' medical records, and had informed the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and Nottinghamshire Police of the investigation.

At the time, the ICO told the BBC it would "assess any evidence provided by the trust in due course and consider our next steps", while police said there was "no criminal investigation".

In its update about further dismissals on Friday, NUH said it had taken action against "doctors, nurses, registered healthcare professionals and other staff", and that independent regulators such as the Nursing and Midwifery Council and General Medical Council, the ICO and Nottinghamshire Police had been informed.

NUH added a new system, currently under testing, was being implemented to protect patient records in future and alert the trust to potential breaches.

News.title: Boy, 14, stabbed in shopping centre attack
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has been stabbed in a car park at Manchester's Arndale Centre shopping mall.

Greater Manchester Police said the boy was injured on the 9th floor of Manchester's Arndale Centre just after 15:00 BST on Saturday.

The force said his injuries were not believed to be life threatening or life changing. The Arndale was closed for several hours after the stabbing.

Det Insp Sam Jones said: "This is believed to be an isolated incident with no risk to the wider public."

The BBC understands a row with other males had taken place beforehand.

No arrests have been made in connection with the stabbing so far and inquiries were continuing.

News.title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked
News.content:
An officer who inappropriately accessed police records more than 2,000 times has been sacked for gross misconduct.

A West Midlands Police misconduct hearing acknowledged PC Shannon Parsons felt "isolated and disconnected" due to working part-time and returning from maternity leave, but had breached standards of professional behaviour.

Parsons had claimed there was a policing purpose to her searches, the panel said, and was seeking to "keep herself up to date, informed and was often in a position to support and assist other colleagues in operational matters".

However, chair of the panel Debra Tedds concluded the searches were carried out for the officer's "own personal benefit".

As a result, Parsons was dismissed without notice and barred from future work in policing.

The searches took part over a period of about five years, the panel heard, and many included incidents near her home address.

Parsons had an otherwise unblemished career in policing in the West Midlands, lasting 13 years, but was said to show no insight or remorse "as to the potential harm that has been caused by accessing the amount of information over a significant time period," according to the panel's report.

News.title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme
News.content:
The BBC says it will pause secondments of government statisticians to its fact checking service, BBC Verify, and review their roles.

Since 2018 the BBC has offered six-month secondment opportunities for up to two civil servant statisticians to work for BBC News's head of statistics.

A BBC spokesperson said: "All BBC journalism and editorial decisions are made by BBC journalists and editors, in line with the BBC's editorial guidelines, so the statisticians never make editorial decisions."

Those currently on secondment would not be involved in the publication of news or content during the review and the current round of recruitment will be paused while the role is reviewed, the corporation added.

The decision follows a report in The Telegraph which said embedded civil servants had been engaging in editorial tasks and raised questions about a breach of impartiality rules.

The spokesperson added that the BBC "takes independence and transparency incredibly seriously, and we must ensure we are meeting the highest standards".

They said although statisticians' work had sometimes been recognised with their names on the BBC website, "they never made editorial decisions".

According to The Telegraph, external, a job advert for the 2027 secondment said a successful candidate would have "the ability to influence decision making, working with credibility and proactively with customers to share knowledge and information".

A now-removed blog post written by one civil servant about their placements showed a secondee describing how they had drafted copy for the news website.

Under the scheme, it is understood that statisticians explain data in writing that can be incorporated into stories, but they do not write the copy itself.

Secondees' contributions can be incorporated into journalism that scrutinises the current government, as well as all political parties.

The seconded statisticians also have to adhere to the Civil Service Code of Practice for Statistics. It requires them to present and use data and statistics objectively and not to withhold or misrepresent data due to political or commercial influence.

News.title: Man arrested after boy, 16, dies in crash
News.content:
A man has been arrested after a 16-year-old boy was killed in a crash in Birmingham.

Police said the teenager was in a white Seat Ibiza which was understood to have hit railings on Shaftmoor Lane at about 20:30 BST on Saturday.

A second passenger, a boy in his teens, was taken to hospital with a serious arm injury.

A 19-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of causing death and serious injury by dangerous driving and failing to provide a breath specimen, West Midlands Police said.

The force stated the 16-year-old boy who lost his life was pronounced dead at the scene, in the Acocks Green area, despite the best efforts of paramedics.

It appealed for information, adding specialist officers from the serious collision investigation unit were asking anyone who had dashcam footage from around the time of the crash to get in touch.

News.title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'
News.content:
An 86-year-old man said learning to read has enabled him to read his and his wife's anniversary cards for the first time in 65 years.

Alan Hannay, from Dibden Purlieu, learned to read through the charity Read Easy, which helps adults across the country who struggle with the skill many of us take for granted.

Hannay told BBC Radio Solent: "It's changed my whole life, my confidence, changed my family life and everything around me.

"It's one of the best experiences I've ever had in my life."

Hannay said he now reads every morning for about an hour and a half and goes to the class twice a week.

"I enjoy it so much now," he said.

The charity said Hannay is an "inspiring example of determination and courage".

It said he asked his local library in Hythe, Southampton, about learning to read, which led him to the charity and his reading coach, Angie.

During his working life as a professional chauffeur, he relied on his memory to drive his clients around London, and at the age of 70 he attended evening classes to improve his reading.

However, he found the group situation difficult.

News.title: House that looks like boulders to be built on moor
News.content:
Plans for a house designed to look like rocks on a famous Yorkshire moor have been approved.

The contemporary structure, which has large irregular-shaped windows and a natural outdoor pool, looks similar to the landmark Cow and Calf Rocks in Ilkley, West Yorkshire.

The house will be built on green belt land which is the garden of a home off Heber's Ghyll Drive, and will be eco-friendly, to an ultra-low energy standard called Passivhaus.

Harrogate-based architects Shaw & Jagger said the scheme was eventually passed by HM Planning Inspectorate through the country house clause, which allows development on green belt for buildings of "exceptional quality".

The architect Matt Masserella-Gill was commissioned to design the home by the landowner David Rasche.

He said the design was "arguably the most complex country house application ever made in this country".

The house has been named Fomorian - meaning a supernatural race of giants in Irish mythology - taking inspiration from the mythical giant Rombald who is told to have lived on Ilkley Moor.

Masserella-Gill said: "The design approach was to propose a scheme that is intrinsically linked to the spirit of its place. Fomorian is of its place, part of the moors, its geology and its spirit.

"We took cues from local folklore, the surrounding rocks; ancient carvings, standing stones and escarpments that are synonymous with the landscape."

News.title: Three officers injured after lorry crashes into police vehicle
News.content:
Three police officers have been injured in County Down after a lorry they were pursuing drove on the wrong side of the road and collided with their vehicle at speed.

A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of driving while unfit through drink or drugs, driving while disqualified and dangerous driving.

A police vehicle was extensively damaged but the officers injuries are thought not to be serious at this time.

The incident began following a report of a blue articulated lorry swerving on Moygannon Road in the Warrenpoint area shortly before 23:30 BST.

"Officers responded and located a lorry matching the description on the Derryleckagh Road, Newry," said Ch Insp Will Brown.

When signalled to stop, the lorry then made off "at speed and on the wrong side of the road", before smashing into a police vehicle and continuing towards Rostrevor.

Brown continued: "The lorry later came to a stop in the Water Street area of Rostrevor where the driver, aged 36, made off on foot but was detained by officers following a short foot chase."

He remains in custody.

Brown said: "Our officers put themselves on the front line to help keep people safe. Thankfully, no one sustained more serious injuries during this incident, including officers and other road users."

News.title: Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock unveils Miranda Hart ‘Big Mix’ vinyl
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Little Mix singer Leigh-Anne Pinnock has unveiled a spoof "Big Mix" project featuring Miranda Hart, after the pair went viral for their dance routine on Celebrity Traitors.

The performer, 35, and comedian, 53, are among the stars currently appearing on the BBC reality gameshow, having attracted wide attention for their antics during Friday’s episode.

During a particularly tense moment as traitors Maya Jama, James Acaster and King Kenny tried to commit a murder in plain sight, the duo lightened the mood with a playful routine.

Pinnock taught Hart the steps to her band’s hit Touch, with hilarity following as the comedian, who dubbed herself "Big Mix", struggled to grasp the choreography.

The scene inspired widespread online memes, with the singer previously commenting that their dance break "saved my life" by helping her and Hart avoid being murdered by the traitors.

Pinnock also uploaded a mock poster for "Big Mix: The Tour" to her Instagram story on Sunday, featuring photos of them singing into microphones alongside a fake link to "get tickets"

She posted on Instagram later that evening and unboxed a framed vinyl “Big Mix” record, which she said had been sent to her by the BBC.

Pinnock said: “It looks like a plaque or a vinyl or something? Why am I nervous, what is this?”

The star, who is currently expecting her third child with her husband, footballer Andre Gray, is heavily pregnant in the video and wearing a white top and grey joggers.

Pinnock giggled as she unpacked a framed vinyl record, which featured an edited photo of herself and Hart on the album cover which read: “Big Mix: Gory Days.”

“Oh. My. Gosh. This… Is iconic,” Pinnock said.

Reading the plaque beneath the item, she said: “Big Mix: Gory Days, commemorating a killer debut performance. The Celebrity Traitors 2026.

“Now that is insane. What an iconic moment, and an iconic woman.

“Are you around for the reunion, Miranda, because… Just saying.”

The video ended with Pinnock gleefully showing off her “cute” new record and pointing out the peacock on the vinyl, a nod to the birds at the Scottish castle where Celebrity Traitors is filmed.

In the caption, she wrote: “I guess it’s official, Big Mix are taking over.

“@realmirandahart you are simply the best.”

Her former bandmates Jade Thirlwall and Perrie Edwards both posted laughing emojis, and her Celebrity Traitors co-star Sebastian Croft said: “This is so good. Are they for sale, I want one.”

open image in gallery Leigh-Anne Pinnock ( BBC )

Pinnock rose to fame after winning The X Factor in 2011 with the pop group Little Mix which included Edwards, Thirlwall and Jesy Nelson.

The group had five UK number one singles including Wings, Black Magic, and Shout Out To My Ex and one UK number one album, 2016’s Glory Days.

After Nelson left the band in December 2020, the group continued to perform as a trio until they went on a hiatus in 2022.

They have since all pursued solo careers with Pinnock releasing her debut solo album, My Ego Told Me To, earlier this year.

Going by the stage name Leigh-Anne, she has also released the songs Clickbait, My Love, Don’t Say Love and Been A Minute.

News.title: Manchester United miss chance to make statement after turbulent week with draw at Leeds
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A 1-1 draw at Elland Road in January 2026 for a Manchester United side with a back three and framed by some incendiary comments about Jason Wilcox precipitated the departure of a manager.

A repeat result is less likely to bring the same outcome, not least because Michael Carrick was not the one criticising the director of football. Yet when it seemed Carrick might be turning a corner, that his side were set for their finest result of a stuttering season and that his players were, as he claimed, galvanised by the events of the last week, United lost another lead and the chance to deliver a statement on the pitch.

Compared to the injury-time goals Everton and Tottenham scored, at least there was no late letdown for United – not with Noussair Mazraoui clearing off the line from Anton Stach in the 92nd minute – but they can summon different types of disappointment.

Even as, after adopting Ruben Amorim’s favourite system – probably not a tribute to the Portuguese, even if his valedictory game came against Leeds – they looked more solid in open play, they have now conceded three set-piece goals in Yorkshire already this season, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser. It is a reason why their wait for a Premier League clean sheet goes on.

And, indeed, why their wait for a win does. They have shared the points in their last three top-flight games but, in all competitions, they are without a victory in six matches. Even Amorim never went six without winning, if a triumph on penalties is factored in.

“We are not getting too carried away, because we didn’t win, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons you get what you deserve in the end,” said Carrick. “It wasn't a perfect performance, it wasn't our most unbelievable performance, but there was definitely a lot in there that you can show how together the group were. It felt like a fresh start today.” But without the result which would have demonstrated that.

So it did not get worse for Carrick, though there was insufficient evidence to argue it got much better. United had too little threat after conceding. They did not have that much before, either, but at least there was some solidity in a 3-4-3 system, with a back three shielded by twin defensive midfielders.

open image in gallery Dominic Calvert-Lewin sealed a point for Leeds ( Getty )

A half-time lead lent itself to the suggestion their players should criticise Jason Wilcox more often. Two of the players bought by Wilcox combined for the goal. Perhaps, deep in the defence, Lisandro Martinez was celebrating the recruitment he had lamented. But the Argentinian’s eventful week came to an early, and anticlimactic, end as he went off at half-time; if nothing else, that may have spared him the post-match interviews.

United were breached soon after Mazraoui replaced Martinez; even with three centre-backs, none were near Leeds’ likeliest scorer when he got his fourth goal in five games. Calvert-Lewin ran away from Carlos Baleba and held off Bryan Mbeumo when he met Nico Elvedi’s header and hooked in a shot. They had failed to heed the warning from an earlier set-piece from Stach, with Senne Lammens saving Elvedi’s first-half header.

And there was a spirit and a resilience to Leeds, now only beaten in six of their last 32 league matches, and only by champions Arsenal this season. Yet they were below their best. “It says a lot that we are even slightly disappointed with a point against Manchester United,” manager Daniel Farke said. “You always have to be aware, it is still Manchester United. Many, many compliments to my players for a dominant performance against Man United.”

open image in gallery The outspoken Lisandro Martinez was hooked at half-time ( Reuters )

He noted the team that switched shape because of the opposition was in fact United. “It says a lot about how much respect we've earned,” the German said. Carrick only called it a “tweak” but it at least offered indications he can change. His United have floundered against sides with a back three, so he borrowed from Amorim’s infamous fondness for the formation. At times, it seemed United had no centre-forward; at others, it was Mbeumo. Youri Tielemans, signed as a central midfielder, has looked better when others play that role. He was in the front three, and integral in the supply line. “I am really impressed with Youri,” Carrick said.

United led when Mbeumo poked in a shot from Tielemans’ low centre. The same combination had almost brought an earlier breakthrough, with Tielemans’ quality apparent in the inside-right channel as the unmarked Mbeumo headed wide from the Belgian’s cross.

“Bryan gives so much to the team,” said Carrick. With Benjamin Sesko injured, Marcus Rashford unused and Matheus Cunha limited to a cameo, Mbeumo had to. United’s new look was a more defensive one. It still did not lend itself to either a shutout or a victory.

News.title: Woman condemns ‘degrading’ and ‘disturbing’ Halloween Park experience
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A woman has condemned a “depraved” adults-only Halloween Park experience in Liverpool after she was left shocked by the sexually graphic nature of her experience.

Robyn Doughty, 33, said the optional Hellfire Club experience at Newsham Scream Park felt like a “simulation of... sexual degradation, and sexual violation.”

The tattoo artist went with a group of friends on Thursday and was asked to sign a waiver before entering the over-18s section.

But Ms Doughty has since taken to social media to call out the park, saying there should have been more warning after staff called them “s****” and made “all kinds of horrific sexual noises”.

“The whole time they’re just calling you “s****” and berating you,” she said in a video shared to TikTok.

“My friend walked out in tears and couldn’t even explain why she was horrified, and when I complained, I was told ‘oh it’s subjective’.

"Where’s the warning? Their website lists be aware of PTSD and anxiety but nowhere does it say graphically sexual.”

The scream park said its "terms and conditions, which must be agreed to before entering the attraction, outline the nature of the experience, including its adult and horror themes, physical interaction and sensory effects".

open image in gallery Robyn Doughty complained to staff after her friend walked out in tears ( Facebook/Newsham Scream Park )

Ms Doughty told Liverpool Echo: “I don't think I fully realised the scale of it myself until all these other people started coming forward.

“I've had countless people in my DMs sharing similar stories, men and women, girlfriends and boyfriends, and the common denominator has been the same: it's degrading, humiliating and quite disturbing.

“I think it's more complicated than just a scare. It's not a fun, physical scare - it's psychological. Because it's presented in such a light-hearted setting, people aren't prepared for it. These young, impressionable kids and people who might have experienced past trauma aren't prepared for it, because it's in a light-hearted setting.”

On its website, Newsham Scream Park says it recommends the experience for adults only because of the “extreme level scare attractions designed to unsettle and terrify”.

The park transforms a derelict Victorian-era building into an immersive horror experience every year for Halloween.

“Step inside the darkness and face your fears across a series of live-action horror mazes, scare zones, and twisted theatrical experiences,” it says.

“Our scare actors will bring your nightmares to life as you navigate haunted wards, deranged experiments, and unspeakable horrors lurking around every corner. Every room tells a story. Every hallway hides a scream.”

Newsham Scream Park said: “The Hellfire Club is an optional, adults-only immersive horror attraction designed to deliver an intense experience. It is clearly identified as an 18+ attraction, with ID required for anyone under the age of 21. All guests must complete a digital waiver before entering and there is CCTV in place covering the entirety of this attraction and the full event to protect all participating guests and actors.

“Guest welfare is a priority throughout the attraction and our terms and conditions, which much be agreed to before entering the attraction, outline the nature of the experience, including its adult and horror themes, physical interaction and sensory effects. They also highlight that some elements may cause distress, identify circumstances in which the attraction may not be suitable, and explain that guests can end their participation immediately, at any time, using the safe word provided without explanation.

“The extensive CCTV coverage is constantly monitored and the entire team is always in contact via radio, with production in all attractions and immediately halting any of the attractions if there are any issues.”

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), email jo@samaritans.org, or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch

News.title: Kevin Bacon calls out FedEx for misplacing his beloved vintage clothes
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kevin Bacon is bringing out the big guns to help find his missing clothes: he took it to Instagram.

The Footloose star, 68, said in a video posted Friday that he decided to ship some of his favorite clothes to himself while he works in Ireland. However, the box of clothes has still not arrived.

In a video captioned, “Where are my clothes,” Bacon said: “I wanted to pack light, so I decided to ship some old clothes over here to Ireland.”

“I don’t buy a lot of clothes; I’ve had these clothes probably since the 90s,” he explained.

He then went on to imply that he used FedEx to deliver the clothes, saying, “I used a shipping service that I don’t want to say the name, but it rhymes with Bread Ex.”

open image in gallery Kevin Bacon is asking for help getting his vintage clothes back ( Getty )

Bacon said that on September 26, the box left upstate New York and went to Memphis, Tennessee, before flying to France.

“By September 28th, it had arrived in Germany,” he said, adding, “on September 29th, they shipped it straight to Israel. Not Ireland, Israel.”

From there, on October 3, the package went from Israel back to France, he said. It was then shipped back to Israel the next day, and to Germany the day after that.

“Then October 6th, it went back to Israel, not to Ireland, back to Israel,” he said. “But on October 10th, that box of old clothes made its way all the way to France, and on October 11th, it arrived in the UK, in England.”

“Pretty close,” he joked. He said the box was then finally shipped from the UK to Ireland “where it has been sitting for five days.”

However, Bacon continued, the shipping service said that it cannot be delivered.

“I don’t understand why,” he said. “It’s just sitting there. I can’t get a person on the phone. I have not been able to talk to anybody.”

In response to people who might tell him to buy new clothes, Bacon said, “I could buy some clothes, but I want these clothes.”

“I’ve had them since the 90s,” he explained. “They have a certain sentimental value. Old boots, old jeans, old hats.”

He then asked for any suggestions from people who want to help. “Am I ever going to see this stuff?” he asked. “It’s starting to get cold here.”

Bacon’s Instagram post has prompted a number of comments joking about the dilemma, including one from fellow actor Justin Long, teasing: “You should’ve just had them sent to Israel. You’d be in full 90’s grunge glory by now.”

FedEx said in a statement shared with The Independent: “We sincerely apologize for this experience. We are in direct contact with Mr. Bacon to deliver the package. This outcome should have happened sooner, and we are reviewing what went wrong to help ensure we deliver the level of service our customers expect and deserve.”

News.title: Sonay Kartal’s dream run to Wuhan Open final ends in defeat to Maja Chwalinska
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Sonay Kartal’s brilliant run at the Wuhan Open ended in a bruising three-set loss to French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska.

The Briton dominated the first set but was reeled back in thanks to a gritty performance from 16th seed Chwalinska, who converted her third match point at the end of a nervy final game to win 2-6, 6-4, 6-2.

The 25-year-old, who beat world No 11 Iva Jovic and six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek to make her first WTA 1000 final, collapsed to the court in relief as she sealed the title in two hours and 43 minutes.

While it’s a disappointing result for Kartal, this week has nonetheless been a superb step up in only her third tournament since a six-month injury layoff following a stress fracture in her back.

She had never previously gone beyond the quarter-finals at a WTA 1000 event, the level below the majors. The 24-year-old did it the hard way, dispatching three seeded players in a row in former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, two-time major finalist Jasmine Paolini and world No 6 Elina Svitolina, before beating former French Open winner Jelena Ostapenko in the semi-finals.

Having been ranked 170th in the world after her injury lay-off, Kartal was the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 finalist since the format was introduced 17 years ago, and only the second British woman ever to make a final at this level after Johanna Konta.

She will climb to 50th in the world when the rankings are updated on Monday and replace Katie Boulter as the British No 1.

Momentum swung repeatedly over the course of the encounter, with nine breaks in the first 18 games. Kartal was superior in the first set against a flat Chwalinska but the Pole came out fighting in the second, with her unusual, crafty style, changes of pace and direction and lefty serve causing problems.

Kartal was broken in a mammoth game at 3-3 but upped her aggression to break straight back, only to be on the receiving end of a third straight break thanks to an unlucky net cord at 40-15. Chwalinska deployed the drop shot to great effect and forced a deciding set with a tidy backhand volley at the net.

open image in gallery Chwalinska fell to the ground in relief as she converted her third championship point ( Reuters )

After a run of four straight holds, Kartal was first to blink in the decider, with the Briton broken to love as she shanked a forehand wide for 2-3.

Chwalinska continued to impose herself, replying to a Kartal drop shot with a better one of her own to earn a break point at 4-2, and converting it immediately as she pushed Kartal behind the baseline, with the world No 170 firing long under pressure.

Both players were wracked with nerves as Chwalinska served for the title: Kartal missed three break points while Chwalinska spurned her first two championship points before finally converting the third as the Brit hit long.

News.title: Jaguars stunned by Texans in Wembley thriller – but are they still London’s NFL team?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A stroll along Olympic Way down from Wembley Park tube station on an NFL matchday is a study in sound and vision, a mass of bodies in kaleidoscopic colour moving at random with reckless abandon for itself and anything in the way. There is no time, mind, to be tribal – in the Jubilee Line carriages those in Packers and Bears jerseys mingle and mix, sharing in the common cause that is American football fandom at a distance. One can find just about each and every franchise represented within the throng, jerseys sported with pride and passion regardless of which teams are actually involved.

It will be two decades next year since the International Series first launched and still that festival feel remains. The NFL seems more intent than ever on global expansion but London remains its home away from home; this encounter between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans was the 28th game at Wembley and 45th in all.

open image in gallery Wembley was packed with NFL fans as always ( Getty )

But does that trans-Atlantic special relationship remain just as strong? For the first time in a good while, it feels fair to ask that question. The opening encounter of this year’s three-game slate between the Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts only came close to a sellout thanks to a late surge of sales driven by a drop in ticket prices, and there were a smattering of empty seats evident around Wembley – even if a crowd north of 82,000 was recorded on a damp Sunday afternoon for the meeting of two of the league’s more unfashionable franchises.

The sense of spectacle remains, mind, the product not at all cheapened 19 years on. From the Jaguars mascot bungee jumping off the roof – supported, of course, by the sponsorship of an insurance broker – through the assault on the ears and eyes that accompanies any pause, everything is dressed up in pomp and ceremony. A half-time “Duval Derby” featuring corgis felt, in some way, appropriate.

open image in gallery CJ Stroud led the Houston Texans to victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars ( Reuters )

The crowd were royally treated, too, to a thrilling duel between CJ Stroud and Trevor Lawrence settled with the last kick. Even in a wretched start to the season for the Texans, quarterback Stroud had looked back to somewhere near his best, sending a message as the Houston hierarchy deliberate over a long-term contract. With offensive personnel bolstered by the arrival of Marvin Harrison Jr from Arizona for a second round pick, Stroud carved the Jaguars secondary apart, hitting Nico Collins and Jaylin Noel repeatedly downfield and picking out tight end Foster Moreau twice underneath for touchdowns once within range. Noel also added a touchdown, while a scamper from back-up running back Jawhar Jordan brought seven more points.

The Jaguars stayed with them, though, with Bhayshul Tuten twice navigating from the flats to the endzone after short Lawrence passes, and unheralded Nate Boerkircher snaring one of his own with a sensational one-handed grab over his head. It was Travis Hunter, though, who really gave them hope: the two-way talent first capitalising on some gorgeous Coen play design to score, before picking off Stroud in the other endzone a matter of minutes later.

open image in gallery Travis Hunter kept the Jaguars alive ( PA )

It gave Jacksonville the chance to launch a game-tying drive. Courtesy of a 60-yard field goal from Cam Little, they did precisely that. His hasty hoisting left two minutes on the clock, though – more than enough time for Stroud to work Houston into field goal range and allow kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn to do the rest and restore belief in a Texans turnaround. “We stumbled in a few games earlier in the season when we didn’t finish the game,” head coach Demeco Ryans said. “We found a way today.”

open image in gallery Ka'imi Fairbairn slotted a field goal as time expired to give the Texans victory at Wembley ( Getty )

It capped a mixed trip for the Jaguars, beating the Philadelphia Eagles at the last seven days ago but falling just short this to drop to 4-2. Perhaps the staunchest supporters of the international games, even they appear slightly uncertain about the future. No team has done more in London than the Jaguars, quick to seize on an opportunity to develop their fanbase abroad in 2013 and regular visitors ever since. Liam Coen’s side have spent the last fortnight at their training base at the Grove in Watford, able to settle in on British soil with back-to-back games here.

The Jaguars are locked in for another game overseas in 2027, but it is not clear what lies beyond that. Come 2028, there will be a gleaming new facility in Jacksonville to enjoy, with a $1.4 billion revamp of Everbank Stadium underway – putting an end to speculation that the Jags could be a prime relocation candidate away from a market that, by NFL standards, is small. A temporary move to Orlando, and that game in London, next year will allow that work to be done.

Jaguars president Mark Lamping indicated this week, though, to travelling media from Jacksonville that he would very much like every home game of the 2028 season at their new stadium in Florida. Meanwhile, the economic benefits that have been felt by having such close ties across the pond will not be quite so necessary. Another team could yet spot an opportunity. “I feel like we have a strong connection and tie to London,” quarterback Lawrence said this week. “We’ve been playing here for a long time. Who knows if that will change?”

open image in gallery It is not clear if the Jaguars wish to continue their long-term relationship with London ( PA )

Every NFL team is currently required to give up a home game every four years to be played internationally, though that may change if an expanded season or international slate is agreed. Might the NFL look to intensify its efforts away from London anyway? The drive to access new territories will continue but something, at some stage, will surely have to give to avoid total saturation. Some of the scarcity value with the games in London already feels to have been lost – but if every contest was as good as this, few would really care.

News.title: Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation
News.content:
Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace and said that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

News.title: Man Utd fail to relieve pressure on Carrick after draw at Leeds
News.content:
“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years.

“I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

News.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes in tatters after Tonga defeat
News.content:
McDermott was full of credit. “They’re a big team, a strong team,” he said. “They’ve got some tremendous players in there, and I thought we stuck toe-to-toe with them for nearly all the game.

“They scored some tries through kicks, which are always hard to defend, and then towards the back-end of the game we made some errors chasing the scoreboard.”

It should be factored in that this was McDermott’s first match in charge and strides have clearly been made since England were woeful in losing the Ashes 3-0 last year.

“I thought we opened up Tonga in that first 20,” McDermott added. “Whether we went through the middle or the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position, but we had some scrappy finishes to the good ball sets. It was too erratic. We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga, but credit to them. I thought they were terrific defensively.”

Having been beaten by Samoa in the World Cup four years ago, England must face up to the burgeoning conviction that they are no longer among the top three countries in international rugby league. There was the palpable sense of the old order being changed in a stadium packed with the red shirts of Tonga.

As Williams said in the build-up, this is a “mad” format, with only the top two from the combined six-team group of Pool B and C going through to the semi-finals, but now it is very simple as far as England are concerned. They must beat France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining two matches, and do so heavily, then pray that Tonga can beat Samoa in the last match of the pool stage. However, Samoa thumped France 78-4 on Friday, so even that potential avenue appears blocked. McDermott has no other option but to look ahead.

“We know what’s in front of us now, we’ve got to win the next two games and improve on the things we need to improve on,” he said. “But I’ve seen enough tonight that is telling me we’re heading in the right direction.

“It would be tremendously disrespectful to either France or PNG to suggest we’re going to rack up points. I can start looking at points difference and start working out our strategies, but the road will lead us back to winning those two games, and winning them in a strong way.”

Team details

England Radley, Pearce-Paul, Nsemba (King 62), Thompson (Harvard 29, Currie 69), O’Neill (Litten 58); Brimson (Nsemba 79), Young, Savala, Farnworth, Eckersley, Williams, Smith, King (Walters 33, Thompson 76).

Tonga Frizell (Vaimauga 28, Taumalolo 64), Wong (Olakau’atu 41), Olakau’atu (Fonua-Blake 38, Utoikamanu 66), Taumalolo (Halasima 31), Foketi; Hopoate, Watene-Zelezniak, Koula, Toia, Fifita, Fainu (Lolohea 17), Katoa, Fonua-Blake (Utoikamanu 21, Wong 52).

Referee Gerard Sutton (Australia).

England’s Rugby League World Cup challenge could well be over, just 80 minutes after it started.

Brian McDermott’s hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals were all but shattered in his side’s first pool match in a brutal encounter in which Pacific Island physicality and passion ultimately earned Tonga a famous victory.

England displayed huge attacking courage with their offload strategy – in all, they made 26 – but their adventurous intent could not find the finishing touch and was not enough to topple a ferocious opposition defence in Perth. Despite excellent performances from captain George Williams and Dom Young, they were ultimately blown off HBF Park.

On their seventh attempt, this was Tonga’s first win over England and although this intense contest was for, so long, much closer than the scoreboard finally showed, there can be no doubting the excellence of Kristian Woolf’s team and the ruthlessness they displayed in the last quarter in which they never stopped tackling refused to stop coming.

Sports.title: Ex-Prem goalkeeper scores stunning last minute equaliser to lead team to victory on penalties in cup clash
Sports.content:

A FORMER Premier League goalkeeper scored a dramatic late equaliser to force penalties in a Welsh Cup clash on Saturday.

Colwyn Bay goalkeeper Mark Halstead, formerly of the Premier League and EFL, smashed in a volley from close range in the dying stages before his team won on penalties.



Having led at the beginning of the tie, Colwyn Bay found themselves 2-1 down to Buckley Town on the hour mark.

The pressure built on Buckley until boiling point in the 94th minute, as an unlikely scorer restored order for the North coast side.



Halstead smashed in a volley like a centre-forward in his prime before nonchalantly jogging back to his goal.

And it proved to be the last kick of the game before penalty kicks were taken.



Colwyn Bay came out 4-3 winners on pens and had their goalkeeper to thank for providing the goods in added time.

The result sees them advance into the third round of the Welsh Cup, from a tie which they would have expected to win, considering Buckley play in the division below.

Halstead, 36, is clearly still enjoying his football, having joined Colwyn Bay in the summer.

The keeper, who stands at 6ft3in, started his career at Blackpool in 2009 having come through the academy – despite not making a Prem appearance for the Tangerines – he did play at Stamford Bridge for Morecambe in 2021.

Sports.title: Barnet star forced to have three teeth removed from lip after brutal collision during EFL clash
Sports.content:
Next

BARNET star Romoney Crichlow-Noble was forced to have three teeth removed from his lip after suffering a horror facial injury during his side’s clash with Tranmere Rovers.

The Bees’ defender was left needing stitches after a nasty collision during the League Two encounter yesterday.



But thankfully, the 27-year-old was given the all-clear after undergoing scans and X-rays, with no serious injuries detected.

Barnet confirmed the news in a statement on X, writing: “Romoney’s scans and X-rays are all clear. He required stitches and had three teeth removed from his lip, but is now on his way home.



“Glad was nothing more serious @romoneyc 🐝.”

Crichlow also shared an update with supporters alongside a picture of himself after receiving treatment.

He wrote: “5 hours later, 3 teeth through my lip, some loose and rocky teeth and a sore sternum but I’m grand 🤞 ❤️.

“Thanks for the messages, up the f bees 🤣 🤝.”

The defender suffered the injuries following a late challenge from Tranmere’s Joel Senior, leaving him requiring medical attention.

Despite the frightening incident, Crichlow was able to leave hospital later that evening after being checked over by medical staff.



And his team-mates made sure the day ended on a high as Barnet battled back from a half-time deficit to claim a 2-1 victory.

Kabongo Tshimanga proved the match-winner, scoring both goals to complete the comeback and secure all three points for the Bees.

The result leaves Barnet – where former Tottenham star Dele Alli has been training recently – in a strong position in League Two, sitting second in the table and just one point behind leaders Salford City, with two games in hand.



They have also been the division’s most prolific side so far, scoring 22 goals as they chase promotion to League One next season.

Sports.title: Man City’s kit ‘set to undergo subtle change’ following Premier League guilty verdict
Sports.content:

MANCHESTER CITY’S kit manufacturer Puma are set to make a big change from next season.

The news comes after Man City were found guilty of more than 100 charges by the Premier League.



According to Footy Headlines, Puma is set to make a major branding change across its football kits.

From next season, the Puma logo will not appear on the sleeves of kits, instead there will be a singular logo in the middle of kits.



But with a potential punishment still unknown, City could even end up repping Puma in a lower league, depending on the verdict of the Prem and result of an appeal.

Puma’s branding update marks the first major change this century giving clubs a significantly cleaner and more premium aesthetic.

Despite the charges dominating the Man City discourse, the players don’t seem affected, as they’ve kept their perfect league start intact.

Sports.title: Bournemouth 2 Sunderland 0: Danso sent off for Black Cats as Cherries end poor run with convincing win
Sports.content:
CHERRIES ON TOP Bournemouth 2 Sunderland 0: Danso sent off for Black Cats as Cherries end poor run with convincing win







Next

EVANILSON scored and contributed an assist as Bournemouth comfortably beat 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality Stadium.

The Brazilian got himself stuck in early, unselfishly teeing up Marcus Tavernier, who nodded in a sixth-minute opener.



Evanilson was then dragged down by central defender Kevin Danso, who was dismissed in the 17th minute.

The Cherries perhaps would have wanted more from their man advantage, but Evanilson capitalised on an error to double the scoring three minutes after the break and mark a career century of goals.



An eventful opening 20 minutes of the first half began with Tyler Adams’ early attempt through a crowd before Danso blocked an initial Evanilson effort.

Tavernier nodded the Cherries in front after Danso and Omar Alderete bungled their effort to keep the speedy Brazilian from reaching a ball over the top.

Evanilson might have taken the chance himself, but picked out the unmarked Tavernier, who planted a header past a visibly frustrated Robin Roefs.

It went from bad to worse for the visitors from another long ball, again tracked by Evanilson, who was the last man when he was tugged down, and referee Craig Pawson’s decision to dismiss Danso was almost immediate.

Tavernier curled the subsequent free-kick over, and there was a lengthy pause to treat Nordi Mukiele, who looked to have a leg issue, but carried on.

Roefs saved from Rayan after the half hour, and Adam Smith could not redirect the follow-up from an awkward angle to the right of the Sunderland goal.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Mukiele’s presence was felt when he made a timely tackle to deny Evanilson what would have been an excellent scoring opportunity, and Roefs saved a sharp Rayan effort.

Sunderland were able to limit the first-half damage to just the opener after Evanilson could not take advantage of the Sunderland keeper coming off his line late on and curled over the empty net.

The Cherries doubled their lead three minutes into the second half, the result of another Alderete error from a poor backpass.

Evanilson pounced and patiently rounded Roefs before applying the straightforward low finish into the corner to score for a third successive game in all competitions.

The Brazilian continued to pose the biggest threat, and Tavernier drew another save just after the hour as the hosts looked to add a cushion.



Sunderland enjoyed a brief spell deep in the hosts’ half late in the period, but did not manage to register a first shot on target.

Justin Kluivert missed a chance to make it three in stoppage time before the Cherries comfortably closed out the contest, ensuring a first win of the Premier League campaign.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Richarlison accuses Brazilian presidential frontrunner of stealing his PRIVATE ISLAND in shock video

TOTTENHAM star Richarlison has accused the Brazilian presidential frontrunner of STEALING his private island.

The Spurs outcast revealed that he believes Senator Flavio Bolsonaro got control of the island without payment.



In his statement the Brazil international said he bought the island in Angra dos Reis, on the Green Coast of Rio de Janeiro, between 2020 and 2021.

He also added that he received numerous purchase offers including from Bolsonaro, but he refused to sell to the senator.



Richarlison said: “I didn’t want to sell the island to him. Because I didn’t want to, those guys took advantage of the situation in court. We were sorting out the paperwork (documentation for the island’s ownership), and they said it would take months or even years to resolve.

“Flavio Bolsonaro and this guy Willer Tomaz went there and, in 24 hours, took possession of the island. That’s where the justice system failed. Those guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know. I spent around R$ 10 million there and received nothing.”



In the video, Richarlison asked the police to investigate the case and stated that he is seeking answers about the money invested.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans say ‘another bust-up with Wilcox?’ as Lisandro Martinez subbed off at half time in Leeds clash
Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED fans believe Lisandro Martinez has had another bust-up with executive Jason Wilcox.

The Argentine centre-back was unexpectedly subbed off at half-time of United‘s clash against Leeds.



Fans have flooded social media suggesting that the fallout of Martinez’s rant against the club has intensified.

Martinez claimed that the Red Devils have not invested well amid a disappointing start to the Premier League season.



He has since been fined and issued an apology after doubling down following United’s 2-0 Champions League loss against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night.

Head coach Michael Carrick has insisted that the incident has been put to bed, but several fans on social media are unconvinced.

One fan on X said: “Wilcox got to Lisandro at HT then.”

Another commented: “Lisandro had another bust up with Wilcox.”

A third fan posted: “Carrick took Lisandro off following a call from Wilcox; otherwise, there’s no explaining why he took him off.”

Martinez is expected to leave the club on a free transfer when his contract expires in the summer.

But head coach Carrick has suggested that his outburst has had little impact on the team’s performance against Leeds.

Sports.title: Leeds miss golden chance to pile misery on Man Utd - but match didn't deserve a winner
Sports.content:
Leeds miss golden chance to pile misery on Man Utd - but match didn't deserve a winner

LEEDS 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: Bryan Mbeumo fired the Red Devils ahead before the break but Dominic Calvert-Lewin struck in the second half to earn a point for the hosts

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin scores the equaliser for Leeds (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Dominic Calvert-Lewin denied Manchester United their first win in six games - to pile more pressure on Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



Calvert-Lewin's second half equaliser cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's 35th minute strike, to make it honours even at a white hot Elland Road.

‌



But if Carrick returned across the Pennines feeling satisfied, he shouldn't have done. The United boss insists he has the best job possible and is still 'loving it'.

‌



But no manager in their right mind should be loving the fact their side has not won a single game for more than five weeks.

Or kept a clean sheet in the league all season. At this rate, United will be airing the club's dirty laundry in public again, by sacking another manager.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Carrick had needed this trip to Elland Road like a hole in the head. The cauldron of hate is bad enough in normal circumstances, let alone when United had not won in five games in all competitions.

Leeds never need an excuse to pile pain on their bitter rivals, but on this occasion the hosts must have been relishing the visit of Carrick's men more than ever.

‌



Leeds went into this clash above United in the table. The last time this happened was back in 2002, which was also the last time Leeds beat United at home. But this time round United appeared vulnerable and there for the taking.

Not least because United started with a right back at left back, and a centre back at right back. While Lisandro Martinez owed his manager a big performance, considering his outburst in the wake of the defeat at Atletico Madrid.

Most of the first half was high on toxicity and low on quality. Ethan Ampadu made three crunching tackles on Andrey Santos, Kobbie Mainoo and Mbeumo.

‌



View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo opened the scoring (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

While Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson were booked for two crude challenges of their own. This was no place for shrinking violets. But a football match broke out just before the half hour mark.

Nico Elvedi saw a header well saved by Senne Lammens. While at the opposite end Youri Tielemans put a chance on a plate for Mbeumo, who made a complete meal of it by heading wide with just James Trafford to beat.

‌



Trafford then had to charge from goal to stop Amad Diallo. It was fast, furious and frantic in equal measure. But 10 minutes before the break Mbeumo made amends to give United the lead.

He brushed aside a feeble challenge from James Justin to meet another Tielemans cross and beat Trafford with a cool finish. Ao Tanaka shot straight at Lammens before Calvert-Lewin headed just wide, as Leeds looked to hit back.

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

‌



Which they eventually did six minutes into the second half, when Calvert-Lewin lashed home from close range after United had failed to deal with a corner.

Leeds had their tails up, and Tanaka smashed a volley over the top. Harry Maguire was fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty after pulling Ampadu to the ground inside the box.

Tensions continued to simmer, with Ampadu and Fernandes involved in a spiteful exchange of words, while Tanaka left Diallo writhing in pain following a brutal - but legal - tackle.

Article continues below

Fernandes dragged a shot wide and Anton Stach blazed over as both sides went in search of winner. But in truth, the game didn't deserve one.
