Sports.title: Michael Carrick's masterplan scuppered by injury blow as Leeds deny Man Utd win
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's masterplan scuppered by injury blow as Leeds deny Man Utd win

LEEDS 1-1 MAN UTD: Dominic Calvert-Lewin may have cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's opening goal but Michael Carrick's side stopped the rot after two defeats since the international break

View 4 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

The spoils were shared at Elland Road as spirited Leeds came from behind to earn a draw with Manchester United. Goals from Bryan Mbeumo and Dominic Calvert-Lewin meant that both teams had to settle for 1-1, just as they did in the same fixture last season.

‌



‌



Michael Carrick went into the clash between these old foes fearing a third consecutive defeat, and while his side stopped the rot, it's their worst-ever start to a Premier League season. But Leeds rallied in the second period and were worthy of a point themselves.

‌



The headline from from the team news was that Lisandro Martinez kept his place in United's starting line-up, despite his attack on the club's hierarchy in midweek and subsequent fine. Jason Wilcox, who was targeted by Martinez in his explosive post-match rant, made the trip to Elland Road, his old stomping ground as a player.

‌



Martinez's day would only last 45 minutes, having to be substituted at half-time with United leading 1-0. Leeds, on the other hand, named the same starting XI for the fifth Premier League game running.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Carrick's 'massive' tactical change pays dividends

Something had to change, didn't it? Without Benjamin Sesko for the vast majority of the season, Manchester United's attack has been blunt.

Michael Carrick has tried both Mbeumo and Joshua Zirzkee up front, but he opted for something different at Elland Road. United's midfield resembled a square, with Bruno Fernandes and Your Tielemans well in front of Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, while Mbeumo and Amad were deployed as wide forwards.

It was - in the words of Gary Neville - a 'massive' tactical change that left the Red Devils without a traditional striker, but gave them numbers to create overloads and a fluidity which Leeds found difficult to handle. Fernandes and Tielemans made United's intentions clear by relentlessly pressing the hosts' backline in the opening exchanges.

‌



View 4 Images Michael Carrick changed his formation (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

The system almost paid dividends with 27 minutes on the clock, as runs from Fernandes and Diogo Dalot opened a gaping hole in the Leeds penalty area. Mbeumo charged into the space and met Tielemans' cross. With no one marking him, the United forward looked certain to score. Instead, his header flashed wide.

Mbeumo wouldn't make the same mistake when the next chance came his way, again courtesy of Tielemans. This time, the Belgian played a low ball across the box and when James Trafford opted not to come, Mbeumo used his pace to get there first and slid home a deserved opener.

‌



It was the first time that United had led at half-time in a Premier League game this season. The untimely departure of Martinez prompted Carrick to alter his system, bringing on Noussair Mazraoui and going to a three-at-the-back formation.

View 4 Images Bryan Mbeumo broke the deadlock (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

Bogle impresses again as Leeds rally

It speaks to England's strength in depth at right-back that there's been little talk of Jayden Bogle getting a call-up amid his good run of form. His impressive 2025-26 season was rewarded in the summer when Leeds handed him a new four-year contract, and it's easy to see why Daniel Farke wants to keep him.

‌



The 26-year-old was Leeds' best player in the first half, causing Dalot problems with his runs both inside and out. Bogle picked up where he left off at the start of the second period, curling in a teasing cross that a Leeds team-mated failed to get on the end of.

Somewhat surprisingly, the Whites' equaliser came from another source. After Mazraoui gave away a cheap corner, Anton Stach's ball was flicked on by the head of Tarik Muharemovic and finished by Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who evaded Baleba and outstrengthed Mbeumo to level the scores.

Does Jayden Bogle deserve an England call-up? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 4 Images Jayden Bogle was a standout for Leeds (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Yoro finding his feet in new role

Three seasons, three managers, Leny Yoro hasn't had it easy settling in at Old Trafford. But is right-back where he'll finally nail down a place in Carrick's first XI?

Since his £52million move from Lille, Yoro was exclusively used as a centre-back - until this month. Although the Frenchman was (harshly) sent off against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, he's impressed out wide.

Article continues below

Yoro's defensive work was solid and he could've had an assist when Fernandes fired just wide of Trafford's goal midway through the second half. With Martinez, Ayden Heaven and Luke Shaw sidelined, and Matthijs de Ligt not yet match fit, having a defender who looks to be coming into his own is a timely boost for Carrick.

Sports.title: Ethan Nwaneri shown red card by mistake as Arsenal loanee's Dortmund struggles continue
Sports.content:
Ethan Nwaneri shown red card by mistake as Arsenal loanee's Dortmund struggles continue

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri was in Bundesliga action for Borussia Dortmund in their goalless draw with Union Berlin

View Image Ethan Nwaneri thought he had been sent off

Ethan Nwaneri could hardly have wished for a more difficult start to life at Borussia Dortmund after joining the German club on loan from Arsenal in the summer. The 19-year-old appeared to be sent off just seconds into Dortmund's Bundesliga clash against Union Berlin on Saturday after catching Tom Rothe with a heavy challenge.

‌



‌



However, Nwaneri's confusion at the decision was swiftly cleared up when referee Daniel Schlager realised he had accidentally pulled the wrong card from his pocket. The official quickly corrected his mistake, showing Nwaneri a yellow card instead and allowing him to continue in the match.

‌



However, the Arsenal loanee struggled to make the desired impact and, having been booked so early in the contest, was substituted shortly after the hour mark. His display was called out by the German media, however.

‌



Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta makes telling Kai Havertz prediction after clear Viktor Gyokeres decision READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Bild described the team's start as 'nothing short of explosive' and Nwaneri's challenge as 'brutal'. Meanwhile, local newspaper Ruhr Nachrichten was unimpressed, awarding him a 5/10 rating and suggesting he has yet to prove his worth.

While Goal claimed Nwaneri was Dortmund's most dangerous player during his 60 minutes on the pitch, other assessments were less favourable, describing him as 'largely anonymous'. Ran was even more critical, giving him a rating of 5 for a 'mostly negative' performance, which was characterised by 'poor ball control' and 'inaccurate finishing'.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Dortmund sporting director Nils-Ole Book criticised the team for a lack of courage, saying: "We're disappointed. We wanted to do a lot more.

"To get in behind, you need to play with more courage all over the field. We started doing that far too late. When we're bolder, we play really good football and are able to put pressure on our opponents."

Article continues below

The Premier League's youngest-ever player has made seven appearances for Dortmund across the Bundesliga and Champions League. He has started four league matches but is yet to feature in the starting XI for a European fixture.

Dortmund, who suffered a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt earlier this week, face Azerbaijani side Sabah on Tuesday as they look to secure their second win in the competition.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick laughs off worrying Nicky Butt claim that left Man Utd unhappy
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick laughs off worrying Nicky Butt claim that left Man Utd unhappy

Nicky Butt recently made headlines by claiming that Michael Carrick had serious reservations about returning to management before he landed the Manchester United job

View 3 Images Michael Carrick smiled as he responded (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has laughed off suggestions that he didn't want to become a manager again after being sacked by Middlesbrough, insisting that he's 'loving' life in the dugout. Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt recently revealed a conversation that he'd had with Carrick prior to him taking over at Old Trafford in January.

‌



‌



Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, Butt recalled: "I was with Michael before he got the Man United job and spoke to him about management. He went, 'No it's not for me, it's too much. My head's all over the show. I'd only do it for the big job.' The big job is Man United."

‌



Those comments from Butt were put to Carrick at his press conference on Friday ahead of United's trip to Leeds, with his side searching for only their second Premier League win of the season. "I definitely wouldn't be here if that was the case, would I?" the Red Devils boss smiled.

‌



"At this stage. It's the best job I could possibly have. It's the best role I could possibly have. I feel a real privilege of being in this position and a real responsibility, but equally a drive of wanting to make a difference and having success here.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"So yeah, I'm loving it. I love the situation when actually you get a little bit of a some sort of struggle where you've got to find a way out of it.

"I actually really enjoy that because that's part of what drives you to have success, and that's part of the end of it. And if you're not ready for that and you can't do anything that's difficult, then you're never going to be great. So we've got to work our way through it and I'm enjoying it as we go."

United are understood to have taken a dim view of Butt's decision to go public with their conversation, especially at a time when results aren't going Carrick's way. The 45-year-old has only won two of his nine games in his first season as the club's permanent manager, a stark contrast to the form which the Red Devils enjoyed earlier this year after he was appointed initially on an interim basis.

‌



Is Michael Carrick the right man for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Nicky Butt said that Michael Carrick was reluctant to return to management (Image: The Good, The Ball & The Football)

But Carrick, who was dismissed by Middlesbrough in the summer of 2025, denied the notion that he needs a positive result against Leeds to keep his job. "I don't think it's the last game I need right now, for sure," he said.

‌



"I'm really looking forward to the game. I generally feel the drive for myself to want to push this club forward more than anything. There's always negativity if you want to look for it or you want to feel it, but I don't go looking for it. I don't want to feel it.

"I understand the reality and I've said it enough in terms of feeling like I'm saying the same things, but accepting where we are, but I don't feel that. I'm totally focused on what's best for this place and this football club and what it's going to take to win games, you know, and get the boys playing what we know we're capable of, which we still don't think we're that far away.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is determined to get Manchester United back on track (Image: Cesar Cebolla/Pressinphoto/Icon Sport)

Article continues below

"You know, we can turn a few things in our favour and we'll be in good shape again and we can move forward pretty quickly. So, like I said earlier, I really don't think about me.

"I don't think 'how am I going to get through this, how am I going to survive this and what do I need to do to look after myself'. It's not important. It's about this football club and winning football matches."

Sports.title: Harry Redknapp's brutal Michael Carrick manager verdict is a warning Man Utd must heed
Sports.content:
Harry Redknapp's brutal Michael Carrick manager verdict is a warning Man Utd must heed

Harry Redknapp has delivered a brutal assessment of Michael Carrick's managerial qualities at Manchester United

View Image Michael Carrick is under pressure at Man Utd

Harry Redknapp has branded Manchester United boss Michael Carrick as 'too laid back' and admitted he never envisioned him going into management. The 45-year-old, who was handed his senior debut by Redknapp, impressed during a brief caretaker stint at Old Trafford earlier this year but has found wins hard to come by since taking the reins permanently.

‌



‌



Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid extended United's winless run to five matches. Carrick's only victories this season have come against Ipswich Town and Azerbaijani side Sabah.

‌



Sunday's trip to Elland Road to take on local rivals Leeds United is therefore crucial, with tricky fixtures against Como, Bournemouth and Chelsea to follow. Carrick's first managerial role at Middlesbrough began promisingly before unravelling, with the former midfielder dismissed after two-and-a-half years at the helm.

‌



Will Lisandro Martinez play for Man Utd vs Leeds? Everything we know after bombshell comments READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Whether he can navigate his way through this difficult patch remains to be seen, with Redknapp's candid assessment of his personality and approach raising further questions about his prospects. He wrote in his column for The Sun: "I've known Michael since he was 12-years-old at West Ham.

"I can't say I always saw a manager in him. Michael's always been a lovely guy from a lovely family, a really intelligent footballer who knew the game, read it, controlled matches. But he's always been a quiet lad, too, laid-back. It's what he is.

‌



"When United scored against Tottenham the other day, he wasn't running up and down the touchline - the complete opposite to Roberto De Zerbi, kissing the ball and all that when they equalised. Results haven't been great but I hope he turns it around and keeps the job because I love him.

"You can change Michael tomorrow and they are still not going to finish any higher than fifth or sixth this season. That's how I see their team. They're nowhere near good enough to challenge for a title.

"That's what Michael is dealing with. And it would be the same for anyone else, whoever they bring in."

‌

The dismal run of results and a daunting fixture awaiting United have already heaped considerable pressure on Carrick, with inflammatory remarks from Lisandro Martinez directed at Jason Wilcox only intensifying the scrutiny.

The Argentine slammed his failure to strengthen the squad during the summer window, with injuries leaving Ayden Heaven to fill in out of position in the Spanish capital. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have also been pressed into service up front in the absence of Benjamin Sesko.

Sports.title: Graeme Souness on Liverpool and Rangers glory, being player-manager and 'never letting mum down'
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Graeme Souness on Liverpool and Rangers glory, being player-manager and 'never letting mum down'

EXCLUSIVE: Graeme Souness enjoyed a long career as both a player and manager and added to his trophy collection considerably during his spells with Liverpool and Rangers but the ex-Scottish international was never afraid to break the mould

View 4 Images Souness has enjoyed a long career as a pundit since giving up management (Image: Getty Images)

‘It’s never a dull moment wherever he goes’: The the words of Graeme Souness’ mum Elizabeth from his childhood - and it’s fair to say that she was spot on.

‌



‌



Souness, 73, enjoyed a glittering career with Middlesbrough, Liverpool, Sampdoria and Rangers before moving into management. It only got more chaotic from there with the dugouts at Ibrox, Anfield and Galatasaray’s fearsome former home of the Ali Sami Yen Stadium, among others, having welcomed all Souness’ staunch Scottish silhouette.

‌



Opening up to Mirror Football ahead of the release of his new book ‘Graeme Souness: My Rangers’, Souness said: “Let me tell I'm the youngest of three boys and I had the most wonderful childhood.

‌



“It seems to be a competition for people from my generation to tell youngsters who are willing to listen how tough they had it. I had everything I ever wanted in as a child.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“I've always had confidence, that comes from being part of a solid family unit. That's me. My upbringing was that I was made to feel rightly or wrongly very special in my household. I was youngest and I got treated better than my two brothers and they would tell you that was the case.

“Mum and dad were gentle people and then I came along but I can remember my mom several times looking at the three of us and saying to my dad ‘there's something wrong with that one’.

“She wouldn't use my name but say 'there's something wrong with that one. Never a dull moment wherever he goes'. And I've never let her down.”

‌



He certainly hasn’t. Souness has eight league titles to his name as both a player and manager, as well as three European cups and a whole host of other trophies.

Winning was basically all the former midfielder knew. He added: “As a player at Liverpool, winning the league was always the most important thing. It said more about you as a team, as an individual.

View 4 Images Graeme Souness celebrates winning the FA Cup with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“You've dealt with the disappointments, injuries, loss of form, bad decisions. To win a league is not easy.

“But then winning a European Cup in one of Europe's great cities on a warm May evening, that's a special feeling. But when I went to Liverpool, they were already serial winners. They had won multiple leagues, other European competitions were the current European champions. So when I went there, there was nothing new, it was just win it all again.

“And then when I went to Glasgow Rangers the first year I was there and the end of that season we played Aberdeen and we needed a draw to win the league and we did and that was the first time they won the league in nine years.

‌



“I was on the pitch afterwards and the crowd invaded the pitch and there was a grown man older than me - I would have been 33 at the time - had tears in his eyes and said can I kiss your feet Mr. Souness and I didn't know how to handle it. So, the emotion I saw on that day, it was raw. It was the most intense I've ever seen and felt.

View 4 Images Souness alongside Mo Johnston, Mark Hateley, Richard Gough, Boni Ginzburg and Mark Walters (Image: Getty Images)

“It's quite simple. If you finish second in Scotland, you're a failure. That's the price on the ticket. If you're managing Rangers or Celtic and you finish second, you're a failure.”

‌



Souness spent five years with Rangers as player-manager, with many signalling his arrival at Ibrox as being the start of a revolution within Scottish football. It’s a role that has almost gone out of fashion in the modern game - the most recent example being Ryan Giggs’ short spell as Manchester United player manager in 2014.

“It couldn't be done today,” Souness explains. “Not at a big club. You can’t be a player-manager because the demands on you as a manager are far greater now than they ever were.

“There's managing a big club with all the demands that come with that. So you can’t be a player-manager at Rangers today.

‌



“At night I'm not going home to rest. I'm off traveling into England to look at players or going abroad to look at players and going to dinners that you don't really want to go to. But as a club manager, you have to. So, you can't really rest up properly.”

View 4 Images Graeme Souness has never been afraid to let his feelings be known (Image: Getty Images)

When it comes to managers, Souness played under some of the best that the UK had to offer at the time including Bob Paisley, Joe Fagan and Sir Alex Ferguson - the latter with the Scottish national team.

‌



Asked who had shaped his coaching style the most, Souness replied: “I'd learned everything when I was at Liverpool. I think I went to the equivalent of Oxbridge with the education I had at Liverpool.

“Obviously Shankly was the first one, Paisley to Joe Fagan, Ronnie Moran and Roy Evans that's where I learned it. Fergie was just a mirror of those and their attitude to the game.”

Souness has however never been afraid to break the mould when it comes to his managerial style - or indeed his post-match celebrations. The image of him planting a Galatasaray flag in the middle of the pitch at arch-rivals Fenerbahce is infamous.

Article continues below

And it all echoes back to the words of his mum. Souness says: “You don't want to be the one sitting quietly. You want to be there making an impact. I try to be low key. But if I feel strongly about something, then I'll tell you what I think.

“Jock Stein said something decent. As a football manager, don't go looking for trouble because it finds you on a daily basis. Don't go looking for it.”

Sports.title: Graeme Souness sends Virgil van Dijk contract demand and unearths Liverpool issue
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness sends Virgil van Dijk contract demand and unearths Liverpool issue

EXCLUSIVE: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk sees his contract with the Reds expire next summer but club icon Graeme Souness believes that he should be rewarded with a new deal at Anfield

View 3 Images Graeme Souness has offered his take on former club Rangers (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool legend Graeme Souness has implored the Reds to hand ‘Rolls Royce’ captain Virgil van Dijk a new deal - and has claimed that Dominik Szoboszlai should shoulder some of the blame for their inconsistent start this season.

‌



‌



Van Dijk, 35, sees his current contract with Liverpool expire next summer and a decision is yet to be made on an extended stay on Merseyside.

‌



But despite now being in the twilight of his career, former Reds star Souness believes that he is only getting better and should be offered a new contract at Anfield.

‌



Speaking exclusively to Mirror Football ahead of the release of his new book ‘Graeme Souness: My Rangers’, he said: “I think there's still life left in Virgil, but what is he 35 now? I think there's definitely another year left on him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“I mean, people criticized him when he got that terrible injury from the Everton goalkeeper Pickford, but he came back from that and it's a lazy thing to say, he's not the same player. I didn't see that.

“I think [Ibrahima] Konate was a difficult player to be playing with. I see there's still life left in Virgil. I'll be giving him another year anyway with an option to take a second year because he's a Rolls-Royce of a player. And if anything, he's got better the longer he's been at Liverpool.

“I mean that's one. He's a Rolls-Royce. He's always been a Rolls-Royce. But as you get older, your brain should be kicking in and even seeing things earlier.”

‌



Van Dijk has already had a key role to play under new boss Andoni Iraola, albeit Liverpool have endured an inconsistent start to the campaign.

Souness has full confidence that things will eventually work out under the Spaniard, but has concerns over Dominik Szoboszlai’s place in the side.

View 3 Images Van Dijk is out of contract at the end of the season (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He added: “I've not seen enough of them. But I do like the manager. I live down in Poole. I've seen Areola work at Bournemouth and he was a fabulous manager or coach there.

“Bournemouth are one of the best teams to watch. High intensity front foot football. And he was responsible for that. He knows what he's doing.

“And why Liverpool made a slow start, I don't know. I think the bits I've seen on television, maybe the intensity when they don't have the ball from their midfield, which in turn makes you vulnerable. It's not just center backs not doing their job or the goalkeeper having a bad game.

‌



“A lot of it can be traced back to the midfield not putting the ball under pressure. When you don't have it, working the players who are in possession to keep their heads down so they can't pick a cute pass against you.

“I think Szoboszlai is a fabulous player with the ball. I just think that area there in midfield is a key. I think if they can keep Isak fit and get Ekitike back, they’ve got goals in the team. I just think the midfield is not the best when they don’t have the ball.”

View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai has come in for criticism (Image: Getty Images)

‌



While Souness is sure that Iraola will get Liverpool shaped into his image sooner rather than later, one man who has already enjoyed success at his current club is former Chelsea boss Frank Lampard.

Souness has revealed that he was keen to see the ex-England man appointed by former club Rangers after being named on the interviewing panel.

He said: “I was mighty impressed by him. He's had his knocks as a manager and, given he was such a successful player and is financially independent, he still wanted to take on the mad house that exists in the west of Scotland.

‌



“I’ll come back to the fact that if you finish second, you're deemed a failure. And he would have known all that because his wife is from Northern Ireland and I believe the family are Rangers supporters. He would have known that but he's still desperate for that job and I was very impressed by him when I interviewed him.

“It just wasn't my choice. That's the one that was my first choice. They went for Philippe Clement who I think is a very good manager.

“And I think if Philippe Clement had the backing that these Americans are now giving their managers, I think he might still be there. But that's been and gone.”

Sports.content:
Our top tipster Lewis Jones, aka Jones Knows, provides his analysis and betting insight for a busy weekend of Premier League action.

Tottenham Hotspur vs Coventry City, Monday 8pm, live on Sky Sports

There is a disciplinary angle worth following with Roberto De Zerbi's attacking approach creating the conditions for opponents to find themselves making fouls and being shown cards.

Since De Zerbi took charge, opposition teams have averaged 2.3 cards per 90 minutes against Spurs. That is an interesting trend particularly when you consider the type of wide players Tottenham have. Savio and Mohamed Kudus are dangerous one-vs-one operators who thrive on committing defenders.

Savio has drawn a card every 154 minutes of Premier League action in his career while Kudus won 21 bookings off the opposition in his final season at West Ham, ranking third for cards drawn per game that campaign of all Premier League players to have played more than 1,000 minutes.

Coventry full-back Milan van Ewijk is in the firing line then.

Van Ewijk has already been booked twice this season, giving us some evidence that he is not immune to getting stuck in.

At 7/2 with Sky Bet, the price offers an appealing return for a player who could be under sustained pressure.

Sports.title: Man Utd held by Leeds as winless run continues
Sports.content:
Manchester United delivered a more committed performance in a changed formation but were held to a 1-1 draw by Leeds as pressure on Michael Carrick continues to grow.

In a week that included defeat to Atletico Madrid and an explosive interview from Lisandro Martinez - who started at Elland Road - the noise was calmed somewhat by a display that showed character, if not enough quality to claim a second league win of the season.

United played without a recognised striker for the majority, allowing Youri Tielemans a more offensive role and he combined with Bryan Mbeumo to open the scoring in the first half.

But Carrick's side faded badly as the game went on, another fixture in which they were outrun, eventually pegged back by an instinctive Dominic Calvert-Lewin strike from a poorly defended corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryan Mbeumo guides in opener for Man Utd.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Instinctive Dominic Calvert-Lewin finish fires Leeds level against Man Utd

Leeds away was pitched as the worst game to end a fractious week. In reality, it forced United to scrap and that at least appeared to show appetite for the fight. "In isolation, going to Leeds and performing how they did was a decent result," reflected Jamie Carragher. They were helped by the fact that Daniel Farke's side were not at their battling best either.

Man Utd winless since August Man Utd have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4 L2), their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87.

There was, however, far more intent shown than in last week's drab draw with Spurs at Old Trafford, where disgruntled fans booed the team off, albeit results will read one Premier League win from seven - and none since August.

Carrick will know that return is not good enough to dispel unwanted talk of pressure on his position.

The key moments from Elland Road

27: CHANCE! Mbeumo connects with Tielemans' cross but heads off target unmarked.

35: GOAL! Mbeumo makes no mistake with his second chance from the boot of Tielemans, guiding a low finish past James Trafford.

45: SUB! Martinez is replaced at half-time by Noussair Mazraoui but Carrick sticks with back-three formation.

51: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin latches onto Tarik Muharemovic's knockdown from a corner and beats Senne Lammens from close range.

Maguire: Man Utd lack bravery

Man Utd defender Harry Maguire:

"We worked on it [the change of shape] this week. We wanted to match them up without the ball and go quite aggressive.

"We knew we could get a lot of joy in the middle of the pitch with them only playing two in there.

"That's probably the area of the game where we could have done more. We could have been a bit braver with the ball and taken the ball under pressure.

"But we're in a circumstance where we are not as brave as we should be, and we have to get that back because to win games for Manchester United we have to have that bravery and composure."

Carrick calls Leeds draw 'fresh start'

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick:

"There was definitely commitment. It had to be there today. I didn't doubt that. I was looking forward to the game to see that, there was definitely an edge and intensity to it.

"I spoke to the boys this morning about the history of this game, what it means to the supporters, to the football club. It definitely tests you. It wasn't a perfect performance but there was a lot in there to show determination to get a result.

"We're not getting too carried away because we didn't win the game. It felt like a bit of a fresh start today, in terms of where we're at. The boys are desperate to do well for each other and the club."

On the formation change: "There was a freshness. We had a different spine, that's a massive positive for us. A little tweak tactically, not a huge change. We had to adapt to what their strengths are."

Farke: We were dominant

Leeds boss Daniel Farke:

"It says a lot about how far we've come in the last three years that we are slightly disappointed it was just a point against Manchester United. Overall, it was not necessary to be in a losing position at half-time, I thought we were the dominant side.

"We lacked a bit in our decision-making in the first half, we added clarity in the second half. We had momentum completely on our side. We threatened them with physicality, maybe it wasn't the time for our more technical players.

"We are definitely on the right path. This is a special game. I wanted to go for it, it's a sign that we're doing many things in the right way."

Calvert-Lewin: Leeds 'unlucky' not to win

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin:

"We could've played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box, but just not enough numbers.

"We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: South Africa stutter on rain-hit day one against Australia
Sports.content:
South Africa stuttered to 20-2 in the 12.2 overs possible on a rain-hit day one of the second Test against Australia as Scott Boland struck twice in as many balls.

Boland, selected in Gqeberha as Australia omitted off-spinner Nathan Lyon and went in with a four-pronged pace attack, bowled Aiden Markam (11) off an inside edge in the ninth over before then nicking off David Bedingham (0) with his next delivery.

South Africa, 1-0 down in the three-match series after a 214-run defeat in the opening game at Durban, were 12-2 at that stage having been put into bat but reached the premature stumps without any further casualties as debutant Marques Ackerman (5no off 32 balls) and captain Temba Bavuma (4no off 13) battled.

Score summary - South Africa vs Australia, second Test, Gqeberha South Africa 20-2 after 12.2 overs in first innings: Aiden Markram (11), Marques Ackerman (5no off 32); Scott Boland (2-5 from 3.2 overs)

Rain meant play started around two hours later than scheduled and it returned to bring about an early lunch after just 5.3 overs before another downpour led to the day being abandoned at 4.15pm local time at St George's Park.

Boland for Lyon was Australia's only change from the first match, with the Baggy Greens leaving their premier spinner out of a red-ball Test in which he was fit to play for the first time since 2013.

Image: Markram dragged onto his stumps on a rain-hit day in Gqeberha

South Africa made three alterations with left-arm spinner Keshav Maharaj, wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne and batter Tristan Stubbs axed for batters Ackerman and Matthew Breetzke and fit-again paceman Kagiso Rabada.

Ryan Rickelton took the wicketkeeping gloves in Verreynne's absence and dropped down from his opening position to No 6, with Ackerman coming in to partner Markam at the top of the order.

Ackerman, 30, was opening in a first-class match for the first time and dug in on a seam-friendly wicket.

Sports.title: Man City maintain perfect WSL record as Chelsea, Man Utd, London City win
Sports.content:
Manchester City held off a spirited fightback from Brighton to close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League.

Andree Jeglertz's side raced to a 3-0 lead within 18 minutes, with an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles.

Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur

City remain two points ahead of Chelsea, who thrashed Tottenham 6-2.

Lauren James starred for Sonia Bompastor's side with two goals, which was matched by her team-mate Ellie Carpenter.

Spurs were level at the break thanks to Matilda Vinberg, but three goals in nine blistering second-half minutes swung the game Chelsea's way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between London City Lionesses and Everton

London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1.

First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control.

Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between Charlton Athletic and Manchester United

Manchester United are up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1.

Three goals in the opening 13 minutes saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back.

Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between Aston Villa and Liverpool

Aston Villa stunned faltering Liverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season.

Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal.

Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half as West Ham defeated Crystal Palace 1-0.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest v Arsenal: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
now 12.39 EDT 48 min McAtee watches a dropping ball, tries a volley, slices it …, so badly, it flies at the nearby Havertz, who protects face with hands. Free-kick Forest, again just outside the D, again McAtee and Williams behind it. Share

1m ago 12.37 EDT 47 min Arsenal move down the left but are forced backwards and Forest counter, Delap doing well to slow down Konsa before accelerating again and crossing low, Williams just unable to get on the end of it. Share

2m ago 12.36 EDT 46 min If Arsenal want Madueke to go on the outside and, by sticking him on the left it seems they do, they have to get men into the box. Share

4m ago 12.35 EDT Arsenal are making a change, Madueke for Eze. They’ll hope he can keep maximum width and stretch the play, opening space for Calafiori to underlap. Share

7m ago 12.31 EDT Half-time email: “Arteta’s risk aversion has served him and Arsenal well,” reckons Kári Tulinius. “If Pep Guardiola hadn’t been playing with house money, he’d have a lot more silverware on his mantelpiece. But it can sometimes be counterproductive. For example, in terms of each individual match, the sensible thing to do is to start Declan Rice, because he’s the best Arsenal have got at dead ball deliveries. However, he seems to be permanently a tick below full fitness these days, which makes him less effective in open play. By contrast, Luis Enrique, Jürgen Klopp and Zinedine Zidane both have a high tolerance for risk.” Yes, I agree – Arteta has been given the funds to build near-enough two teams, so the profiles he has are his choice. And that’s part of today’s problem, but I also think the players need to take responsibility and move the ball quicker, with more risk in their passing. We’ve not seen much of the full-backs in attack, either; can they get forward to create 2v1s? Share

19m ago 12.20 EDT HALF-TIME: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Arsenal No shots on target and very little good football. A blinder it is not. Share

20m ago 12.19 EDT 45+3 min And the do, heading clear before Murillo’s hopeful hooked shot trickles through to Raya. Share Updated at 12.19 EDT

20m ago 12.18 EDT 45+2 min McAtee spreads to Williams, whose cross is blocked behind and, with Guimaraes off the pitch having taken treatment blocking the free-kick, they’ve got to defend the corner with 10. Share

22m ago 12.16 EDT 45 min We’ll have two additional minutes. Share

22m ago 12.16 EDT 45 min McAtee makes to run over it but backheels inside to change the angle, then Williams curls hard into Guimaraes and the ball sails behind. Share

24m ago 12.15 EDT 44 min Oh, but Forest counter, a long pass out to Delap allowing him to run at the Arsenal defence, twisting to confuse Konsa before Rice brings him down. Free-kick, just outside the D, left of centre … Williams and McAtee behind it. Share

25m ago 12.14 EDT 43 min This is not good. Arsenal lack the quality and profile of players to get quick combinations going and could, I think, do with Lewis-Skelly’s dynamism and desire to commit defenders. Share

27m ago 12.11 EDT 40 min At no point of this half has a goal looked likely. But a clever reverse-pass from Rice – more of these, please – sends Havertz into the box, his shot always going wide of the near post. Share

29m ago 12.10 EDT 38 min On Havertz, he’s more a big-game striker, I think, good at moving defenders about and a reliable finisher when the pressure is on, than he is a regular centre-forward. His goal record just isn’t good enough and he doesn’t have the pace to threaten the last line; I actually wonder if he might work as an attacking midfielder, because hie has the feet to conjure – when he broke through at Leverkusen, he was more magic man than target man. View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz of Arsenal challenges Xaver Schlager of Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at 12.28 EDT

31m ago 12.08 EDT 37 min Arsenal win a corner out on the right, 25 yards from goal, Rice judges an outswinger into the corridor of uncertainty and Havertz is up … but he mistimes his jump, heading wide. Share

33m ago 12.06 EDT 35 min McAtee, celebrating his 24th birthday, curls the corner directly into Raya’s gloves. Share

33m ago 12.05 EDT 35 min Good from Delap, Schlager controlling a dropping ball well before the centre-forward bustles through a challenge, his shot from distance deflected behind. Share

35m ago 12.04 EDT 33 min “Charles Antaki: ask and you shall absolutely not receive,” writes Sean Orlowicz. The last few minutes have been better, I think, but Arsenal need to move the ball quicker and stretch the play more. They also lack one v one ability – we saw the same with Man United in one of our early games – which makes it hard when facing a set defence. Share

36m ago 12.02 EDT 31 min Of course, as I type, he lofts a fine first-time pass over the top from centre to right – if he did that much more often, we’d not be having the conversation below – but White shanks the eventuating cross behind. Share

37m ago 12.01 EDT 30 min Declan Rice has some fantastic attributes, but his work with both Arsenal and England illustrates the difficulty of balancing a midfield with him in. He doesn’t have the technique to take the ball off the defence – Arteta signed Zubimendi partly for that reason – but going forward, there’s not enough quality on the ball. So in games like this one, when there’s not much call for the big-space work at which he excels, an auxiliary attacker like Merino might make more sense. Share

40m ago 11.59 EDT 29 min Saka again goes near post, but picks out a defender then, when the ball comes out to Odegaard, his inswinger is easily collects by Sels. Share

40m ago 11.58 EDT 28 min Arsenal take a quick throw and Guimaraes wins a corner; he’s starting to influence proceedings. Share

41m ago 11.57 EDT 26 min A flat corner and near-post flick causes confusion – classic Arsenal, but from another era – and Gabriel, facing his own goal, backheels, but into Konsa, and Forest clear. Share

42m ago 11.56 EDT 25 min Again, the outlet is Saka, whose cross is headed behind for a corner. Last season, this would have the ground going. Share

43m ago 11.55 EDT 24 min The buzz you get from knowing you’re good, though, is the calmness to know that if you’re patient, secure at the back and keep doing the right things, the chances will come. I’d just like to see a bit more risk in Arsenal’s play, off the ball as much as on it. Rice and Bruno have done almost nothing going forward. Share

45m ago 11.54 EDT 23 min So far, not much has happened. Forest will be delighted with that, Arsenal less so. Can they get Calafiori going? His runs from deep are hard to track and might make an extra man in attack. Share

47m ago 11.51 EDT 20 min The corner picks out Murillo at the back post; he heads down … and wide, but the flag goes up for a foul of some sort. There’s then a pause as Murillo is bleeding near the corner of his eye, but he’ll be fine. Share

49m ago 11.50 EDT 19 min Calafiori is short with a pass back to Gabriel and Ndoye sends Munoz away. His cross is deflected and Delap does well to recycle at the back post, Ndoye, now on the left, shooting wide of the near post … with the help of a defection. Share

50m ago 11.48 EDT 18 min And he hits a defender, failing to impart the necessary elevation. Arsenal are one of four sides yet to score from a set-piece this season – and Forest are another. Share

51m ago 11.48 EDT 16 min This feels like a Mikel Merino kind of game; his ability to find space and finish is missing from Arsenal’s midfield. Anyhow, Saka slows Williams down, moves away, wears the foul … and that’s a yellow card. A little harsh, but Rice now has a chance to swing over a free-kick. Share

53m ago 11.46 EDT 15 min “Last week Forest controlled possession against Palace but messed up so many of their chances in losing at Selhurst Park,” says Eric Peterson. “I actually like Forest’s chances today as much as I did last week. It’s more in their DNA to make the opponent drown in their possession and catch them out on their break, no matter who the manager is. And with Arsenal’s occasional tendency to possess without thinking ahead on how to use it, that could play into Forest’s hands. Unless Arsenal take the lead, in which case please disregard all this.” Without Gibbs-White, though, that tactic loses a lot of what makes it work: an individual able to make the difference, while also contributing physically. For now, though, they’re defending well. Share

55m ago 11.44 EDT 13 min I’m not surprised Glasner insisted Forest deliver him Munoz, who was the batter of his Palace team, stretching and creating. He makes his first run forward, but without any support is easily unloaded. Share

1h ago 11.43 EDT 11 min Better from Arsenal, building through the middle and quick pokes from Guimaraes and Odegaard finding Eze … who runs the ball into touch. I get strong Cunha vibes from him: a player better suited to being the man in a less good team rather than operating in concert as part of a system. View image in fullscreen Eberechi Eze of Arsenal runs with the ball under pressure from Jair Cunha of Nottingham Forest. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images Share Updated at 12.02 EDT

1h ago 11.40 EDT 10 min A Saka cross is deflected and rears up, arcing under the bar and forcing Sels to claw away, then Arsenal build again. Share

1h ago 11.40 EDT 9 min Forest are looking at Delap to pull off or challenge the last line, but does he have the feet for that? I’m not sure. Share

1h ago 11.39 EDT 7 min The pattern looks set, Forest sitting back and daring Arsenal to break them down. They need, in mine, to get Guimaraes higher and Odegaard on the ball, but for now are moving the ball wide to try and open opportunities from there. Share

1h ago 11.37 EDT 5 min As Arsène Wenger liked to say, an “internal solution”. Meantime, Arsenal probe for gaps the, when Forest clear, Delap puts Konsa under pressure; can you guess what happens next? Yup, he barges through him as cute as Coldplay, and allows the defender to escape a potentially tricky situation with a free-kick. Share

1h ago 11.35 EDT 3 min “You mentioned that the Arsenal’s midfield and attack aren’t strong enough,” says Bill Hargreaves. “Any particular areas or ideas for upgrade?” The midfield is strong enough and, with Odegaard playing well, it probably has just enough guile – even if it lacks goals. Up front, they tried for Vincius, who stopped where he was, opting not to risk on a player they weren’t certain was better than what they have. At some point soon, Dowman will too good to leave out… Share

1h ago 11.32 EDT 1 min Forest will, of course, miss Gibbs-White, who, though he’s scored only once this term, is the player who elevates them. Meantime, Odegaard sends Havertz away down the right, but his cross is overhit. Share

1h ago 11.30 EDT James Kerry, a young Forest fan who died of a brain tumour, struck up a friendship with Morgan Gibbs-White and is being celebrated with a round of applause. His parents and younger brother are on the touchline; godspeed, people. Share

1h ago 11.26 EDT Our teams are tunnelled … and here they come. Or, as Peter Drury would say, HERE! THEY! COME! View image in fullscreen Declan Rice of Arsenal walks out onto the pitch before the match. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images Share Updated at 12.10 EDT

1h ago 11.24 EDT Artetz says your capacity to react to going behind, as Arsenal have in their last three league games, is part of the game. He knows Glasner is an extraordinary manager who’ll have Forest organised, so “you have to insist and insist” – that’s a lovely phrase. Glasner says Arsenal good at managing space and being patient, waiting for chances. They defend well as a team, but he thinks his team can create two or three chances and see what happens. Share

1h ago 11.19 EDT Email! “I don’t want much from this Arsenal team,” writes Charles Antaki. “All I ask is they score a couple of goals early, dominate the other team into hopeless submission, then entertain us all with a fine sporting display of skill, inventiveness, charisma and more goals. I’ve been watching their games for years, and have ground my teeth through long anxious matches enough times to qualify for a bit of credit in the bank. Winning the league last year was all very well, but I want to sit back and wallow in pure unadulterated enjoyment. Isn’t it about time they did the decent thing?” They’re trying, but they don’t yet have the class in midfield and attack to take teams apart in that way – especially given that, though the standard at the top of the Prem is relatively low, from immediately below that and all the way to the bottom, it’s never been higher. Share

1h ago 11.17 EDT I’m really looking forward to seeing Calafiori today. The freedom he has to make things happen evidences a developing total footballer – and, on the other side, I think Timber can be a less powerful but more skilful version of the same. I wonder if, at some point, we see Rice drop a bit deeper to make three centre-backs – which might also facilitate the ball-carrying that is his best attacking attribute. Share

1h ago 11.13 EDT How good are Brighton? It’s early to think about a title challenge, but a top-five spot feels realistic – and if give their talent ID Champions League money, you could be talking about something very serious. Share

2h ago 11.05 EDT That said, Arsenal still have plenty of ways to win a scrappy one, the box-crashing of Calafiori and Rice hard to track and, given their physicality, hard to match. And, if things don’t go as planned, there are options on the bench to change things/ Share

2h ago 11.04 EDT Forest will want – and probably need – to make this game a mess. If it’s open and played through midfield, Arsenal will open them up because, with the guile they’ve added by buying Guimaraes, along with an in-form Odegaard, they have the ability to exploit space. For that reason, Forest need bodies everywhere, especially in the middle of the pitch, forcing them wide, where Saka might just’ve lost the spring in his acceleration following last season’s achilles injury while, on the other side, Eze isn’t going to go on the outside. Share

2h ago 10.58 EDT Elsewhere, 10-man Sunderland trail Bournemouth 2-0 with seconds remaining, while Brighton have splattered Palace 5-0 to move second above Arsenal, their goal difference +18. Ridiculous behaviour. Share

2h ago 10.55 EDT Arsenal, meanwhile, will look for Odegaard to make their play, directing attacks with the direction of his passes. Saka will reckon he can get at Murillo, and hit the by-line, with Havertz pulling off for cut-backs, while Eze wanders infield to look for little passes in behind. Share

2h ago 10.51 EDT So where is the game? Forest will look to play into and off Delap; he’ll be looking to pin a centre-back and lay off for McAtee and Ndoye to run at the Arsenal defence. Otherwise, they’ll want Munoz to target White and Williams to attack the space Calafiori vacates when going off on adventures and look to hit Delat the near post. Otherwise, expect to see Delap initiating contact in exchange for some cheap cheers celebrating his pashun. Share

2h ago 10.45 EDT Arsenal, meanwhile, make six changes to the side that handled Lille in midweek, Arteta reaping the benefits of having a full squad built to his specifications. At the back, Ben White and Riccardo Calafiori replace Jurrien Timber and Myles Lewis-Skelly; in midfield, it’s Burno Guimaraes, not Mikel Merino; and in front of him, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz replace Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyökeres. Share

2h ago 10.39 EDT Back to those teams, Forest make two changes the side undressed at Crystal Palace last weekend, Ola Aina and the injured Morgan Gibbs-White dropping out, with Jair Cunha and Nicolás Domínguez coming in. Nikola Milenkovic, absent since the week of September, returns to the bench. Share
