Sports.title: Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin’s Leeds leveller keeps pressure on Carrick
Sports.content:
What next for Michael Carrick and Manchester United? Game-wise the answer is Wednesday’s trip to Como yet after failing, again, to double the campaign’s league wins tally to two you have to wonder where this already flatlining team are heading.

Sunday afternoon’s display was the latest unconvincing outing under the 45-year-old. It featured an odd formation, zero rhythm or control, and the same prevailing sense that the wheels could clatter off anytime.

Bryan Mbeumo’s first-half opener was answered, inevitably, by Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser after the interval for hosts who were not markedly better but did not need to be so fragile are Carrick’s cadre. Elland Road was the scene of Ruben Amorim’s last stand, Carrick’s predecessor reacting to January’s 1-1 draw by demanding his colleagues in the recruitment department “do their job”. The result? Being sacked two days later.

For now Carrick avoids a similar fate but for how long? United remain stuck on a solitary league victory – back at the end of August, versus Ipswich – and so Como, in the Champions League, becomes the next must-win fixture.

Five days after his scathing diatribe aimed at Jason Wilcox – for the director of football’s iffy recruitment – Lisandro Martínez was selected by Carrick, the defender’s Thursday apology enough to clear the way though his day ended at the interval.

Daniel Farke’s team, unchanged for a fifth consecutive game, were roared on by a crowd who delighted in Martínez’s first contribution, a stray pass hoofed out of play.

View image in fullscreen Bryan Mbeumo slides in to open the scoring for Manchester United. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

The visitors lined up in an “Amorim formation” of 3-4-3, a lesser-seen Carrick configuration. In this, Bruno Fernandes was fielded as the nominal central forward, curtailing the captain’s ability to pull strings from midfield, though his was a free role.

The noise from a febrile home support was dialled up when Carlos Baleba sent Anton Stach to the turf and Darren England saw no infringement. When Fernandes ran though and a clumsy touch caused him to scythe down Tarik Muharemovic, England did act – booking Manchester United’s captain when play next paused, to the delight of Leeds fans.

Gabriel Gudmundsson was also shown a yellow card – for clipping Andrey Santos – in a contest that was blood and thunderous but lacked regular goalmouth incident.

Gudmundsson, the left wing-back in Farke’s 5-2-2-1, did splay the visitors’ defence with a cross that wrongfooted Harry Maguire but it found no teammate, before Jayden Bogle, the right wing-back, repeated the act as Leeds exerted momentary control.

Stach’s free-kick, from the right, had Nico Elvedi flying at the ball to fashion a header Senne Lammens had to be quick to repel.

View image in fullscreen Leeds’ Dominic Calvert-Lewin is mobbed by his teammates after scoring the equaliser. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

At last, the match was alive. Carrick’s men carved a clear chance when Youri Tielemans dropped the ball onto Mbeumo’s head at close-range but he missed – badly.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But next Mbeumo struck via a quick move that sundered Leeds. Along the right Tielamans found Amad Diallo who returned the ball and the Belgian’s cross was slid home by the forward.

Martínez’s removal for the second half brought Noussair Mazraoui to the fray as 45 minutes stood between Carrick and a morale-boosting victory.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Lisandro Martínez on the bench after he was taken off at half-time. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

They held firm for five. A Mazraoui header sent Bogle’s cross out for a corner on the right. When this was swung in Mazraoui was bested by Muharemovic whose flick came to Calvert-Lewin: he outmuscled Mbeumo and crashed home.

With the crowd propelling them forward, Ao Tanaka boomed a volley just over and Farke’s men pinned back Carrick’s side, who lacked ideas: Baleba’s unconvincing long-range effort summed them up.

Better was Fernandes’s turn and shot that spun narrowly wide but he followed this with a weak attempt that the Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford clutched simply.

On 73 minutes Farke took off Noah Okafor for Lukas Nmecha and Carrick removed Baleba for Mason Mount but none of the changes could spark a winner.

Sports.title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.

Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late header matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.

The concerning news for Sage, whose decision to field the teenager Honest Ahanor and 20-year-old Canvot in defence backfired spectacularly, is that two of his predecessors – Patrick Vieira and Roy Hodgson – were relieved of their jobs not long after losing against Brighton. Palace have conceded more goals than any other Premier League side this season and it is understood that there have been some disagreements behind the scenes since the Frenchman took over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, although it remains to be seen whether the chair, Steve Parish, will act on suggestions from the gleeful Brighton supporters during the second half that he will be sacked in the morning.

“It’s not my decision. I don’t know,” said Sage when asked if he will be given time to fix Palace’s leaky defence. “I will always give my best. I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face. My feeling after the game is shame.”

It was Hürzleler who was on the receiving end of that chant in February after Palace’s smash-and-grab victory on the south coast. How things have changed. His vibrant side now find themselves in the conversation for Champions League qualification and they have a squad that also looks capable of coping with the demands of European football.

“The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism. It wasn’t easy,” said Hürzeler. “Now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud to beat Palace. I experienced some derbies and I’m part of this club, I’m part of the journey, that’s why I’m also part of the history. The players deserve it for the hard work they did in the last month because they really stuck together, they faced adversity. They were always there for each other.”

The usual hostility greeted the travelling fans after Sussex police had warned they would be deploying extra officers to deal with what remains very much a grudge match. But a torrential downpour before kick-off didn’t dampen Brighton’s desire for revenge. They tore into Palace’s inexperienced defence from the first whistle and Canvot was caught flat-footed as he headed a pinpoint free-kick from Pascal Gross past Walter Benítez. The Palace goalkeeper could then only watch in horror when Olivier Boscagli fed Gómez on the halfway line after Adam Wharton had lost possession cheaply and the ball sailed over his head into the net after the sweetest of contacts. No wonder that Hürzeler has been urging his players to take more shots from long range this season – they were already the division’s top scorers with efforts from outside the box this season with four. Gómez’s strike from 51 metres was the Premier League goal from furthest out since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

View image in fullscreen Yasin Ayari’s deflected effort results in Brighton’s third goal. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Things got even better for Brighton when a flowing move down the right allowed Kostoulas to tee up Ayari to sweep home via a deflection off the unfortunate Canvot. Sage looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

If he hoped things might improve after the break then he was mistaken. It took Kostoulas only four minutes to make it 4-0 after the ball deflected into his path after good work from Gross. To the delight of the Brighton fans, Jean-Philippe Mateta contrived to hit the crossbar with the goal gaping on his return from injury before Eddie Nketiah also fluffed the chance to grab a consolation.

Sage’s assistant, Paddy McCarthy, had to be held back from confronting the Brighton bench, with tempers threatening to spill over. Plenty of Palace fans had already seen enough by then as they made their escape after a nightmarish afternoon. They missed Hinshelwood heading in from a corner six minutes from the end to round off the perfect afternoon for Hürzeler, who could not hide his emotion as he celebrated with his players at full time.

Sports.title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland
Sports.content:
Bournemouth’s and Marco Rose’s wait for a Premier League win is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far too fast.

Sixth and seventh last season, that both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League speaks to a continental drift where talent from mid-range but historically grander clubs is readily picked off by Premier League clubs.

Two of Bournemouth’s summer additions came via Benfica and Sevilla, Sunderland bought from Lille and Lyon. None of which is any guarantee of Premier League safety. Once Kevin Danso, on loan from Tottenham, was dismissed in the 17th minute for a blatant denial of a goalscoring opportunity, Sunderland were sunk on the south coast.

With a turnaround tight time from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, resources are stretched thinly for Régis Le Bris, at a club where the European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale to new investors has not abated, with a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day-to-day operations. And to place in pure football terms, Sunderland have not celebrated a league win since August, and lost four in succession.

Both managers had selected stronger teams for Sunday’s fixtures compared to Thursday’s. Five changes for Sunderland from Torreense, with Granit Xhaka restored, spelled out Le Bris’s priorities, as did the selection of James Hill, Adrien Truffert and Rayan as Rose likewise made five alterations from beating Sturm Graz at home.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Danso brings down Evanilson before being shown a red card by referee Craig Pawson. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Xhaka’s early mistake prefaced the jet-lagged, error strewn performance that followed Sunderland’s first European away match since 1973. Bournemouth began as Rose demanded, high-press from the get-go, vertical when possible. After Lewis Cook dabbed the ball forward, Evanilson, restored to the line-leading striker’s role, seized on a collective muddle between Danso and Omar Alderete. The Brazilian’s reputation for unselfishness was deepened by his next choice of action. Instead of shooting, he laid up a diving Marcus Tavernier to head home.

Danso’s exit swiftly followed. Evanilson escaped beyond the dallying defender and clumsiness served as no excuse. Craig Pawson, the referee, and his team, could reach no decision other than sending the Austrian for an early sachet of shower gel. A goal up, a man up represented a challenge to Bournemouth’s presence of mind; they had previously conceded nine points from winning positions. First-half chances piled up, Robin Roefs asked to bail out bungling defenders on repeated occasions. There was audible and visible squabbling within the Sunderland ranks over the blame for Rayan and Evanilson enjoying such space.

View image in fullscreen Marcus Tavernier points the way after scoring Bournemouth’s first goal. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

With pressure piling on, the season lurching, Le Bris might argue he can only fight with the resources available to him. Brian Brobbey, on the bench in Portugal after injury on international duty, was missing altogether. Timur Tutierov, 21, last season loaned to Exeter, played as an increasingly lonesome striker, chasing autumnal shadows before a merciful substitution before the hour. That a Danso header was Sunderland’s final attempt on goal of the first half said it all about the direction of travel.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Rose, who revealed this week he had binge-watched Sunderland ’Til I Die on Netflix, kicked every ball on the sidelines. The German’s need for three points was implicit. Patience has been a virtue of the Bournemouth project, but with the Vitality Stadium modernising fast, fans sitting in new-build corner stands as part of renovations, relegation battles cannot be countenanced.

The second goal came with a collective sigh of relief, and via more Sunderland benevolence. Evanilson, given nobody else to pass to by Alderete’s brain-fogged back-pass, supplied a hip swivel Rudolf Nureyev might have been proud of to sit Roefs down and slot into an empty net. A popular goal for a popular player, one of many signings the Bournemouth back office have been successful in making.

Bournemouth could and should have scored more, raining 29 shots on Sunderland’s goal by the 70th minute, including Rayan’s header being hacked from the line. If thoughts were understandably drifting to Thursday and Milan, seven-times European champions, coming to Dorset in the Europa League, Rose would not allow his players to be distracted.

After Sunderland enjoyed a late spell of the game that at last had mackem visitors in full voice, Rose’s team played out the game with admirable calm, Rayan’s dancing feet to the fore as the ball was retained. On this evidence, two clubs facing similar challenges are on very different trajectories.

Sports.title: James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again
Sports.content:
Two goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.

It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.

James’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.

On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”

Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.

View image in fullscreen Lauren James squeezes in Chelsea’s opener from the tightest of angles. Photograph: John Walton/PA

The bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.

If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.

“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: City hold off Brighton to maintain 100% record Show Manchester City held off a spirited fightback from Brighton to close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League. Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles. Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea. London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control. Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left. Manchester United are up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1. Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark. Aston Villa stunned faltering Liverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal. Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half as West Ham defeated Crystal Palace 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“When you’re on top and you concede that second, the way we conceded, from our possession, then that deflates you maybe as a group a little bit. But we have to recover quickly psychologically.”

It was not so much a Spurs collapse as Chelsea putting their foot on the gas, channelling any anger and frustration felt at a less than dominant first-half performance into one full of gut-busting intensity in the second half. Just before the hour Bompastor’s side retook the lead, when Alyssa Thompson surged into the penalty area from the left before sending an angled cutback for the arriving Carpenter to power in.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Four minutes later James extended their lead, collecting the ball from Lucy Bronze in the centre circle before she powered towards goal, wrongfooted Koga and curled an effort past Lize Kop.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea retake the lead in the second half thanks to Ellie Carpenter’s first goal. Photograph: John Walton/PA

“It’s a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,” Bompastor said of James. “I’m pleased, but I want to highlight the team performance. When the individuals are performing it’s because the team is performing as well and the players around her are doing the job for her to express her quality on the ball.”

Chelsea’s fourth was equally as stylish; Keira Walsh flicked the ball to Nüsken and she blasted a rising strike home six minutes after coming on.

Hamano found herself in acres of space for the fifth, sending a curling shot into the top corner. Walsh was at fault for Spurs’ late second, waiting too long to receive a pass which Gaupset pounced on and then fired a low effort past Hannah Hampton. Unwilling to let the game finish on a down note, Carpenter swapped the ball from her left foot to her right as she turned and fired in her second.

It was a chaotic finish to an end‑to‑end match, as Chelsea continue to assert their status as serious title contenders.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Osmand and Nygren at the double as Celtic thrash Hearts 7-1
Sports.content:
Callum Osmand was on target again as Celtic inflicted more misery on Hearts with a 7-1 thrashing at Parkhead.

Osmand netted twice in three first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.

The Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.

Camilo Durán piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear of Rangers.

Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.

They produced 20 shots at goal, one of which found the net from Laurent Mendy, but Celtic were far superior in the final third and benefited from some extremely slack defending.

Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park on Saturday. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.

Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Fink gives Dundee the lead against Rangers from close range. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Motherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a 1-1 draw at St Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.

Sports.title: Martínez back ‘in a few weeks’ after jaw surgery; Liverpool lose Szoboszlai for ‘some time’ – matchday live
Sports.content:
From 9h ago 03.14 EDT Martinez back 'in a few weeks' after jaw surgery Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez said he would be fit to return “in a few weeks” following surgery on a fractured jaw sustained during his team’s 2-0 Premier League win at Everton. The Argentina international was taken to hospital after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during the second half of Saturday’s game at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Martínez, 34, required eight minutes of treatment on the pitch before he was carried off on a stretcher. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso later said he had suffered a concussion. “Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well,” Martínez wrote on social media on Sunday alongside a photo of himself in a hospital bed. “The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. We’ll be back in a few weeks.” Mike Penders is set to deputise in Martínez’s absence. The 21-year-old made his Premier League debut as a substitute against Everton. He joined from Belgian club Genk in August 2024 and has spent the past two seasons out on loan, including a spell at Strasbourg last term. 4h ago 07.25 EDT Donald McRae “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” But there’s sadness, too, in the way his life and career were scarred by his refusal to wear the poppy when playing games around Remembrance Sunday in England. “It’s completely changed me as a person,” McClean says. “It’s made me a bit of a recluse because I don’t trust a lot of people now. I’ve been stung bad.” McClean’s autobiography, The Walls, is one of the best sports books of the year. It’s a powerful and sometimes disturbing read elevated by McClean’s willingness to show himself in an unflattering light. 7h ago 04.48 EDT From the archive: Leeds United v Man Utd classics double quotation mark Leeds United 1-0 Manchester United (FA Cup semi-final replay, 31 March 1965); Leeds United 0-1 Manchester United (Division One, 17 April 1965) Here’s where the stags really begin to rut. Don Revie’s side, freshly promoted, were on course for the Double. Only problem was, so were Matt Busby’s men. The pair were drawn in the semi-final of the FA Cup, and spent 90 minutes at Hillsborough kicking seven colours out of each other, Jack Charlton, Billy Bremner, Nobby Stiles, Denis Law and Paddy Crerand enjoying themselves like the proverbial pigs. Good luck if you found yourself in the middle of that. Brouhahas broke out on the terraces as well, and did so again four days later during the replay at the City Ground. The on-field behaviour was much improved, though. According to Big Jack, Manchester United put on a performance as stylish and dangerous as they ever were under Busby, but Leeds somehow held on, wrested the ascendency, and nicked it in the last minute, Bremner twisting in mid-air to steer home an outrageous curling header. Bremner was missing 18 days later when Manchester United came to Elland Road in the league. Had they won, Leeds would have gone five clear at the top with four games left. They went into the game as favourites, Busby’s side having failed to find the net against Leeds in both Cup games and the earlier league match at Old Trafford, which the visitors won 1-0. That particular lean spell ended after 14 minutes – or 284, if you like – when John Connelly drove home. Leeds failed to respond, despite the best efforts of the newly crowned Football Writers’ player of the year, Bobby Collins, and went down again in their next Bremner-less match, a 3-0 hosing at Sheffield Wednesday. Busby’s third great side won their first title; Revie’s team, not quite ready yet, lost the Cup final as well. This will be the fifth time we have faced them, the third at Anfield. The other two were European semi-finals. I’ll watch the morning training session, travel with the team. 7h ago 04.21 EDT Dominic Booth If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics last season was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell. Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction and relegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted. The problem is the Dansons have been unable to find an ambitious buyer to take the club to the next level. Now the prospect of a first season in the fourth tier since 1996-97 is a distinct possibility, although victory against Reading – the Latics’ second league win of the campaign, sealed by Scott Hogan’s 71st-minute strike – made the picture a little rosier. Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One Read more Share

8h ago 03.28 EDT Jonathan Wilson The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” This was everything Sunderland fans could have wished for from their first European away game in 53 years and more. They had seen other fans experience these things, and now they could tick off the checklist: complicated travel to a pretty foreign town they would otherwise never visit, a fussy Albanian referee and a great sense of togetherness and community. There was even an injury-time winner from, miracle of miracles, Noah Sadiki. Ask any of the 5,000 or so Wearsiders who made the trip to Portugal if the Europa League was worth it and the answer would be unanimous. Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Brighton fans would surely say something similar: European football, especially for clubs who are unfamiliar with it, is a joy and an adventure. It generates experiences that will be remembered for ever, and if the cost is that the risk of relegation goes up, that’s a price worth paying. Others at those clubs may see things differently. Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson Read more Share

Sports.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
Sports.content:
There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games.

Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules. Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming.

“I didn’t expect to win seven out of seven, but we are working well,” Maresca said. “This is the most important thing.”

Victory came at a cost as Haaland and Antoine Semenyo limped off at full-time, in addition to Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly suffering injuries, although Maresca was left unsure of the severity as City prepare to host AEK Athens on Tuesday.

If City have felt like it has been their backs against the wall for the past few weeks, it was Ipswich’s turn. Gary O’Neil put 11 men behind the ball whenever the hosts ventured over the halfway line as City enjoyed 90% possession in the opening quarter-hour, but without truly threatening as they struggled to find space in the lowest of blocks, expertly organised and fully disciplined.

Maresca had made six changes to refresh the side and it took time to understand one another’s rhythm, with Ayyoub Bouaddi creating it from defensive midfield in another mature performance from the teenager making his first Premier League start.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca has guided Manchester City a record seven-match winning start in the Premier League. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images

It was inevitable what was coming as there was irrefutable evidence that City were dominant. As at Anfield, Jérémy Doku was a key instigator, showing mesmeric skill on the left of the area before finding Foden to sweep home for his first goal since mid-December.

“I know him from years ago, for me he’s one of the best Premier League players,” Maresca said. “Since day one, it’s my duty to help him to be again one of the best players. I’m very happy for his goal and hopefully it can be just the beginning of many goals and many good performances.”

There was an element of pantomime around the ground from the booing of the Premier League anthem, the singalongs and inflatables. It was fitting Marc Guéhi did not know Maeda was behind him, allowing the Ipswich man to latch on to a sublime curved through ball from Abdoul Ouattara and equalise two minutes after the opener.

Quick Guide Manchester City 3-2 Ipswich key facts Show • With Manchester City maintaining their 100% record, Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team. • Manchester City are the third team to win their opening seven games of a Premier League season, after Liverpool in 2019-20 (first 8) and Chelsea in 2005-06 (first 9). • Erling Haaland (pictured) has now scored 100 non-penalty goals in the Premier League, reaching this milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139). The previous fewest was 150 appearances, by Alan Shearer in 1996. Opta Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

After a missed chance, Haaland showed it is possible to get a better result second time around, making the most of Kovacic becoming an auxiliary winger. The header lacked power, but Christian Walton could not keep it out, palming the ball from one hand to the other and into the net before Haaland was serenaded with the clap of bananas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City found themselves stuck in a lull, unable to prise open Ipswich, instead having to bide their time. It was a test of patience and a sweeping move upfield concluded with a precision pass from Iliman Ndiaye and an aggressive finish from Haaland, who was later denied a hat-trick by the video assistant referee.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City fans have gone back to more innocent times with their inflatable bananas. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Farai Hallam reviewed footage of Guéhi taking out Abdul Fatawu in the area and Flemming did the rest in the 90th minute, as reward for an impressive team performance, leaving O’Neil upset Ipswich departed with nothing.

“They’re an incredible group,” he said. “Players giving everything. It’s a privilege to stand there and represent them because they’re an incredible group.”

City were left to complain about a Premier League official’s decision when 12 minutes was added on, with few knowing why, but this result will not be questioned.

Maresca called on his team to make their own noise while a cacophony swirls around them, but on-pitch success will not speak louder while what is happening off it is unresolved. The fans sang about relegation and trips to Stockport, embracing a dark situation with humour to match.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reveals why Lisandro Martinez was substituted at half-time
Sports.content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has revealed why Lisandro Martinez was substitute at half-time against Leeds.

Martinez started for United at Elland Road just days after he launched an angry outburst towards the club's board.

3 Carrick started for Man United a few days after his outburst, but was substituted at half time against Leeds Credit: Getty

The Argentinian centre-back slammed their recruitment after a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid.

But Carrick admitted on Friday that the drama following Martinez's comments was 'done' and that he was available for selection.

He went on to start against Leeds for the Red Devils and kept a clean sheet in the first half, as his side went in 1-0 up.

Bryan Mbeumo's goal was the difference and United looked to be on the top, leading their rivals as the whistle blew.

However, when coming back out for the second half, Martinez didn't return to the pitch, sitting on the bench instead.

Carrick replaced the defender with Noussair Mazraoui, with Leeds going on to score an equaliser as the game ended 1-1.

Why did Carrick substitute Martinez?

Speaking post-match, Man United boss Carrick explained the reasoning behind Martinez's half-time withdrawal.

He said: "He felt his thigh a little bit."

Martinez had been spotted hobbling during the first half.

He could potentially now be a doubt for United's Champions League trip to Como on Wednesday, which will be live on talkSPORT 2.

3 Carrick has revealed why he took Martinez off at the break after his side drew 1-1 at Elland Road Credit: AFP

Martinez's angry outburst

Martinez, who has started eight games in all competitions for Man United this season, was not substituted for off-the-pitch reasons.

He was reportedly fined for his outburst, but Carrick was clearly happy enough to keep him in his team on Sunday and only took him off due to his knock.

The 28-year-old targeted United's technical director Jason Wilcox in his rant, which he went on to apologise for.

"I have to control myself a lot," Martinez said on Tuesday. "But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."

3 Martinez was fined by United for his comments about the club on Tuesday, but he started for them again on Sunday Credit: Getty

On whether Carrick has not been backed enough, he added: "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas. I can't say more.

"It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Sports.title: Premier League manager tipped to be sacked instantly after 70-year first
Sports.content:
Premier League manager tipped to be sacked instantly after 70-year first

Pierre Sage has been warned he could be sacked by Crystal Palace if they risk being sucked into a relegation battle.

It follows the Eagles' heavy defeat to bitter rivals Brighton on Sunday afternoon.



3 Sage's side made a disastrous start to their clash with Brighton on Sunday Credit: Getty

Palace were thrashed 5-0 at the Amex after shipping three goals inside the opening 10 minutes.

Those included an own goal from Jaydee Canvot before Diego Gomez scored a goal of the season contender from the halfway line.

The defeat marks Palace's heaviest loss to Brighton since January 1956 and leaves Sage's side just two points above the relegation zone.



A toxic atmosphere amongst the travelling supporters also saw his players booed off at the final whistle.

Assistant manager Paddy McCarthy did his best to calm the situation as Sage was met with jeers from the Palace fans.



Despite only being appointed in the summer, the Frenchman could now find himself under pressure at Selhurst Park.

Sage under pressure

talkSPORT's Perry Groves admitted Sage is 'done' after the derby defeat.



Speaking to Sam Matterface on GameDay Live, Groves said: "I think Sage is going to be demobbed at the end of this game. He’s done."

Alex Crook echoed the sentiment that Palace chairman Steve Parish could soon consider a change in the dugout.

He explained: "There was that story earlier in the season that Jaydee Canvot, who scored the own goal today, was left out of the team.

3 Brighton secured their biggest win over Palace for 70 years Credit: Getty



"Steve Parish wasn’t particularly happy with Pierre Sage for that decision. So I think there are signs of cracks in the relationship.

"I know Steve Parish came out and did quite an in-depth interview with our colleagues at The Athletic and said it’s going to take time, ‘we’re behind him’, but they are giving away too many chances, no doubt about that.

"I fancy Brighton today, despite the fact they’ve got a dreadful recent record in this fixture, because even though they won last weekend against Forest, Crystal Palace, they should have been out of the game by half-time.

"It was down to Forest’s wastefulness, really, that they ended up getting all three points in that match.



"History tells us that if Steve Parish sees signals that his side are heading for a relegation fight, he will make a change. He did with (Frank) De Boer when he was brought in to change the playing style.

"I think that lasted 10 matches, so at the moment, I don’t think the manager is covering himself in glory."

3 Sage was appointed on a three-year deal in the summer Credit: AFP

What's next for Palace?

Frank De Boer was sacked just four matches into the 2017/18 season after suffering four successive Premier League defeats without scoring a goal.



Sage has already seen his side lose four of his nine matches across all competitions.

The loss to Brighton followed league defeats against both Everton and Ipswich Town so far this term.

Meanwhile, Palace were beaten by Lyon in the Europa League in midweek.

They are once again in European action on Thursday as they travel to Turkey to face Besiktas.



Palace then host Newcastle United in the Premier League three days later.

Sports.title: Premier League LIVE: Arsenal eyeing opener against Nottingham Forest, Leeds draw with Man United, Brighton hammer Palace
Sports.content:
'The time has come to hang up the boots'

Saido Berahino has announced his retirement from football.

The 33-year-old striker has called time on his career after 14 years in the game, having played for 11 clubs in total.

He was once tipped to become England's next big thing, having starred as a youngster in the Premier League.

Berahino played 133 top flight games, scoring 23 goals and providing three assists, also playing 84 games in the EFL.

Most of his career was spent at West Brom, while he also had stints with Stoke and Sheffield Wednesday before spending two years in Cyprus and last playing for Tabor Sezana in Slovenia.

Issues off the pitch around transfers and general conduct largely derailed his progress, and now, he's retired from the game.

He wrote on Instagram: "A Letter to the Game Football has given me everything. From the streets of Bujumbura to the Hawthorns, from the Premier League to places I never imagined I’d play — this game carried a young refugee kid through life.

"I want to thank West Bromwich Albion for believing in me when I was a boy. Those years at the club, the goals, the fans, the moments… they will always be special. To every teammate, coach, and supporter who shared the journey — thank you.

"There were highs and lows, mistakes and lessons. I learned that the game can lift you up and test you at the same time. Through it all, football remained my constant.

"The time has come to hang up the boots. My body and my heart are ready for the next chapter. I am proud and grateful to now serve the Burundi national team as a coach. Giving back to the country that made me, and helping the next generation, feels right.

"To my family — you have been my strength. To the fans who stayed with me through every chapter — I will never forget your support.

"This is not goodbye to football. It is simply the end of one story and the beginning of another."

Sports.title: Brighton star scores outrageous goal of the season as Seagulls tear rivals Crystal Palace apart
Sports.content:
Brighton star scores outrageous goal of the season as Seagulls tear rivals Crystal Palace apart

Brighton's Diego Gomez scored the Premier League's 'goal of the season' on Sunday during a 10-minute rout of Crystal Palace.

Gomez incredibly scored from the halfway line in the opening stages of the Seagulls' 5-0 win over rivals Palace at the Amex Stadium.

2 Gomez and his teammates couldn't believe what had just happened after the Brighton star scored from the halfway line Credit: Getty

The Paraguay international received a quick pass into his feet from Oliver Boscagli after Adam Wharton lost possession.

He took one touch, turned and spotted Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez well off his line in the goal.

And he unleashed a perfect strike, beating Benitez with a powerful effort that sailed over him and into the net.

The Brighton fans roared as the players chased after Gomez in disbelief at what had just happened.

Speaking on talkSPORT, ex-Arsenal winger Perry Groves said: "Don't worry about goal of the season. We've just seen it."

Gomez's remarkable strike was from 51 metres out from the goal.

That is the furthest range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney for Everton vs West Ham in November 2017 (58m).

Brighton's 10-minute triple

Gomez's incredible halfway line strike was the second goal of the game for Brighton after just seven minutes.

Palace's Jaydee Canvot had already headed into his own net just moments before, putting the hosts into the lead.

And then just three minutes after Gomez's goal, Yasin Ayari got in on the act and finished into the bottom corner.

2 Gomez's goal was from the furthest distance since 2017 in the Premier League, proving just how incredible the strike was Credit: AFP

By scoring three in 10 minutes, Brighton became the ninth side in Premier League history to score three in that time.

They are the first since Newcastle against Tottenham in April 2023.

Spurs conceded three in 9 minutes on that day, before the Magpies went on to win the match 6-1 in the end.

Brighton then went on to add a fourth just after half time, with Charalampos Kostoulas finishing after a ricochet in the box.

And Jack Hinshelwood added his side's fifth with a tap-in from close range in the final stages of the match.

Gomez's stunner was his first of the season for Brighton in all competitions, adding to his two assists.

He had a hand in a goal in the Seagulls' 3-0 win over Arsenal in September and their season opener against Aston Villa.

Since joining the club last January from Lionel Messi's Inter Miami, the right midfielder has scored 12 times in 66 appearances.

Sports.title: Football clubs should be blocked from sacking managers in radical new rule change
Sports.content:
Football clubs should be blocked from sacking managers in radical new rule change

Tony Cascarino and Shebahn Aherne believe that football clubs shouldn't be allowed to sack managers until a certain point in the season.

The conversation was sparked because a host of under pressure managers won their respective games.

3 Alvaro Arbeloa lives to fight another day after Fulham's 1-0 win over Hull City Credit: Getty

Russell Martin, Alvaro Arbeloa, Alessio Dionisi and Phil Parkinson all won despite building pressure.

Across the top five divisions in England, we have already seen five sacked.

The first gaffer to go was Michael Duff at Wycombe Wanderers before Paul Heckingbottom at Preston North End soon followed.

Of course, their dismissals weren't based purely on this campaign and were a hangover from the previous one.

Lee Cattermole at Gateshead in the National League was one of the managers appointed in the summer and already sacked.

So, with that in mind, Aherne and Cascarino discussed the problem on Weekend Sports Breakfast.

Former Millwall and Chelsea striker Cascarino said: "I've always argued the point that there should be a window for managers, they should all be able to survive until a certain period.

"So, even if you appoint a manager in June, they get until the next window without anyone being allowed to sack them.

"Some people won't like it because they'll say, 'well, look, he'll take us down'. Well, that's your fault for making the decision on who to employ."

Aherne then added: "Mangers get a juicy pay-off, and they will probably get another job, but you wonder if they are protected enough contractually.

"I do wonder if you could put in a clause that there are a minimum number of games or to get to January.

"It offer them a bit more protection, and it takes out the conversation of pressure."

3 Parkinson is another manager is under a lot of pressure Credit: Getty

Cascarino responded: "It would be fair. You have got to give people backing.

"If you are going to employ them, you have got to give them the opportunity.

"There are very few fixed contracts, as in where a manager gets a whole term, so you have to to give them time.

"If you had a date across the board of say January 1, then that's fair."

Aherne used Fulham as an example.

"Now Fulham have won, they can turn it around, but if they'd not won yesterday would it be a case of, you're done now.

"It's so quick. It is definitely too quick."

3 It ended in tears for Cattermole at Gateshead Credit: Getty

Results determine futures

All clubs appoint managers to get the best results, whether that be to survive, compete for higher spots or titles.

And as much as some fans will be more patient than others, it is a results game.

But managers can turn it around.

talkSPORT reported earlier in the week that Arbeloa was under intense pressure to win.

They did just that with a much-needed 1-0 victory over Hull City.

We also reported that Steven Gerrard would be interested in taking the Wrexham job after one win in ten for Parkinson before smashing Preston 4-1.

And Martin is not the most popular person at the King Power Stadium at the moment, but Leicester City beat Doncaster Rovers 2-1.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals Tottenhan star will be out for weeks in fresh injury blow
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi reveals Tottenhan star will be out for weeks in fresh injury blow

Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that new signing Savio will be out for a number of weeks.

Meanwhile, Dejan Kulusevski will be on the bench when Tottenham Hotspur face Coventry City on Monday night for the first time in more than 500 days.



3 Kulusevski is a massive fans' favourite at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium Credit: Getty

The game is live on talkSPORT and, after nearly a year-and-a-half out, the Swedish international could play a first-team game for Spurs.

His return is a huge boost for the home team, who are still seeking a first win of the season in the Premier League.

However, there can never be just positive injury news when it comes to Tottenham.



That is because Savio and Lucas Bergvall have been ruled out of the match.

The duo started the draw against Manchester United at Old Trafford last weekend and impressed.



But Spurs will be without them, while it comes too soon for Pedro Porro's return.

The Spaniard limped off in the 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa before the international break and hasn't kicked a ball since.



On Kulusevski, De Zerbi said: “Yes [he will be on the bench], the medical staff have given the okay. It's probably the greatest news since the Everton game.

“He has suffered too much.

"I told him yesterday and he had a big smile on his face."

3 De Zerbi will be desperately hoping that Tottenham can get a win to kickstart their season Credit: AFP

And those set to miss out, he said: “No Savio, unfortunately Savio on Tuesday before leaving for Marbella felt a muscular problem and we have lost him for some weeks.

“And Lucas Bergvall because he had a problem in Manchester early on in the first chance he created for Dominic Solanke.



“He felt pain in his knee but felt fine and on Sunday he came to the training ground and he'll be out for two weeks.”

Kulusevski's injury

The 26-year-old hasn't kicked a football for Tottenham since May 11 in 2025 against Crystal Palace.

He went off after 19 minutes in a 2-0 defeat, and it is now well over 500 days since he played for Spurs.

But Kulusevski has still started a game more recently than James Maddison, showing that Tottenham have been deprived of two of their most creative players for a long time.



The injury he suffered is known as a patella, and he actually walked off the pitch before scans revealed he needed surgery despite then-Spurs gaffer Ange Postecoglou describing the injury as a 'knock'.

He was expected to be out for a few months but had a setback and needed further surgery around the knee to clean up debris.

Kulusevski had hoped to be fit for Sweden at the World Cup, but that didn't happen either.

3 No one at the time expected the former Juventus man to be out for so long Credit: Getty



Sweden's national team doctor Jonas Werner tried to explain why Kulusevski has been out for so long.

He said: “They are difficult to treat. Cartilage has no blood supply and no nerves. They do not heal in the usual way.

“In addition, his injury is in a place where a lot of strain occurs for a football player.

“The kneecap [patella] slides back and forth over the femur [the thigh bone]. An enormous compressive force is developed.



“It is likely that his injury has not healed enough for him to cope with that strain yet.”

Spurs' injury woes

The injury problems at Tottenham have been rife for a long time, and they are still without a couple of players with long-term injuries.

Xavi Simons tore his ACL at the back end of last season and Wilson Odobert is out with the same injury.

Then you have Maddison just returning, but Bergvall and now Savio are out.



Mohammed Kudus spent a long time on the sidelines last year as well, so it has been a problem for some time at Tottenham.

Sports.title: 49-cap England star told international career could be done – he must focus on club football
Sports.content:
49-cap England star told international career could be done – he must focus on club football

Phil Foden has been warned he is unlikely to fight his way back into the England squad anytime soon.

Foden scored in Man City’s 3-2 win over Ipswich on Saturday - his first of the season.



3 Foden scored his first goal of the season for City on Saturday Credit: Getty

It was also the first time he featured for City in nearly a month as he served a suspension for his red card in September’s Manchester derby.

The 26-year-old has played for England 49 times since making his debut in 2020, but was not selected for the 2026 World Cup.

He was also omitted from Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the recent Nations League games.



Foden last featured for England in March in two pre-World Cup friendlies, but failed to stake a claim for a place at the tournament in the US, Canada and Mexico.

He seems to be well out of Tuchel’s plans with a glut of options in the No.10 role and on the left.



Journalist Henry Winter told talkSPORT’s Sunday Edition that he is unlikely to regain a spot in the squad.

When asked where his career is at the moment, Winter said: “It's very much at City. I don't really see him getting back into the England fold.



“Where is he going to fit in now? We've got rid of this daft argument which seemed to be occurring of who should be England’s starting number 10. Should it be Rogers or Bellingham? Bellingham is an absolute elite world class player and the World Cup highlighted that as if anyone who's watched England needed any reminding of that.

“So you've got Bellingham at 10. You've got Rogers obviously going. He can also play wide as he's showing at Chelsea. They're slightly tucked in.

“Then you've got so many others who are ahead of him. Not necessarily [Eberechi] Eze, but [Morgan] Gibbs-White, [Cole] Palmer, and you've got Josh King. He's playing so well for Fulham.

3 Foden last played for England in March- but is unlikely to be back soon Credit: Getty



“So does Foden necessarily get back in? I'm not so sure.”

Foden on Man City charges

Foden conducted his post-match interview with an inflatable banana, which has become the symbol of City defiance after being found guilty of significant financial rule breaches.

City were found guilty in September of all charges relating to financial rule breaks by an independent commission.

The club, who have appealed, were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by £900million via 'sham' contracts from the 2009/10 season to 2017/18.

"I'm going to get one for my son as a present, I think," Foden told club media. "I think he wanted one, so I can give him one now."



"It hasn't affected us one bit," the 26-year-old added to Sky Sports.

3 City fans brandished inflatable bananas at the Etihad on Saturday Credit: AFP

"We've just stuck together, just did what we normally do and focus on the games one by one and just be ourselves. I think we've done that really well.

"We have great characters and leaders in the changing room. Nothing's changed. We're just fully focused and trying to do the best for the fans that we can."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho declares Vinicius Jr should have left Real Madrid in summer after failed Arsenal transfer
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho declares Vinicius Jr should have left Real Madrid in summer after failed Arsenal transfer

Jose Mourinho believes Vinicius Jr should have left Real Madrid in the summer, but has praised his commitment to the club.

Arsenal were heavily linked with a move for the Brazilian international following their Premier League title win last season.



2 Vinicius committed his future to Madrid until 2032, but could have moved to the Premier League as Arsenal eyed a move Credit: Getty

talkSPORT reported in July that they contemplated a transfer, which would have been one of the most audacious deals in football history.

Vinicius ended speculation over his future by signing a new deal with Madrid that runs until 2032.

However, his head coach Mourinho feels as though the 26-year-old winger may have benefited from leaving the Bernabeu.



"If I were (Vinicius), in his place, I probably wouldn't be here," he told the media ahead of Madrid's LaLiga clash against Sevilla, via ESPN.

"Last summer I would have forced my exit to a league, to a country, to clubs and stadiums where they'd respect him.



"But because he's a Madrid fan, he has love for the club and the city, he believes things can always improve, he renewed, and he'll keep that smile.

"I think there's nothing or no-one that can take that away, that joy for living and working. He's a great boy."



When clarifying what he said, Mourinho added: "When he signed that contract, he signed it because Madrid is his home, and Real Madrid is his home. He's one of the main sources of joy in that dressing room.

"What I said before was that I doubt I'd be able - as a player with lots of options - I doubt whether I'd be able to have his psychological strength, to hold on."

According to Forbes, Vinicius is the world's fifth-highest paid player in 2026 with a $76million (£57m) income.

2 Mourinho put himself in Vinicius' shoes and surprisingly claimed he should have left the club Credit: Getty



How has Vinicius played this season?

Since signing his new deal at Madrid, Vinicius has made a slow start to the 2026/27 season with one goal and three assists in ten matches.

He has not found the back of the net since their 4-1 victory over Real Sociedad on August 26.

Vinicius has played in all eight of their LaLiga matches in the current campaign, but is out for the next four matches.

During a 1-0 win against Villarreal last weekend, he was shown a red card for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba.



Vinicius was given a two-match ban for the hair pull and the same sanction for his 'aggressive' reaction, making it a four-match ban.

He will miss the match with Sevilla on Sunday night and El Clasico against rivals Barcelona, as well as the fixtures with Racing Santander and Valencia.
