Sports.title: Leeds 1-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Who 'still looks short of his best'? Which star was 'a real handful'? And whose performance will have pleased Michael Carrick? Plus, vote for YOUR scores
Sports.content:
Leeds 1-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Who 'still looks short of his best'? Which star was 'a real handful'? And whose performance will have pleased Michael Carrick? Plus, vote for YOUR scores

Leeds and Manchester United played out a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Elland Road in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

Under-fire United boss Michael Carrick saw his side go 1-0 up through Bryan Mbeumo after he turned home Youri Tielemans' cross, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised early in the second half when he fired home from close range.

Both sides pushed for a winner but neither could find a breakthrough as they were forced to settle for a point on an intense afternoon.

The result leaves United with seven points from seven league games, while Leeds are up in seventh place after racking up ten points so far this season.

Daily Mail Sport's CHRIS WHEELER was at Elland Road and he has rated both sets of players below...

Manchester United and Leeds played out a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Elland Road on Sunday

LEEDS UTD (3-4-2-1)

JAMES TRAFFORD 6 – Looked solid and showed good anticipation to race 40 yards out of his goal and clear at the feet of Diallo. Had little chance with Mbeumo’s goal from close-range.

JAMES JUSTIN 4 – Will be angry at himself that he lost track of Mbeumo for United’s opener. You can’t afford to switch off in games like this.

NICO ELVEDI 6 – Presented with one of Leeds’ few chances in the first half when his header was saved by Lammens. Had his hands full with Mbeumo as United’s forward line chopped and changed.

TARIK MUHAREMOVIC 6 – The big Bosnia defender was on the end of an ugly challenge from Fernandes early on, but recovered to get the crucial knockdown for Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

JAYDEN BOGLE 7 – Got forward to offer a real threat at times and also defended well. Great interception tackle on Dalot in the first half got a huge cheer.

ETHAN AMPADU 7 – Right in the thick of it. Set the tone with a couple of strong tackles early on, and squared up to Fernandes in the second half. Just the kind of approach Leeds fans love to see in this fixture.

Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu was up for the fight on what was an intense afternoon

But James Justin (right) was caught out after switching off for Bryan Mbeumo's opener

AO TANAKA 5 – Had a couple of half chances, including a volley over the bar shortly after Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser. Replaced by Longstaff towards the end.

GABRIEL GUDMUNDSSON 5 – Booked for a challenge on Andrey Santos in the first half and was perhaps fortunate it wasn’t a red. Referee Darren England did well to let the tackles go in a fixture that was never going to be short on intensity.

ANTON STACH 6 – Had two chances to make his mark on this game but volleyed over in the 72nd minute and then side-footed straight at Lammens late on. Got away with a cheap shot on Fernandes but the United captain was never going to have much sympathy here.

NOAH OKAFOR 5 – Leeds’ two-goal hero from the win at Old Trafford in April rarely looked like scoring in this one and was replaced by Nmecha for the final quarter of the game.

DOMINIC CALVERT-LEWIN 8 – Playing with the confidence of a striker who only needs one chance and he took it with a clinical finish early in the second half. A real handful for United’s defenders.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is in the form of his life and was a real handful for United's defence

Subs: Zetterer, Longstaff (for Tanaka 80, 6), Wilson, Aaronson, Nmecha (for Okafor 73, 6), Bijol, Bahoya, Bard, Gruev.

Scorer: Calvert-Lewin 51

Booked: Gudmundsson, Ampadu

DANIEL FARKE 6 - Will see this as a missed opportunity with Leeds on such a good run and their opponents struggling so far this season.

MAN UTD (4-2-3-1)

SENNE LAMMENS 5 – Couldn’t be faulted for the goal but still lacks the composure of last season which is perhaps inevitable in a United side short of confidence.

LENY YORO 6 – Looking more comfortable at right-back with each game he plays there. Took a blow to the face from Calvert-Lewin in the first half, but recovered well and stood strong against Okafor.

HARRY MAGUIRE 7 – His physicality was important here after missing out against Madrid in midweek. Good battle against Calvert-Lewin but wasn’t marking the Leeds striker when he equalised which was odd.

LISANDRO MARTINEZ 6 – Kept his place as expected after the furore over his post-match comments in Madrid and subsequent apology, but went off at half-time. Showed why United needed him here with a solid first-half display.

DIOGO DALOT 6 – Played out of position at left-back in the absence of Luke Shaw again and performed well in his duel with Bogle. Got forward well on occasions.

ANDREY SANTOS 6 – This was a big test for the Brazilian and Carrick chose to keep him on the pitch when he replaced Baleba, which says a lot for what the head coach thought of his performance.

Andrey Santos faced a big test in this game but he impressed and Carrick will be pleased

CARLOS BALEBA 6 – Cool presence in midfield after he was flattened by Ampadu early on. He has brought a calmness and composure to this United team that was needed in the cauldron of Elland Road.

AMAD DIALLO 5 – Returned on the right flank and there is room for improvement after his injury lay-off in the first part of the season. There were concerns Diallo had suffered another one when he needed treatment after a challenge by Tanaka, but he recovered.

YOURI TIELEMANS 6 – Playing at No.10 suits his game better. In a game of very few chances, he created both openings for Mbeumo in the first half.

BRUNO FERNANDES 5 – Switched between the left flank and striker with Mbeumo in a fluid United formation, but still short of his best. Had to be careful after picking up an early yellow card for a lunging tackle on Muharemovic which had the home fans baying for a red.

BRYAN MBEUMO 7 – United’s most dangerous player. Scored the first goal with a simple finish after heading wide unmarked in front of goal. Was outmuscled by Calvert-Lewin for the equaliser, but it’s anyone’s guess why he was marking the big Leeds striker.

Bryan Mbeumo was United's most dangerous player and put them ahead in the first half

But Bruno Fernandes continues to look out of form and had to be careful after an early booking

Subs: Darlow, Amass, De Ligt, Mazraoui (for Martinez 46), Mount (for Baleba 74), Lacey, Cunha (for Tielemans 84), Rashford, Zirkzee.

Scorer: Mbeumo 35

Booked: Fernandes, Andrey Santos

MICHAEL CARRICK 6 - It’s only two wins in 10 games this season, but the United boss will take a point here after another difficult week.

Sports.title: This is how far ragged Man United have fallen. Anything that isn't a defeat is a good result, they can't control games, are weak in the centre and had to hang on against Leeds, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
This is how far ragged Man United have fallen. Anything that isn't a defeat is a good result, they can't control games, are weak in the centre and had to hang on against Leeds, writes IAN LADYMAN

It may not have looked, felt or smelled like it, but this was a good result for Manchester United.

It wasn't a performance or an outcome to mask problems or deficiencies that run right through Michael Carrick's squad but in terms of an outcome it was about par.

For this is where United are right now. Anything that isn't a defeat – especially away from home – to a team with ideas and ambition and a good coach represents a decent day out. This, frankly, is how far they have fallen.

Carrick's team took the lead in the first half and had the better of it for a while. But then they lost control of things to the extent that it took them half an hour to have another shot. By then Leeds had equalised and taken a grip of the game.

In fact, by the end, Daniel Farke's energetic and likeable team had mustered 62 per cent of the possession and this is one of the reasons that the other United – the one from along the M62 – are stuck in such a rut. They simply cannot control games.

They have some good players and Bryan Mbeumo is one of them. He scored in the 35th minute. But in the centre of the field where tempo and rhythm are set and territory is won, United are weak.

Manchester United and Leeds played out a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Elland Road on Sunday

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the second half after Bryan Mbeumo had put United ahead

Here, with Carrick betraying the look of the team sheet by deploying what looked like a back three, it was new signings Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba who were given the job of securing ball and position. They were okay but that was all they were.

Over time, Leeds won that battle and as the game wore on, it was they who had the loftier ambitions. It was they who sensed a win and Carrick's players who were looking to get out of town with what they had.

They were a little bit all over the place by the end. Three promising counters in the space of five minutes, for example, were halted by utterly needless and brainless offsides.

But United survived and some of the noise around Carrick's position will quieten between now and Wednesday's Champions League game in Como. The pattern seems once again set now, however.

We are seven games in to the new Premier League season and United have won just once – against Ipswich at home.

Here Carrick's formation had a look of Ruben Amorim's back five about it. It was inflexibility – not to mention poor results – that got Amorim the sack last season but at least Carrick appeared to be trying something different.

Mbeumo slid home from close range in the first half after Youri Tielemans' inviting cross

Calvert-Lewin levelled by firing home from close range after the ball broke to him from a corner

Diogo Dalot and Amad Diallo appeared to be playing as wing-backs in a line-up that saw United start without a clear centre forward. Youri Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Mbeumo were the front three with Fernandes more often than not occupying the central position. After all the fuss of the week, Lisandro Martinez was in the team but only until half-time, after which the Argentinean failed to appear.

Arguably, United's problems have not been about tactics and formations but about application. Here, against an upwardly mobile Leeds team, Carrick's team seemed for a while to have more about them than they showed in drawing against ten-man Tottenham eight days earlier.

They were more compact but also more energetic and it ensured they initially competed with the home team on the metrics that really mattered. Sadly for United, it wasn't to last. Leeds were honest and spirited but lacked consistent tempo in the first half. They created sporadic half chances but nothing that sufficiently engaged the home crowd. Indeed Elland Road was rather quiet at times and that told part of the early story.

Mbeumo's opening goal didn't arrive until the 35th minute. Up until that point the game had been scrappy and occasionally required the vigilance of referee Darren England.

Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu should have been booked for an early stamp – accidental or not – on Mbeumo while Fernandes was indeed cautioned for a late challenge on Tarik Muharemovic. That offence came after Fernandes applied a heavy touch to the through pass and was perhaps indicative of his recent poor form. Prior to that, the United captain had taken a free-kick from a good position on the far side and delivered it straight out of play.

Leeds were occasionally progressive around this point and United keeper Senne Lammens was sharp enough to touch a header from Nico Elvedi over the bar in the 25th minute. At that stage, it stood as the only chance of the game.

The result slightly eases the pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick

Lisandro Martinez was subbed off at half-time in the first game since his explosive rant

United always looked as they may carry a threat when they did motor up field, though, and Mbeumo served notice of this almost immediately when he found space to meet a Tielemans cross six yards out only to head the ball six inches wide of James Trafford's left hand post.

As the visiting team grew into the game, so they settled a little. There was nothing haphazard about this performance at this point and after Trafford tore from goal to stop one dangerous attack with a slide tackle on Diallo, United returned again to take the lead.

It was Tielemans again with the cross from the right only this time it was a low one. Mbeumo was under pressure from James Justin with the Leeds defender taking a piece of his shirt. But the United forward was strong and determined and he kept enough of his balance to side foot the ball in from a few yards out.

United just about deserved their lead. They had looked just a little more clinical than their opponents. They held it until half-time – despite half chances for Calvert-Lewin and Jayden Bogle – but it took only six minutes of the second period for the game to change.

With Noussair Mazraoui replacing Martinez at half-time, the Moroccan conceded a corner in the 51st minute. When the kick arrived, however, he was beaten to it in the air by Muharemovic who headed the ball down for Calvert-Lewin to swivel and volley in.

Thereafter United were ragged. All their previous structure and composure had gone and for a period they hung on. There was nothing particularly sophisticated about Leeds' football. It involved width and crosses – not always as accurate as Farke would have liked - and high energy. But it made United look ordinary and uncomfortable. Indeed when Fernandes swivelled and drove a low shot across goal and wide in the 65th minute, it represented United's first effort on goal of note since they scored.

Bruno Fernandes, Carrick and Amad Diallo salute United's fans at the final whistle

Technical director Jason Wilcox, the subject of much of Martinez's ire, was in attendnace

Leeds were not creating lots of chances, either. Just a couple of smashed shots over from Ao Tanaka and Noah Okafor and then another from Anton Stach with 18 minutes left. But the home team did have some momentum and that threatened to be precious.

As they looked to turn the game back their way, United's options from the bench were limited. Mason Mount came on for Carlos Baleba with 15 minutes left but Carrick seemed reluctant to introduce Marcus Rashford or Matheus Cunha. Maybe that was a sign that the United manager valued a point above anything else. Eventually, with six and a half minutes left, Cunha was given his chance.

It was still Leeds who finished the stronger and they could have stolen it in added time. United keeper Lammens applied a weak punch to a cross and watched Stach's shot dribble through his legs. Fortunately for Lammens – and indeed Carrick's emotional wellbeing – Mazraoui was positioned behind him to hack the ball away.

Sports.title: MORE Premier League stars join rejection of taking the knee as fans boo the anti-racism gesture amid growing doubts over its impact
Sports.content:
More Premier League players have rejected taking the knee before kick-off – with fans booing the anti-racism gesture as doubts over its impact continue to grow.

Bournemouth stars Rayan and Tyler Adams both refused to kneel alongside their team-mates before their game against Sunderland got under way.

Meanwhile, fans in the stands loudly booed the gesture as Leeds prepared to face Manchester United at Elland Road.

It comes after three players snubbed the token act on Saturday in a shaky start to the Premier League's 'No Room For Racism' month.

Everton star Ainsley Maitland-Niles refused to kneel as his side hosted Chelsea in Saturday's early kick-off – despite other players doing so.

England defender Marc Guehi and Issa Diop did the same just before the game between Manchester City and Ipswich at the Etihad Stadium.

Two Bournemouth players stood while their team-mates took the knee against Sunderland

Everton's Ainsley Maitland-Niles refused to take the knee before the game against Chelsea

The players' reasons for not kneeling are not yet known. However, a number of footballers have expressed concern that the gesture has lost its value.

In 2021, former Crystal Palace star Wilfried Zaha questioned the impact of taking the knee while ex-Brentford striker Ivan Toney said: 'We are being used as puppets.'

Zaha added: 'I feel like taking the knee is degrading, because growing up my parents just let me know that I should be proud to be Black no matter what and I feel like we should just stand tall.'

It is not the first time players have refused to take the knee. Last year Dominic Calvert-Lewin did so in Burnley's fixture with Leeds, while Crysencio Summerville has been known to take the same action.

When Marcos Alonso was at Chelsea, he opted to point to the Premier League's 'No Room For Racism' badge on his arm rather than join his fellow players.

Ahead of the 2021-22 season, Luton indicated that they would not be taking the knee and instead all stood in the centre circle.

At that stage, players were still taking the knee ahead of every game – but that policy was stopped in August 2022.

Instead, a decision was made to limit the gesture to match rounds falling during the No Room For Racism initiative.

Man City's Marc Guehi, right, and Issa Diop, left, of Ipswich refused to kneel before kick off

Maitland-Niles took the knee for West Bromwich Albion in 2021 but has since opted against making the gesture

But it was agreed ahead of the season among Premier League captains that they would continue to perform the gesture twice per season.

Pockets of matchgoers have expressed frustration at the gesture in the past. In 2021 that led to Burnley captain Ben Mee hitting back: 'It gets to the point where if you're booing, it doesn't look good on those individuals that are booing. Disappointed, but there was a lot of positive there as well.

'Support us in what we're trying to achieve as a group of players and a football community.'

Players and staff have the opportunity to perform the pre-match gesture for the next two gameweeks in October, with the Premier League reiterating 'the commitment to tackling discrimination and highlight the importance of diversity in football'.

The move started in the UK in 2020 following the death of George Floyd in US police custody, which sparked the Black Lives Matter movement.

Last year, the Lionesses chose not to kneel before their Euro 2025 semi-final against Italy following racist abuse aimed at defender Jess Carter on social media.

Captain Lucy Bronze said the anti-racism message is not 'as strong as it used to be' following the abuse of her teammate.

'It was driven by the group – obviously certain individuals more than others,' Bronze explained. 'I think it was just the fact that we feel as a collective, is the message as strong as it used to be? Is the message really hitting hard? Because to us it feels like it's not if these things are still happening to our players in the biggest tournaments of their lives.

'It's about putting another statement out there to say, it's something that still is a problem, it's something that still needs to be put right. More needs to be done in football, more needs to be done in society. What that is right now as an individual, I don't exactly know.'

Ex-Chelsea star Marcos Alonso points to his 'No Room For Racism' badge rather than taking the knee

But the head of football's international anti-discrimination body, Fare, questioned the Lionesses' decision to stop taking the knee.

Piara Powar told BBC Sport: 'The players have taken a decision to stop taking the knee, which is their right.

'Personally don't see the link between the two. The taking of the knee is a powerful anti-racist act and this England team have shown leadership across Europe in taking it for so long.

'Powerful actions are needed right now, to deal with the issues that are being played out as we speak.'

Guehi also made headlines in 2024 when, as Crystal Palace captain, he wrote 'I love Jesus' on a modified captain's armband given to all Premier League skippers to promote LGBTQ rights.

He was formally reprimanded for that, but followed it up by wearing an armband with 'Jesus loves you' written on it in the next game.

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha: I'm learning from Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka... and in talks for new Liverpool contract
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha: I'm learning from Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka... and in talks for new Liverpool contract

Liverpool starlet Rio Ngumoha says he has been inspired after watching Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon for England – and insists talks over a new Anfield contract are 'going well'.

The 18-year-old played an integral role in the Reds' comeback victory at Brentford on Saturday and is well-trusted by boss Andoni Iraola, also starting in the Champions League midweek game.

Ngumoha has also won three caps for England and said: 'Playing on the right (wing) was good for England but also watching the likes of Anthony Gordon, Bukayo Saka… they are top, top wingers.

'Training with them every day and just seeing what they do, that can really help me and I take some of the stuff they tell me on board and it is really helpful.'

Ngumoha is in talks over a new bumper contract at Liverpool, having signed for the club in 2024 from Chelsea – much to the dismay of the Stamford Bridge club.

He has also been learning a new role at Anfield as Iraola demands all of his wingers can play on either flank.

Rio Ngumoha is in talks to sign a new contract at Liverpool to reward his growing role

Ngumoha added: 'To be fair (the contract) is all with my agent now. I think it is all going well. I am not too sure.

'I just let the football do the talking at the end of the day, so I enjoy playing and all of that stuff is in the back of my mind really. I just play for the club, play for Liverpool and hopefully I can carry on doing well.

'(Playing on both sides) gives me a bit of unpredictability, so if teams see me playing, they might think I am on the left but I can offer something different on the right.

'So it is good, I think at a young age, being able to play off the right or the opposite side and be unpredictable, I think that is something that is really key and I am enjoying it. It is good.

'I can't thank the gaffer much more really for putting me on so early in the game and like I said, whether I start or if I come on, I just have the same mentality.'

Liverpool duo Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong are set for scans, meanwhile, after suffering injuries in the win at Brentford.

Sports.title: The Brighton Beckham! Premier League star scores INCREDIBLE goal from the halfway line, 30 years on from when David did the same
Sports.content:
Brighton star Diego Gomez channelled his inner David Beckham with a remarkable goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace. His strike, a goal of the season contender from 51 yards, helped move Brighton up to second in the Premier League in a thumping first-half performance which saw them go 3-0 up. Paraguay international Gomez, 23, took control of the ball inside his own half and turned, taking aim from the halfway line to beat Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez with a right-footed shot. Brighton had already taken the lead in the fourth minute thanks to an own goal by Jaydee Canvot, and by the 10th they were 3-0 up after Yasin Ayari got on the scoresheet. Holding on to victory would see Brighton go second behind Manchester City, who have a flawless record but are in limbo after being found guilty of financial rule breaks. Ironically, Gomez used to play for the Beckham-owned Inter Miami - and his effort was reminiscent of the long-range scorcher scored by the former Manchester United man against Wimbledon in 1996. Diego Gomez channelled his inner David Beckham as his shot from the halfway line beat Walter Benitez The Brighton star could barely believe what was happening as he ran away in celebration "Would you look at that!" DIEGO GOMEZ SCORES FROM THE HALFWAY LINE! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/qmagVbGEb4 — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) October 18, 2026 His goal has already been making headlines in the United States, where David and his wife Victoria share a waterfront Miami property. 'Would you look at that! Diego Gomez with a goal that the Brighton fans will never forget,' purred Sky Sports commentator Bill Leslie. 'It didn't seem possible, it shouldn't have been possible. It's just become a glorious Brighton reality. Palace custodian Benitez went pale as Brighton's team wheeled away in celebration with Gomez, who geed up the crowd and kissed the badge on his shirt. It is the longest-range goal in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney stunned the crowd from 58 yards as Everton thrashed West Ham 4-0 in November 2017. That day, Rooney bagged a hat-trick. Gomez has become an important player for Brighton, who he debuted for in January last year, and scored 10 goals in all competitions last season. This is not the first time he has scored a 'worldie'. Against Barnsley in the Carabao Cup last season, he netted four times, including a half-volley from around 35 yards out. The goal reminded fans of David Beckham's strike against Wimbledon back in August 1996 He is also a significant star for Paraguay, who he helped to the last 16 of the World Cup over the summer. While more of a box-to-box midfielder than a flair player, perhaps it is no surprise he has a dash of magic in his locker after previously being team-mates with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez. Brighton are making a habit of blockbuster strikes, with Lewis Dunk having won goal of the month against for his spectacular effort against Coventry in September.

Sports.title: Former heavyweight world title contender boxer dies 'suddenly' aged 40: Denis Boytsov, once set to fight Tyson Fury, was unable to speak for 11 years after mysterious 'attack'
Sports.content:
A former world No 2 heavyweight boxer once primed to fight Tyson Fury has died aged just 40, after 11 years of care following an 'attack' in which the perpetrators were never found.

Russian Denis Boytsov pulled out of a fight with Fury in December 2012 and was considered the world's second-best heavyweight behind Wladimir Klitschko. He had a 36-1 record when his career was cut short in 2015.

Boytsov suffered serious head injuries in a Berlin subway tunnel and had to be placed into a medically induced coma because of swelling on the brain.

A statement on the boxer's website suggested he was the victim of an attack linked to his boxing career. 'It is possible that this attack was linked to the boxer's sporting activity,' the statement said. 'Around two years ago, Boytsov was receiving threats constantly.'

His wife Olga Litvinova was left deeply upset and suggested Boytsov may have been the victim of an attempted 'assassination' after that series of threats.

Now, 11 years on, Boytsov's family have revealed he died 'suddenly' this week after many years in care. His father says the cause of death was a detached blood clot.

Russian boxer Denis Boytsov died this week from a detached blood clot at home

Boystov is pictured in his boxing gear in hospital after the 'attack' on him in 2015

'A blood clot broke off,' Nikolai Boytsov told Russian news agency TASS. 'There was nothing they could do; it was instant death. Three minutes and that was it.

'This happened at home. His wife fed him and started turning him to the side. He suddenly broke down, started shaking, turned blue. And his whole life was over.'

Brother Maxim Boytsov revealed Denis had been unable to speak in the 11 years following the Berlin incident. Boytsov underwent extensive treatment in Germany and then back in his homeland.

'No, we didn't communicate. He just nodded yes and no. But he understood everything. I courted him for ten years. But it didn't work out,' said Maxim.

Boytsov's funeral is set for today in the Russian region of Oryol.

British former heavyweight boxer David Price - who once beat Fury in 2005 - revealed Boytsov's punching power was much stronger than that of Anthony Joshua, having trained with both.

Boytsov's wife Olga was by his side as he died in Russia this week

Boytsov was due to fight Tyson Fury in 2012 and was considered a top heavyweight fighter

'I sparred a Russian called Denis Boytsov in Germany once. He only hit the top of my head, but he was a powerful puncher,' Price told the Daily Star.

'I think he got his career cut short, he got absolutely battered and left for dead, he couldn't fight again. But I remember him being a really powerful puncher.'

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher pinpoints 'vicious circle' Man Utd chiefs must end immediately
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher pinpoints 'vicious circle' Man Utd chiefs must end immediately

Manchester United are in a 'vicious circle', according to Jamie Carragher, and the former Liverpool player has also explained what club chiefs must do to end it

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has spoken about Manchester United's spending over recent seasons (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher claims Manchester United have been in a 'vicious circle' of spending big on underperforming players who they then struggle to sell. The club have not consistently qualified for Champions League football in over a decade despite having one of the Premier League's biggest wage bills during that time.

‌



‌



United spent over £150million on transfer fees alone during the summer transfer window. Last season's Champions League qualification has also increased the wages of several players already in their squad.

‌



Carragher believes the high salaries United pay hinder their ability to sell. The club have struggled to move on players.

‌



He contended that the blend of hefty salaries and underperforming players has made it increasingly difficult for United to offload players. That leaves the club unable to continue spending their way out of difficulties.

Michael Carrick's masterplan scuppered by injury blow as Leeds deny Man Utd win READ MORE :

Speaking on Sky Sports, he said: "I just think when you're at a club that's spending big money, and those players are continuing to fail, you're not getting in the Champions League as well, you've got one of the biggest wages; eventually you can be the bigger spenders of the season, but you're not being successful.

"Liverpool and Manchester City are two of the few clubs that have consistently won trophies and then have big spending sprees.

‌



"The money will always be there because they're one of the biggest football clubs in the world, but it can't just be a tap that never gets turned off - it just can't.

"And then you're talking about net spend; well, you don't get players out. It's difficult to get players out when you continue failing at the club.

View 2 Images Manchester United have assembled a squad at great expense that does not consistently qualify for the Champions League (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Then they're on big wages, and you can't move them on - no one will take them. It's a vicious circle that they're in. Eventually, it gets to a stage where you can't be the biggest spenders and for me, that was this summer."

United have suffered a troubled beginning to the campaign. They have just one victory so far as the heat intensifies on Michael Carrick to reverse their fortunes.

Their problems have sparked doubts about the club's trajectory. Lisandro Martinez's remarks earlier this week only heightened the scrutiny.

The Argentine defender launched a damning critique of Jason Wilcox, insisting he had 'expected more' investment in the squad over the summer before seemingly laying the blame for United's dismal start at the feet of the club's hierarchy. However, they stopped the rot by drawing 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Brighton star scores from HALFWAY LINE as Seagulls run riot against rivals Crystal Palace

Brighton blew rivals Crystal Palace away with a sensational opening ten minutes on Sunday afternoon with Paraguayan midfielder Diego Gomez stealing the show with a stunning goal

View 2 Images Diego Gomez's first goal of the season was one to remember (Image: Getty Images)

Brighton star Diego Gomez has been compared to David Beckham following his wondergoal from the halfway line. The Seagulls enjoyed a scintillating opening half against their rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



They took the lead as Jaydee Canvot put through his own net, with Gomez then doubling the lead just moments later with a stunning strike.

‌



Gomez, 23, picked the ball up in the centre circle and fired a brilliant effort over Palace keeper Walter Benitez and into the back of the net.

‌



Speaking about the striker, former Premier League stopper Shay Given said: “It's an amazing goal. Reminiscent of David Beckham [vs Wimbledon].

Sports.title: Man Utd stars fear Amazon Prime documentary cameras are to blame for struggles
Sports.content:
Man Utd stars fear Amazon Prime documentary cameras are to blame for struggles

Manchester United are set to bank more than £10million through being the subject of Amazon Prime's All or Nothing series, but the cameras for the documentary are said to be causing problems

View 2 Images Manchester United's every move is being filmed by Amazon Prime (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Manchester United's players and staff reportedly fear that Amazon Prime's documentary cameras are contributing to their early-season struggles. The Red Devils are the focus of the latest instalment of All or Nothing, the acclaimed fly-on-the-wall series.

‌



‌



After a deal worth more than £10million was agreed, a crew are following Michael Carrick's side over the course of the 2025-26 season - and there's already been plenty of drama. United's arduous summer transfer window has been followed by a run of poor results to start the campaign and an explosive interview from Lisandro Martinez in midweek.

‌



With only two wins from nine games, Carrick is already under pressure just weeks into his first season as the club's permanent manager. But some fear that Amazon are to blame.

‌



The Sun claim that both players and staff feel that their colleagues are holding their tongue in post-match debriefs knowing that they're being filmed. The cameras are described as a 'pain' and the belief is that 'punches are being pulled'.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Manchester City, Tottenham and Arsenal have previously been the subject of All or Nothing. Amazon has also created series following Australia's Test cricket team and Premiership Rugby.

In August, Carrick was asked what it was like having the cameras around. "That's been fine," the United manager replied. "It's obviously a little bit new, and unique, but the actual day-to-day workings of it, we have that many cameras around anyway that the boys are kind of half-used to it.

"We've got to work through it, of course, but they've been respectful. It probably seems bigger from the outside than it is day-to-day when we're working in it."

Carrick, though, is determined to turn United's form around but is relaxed amid the notion that he needs a positive result at Elland Road to keep his job. "I don't think it's the last game I need right now, for sure," the Red Devils boss said.

"I'm really looking forward to the game. I generally feel the drive for myself to want to push this club forward more than anything. There's always negativity if you want to look for it or you want to feel it, but I don't go looking for it. I don't want to feel it.

"I understand the reality and I've said it enough in terms of feeling like I'm saying the same things, but accepting where we are, but I don't feel that. I'm totally focused on what's best for this place and this football club and what it's going to take to win games, you know, and get the boys playing what we know we're capable of, which we still don't think we're that far away."

Sports.content:
Tyson Fury issues response to Daniel Dubois KO with Anthony Joshua promise

Dubois retained his WBO world heavyweight title with a brutal second-round stoppage of Wardley in London on Saturday night

View 2 Images Daniel Dubois punches Fabio Wardley

Tyson Fury warned Anthony Joshua he faces the same punishment as Fabio Wardley after he was bashed up by Daniel Dubois.

‌



‌



Wardley was stopped inside two rounds in his heavyweight rematch with Dubois, five months on from their thrilling fight-of-the-year contender. Dubois retained his world title and Fury - who takes on Joshua in Cardiff on December 11 - vowed to dish out the same beating.

‌



"That was a very exciting heavyweight fight between Dubois and Wardley, fair play to both guys," he said. "Well done to Daniel for retaining his belt with a big knockout; that's how you get them out of there big Dan! "And that's exactly what's going to happen to AJ on December 11 - spark out."

‌



Daniel Dubois DESTROYS Fabio Wardley in two rounds in rematch READ MORE :

Dubois, meanwhile, Fabio Wardley had felt his “bad intentions” as he set his sights on cleaning up the heavyweight division. Oozing menace, Dubois launched an all-out assault from the first bell and having knocked down his British rival after just 17 seconds the fight was brought to an end a round later when trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel.

It was a devastating display of punching power that retains his WBO world heavyweight belt and lights up the division, positioning the 29-year-old Londoner for big fights against fellow title holders Filip Hrgovic, Agit Kabayel and Murat Gassiev. “Whoever is next in line, really,” Dubois said. “I’m the champion now and I want to get some big fights in. At this stage in my career I want big money, big fights.

‌



“Fabio is a great boy coming in for the second time, but it was my time and it’s my era. I had bad intentions from the beginning. This is God’s victory. We’ve done well.“My b ack was against the wall for the first fight and this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, which is what we did.”

View 2 Images Fabio Wardley is knocked down

Wardley barely threw a shot and spent the 5 minutes 21 seconds the fight lasted in survival mode having never recovered from the brutal right hand that floored him in the opening exchanges.It was reminiscent of the later rounds of their first clash in May when a blood-soaked Wardley was stopped in the 11th having knocked down Dubois in the first and third rounds.

Article continues below

Surprise was expressed by some that Wardley had immediately activated the rematch clause given the punishment he took, but the Ipswich puncher denied the battering five months ago was a factor behind the second defeat of his career.

“No, not in the slightest,” Wardley said. “I just came in and didn’t execute the game plan properly. I hold my hands up to that – that is entirely down to me. “When I step through the ropes, it is only myself. It’s only me bouncing down in the ring, there’s no blame to be passed around. When I win it’s all me as well. There’s no shame in losing to a great competitor like Daniel.

“It’s never fun to lose, but it is what it is. The game is the game. I have always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there – the best in the business, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around – so there’s no shame in a loss when you’re testing yourself against the best.”

Sports.title: Chelsea keeper Emi Martinez sends emotional message from hospital bed after surgery
Sports.content:
Chelsea keeper Emi Martinez sends emotional message from hospital bed after surgery

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez has given an update from his hospital bed after undergoing surgery on his jaw following an awful clash of heads against Everton

View 2 Images Emi Martinez in hospital (Image: Instagram/emi_martinez26)

Emi Martinez has taken to social media to reassure fans following surgery on his jaw after a sickening collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea's 2-0 victory over the Toffees. The goalkeeper suffered the injury in a horrifying clash of heads with Branthwaite, who flung himself towards Martinez while attempting to meet a cross into the box.

‌



‌



Both players were left motionless on the pitch as the match was brought to a standstill for over 10 minutes while Martinez received medical attention. Chelsea's players immediately called for assistance, with Levi Colwill seen holding his head in his hands after witnessing the frightening incident unfold.

‌



Martinez was eventually stretchered off the pitch, and could be seen moving as he was carried away, his hands placed either side of his head, as per football.london.

In a post shared on Instagram, alongside a selfie taken from his hospital bed, Martinez said: "Thanks to everyone for the messages, the operation went well.

"The most important thing is that we won and with a bow at 0. We'll be back in a few weeks."

In the comment section, there were several Chelsea stars who sent their well-wishes to the goalkeeper. Morgan Rogers said: "My GK [Loveheart emojis]" while Moises Caicedo said: "My little brother[hearts]."

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley landed just 4 punches in brutal Daniel Dubois KO
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley landed just 4 punches in brutal Daniel Dubois KO

Dubois retained his WBO world heavyweight title with a brutal second-round stoppage of Wardley in London on Saturday night

View 2 Images Daniel Dubois was devastating (Image: Nick Potts/the Press Association)

Fabio Wardley landed just FOUR shots on Daniel Dubois as he was blasted out inside two rounds.

‌



‌



Dubois retained his WBO world heavyweight title with a brutal second-round stoppage of Wardley as their fight of the year rematch ended in a furious assault from the champion. There were 39 seconds of the round left when referee Steve Gray waved the off the contest at the same time as the towel was thrown into the ring by Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison.

‌



Resuming hostilities just five months after their first encounter, Dubois launched an all-out assault from the first bell and was rewarded with a destructive victory that issued a statement to his rivals in the division. The Londoner’s first defence of the title he seized from Wardley in May positions him for unification fights as well as the possibility of facing the winner of Tyson Fury ’s bout against Anthony Joshua on December 11.

‌



Daniel Dubois DESTROYS Fabio Wardley in two rounds in rematch READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

And on this evidence he will be favourite to unify the heavyweight belts following a display of ferocious punching power that left Wardley in survival mode right from the start. Wardley had vowed to make the adjustments needed to avenge the only defeat of his career, but instead the former white-collar boxer was outclassed as his lack of experience caught up with him.

‌



Dubois had oozed confidence all week and he wasted no time marching into the ring, dispensing with the stage theatrics to get the fight started as soon as possible. And in a dramatic reversal of the first fight, he floored Wardley just seconds into the contest following a barrage of shots that saw a savage right hand do the telling damage.

A one-sided opening round continued with Wardley coming under ferocious attack and it ended with him under pressure against the ropes while Davison hovered in the corner ready to throw in the towel. Images of the battering Wardley took in the later rounds in May came flooding back as he took more punishment in the second and with hardly any shots coming back in response, Gray and Davison intervened.

View 2 Images Fabio Wardley is knocked down

Article continues below

The punch stats show Wardley landed four of the 27 shots he threw compared to Dubois' 60 out of 119. The champion landed 51 of his power shots in a scary showing. Despite taking a fearful battering in the first meeting including extensive damage to his blood-soaked nose, Wardley immediately activated the rematch clause.

He felt that by flooring Dubois during the first and third rounds in Manchester even though he had not connected cleanly, he could force victory by mixing his power with a more nuanced approach.By rising from the canvas twice, meanwhile, Dubois had silenced questions over his mental resilience that first emerged when he was accused of “quitting” against Joe Joyce in 2020.

He entered the rematch as odds-on favourite to claim a 27th professional win and the stage was set for another slugfest between two of the division’s most explosive punchers, but it never materialised as the champion ended his rivalry with Wardley in chilling fashion.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.
