Lukas, who lives in Czechia, says winning the prize would “finally be some peace for my sofa” and promises fans they can “be the team boss” by choosing challenges for him to take part in each race weekend, sharing the results as the season goes on.

India, from the UK, describes herself as a “completely ordinary fan” looking to make next year “extraordinary” – and also asked other fans to set her fun challenges for each race, saying that winning would “bring together my two passions of F1 and seeing the world.”

Joy, whose home race in Singapore took place earlier this month, wants to use the opportunity to experience “the excitement and sportsmanship” of F1 around the world and to have a chance to “share the same passion” with those around her.

Jose, from the USA, is a fan not just of the racing but also of the strategy, technology and teamwork behind F1. He visited his home race in Las Vegas last year and said: “Travelling to every race in the 2027 would honestly be a dream come true.”

Singapore GP Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

Picking a winner

The opportunity to travel to every grand prix opens up unprecedented access to the sport and its fans. The current ticket holder Burgess has shown just how to get the best out of the experience this season and he was on the judging panel that picked the shortlist.

Speaking before the competition began, he said: “The key thing I'll be looking for is the passion for F1, because you have to be a true fan to make the most of this opportunity. It’s going to be hard to give it up and there’s quite a lot of pressure choosing who’s next.”

The competition was open to fans aged 25 or over, with entrants asked to name their favourite team and driver and select who they would take to a future race from a list of options provided by F1 and Heineken.

Fifty entrants were then selected at random and invited to submit a 90-second video on why they should become the next ticket holder – and the final six videos are now available to watch, so fans can determine who should win the adventure of a lifetime.

Meet the final six and decide who you would like to see crowned the 2027 Heineken F1 Season Ticket holder - click here!

Sports.title: Camara over Ocon - did Haas make the correct call for F1 2027?
Sports.content:
Rafael Camara has been announced as a Formula 1 driver for the 2027 season and he will serve as Esteban Ocon’s replacement at Haas.

It will see the 21-year-old Brazilian make his F1 debut after such a rapid rise through the junior formulae.

Camara won the 2024 Formula Regional European Championship and the 2025 Formula 3 title, following that up by currently leading the Formula 2 standings by seven points.

But he is still such a raw talent as opposed to the experience and race-winning know-how of Ocon, who has endured a tough time since joining Haas at the start of 2025.

So has the American outfit made the right move? Our writers have their say.

Raw speed makes Camara a great pick

Rafael Camara, Invicta Racing Photo by: Dom Gibbons / Formula 1 via Getty Images

As the saying goes, you can make a quick driver reliable, but you can’t make a reliable driver quick.

Camara is one of the fastest drivers from the past decade in junior formulae; his qualifying record speaks for him. He took seven poles, more than anyone, on his way to the 2024 Formula Regional European Championship title; his 2025 F3 record was five poles out of nine, which is unprecedented in the current era. You’d have to go back to Luca Ghiotto’s identical feat, in the 2015 GP3 season, to find similar performance. And yet, in perhaps the most competitive title fight ever at that level, Ghiotto had narrowly lost out to Ocon in the title race.

Fast-forward 11 years, and Ocon is losing his Haas seat to Camara. Are the Frenchman’s results this season representative of his actual performance? Probably not, with the VF-26’s infamous inconsistency issue plaguing him for a long time. But it perhaps took a toll on the atmosphere within the team as frustration grew, and in that case, making a change made sense – especially with someone like Camara available.

The Brazilian has it all: backing from Haas supplier Ferrari – just like expected future Haas team-mate Oliver Bearman – obvious pace and potential back-to-back titles in FREC, F3 and F2. The Invicta racer currently leads the standings in F1’s feeder series, with five pole positions out of 13. Nobody else has taken more than two.

Of course, there have been mistakes, like his lock-up into retirement as he fought title rival Nikola Tsolov for victory in Monaco, but Camara has still taken consistent points finishes and commanding feature race wins.

Haas will miss Ocon’s experience, but Bearman can grow into the team leader role, and the decision makes sense to prepare for the future.

- Ben Vinel

Why remove a grand prix winner for a rookie?

Ocon after winning the 2021 Hungarian GP Photo by: Dan Istitene / Getty Images

Ocon was quite frank about it: he doesn't deserve this shit, he said, to be precise. And to be just as frank, I see no reason to disagree with him.

Yes, the numbers usually don't lie. And Ocon, despite being the more experienced driver, with every right to be considered a team leader, has scored fewer points so far than Bearman.

But is that really a case of him underdelivering?

Ayao Komatsu has admitted there have been issues with the car's inconsistency, and if you believe Ocon, he's only had a handful of races in which he's been able to have a proper go at it. And the last few rounds certainly suggest that, even if he's not better than Bearman, he's at least on a par with him.

Throughout its history, Haas has benefited greatly from having drivers with a wealth of experience. The likes of Romain Grosjean and Kevin Magnussen helped develop it into a credible team – and it has also failed spectacularly with rookies in the past. The choice to go with Mick Schumacher and Nikita Mazepin back in the day was a matter of survival, given the financial backing both brought. But does Haas really need to go for a rookie driver now? There's no reason to believe so.

So it appears that the Brazilian has been chosen by Haas on sporting grounds, but I can't see how he can be better right now than a proven race winner. Unless there's simply too much pressure from Ferrari to take on another junior from its Academy, I can't see Camara scoring more points for the team straight away than Ocon, with all his experience.

Ocon is still fast and reliable when the car works as it should. So why make the change? Especially if it's for another driver who can be taken away whenever Ferrari needs him.

How can you build your future around drivers who are basically on loan from a bigger team? I thought the Ocon and Bearman combination made perfect sense in that regard, as the Frenchman was the team's own driver. Now Haas gives more of an impression of becoming a Ferrari junior team rather than an independent outfit.

All of that, of course, becomes irrelevant if Komatsu has seen something absolutely special from Camara during these TPC tests – and given how Bearman has turned out, you'd argue Ayao knows what he's doing.

But still, there's a feeling that Ocon has been hard done by the team – which has almost used its underperforming car as an excuse to get rid of him.

- Oleg Karpov

This is the chance for Haas to sign a potential generational talent

Rafael Camara, Invicta Racing Photo by: Dom Gibbons / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Over recent rounds it’s been hard to feel anything but sympathy for Ocon, watching him deliver such outlandish statements in a clear desperate plea to stay on the grid. Would he have been saying such things if he weren’t up against it? No. It was clearly a tactic from him to remind people of what he’s done in the past, knowing the jury was very much out.

But like it or not, a lot of what he said was actually true. Ocon did cap off a solid junior career by winning GP3 - beating Max Verstappen in European F3 in the process - and more than held his own for a decade in F1.

His very impressive first full season in 2017 mustn’t be forgotten, scoring points in every round bar two for Force India, nor should the fact that he came very close to a career-changing move to Mercedes during its dominant years. There’s also his win at Hungary, 2021, as well as the fact that he’s one of only two drivers - Jenson Button the other - to outscore Fernando Alonso in a season as team-mates - 92 to 81 in 2022.

It is hoped that the above facts are what Ocon will be remembered for, and not his two seasons with Haas. Similarly, Daniel Ricciardo should mostly be remembered for everything but his decline at the end.

Yet there is another fact - or opinion - that mustn’t be ignored: it is time for Ocon to leave. Although results have improved of late, how much of that is down to the 30-year-old knowing he has a point to prove and a job on the line? Haas just isn’t going to get much better with the Frenchman behind the wheel, but it just might with such an exciting youngster in Camara.

Oleg talks about age and experience, but the 2026 champion-in-waiting - Kimi Antonelli - started the season as a teenager. So is that really as important in this day and age? Camara is also the same age as Bearman, and his junior record speaks for itself.

If he becomes F2 champion, he will join Charles Leclerc, George Russell, Oscar Piastri and fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto to win that and F3 as rookies. Camara will also become the only driver to win those two and FREC in consecutive seasons.

These are all the statistics of a future frontrunner and when one considers the 21-year-old’s speed as outlined by Ben, he is already F1-level. There’s no reason to believe he won’t be fighting for wins and titles in 10 years time. A chance for Haas to sign such a driver may not arise again, so this is an opportunity it must pounce on, and fair play for doing so.

- Ed Hardy

Sports.title: Camara to make F1 debut as Ocon's replacement at Haas in 2027
Sports.content:
Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas in 2027 and is expected to line up alongside Oliver Bearman.

The 21-year-old Brazilian is replacing Esteban Ocon who will leave the American outfit at the end of 2026 after two disappointing seasons, his departure being confirmed on 30 September.

Camara has enjoyed a rapid rise through the junior ranks by winning the 2024 Formula Regional European Championship title and 2025 F3 crown, both done in dominant fashion.

So if he clinches the F2 championship for Invicta - he currently leads Nikola Tsolov by seven points - he will become the only driver to have won FRECA, F3 and F2 in consecutive seasons.

“I’m very happy to be joining TGR Haas F1 Team as a Formula 1 driver,” said Camara, who has signed a “multi-year” deal.

“It’s an important step in my career and I want to thank Gene Haas and Ayao Komatsu for the trust they have placed in me.

Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team, Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

“I’m also very grateful to the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for their support and for everything they have contributed to my development over the years, as well as to my family for always being there throughout this journey.

“Now my focus is on preparing myself in the best possible way for this new challenge. There will be a lot to learn, and I’m looking forward to working closely with the team, understanding the car and continuing to develop as a driver.”

Although Haas took its time in confirming this decision, it was entirely expected that Camara would be given the seat and triumph over the likes of reigning F2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli and reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa.

All three have taken part in TPC (Testing of Previous Cars) programmes for Haas, the most notable being a three-day test at Portimao in August as part of a plan to evaluate all candidates.

What also would have helped Camara's cause is him being a Ferrari academy graduate - like Bearman - and the Scuderia has a strong relationship with Haas, selling it many car parts like the power unit.

Team boss Ayao Komatsu said: “I’m really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.

Ayao Komatsu, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

“I don’t need to tell everyone about his achievements in the junior formulas, it’s been very impressive, and in his rookie season in Formula 2, the speed he’s shown in some very difficult moments, like qualifying in Monaco and Montreal – that all goes to show the potential Rafa has.

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC programme in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car, he showed us more than just raw speed.

“Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.

“We’re all excited about this opportunity and really committed as TGR Haas F1 Team to nurture this talent and provide a place where he can flourish.

“We want to create an environment where he’s comfortable and supported, where he can really excel in his capabilities.”

This news means there are now just three seats theoretically left available for 2027, two coming at Racing Bulls, but it is expected to retain Liam Lawson and impressive rookie Arvid Lindblad.

The other is the seat alongside Camara, though it is an open secret that that’ll be taken up by Bearman, 21, who has highly impressed since joining as a rookie last year.

Sports.title: Poll: Does F1 needs its cost cap – or is it just holding back the smaller teams? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
The difficulty of creating a level playing field for sporting competitions in a world where teams teams are sold for billions has been highlighted by recent developments in the English football Premier League.

Multiple champions Manchester City were found guilty of cheating the league’s Financial Fair Play rules using sham contracts to hide funding of over £830 million . The league is yet to confirm their penalty and the club intends to appeal.

F1 introduced its equivalent rules, the budget cap, five years ago. No teams has committed a breach on anything like the same scale as that seen in the Premier League. When Red Bull was found to have overspent in the first year under the budget cap, but their £1.864m overspend amounts to just 0.2% of Manchester City’s breach. What’s more, Red Bull’s error was not found to be deliberate, unlike Manchester City’s.

Other breaches have occured, including in the recently-introduced engine cost cap. But these have usually been relatively minor procedural matters, nothing on the scale of Manchester City case, which spanned nine seasons.

But while F1’s budget cap appears to have been enforced effectively, is it having a positive effect on the championship?

Some of F1’s smaller teams said they would not have been able to continue without it. However others have expressed concerns the spending limit has created a “cost cap trap”.

Williams team principal James Vowles described the problem recently. “When we did the cost cap, this is way back [during] Covid, when we had a phone call about it, there were three key tasks that we wanted out of it,” he explained.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We wanted long-term financial sustainability, and I think in that goal, not just have we achieved it, but we’ve exceeded it. This business now has good investment that allows us to go on, and they’re businesses. They weren’t businesses before 2021 at all.

“The two others, though, that went with it were sporting equity and, effectively, compression of the field, so effectively competitiveness that compressed together. Those are the three goals of cost cap, and those two have failed.”

Vowles said the data shows the leading four teams are in a strong position under the cost cap. “If I take the last five years of the sport, the five that we’ve been in as cost cap right now, currently the top four teams score 83% of the points. Before that it was in the seventies, just to be clear about it.

“In other words, we have made the situation worse, where the top four are the top four and all the rest of us are fighting over, ballpark, 17% of the points.”

According to Vowles, the chasing teams can’t catch up because the cost cap effectively cements their disadvantage. “When you’re in a cost cap, I’m not spending money on the car. I’m spending millions, tens of millions actually, just on basic systems, so you just know where a part is in the factory. So that’s not going to the car, it’s not going to a front wing, it’s not going to an upgrade. It’s going on systems that I need to do just to do the very basics.

“So, we’re caught in a cost cap trap, because if I do anything short-term – and I always talk about investing in the future, now you understand why – if I do anything that’s about this year, I will slow myself down in the future, and I can’t do that.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have a two-tier championship. That’s not me telling you that. That is just what is on the table right now in terms of points score.”

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem indicated his dissatisfaction with the cost cap last year. “I’m looking at the cost cap and it’s just giving the FIA a headache,” he said. “So what’s the point of it? I don’t see the point.”

Does F1’s cost cap still have a point? Is it protecting the smaller teams from collapse or holding them back from competing with the front runners? And could what happened with Manchester City ever happen in F1?

Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: On this day: Wheldon killed in IndyCar horror crash at Las Vegas finale | Briefs
Sports.content:
IndyCar champion and Indianapolis 500 winner Dan Wheldon lost his life in a horrific crash in the season finale at Las Vegas 15 years ago today.

Running in the middle of a 34-car pack on the Las Vegas Motor Speedway, Wheldon was caught up in a multi-car accident and launched into the fencing on the outside of the oval. IndyCar has not returned to the speedway since.

Wheldon’s wife Susie gave birth to their second son earlier that year. Both their sons went into racing and the eldest, Sebastian, will compete in Formula 3 next year.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

Sports.title: On This Day: Stroll wins final race before becoming a Formula 1 driver | Brief
Sports.content:
10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

For his last race at Prema, Stroll lined up fourth on the grid behind Joel Eriksson, Jake Hughes and Callum Ilott. Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Anthoine Hubert, who tragically died in a Formula 2 crash in 2019, lined up seventh.

Sports.title: F1 could make call to move finale to Imola as late as ‘mid-November’ – report | Briefs
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

It comes after missile strikes hit an airport in nearby Saudi Arabia, whose world championship round was cancelled earlier this year. F1 is due to return to the country in March next year.

Sports.title: Official: Camara to make Formula 1 debut with Haas in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas next season.

Haas, one of Ferrari’s customer teams, confirmed the 21-year-old will take the seat vacated by Esteban Ocon at the end of the year. He is expected to partner Oliver Bearman, another member of Ferrari’s driver academy, who has driven for Haas since last year.

Camara has enjoyed a stellar rise through the junior formula series since being picked up by Ferrari in 2022. He currently leads the Formula 2 championship standings, with no indication yet whether the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will be able to go ahead.

Like fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto, Camara won the Formula 3 championship at his first attempt. He also won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before.

Camara has already experienced one of Haas’s Formula 1 chassis in a Test of Previous Cars at the Autodromo do Algarve, which will hold the Portuguese Grand Prix next year. He has also tested for Ferrari.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said he is “really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.”

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car,” Komatsu continued, “he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.”

Camara thanked Komatsu, Haas team owner Gene Haas and the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for his chance to make his F1 debut.

Sports.title: Colapinto tells his supporters to stop abusing rival drivers: “They don’t help me” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has urged his supporters to stop abusing his rivals and others involved in the series online.

“They are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite,” Colapinto told his followers in a video posted on social media.

The FIA and Alpine issued statements in the last two months condemning the abuse which occured following the Dutch, Spanish and Azerbaijan grands prix. Neither specifically mentioned Colapinto’s supporters but both identified the victims of the abuse, including his team mate Pierre Gasly and FIA officials. “It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned,” said Alpine in a statement last month.

Colapinto told his supporters the online abuse must stop.

“I know it makes you feel very proud when I do well, when I get points, me and the whole team, and I will always be very grateful for that,” he said. “But there are times when we end up attacking other pilots, other colleagues, my team mates, my mechanics, my engineers, people I work with day by day.

“I know they are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite. They don’t help me. And I really want you to understand that this is what we have to change, all together.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have to try to improve as a society, and to help me have a better performance, to help get my dream and my results, that is, to score points, I need you to help stop this, all of us together.”

Colapinto made his F1 debut with Williams in the second half of 2024, but the team had no space for him in their line-up for the following season. He joined Alpine, who promoted him to a race seat in place of Jack Doohan early in the season. Doohan later revealed he received death threats from those who wanted him out of the car.

Alpine issued the first in a series of reactions to abuse from Colapinto’s supporters this year following the Chinese Grand Prix, when Esteban Ocon collided with him. Some Colapinto supporters also accused Alpine of sabotaging Colapinto and failing to provide him with the same equipment as Gasly.

Recent flashpoints included the penalties Colapinto received for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags at Zandvoort, Colapinto’s brief delay behind Gasly at the Madring and the collision between the Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in Baku.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford, Tim Bradley Challenge Fundora Stoppage
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s last-second stoppage of Ermal Hadribeaj drew objections during a post-fight discussion involving Terence Crawford and Tim Bradley, while Dan Rafael called for the result to be changed to a decision.

Hadribeaj appeared able to continue when the referee halted Saturday’s fight in Las Vegas. The unusual ending put a cloud over Fundora’s WBC junior middleweight title defense, with the dispute focused on Hadribeaj beating the count after the final bell had already sounded.

“All he had to do was get on his feet,” came one objection during the discussion involving Crawford, Bradley and the referee.

The referee defended his intervention by pointing to Hadribeaj falling back into the ropes and arguing that another attack would have left him in trouble.

“If there’s five seconds left, that guy gets destroyed,” he said.

But those five seconds did not exist. That is the problem with using a possible follow-up attack to justify the stoppage. Hadribeaj had no more fighting left to do if he had beaten the count after the final bell.

Rafael made that argument forcefully on X, urging Hadribeaj’s team to protest to the Nevada State Athletic Commission.

“HE BEAT THE COUNT and the bell had already rung,” Rafael said. “Won’t be surprised at all if the NSAC changes the result to a unanimous decision.”

That was Rafael’s expectation, rather than an announced commission action. Still, his criticism gives Hadribeaj’s team a specific issue to raise: whether the referee improperly extended the process beyond the completed count when the fight had already ended.

This is about dollars and cents, not just hurt feelings. Getting tagged with an illegitimate knockout loss hurts Hadribeaj’s marketability and ruins his leverage for future paydays. Fundora keeps his win on the cards anyway, but the commission needs to step in, overturn the bogus stoppage, and take an undeserved KO loss off Hadribeaj’s record.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Tells Moses Itauma: “No Time For Crying”
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic is having a grand time talking down to Moses Itauma. As the young heavyweight mopes over his first defeat and fixates on replays, Hrgovic delivered a blunt reality check: stop crying, get back in the gym, and figure out how to win when your opponent refuses to fall over.

Itauma admitted this week that rewatching the bout eats away at him. He landed his best artillery, watched Hrgovic walk straight through it, and kept winging power shots until his gas tank emptied completely. He sounds like a fighter in denial, still convinced the knockout was right there if he had just thrown a little harder.

Hrgovic responded with dripping condescension, offering to comfort the 21-year-old prospect like a disappointed toddler.

“I’ll tell him, ‘Look, Moses, everything will be good,'” Hrgovic told The Stomping Ground. “I will cuddle him … on the head, like, ‘Moses, everything will be good. Don’t be upset.'”

The mocking humor carried an unforgiving point. Hrgovic pointed out that a loss should light a fire under a fighter rather than shatter his nerve, before making sure to remind everyone who dismantled the hype train.

“You must learn from that that you can’t knock out Filip Hrgovic,” he said. “You must learn you can’t knock out everyone. You must be ready for a 12-round fight.”

That diagnosis is right on the money. Itauma got exposed by his own reliance on early blowouts. Once his power failed to create a shortcut, he had no Plan B, frantically emptying his reserves against an immovable target walking him down.

Surviving at the top level means knowing how to bank rounds without punching yourself into exhaustion. Itauma needs to accept that durable heavyweights will absorb his Sunday punch and keep coming.

Hrgovic threw in obligatory compliments about Itauma’s raw speed, but the core message was pure dismissal.

“No time for crying. Go back to the gym, and that’s it, man. Simple.”

Staring at the tape will not undo the beating. Itauma either learns how to box when the stoppage vanishes, or the next seasoned heavyweight will run the exact same script on him.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II – FIGHT REVIEW
Sports.content:
This past Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, England, in a championship rematch that was available live worldwide on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois made an emphatic statement, stopping former titleholder Fabio Wardley in the 2nd round to successfully retain his championship.

Get DAZN Ultimate Tier HERE

The heavyweight division has been in total chaos ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts, leaving the rest of the division battling for supremacy in a wide-open landscape. Entering the night, the big question was whether Wardley could make the necessary pacing adjustments after dropping Dubois twice early before being stopped in the 11th round of their first encounter five months ago. Instead, Dubois erased all doubt immediately and authored a destructive blowout.

Rather than another back-and-forth war of attrition, Dubois completely flipped the script from their first clash right out of the gate. In the opening seconds of round 1, Dubois caught Wardley flush with a booming shot that dropped the challenger hard to the canvas. Wardley beat the count, but he remained on unsteady legs for the rest of the frame. Staying cool, calm, and composed, Dubois patiently picked his spots and battered Wardley mercilessly before the bell.

Wardley came out for the 2nd round trying to establish his footing and survive the storm, but Dubois was completely dialed in. Stalking his hurt rival with authority, Dubois unleashed another heavy barrage of clubbing shots traps along the ropes, prompting Wardley’s corner to mercifully throw in the towel to save their fighter from further punishment.

This edition of Rummy’s Corner provides a full recap and post-fight review of Dubois’s dominant title defense, while exploring what could be next in the heavyweight division. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: “The Towering Inferno” Fundora Stops Hadribeaj in Final Round
Sports.content:
WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora stopped Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the twelfth and final round of an action-packed but often sloppy fight at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas, Nevada.

Promoters Tom Brown of TGB Promotions and Sampson Lewkowicz of Sampson Boxing presented the card Saturday on DAZN and TNT.

In the main event, southpaw Fundora, 25-1-1 (17 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped fellow southpaw Hadribeaj, 23-1-1 (8 KOs), of Tirana, Albania, and Miami Beach, Florida, at 2:59 of the final round.

In the second round, Fundora used his considerable height advantage to hurt Hadribeaj early. The challenger fought back and had Fundora in trouble near the end of the round. In the third, referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point from Hadribeaj for excessive holding.

There was nonstop action from the fourth through the tenth as Hadribeaj forced his way inside and Fundora answered with short punches. The challenger made it competitive, although Fundora held an overall edge and increasingly found success with his body attack.

In the eleventh round, Taylor deducted another point from Hadribeaj for holding. Despite his height disadvantage, the challenger continued trying to force the fight at close range.

In the closing seconds of the twelfth, Fundora dropped Hadribeaj with a left hand. Hadribeaj beat the count but was in no condition to continue, prompting Taylor to wave it off with one second remaining.

In the co-main event, former WBA super middleweight champion Armando “Toro” Resendiz, 17-3 (11 KOs), of Guayabitos, Mexico, defeated Koen Mazoudier, 16-5-1 (6 KOs), of Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, by unanimous decision over ten action-packed rounds.

Resendiz rocked Mazoudier with a right hand to the chin in the final seconds of the fourth round, knocking him off balance. From the sixth through the ninth, Mazoudier pressed the action and fought his way back into the contest, giving the crowd plenty to cheer about while Resendiz continued landing the heavier punches.

In the final minute of the tenth, Resendiz hurt Mazoudier with a flurry of unanswered shots. The Australian survived to hear the final bell.

The scores were 98-92 and 97-93 twice. Harvey Dock was the referee.

In an eight-round super middleweight bout, Jaime Osuna, 12-0 (5 KOs), of Guerrero Negro, Baja California Sur, Mexico, won a majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi, 13-1-1 (5 KOs), of Palermo, Italy, and Brooklyn, New York.

Osuna suffered a cut over his right eye from a left hook in the third round, which Cangelosi took with his cleaner work.

In the fifth, Osuna rocked Cangelosi early as the fight developed into a slugfest. Cangelosi answered in the seventh, catching Osuna with a right hand to the chin in the closing seconds.

Both had their moments in the eighth and final round, fighting hard with the result still in doubt.

Two judges scored it 77-75 for Osuna, while the third had it even at 76-76. Robert Hoyle was the referee.

Super middleweight Marco “El Tiburon” Romero, 16-0 (14 KOs), of Olathe, Kansas, stopped Matias Ferreira, 8-4 (3 KOs), of Rosario, Uruguay, at 1:54 of the first round of their scheduled eight-round bout.

Ferreira landed a left hook midway through the opening round, but Romero countered with a right hand to the chin that dropped him onto the seat of his trunks. Referee Tony Weeks stopped the contest following the knockdown.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

The scheduled bout between Brandon Figueroa and Tomoki Kameda was canceled after Figueroa became ill following his weight cut. Figueroa was also stripped of his WBA featherweight title after failing to make the division limit.

Sports.title: Ennis vs. Kelly Winner Targeted By Sebastian Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the Jaron Ennis–Josh Kelly winner next, but a potential Ennis fight comes with a financial obstacle: promoter Sampson Lewkowicz’s demand for a 50-50 purse split.

Fundora called for undisputed after stopping Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round. The WBC junior middleweight champion sounded ready to pursue the other belts, although agreeing on an opponent is only part of getting a unification made.

“Absolutely, let’s go for undisputed,” Fundora told DAZN when asked about facing the Ennis–Kelly winner. “We will break them down like we broke this guy, like the guy before that, before that, and before. We’ll keep breaking these guys down.”

Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) had just completed his fourth successful title defense, wearing down Hadribeaj with short punches and sustained body work before dropping him with a left hand at 2:59 of the final round.

That performance supported his description of breaking opponents down. Hadribeaj made the early rounds competitive by crowding Fundora, but the champion gradually took over through his greater activity inside.

Getting Ennis into the ring could require a different kind of patience. Lewkowicz has called for an equal split for Fundora against Ennis, leaving the financial terms as something the camps would have to resolve if Ennis beats Kelly.

There is no agreement established by Fundora’s post-fight comments, nor do they show that Ennis has accepted or rejected those terms. The potential obstacle is whether an equal split becomes a firm condition or a starting position in negotiations.

Fundora has made his preference clear. If Ennis wins, the next question will be whether the promoters can find a price both sides accept and turn that undisputed ambition into a scheduled fight.

Tonight’s showing only hurts Fundora’s negotiating position. Needing until the final second of the twelfth round to finish a gritty but limited challenger like Hadribeaj showed the exact vulnerabilities that have always followed Fundora. He surrenders his 6’6″ frame, stays glued in the pocket, eats clean shots on the inside, and relies strictly on outlasting foes in a war of attrition.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Stops Ermal Hadribeaj With One Second Left
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora stopped Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round, finishing a physically taxing fight with a left hand after gradually wearing down the challenger with body punches and a higher work rate.

The victory gave Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) his fourth successful defense of the WBC junior middleweight title on Saturday night at The Chelsea at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs) suffered his first defeat after making the champion work considerably harder than his heavy favorite status suggested.

Hadribeaj had little interest in remaining at the end of Fundora’s punches. The challenger stayed low, moved inside and landed hard shots, forcing the taller champion into a fight where his height and reach offered fewer benefits.

A long left hand buzzed Hadribeaj in the second round, but he recovered quickly and returned to pressing the action. Referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point for holding in the third, adding an early cost to the challenger’s attempts to crowd and smother Fundora.

The inside fighting remained competitive through the middle rounds. Hadribeaj landed some of the heavier individual punches, while Fundora answered with more frequent short shots and uppercuts.

Fundora’s body attack became increasingly effective as the fight progressed. Rather than consistently creating distance, he found room to punch where Hadribeaj wanted to fight, digging downstairs and keeping his hands moving.

That made the challenger’s approach harder to sustain. Getting close no longer prevented Fundora from scoring, and Hadribeaj increasingly held as the champion continued working.

Taylor took another point from Hadribeaj in the 11th. By then, Fundora was producing the cleaner, more consistent offense, leaving the challenger needing a dramatic finish.

The decisive punch came from the champion instead. Fundora maintained his pressure in the final round before a left hand dropped Hadribeaj and ended the fight at 2:59.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Super middleweight Armando Resendiz (17-3, 11 KOs) defeated Koen Mazoudier (16-5-1, 6 KOs) by a 10-round unanimous decision in a hard-fought fight. The judges scored it 98-92, 97-93 and 97-93, giving Resendiz a wider victory than the competitive action suggested.

Mazoudier kept coming forward and throwing, making Resendiz work at close range and enjoying success through the middle rounds. Resendiz answered with the heavier punches, hurting the Australian with right hands and left hooks as the two traded throughout.

A sustained attack in the final round left Mazoudier reeling and close to being stopped, but he survived and continued firing back until the bell. Resendiz earned his first victory since losing to Jaime Munguia, while Mazoudier made him fight for it in his U.S. debut.

Marco Romero (16-0, 14 KOs) stopped Braulio Matias Ferreira (8-4, 3 KOs) in the first round of their scheduled eight-round super middleweight fight. The 20-year-old Romero immediately pressed the attack, digging to the body and landing right hands upstairs at close range.

A right hand and left hook to the body helped set up a sweeping right to the chin that dropped Ferreira hard into the ropes. Ferreira beat the count, but he was in no condition to continue, prompting the referee to stop the fight. Romero gave the veteran little chance to settle, keeping him under attack throughout the brief contest. It was the Kansas prospect’s third consecutive first-round stoppage.

Super middleweight Jaime Enrique Osuna Diaz (12-0, 5 KOs) kept his unbeaten record with an eight-round majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi (13-1-1, 5 KOs). The judges scored the competitive bout 77-75, 77-75 and 76-76 on the Sebastian Fundora–Ermal Hadribeaj undercard.

Osuna applied pressure from the start, using his activity and body punching to make Cangelosi work. His best round came in the fifth, when he hurt Cangelosi twice with straight right hands but crowded his own punches while trying to finish.

Cangelosi fought back and had a strong seventh round, landing a big shot to keep the outcome in doubt heading into the eighth. Neither fighter scored a knockdown, with Osuna’s pressure and cleaner work in key stretches earning him the narrow victory.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Underestimates Christian Mbilli’s Threat To Canelo
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford calls Christian Mbilli “tailor-made” for Canelo Alvarez, but that description overlooks what sustained pressure could do to a fighter who increasingly needs breaks between attacks.

Mbilli gives opponents opportunities to hit him. He also keeps punching after they land. Canelo could find the uppercuts and hooks he wants and still struggle if those shots don’t slow the younger fighter down.

“He can’t do nothing but press Canelo,” Crawford told TNT Sports. “I don’t see him beating Canelo in a boxing match. I think his best success is letting his hands go, roughing Canelo up and making it a dogfight.”

That approach is precisely what makes Mbilli dangerous. Canelo’s output has dropped during stretches of recent fights, leaving him throwing isolated power shots while opponents have opportunities to collect points through activity. Against Mbilli, taking a breather could mean absorbing another combination.

Crawford also has something to gain from Canelo winning. It protects the value of his victory over the Mexican star last year and preserves whatever possibility remains of a rematch. A one-sided Mbilli win would invite an uncomfortable question about how much Canelo had left when Crawford beat him.

Calling an opponent tailor-made makes sense if the fighter in question possesses the legs, reflexes, and gas tank to punish mistakes all night. The current Alvarez operates in short spurts. He throws one or two eye-catching power counters, tucks into a high guard, and waits. That approach works fine against timid opposition, but it is a terrible blueprint against someone with an engine like Mbilli.

Mbilli gets hit, but he thrives inside the pocket and throws punches in bunches. In the past, Canelo made aggressive brawlers pay with devastating counters that made them hesitate. Now, he lacks the one-punch erase button at 168 pounds to stop a relentless tank in his tracks. If Canelo lands a crisp left hook and Mbilli shakes his head, walks forward, and fires six shots in return, Alvarez gets trapped working when he desperately needs to catch his breath.

If anything, the script has flipped. Canelo is the one who looks tailor-made for high-output, durable fighters who refuse to stand at mid-range admiring his defensive slips. Crawford is banking on nostalgia, but twelve rounds against a live motor like Mbilli exposes stamina issues that reputation alone cannot fix.

Shawn Porter expects Canelo to stop Mbilli with an uppercut or left hooks. Tim Bradley also sees a possible late stoppage. Yet Canelo hasn’t stopped an opponent since Caleb Plant in November 2021. Those predictions require more than identifying punches Mbilli is available for.

Bradley supplied the strongest qualification himself.

“If Canelo punches him and can’t hurt him and can’t get his respect, Mbilli is in the fight,” he said.

That is the risk. Canelo can land the cleaner punches without controlling the pace. If Mbilli walks through a counter and immediately starts punching again, Canelo has to defend and work before he is ready. The openings will be there. Whether Canelo still has the stamina to keep exploiting them is another question.

Ghana News.title: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November in the UK
Ghana News.content:
Online pornography depicting strangulation or incestuous relationships will be banned from early November, the government has announced.

From 6 November, it will be illegal to possess or publish porn which shows strangulation or suffocation, depicts sexual activity between people who are related or shows adults role-playing as children under 16 in England and Wales.

The new rules follow a review into porn regulation in 2025 which found depictions of choking were "rife" on popular porn sites and had helped normalise the act among young people.

Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin, who headed the review, said the news came "not a moment too soon".

She told the Press Association the change in law would "send the unequivocal signal" to companies that host and facilitate porn, and also to wider society, that "extreme and violent content that encourages real-life harm is not acceptable".

Her independent review, commissioned by former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak's government, cited an account of a 14-year-old boy asking a teacher how to choke girls during sex.

It warned that people imitating such behaviour "may face devastating consequences".

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday, Baroness Bertin said porn showing strangulation had "absolutely sort of normalised this kind of sexual violence".

"That has to come to an end and I hope this law change will be the beginning of that," she said - adding that it aimed to "marry up" differences in the law about what was acceptable online and offline.

Non-fatal strangulation is already an offence if someone does not consent, but its depiction online is currently not illegal.

Amendments to the Crime and Policing Bill, which became law in April, sought to ensure such content would be captured by the legislation and made criminal offences in England and Wales.

Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones said it was not about "criminalising harmless sexual preferences".

But she said "porn can shape what people think a healthy relationship looks like, especially young people". Content which "normalises, or even glorifies" violence against women can "blur the line with what is acceptable in real life", she said.

"If you've got this material, delete it. If you're sharing it, stop," Davies-Jones added.

"It's not as harmless as you may think, and after 6 November, it is criminal."

The new offences each carry a maximum penalty of five years' imprisonment, for publication.

According to the government, this could include uploading, posting or otherwise making the content available to someone online.

Possession, meanwhile, could include keeping an image stored on a phone, computer or in cloud storage, the government says.

Someone found to be in possession of images depicting sexual activity involving a person pretending to be under 16 could face up to three years' imprisonment, after 6 November.

Those found to be in possession of images depicting strangulation, suffocation or penetrative sexual activity between certain relatives could face up to two years' imprisonment.

Porn that shows or depicts sex between step or foster-relations where one person is pretending to be under 18 will also be captured by the new offences.

Durham University law professor Clare McGlynn - who has previously warned widely available extreme content normalises sexual violence - welcomed the laws taking full effect.

"This is a potential turning point, the commencement of these laws marking a line in the sand when we decided that we were no longer going to accept the normalisation of sexually violent content in pornography," she told the BBC.

But she said questions remained over how swiftly tech platforms and regulators would act to remove and mitigate the spread of violating material.

"While these are criminal offences, this is not about prosecuting individuals, but transforming the online pornographic landscape and that requires the platforms and regulator to act," Prof McGlynn added.

Ghana News.title: World Cup visa saga: Tribe Culture Fest rejects Sports Minister’s allegation of receiving $611,000 from individuals
Ghana News.content:
Tribe Culture Fest and its Chief Executive Officer, Nana Boateng Gyimah, have denied allegations that the organisation illegally received $611,000 from private individuals and is refusing to refund the money.

At a press conference on Sunday, Mr Gyimah said the allegations attributed to the Minister for Sports and Recreation, Kofi Adams, were not supported by established facts.

He insisted that neither the organisation nor its CEO had received the money from the individuals referenced in the allegations.

“Our position is clear. Tribe did not receive the alleged $611,000 from the private individuals referred to in the public allegation, and we do not enter into personal financial arrangements being attributed to us,” he said.

Mr Gyimah explained that Tribe’s dealings with the National Sports Authority (NSA) and the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) involved institutional and contractual arrangements for specific programmes and activities.

He said the arrangements covered event logistics, travel arrangements, hotel bookings, transportation and security.

According to him, Tribe charged $3,000 and $2,000 as full and final payments for its role in the relevant activities, stressing that the organisation had not received payments directly from individuals seeking assistance to travel abroad.

Mr Gyimah said the arrangements were not personal financial transactions involving people seeking visas to travel to the United States, Canada or Mexico.

He also referred to information that individuals had allegedly paid between $14,000 and $20,000 to persons at the NSA with promises of securing visas, mainly to the United States and Canada.

However, he called for verifiable evidence to establish who made the alleged payments, who received the money, the dates and methods of payment, and the accounts through which the funds were transferred.

He also demanded evidence of any agreements, receipts or acknowledgements linking Tribe Culture Fest or its CEO to the money, as well as the legal or contractual basis for demanding a refund from the organisation.

“These are not unreasonable demands. They are minimum evidentiary requirements for determining responsibility in a matter of this nature,” he said.

Mr Gyimah maintained that any investigation must identify the actual recipients of the funds and establish whether the money was paid to an intermediary and, if so, where it ultimately went.

“If a claim is made that Tribe received or must refund a particular amount, the evidence should establish the basis for that claim,” he added.

The denial follows allegations concerning the $611,000 and the question of whether the organisation is required to refund the amount. Tribe Culture Fest insists that it did not receive the money from the private individuals in question.

Ghana News.title: Tensions flare again in Paris as France counts cost of worst unrest in years
Ghana News.content:
Fresh clashes broke out in Paris on Sunday a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in ‌years, with protests over high prices leaving one demonstrator dead, thousands arrested and shops across the country looted or damaged.

Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.

One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris. Police made more than 2,000 arrests across France, while more than ​600 officers were injured, the interior minister said.

"It's like a war zone here," said Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who had come to Paris with his children ​to visit a friend and said the protests forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique, a trouble hotspot on ⁠Saturday.

Police again fired tear gas towards protesters at Place de la Republique and bikes were set on fire on Sunday afternoon, a sign that tensions had not fully subsided ​in the capital.

More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities on Saturday, marking the convergence of a month-long student movement with broader social discontent against rising living costs ​and declining public services.

President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8 p.m. local time (1800 GMT) on Sunday, his office said.

Saturday's unrest laid bare the deep anger at Macron, who leaves office in 2027 after a decade in power that has increasingly become defined by social discontent, a weak economy and ballooning debt.

The government has blamed the violence on hard-left and ultra-left groups, as well as criminals who it said ​instigated the looting.

French far-right leader Jordan Bardella said France had been "humiliated" and called on Macron to step down.

"What we are paying for is decades of laxity, a loss of ​authority, and the moral, psychological, and material disarmament of our internal security forces," he said as he was visiting a police station in Paris.

SEVERAL HUNDRED SHOPS DAMAGED

While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe ‌groups targeted ⁠public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets, and attacked police vehicles and officers.

A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said several hundred shops had been damaged on Saturday.

In Limoges, southwestern France, Mayor Guillaume Guerin denounced the chaos after the city's 143-year-old town hall was set ablaze and largely destroyed in an arson attack on Saturday, drawing comparisons to the ​2019 fire that devastated Paris's Notre-Dame Cathedral.

"There was ​a clear, premeditated intention to burn ⁠down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the funds needed to repair the town hall.

PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION TO TAKE PLACE NEXT YEAR

The unrest has increased pressure on President Macron ​and his government ahead of a presidential election due next year. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals.

Economy ​Minister Roland Lescure pledged ⁠support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.

Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses impacted by the violence.

French retailer ⁠Carrefour's CEO Alexandre ​Bompard told French broadcaster BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged, including 20 that were ​looted, with losses from the damage running into the tens of millions of euros.

The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts ​and the rising cost of living.

Ghana News.title: Mahama must outline his long-term economic transformation roadmap to Ghanaians – Prof Stephen Adei
Ghana News.content:
Former Rector of the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), Professor Stephen Adei, has urged President John Mahama to outline a clear long-term economic transformation roadmap, warning that the country must not settle for economic stability without a plan for sustained development.

He said although it would be unfair to judge a government less than two years into its term on the transformation of the economy, President Mahama should now set out his vision for Ghana’s future beyond the current stabilisation efforts.

“It will be unfair to judge a government less than two years old when it comes to transformation of the economy, but President Mahama should now tell the Ghanaians his envisaged roadmap, not because we will allow him for a second term, but at least he should leave us with a roadmap of stability, and I think that it can be one of his biggest legacies,” he said.

Prof Adei was speaking at the 37th CIMG Annual National Marketing Performance Awards at the Labadi Beach Hotel on Saturday, October 17, 2026, under the theme, “Brand Ghana Reimagined: Trust, Innovation and Growth in the AI Economy.”

He said the foundations laid during the government’s first two years should be used to drive broader economic transformation rather than be lost through a return to the economic difficulties Ghana has experienced in the past.

Prof Adei also expressed concern about the possibility of fiscal pressures building up ahead of the 2028 general elections, noting that Ghana had historically experienced increased government spending during election years.

He said the country needed to avoid a repeat of that pattern to protect the progress made in stabilising the economy.

“We hope that history will not repeat itself, and it will be one of the president's legacies not to allow it to happen,” he said.

However, he identified several factors that could help limit election-year fiscal pressures, including Ghana’s participation in the International Monetary Fund’s 36-month Policy Coordination Instrument, the government’s reserve accumulation policy and the debt restructuring completed in 2024 and 2025.

According to him, the IMF arrangement could help keep fiscal performance under regular review, while stronger reserves could provide a buffer against economic pressures.

He added that the debt restructuring had extended debt maturities, reducing the government’s immediate financing pressures.

Prof Adei expressed hope that these measures would help Ghana achieve a more stable economic environment during the 2028 election year than in previous election cycles.

He also called for a long-term national development plan, referring to a 40-year development framework on which he said he had worked with his predecessor as chairpersons of the National Development Planning Commission.

“I’m waiting for the 40-year plan, which is now about 35 left, which my predecessor and myself worked on as chairpersons of the National Development Planning Commission,” he said.

He described the current period as an opportunity to establish a lasting direction for Ghana’s development and urged the government to ensure that the gains from economic stabilisation were not squandered.

“History will not forgive it if we again go into another crisis. Let us truly reset the agenda, and it is possible,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Power deficits, water pollution, unreliable internet threaten 24-hour economy – Prof Stephen Adei
Ghana News.content:
Former Rector of the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), Professor Stephen Adei, has warned that persistent power deficits, water pollution and unreliable internet connectivity could undermine the government’s 24-hour economy initiative.

He said the country’s existing infrastructure and utility challenges must be addressed before the policy can deliver its intended outcomes, particularly in an economy increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence (AI).

“The reality is that if we do not tackle the power deficits, the water pollution, the unreliable internet in an AI economy, you cannot achieve a 24-hour economy,” he said.

Prof Adei was speaking at the 37th CIMG Annual National Marketing Performance Awards at the Labadi Beach Hotel on Saturday, October 17, 2026, under the theme, “Brand Ghana Reimagined: Trust, Innovation and Growth in the AI Economy.”

He acknowledged that the government had begun implementing the 24-hour economy policy, which has been passed into law and is built around eight pillars.

He cited efforts to revive industrial activity in Akosombo and Juapong, as well as the inauguration of some industrial parks, as early signs of implementation.

The initiative, he said, seeks to create jobs and increase capacity utilisation across the economy.

However, he questioned whether some projects being developed under the initiative were adequately equipped to support round-the-clock operations.

Prof Adei said he had seen two proposed 24-hour markets near his village but observed that they did not yet demonstrate the level of activity implied by the concept.

“The fundamentals, in many cases, utilities, do not, at this moment, support an eight-hour economy,” he said, arguing that the country needed to address basic infrastructure constraints before pursuing a full 24-hour operating model.

He urged policymakers to prioritise the underlying requirements for sustained economic activity rather than focus solely on establishing facilities.

“Let's try to learn to walk before we run,” he added.

Prof Adei also acknowledged improvements in the cost of borrowing, crediting the government for a decline in lending rates from about 27 per cent to nearly 16 per cent for some borrowers in good standing.

He cautioned, however, that many businesses and individuals continued to face interest rates in the 20 per cent range, particularly those without access to preferential lending terms.

He said the gap between inflation and interest rates remained a concern because it affected the real cost of borrowing for businesses seeking to invest and expand.

Ghana News.title: Prof Stephen Adei urges Ghanaian businesses to build brands on quality, trust and innovation
Ghana News.content:
Former Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) Rector, Professor Stephen Adei, has urged Ghanaian businesses to build competitive brands on quality, reliability, integrity and innovation to strengthen the country’s reputation in international markets.

He said Ghana’s brand must be built on the consistent value its businesses deliver rather than how the country is perceived globally, stressing that promotion alone would not earn lasting confidence without quality products and reliable services.

Speaking at the 37th CIMG Annual National Marketing Performance Awards at the Labadi Beach Hotel on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Prof Adei said artificial intelligence (AI) was creating new opportunities for businesses to reach consumers, develop products and compete beyond Ghana’s borders.

He noted that small businesses, agribusinesses and manufacturers could use digital tools to access new markets, but cautioned that technology alone would not guarantee success.

“The real opportunity lies in using innovation to create products and services that people need, value, and trust,” he said.

Prof Adei called for a shift from exporting raw materials to developing competitive Ghanaian brands, describing marketing as essential to connecting production with demand and communicating the distinctive value of Ghanaian products and services.

He said trust remained central to sustainable business relationships, even as technology transformed how brands engaged consumers.

“Trust is not just a matter of reputation. It is an economic asset,” he said, explaining that customers remained loyal to brands that kept their promises, investors backed credible businesses, and international buyers relied on suppliers who delivered consistently.

He warned that poor-quality products and broken promises could undermine Ghana’s international reputation, while businesses that maintained standards and honoured contracts helped strengthen confidence in the country.

In an AI-driven marketplace where content could be generated at unprecedented speed, Prof Adei said authenticity, quality assurance and professional integrity must become defining features of Ghanaian businesses.

“We must make authenticity, quality assurance, and professional integrity the defining features of Ghanaian enterprise,” he said.

“That is how we move from promoting brand Ghana to earning confidence in brand Ghana because promotion is not enough if it is not backed by substance.”

He also called for stronger collaboration among industry, professional institutions, educational establishments and government to ensure innovation translates into practical solutions and business growth.

Prof Adei urged the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG) to continue encouraging businesses to regard marketing as a strategic investment rather than a promotional expense.

He said the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), headquartered in Accra, presented opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to access new markets, but warned that market access alone was insufficient to guarantee competitiveness.

Businesses, he said, must invest deliberately in product development, packaging, certification and distribution while competing on quality, effective branding, reliable supply and a clear understanding of customer needs.

He called on the government to create an enabling business environment, businesses to deliver competitive products and services, and marketers to translate that value into trusted brands.

Prof Adei also urged policymakers to recognise marketing as a strategic national asset and strengthen the capacity of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to compete in an AI-enabled economy.

Ghana News.title: Fidel Amakye Owusu warns Ghana against risky new energy deals
Ghana News.content:
Security risk and geopolitics consultant Fidel Amakye Owusu has cautioned Ghana against entering into new energy agreements without carefully assessing the potential long-term risks, warning that large investment commitments could expose the country to challenges that outweigh their immediate benefits.

“No matter how big the bag that firm is carrying in terms of money, it’s risky to do business with. So yes, that money can come as investment, but later you will suffer for that because it might not be as clean as you want it to be. So yes, some investment may be successful, but there are a lot of long-term risks,” he said in an interview with Ismail Akwei.

The chief executive officer of DefSEC Analytics Africa Ltd. said Ghana must weigh the potential benefits of foreign investment against the financial and operational risks, particularly as US sanctions on Russian oil companies raise questions about international commercial relationships.

Africa must strengthen its negotiating position

Fidel Amakye Owusu said Ghana should carefully consider what it stands to gain from joining international groupings, arguing that African countries could achieve more by negotiating collectively rather than approaching major powers individually.

Discussing BRICS, he said the bloc emerged partly from the desire of emerging economies to challenge the dominance of a Western-led global economic system and create a counterweight to established powers.

However, he questioned whether African countries had done enough to build the unity necessary to negotiate on more equal terms with larger economies such as China, India and Russia.

“How has Africa worked towards integrating so that we could have been on this block as a continent rather than as individual countries? Have we tried that?” he asked.

Fidel Amakye Owusu argued that African countries risk perpetuating their unequal position in the global system when they engage powerful economies individually instead of using the continent’s collective economic and demographic weight.

“Why can’t Africa come together and be a member state of BRICS?” he said. “I believe that we’ve not done enough internally. So joining a new organisation as individual states only perpetuates the kind of exploitation that we often face. But if we are going as a continent, our weight is bigger.”

He pointed to Africa’s 54 sovereign states and population of approximately 1.4 billion as potential sources of collective bargaining power.

“When we are together, 54 sovereign states with 1.4 billion population, when we are talking, we are talking with weight,” he said, contrasting that position with the difficulty an individual African country could face when negotiating with economic giants.

Lukoil’s interest raises questions

Lukoil Overseas Ghana Limited holds a 38 per cent participating interest in the Deepwater Tano Cape Three Points block. Pecan Energies holds 50 per cent, the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) holds 10 per cent, and Fueltrade Exploration and Production Limited holds the remaining two per cent, according to Ghana’s Petroleum Register.

The US Treasury designated Lukoil and Rosneft under its Russia sanctions programme in October 2025. Lukoil subsequently pursued the sale of its international assets, raising questions about the future ownership of some of its overseas interests.

Asked about the implications for Ghana’s existing relationship with Lukoil, he said the country should distinguish between agreements already signed and potential new commitments.

“You see, that has to do with pragmatism…Until that expiration date, you are supposed to uphold the sanctity of that deal. You cannot say, well, because of the war in Ukraine, that should stop… It depends on how you protect your interests. If there’s going to be some renegotiation, it depends on you how you can protect your interest,” he said.

Fidel Owusu Amakye said that, based on his understanding, Ghana had not signed new deals with Lukoil since Russia’s war in Ukraine began.

“Ever since the Ukraine war and the sanctions that were imposed, Ghana has not signed any new deal with Lukoil. What we know is what has been there, unless there’s some information that I’m not privy to,” he said.

He warned against entering into new agreements without fully considering the changed circumstances.

“But in terms of if you went ahead to sign new deals, then that means you are just walking into some kind of minefield that could take your legs off,” he added.

Ghana must maximise benefits

Beyond financial and operational risks, he said Ghana should ensure that foreign investment delivers lasting benefits through local employment, skills development and stronger domestic industry.

He pointed to the growing emphasis on resource nationalism across Africa, where governments are seeking to secure greater economic returns from their natural resources.

“Every country is seeking to maximise the benefit from its resources,” he said, adding that global demand for resources had encouraged countries to strengthen their position in negotiations with international investors.

Fidel Amakye Owusu distinguished resource nationalism from nationalisation, arguing that the former should focus on increasing the benefits a country receives from its resources.

“Resource nationalism does not necessarily mean resource nationalisation. Resource nationalisation is quite radical. But resource nationalising means maximising what you get from your resources,” he said.

For Ghana, this means assessing whether energy partnerships create opportunities for Ghanaian businesses, transfer technical expertise and strengthen the country’s ability to manage its own resources.

He also argued that Africa’s natural resources give its countries leverage in negotiations with international partners.

“If you are not going to give me capital, if you are going to support me, I’ll give my resources to who I want to give it to,” he said.

He called for continued democratic oversight and transparency in Ghana’s oil sector, urging authorities to identify and reject investments carrying unacceptable long-term risks before commitments are made.

“We should keep it clean and open so that when some investments are coming in, we think that this has inherent long-term risk, we stop it before it gets there,” he said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
