World.title: Photos: Antigovernment protesters clash with police in Albania’s capital
World.content:
Protesters have clashed with riot police in Albania’s capital, as antigovernment demonstrations escalated into violent unrest.

Demonstrations have shaken Tirana since Tuesday, with thousands of protesters calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down as they rally against poor university conditions, high tuition fees and corruption.

This week’s unrest follows months of antigovernment protests in the Balkan nation, initially prompted by a controversial resort development linked to United States President Donald Trump’s family.

World.title: Manchester United held at Leeds despite improved performance for Carrick
World.content:
Bryan Mbeumo’s goal is not enough to win it for beleaguered United as Dominic Calvert-Lewin levels for Leeds.

Share Manchester United held at Leeds despite improved performance for Carrick on social media

Manchester United ended a turbulent week with a frustrating 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday that does little to ease the pressure on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils travelled to the Yorkshire home of their bitter rivals desperate to find a spark after just two wins in nine games in all competitions this season.

The sense of a growing crisis at the club was exacerbated in midweek by an outburst from defender Lisandro Martinez, who took aim at the United hierarchy after a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The Argentina centre-back said Carrick, in his first full season in charge at Old Trafford, had been left with an under-strength squad after an underwhelming summer transfer window.

The United boss insisted on Friday that the club had “moved on” from the incident and Martinez was named in the starting lineup at Elland Road.

Both teams were fully committed in a feisty start to the match in Leeds but there was little goalmouth action.

The first effort on target came in the 26th minute when United goalkeeper Senne Lammens clawed away a Nico Elvedi header destined for the top corner after bouncing up off the turf.

Bryan Mbeumo, playing as United’s target man, headed wastefully wide a minute later after a fine cross from Youri Tielemans and then shot tamely at Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.

But he finally broke the deadlock in the 35th minute when Tielemans again delivered a low ball from the right which Mbeumo guided into the bottom corner for his fourth Premier League goal of the season.



Martinez went off at half-time as Morocco’s Noussair Mazraoui was brought into the action.

Leeds started strongly after the break and were level in the 51st minute when Dominic Calvert-Lewin controlled the ball on his chest and finished at full stretch after Tarik Muharemovic got his head to the ball following a corner.

The home team were now well on top, largely limiting Carrick’s team to counter-attacks.

The Man United boss made attacking substitutions in the search for a winner, bringing on Mason Mount and Matheus Cunha, but neither team could force a winner.

The point left 20-time English champions Manchester United in 13th place in the table with just one win in seven games while Leeds are seventh.

Brighton stun Crystal Palace with five-star display

Elsewhere on Sunday, Brighton leapfrogged Arsenal into second place, at least temporarily, after humbling Crystal Palace 5-0, including a sensational Diego Gomez effort from the halfway line.

Fabian Hurzeler’s team were three goals up inside 10 minutes after an own goal from Palace defender Jaydee Canvot, Gomez’s spectacular effort and a strike from Yasin Ayari.

Further goals from Charalampos Kostoulas and substitute Jack Hinshelwood in the second half deepened Palace’s pain.

The Gunners, six points behind Manchester City, are in action at Nottingham Forest in the late-afternoon kickoff.

Arsenal need a win to rein in City, who have won all seven of their league games this season.

Enzo Maresca’s men have put together their impressive run despite off-field distractions after the club was charged with multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Bournemouth beat 10-man Sunderland 2-0 with goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson for their first league win of the season.

World.title: EU condemns Israeli settler attack on diplomats in occupied West Bank
World.content:
Share EU condemns Israeli settler attack on diplomats in occupied West Bank on social media

The European Union has condemned an attack by Israeli settlers on a convoy carrying European diplomats in the occupied West Bank and called for action to stop the pogroms.

The 27-member bloc issued its statement on Sunday, the day after masked settlers attacked a visiting delegation near the Palestinian village of Taybeh.

The assault has intensified diplomatic pressure on Israel as attacks on Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest increasingly threaten journalists and foreign visitors accompanying them.

Diplomats from France, Belgium and Poland, along with representatives of the Catholic Church, were visiting the predominantly Christian village east of Ramallah to show support for Palestinian olive growers when masked men attacked them.

They threatened members of the delegation and smashed a window of a Belgian diplomatic vehicle.

Bernard Baudoux, the 78-year-old mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, said he was kicked and beaten, despite wearing the ceremonial sash identifying him as a French official.

“I was thrown to the ground,” Baudoux told the Reuters news agency on Saturday.

The EU said on Sunday it welcomed statements by Israeli officials condemning the attacks but expected “full accountability” and measures to prevent further violence against Palestinians and journalists.

It also called on Israel to respect international law and stop expanding settlements in the occupied territory.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called on Israel on Saturday to arrest those responsible and protect civilians.



Prevot said Belgian personnel were safe, although their vehicle had been damaged.

Poland’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement posted on X on Saturday evening that its diplomats were unharmed and there was no indication they had been specifically targeted.

Warsaw demanded an explanation from Israel and action against the attackers.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the violence on Saturday, describing the perpetrators as rioters and said that police had opened an investigation.

He also criticised the delegation for failing to coordinate its visit with the Israeli military, arguing that advance arrangements could have helped protect the visitors.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said violence against diplomats was unacceptable but questioned whether video circulating online provided enough evidence to establish exactly what happened.

Violence during olive harvest

The diplomatic incident followed another attack on Friday in the village of Abu Falah, near Ramallah. Masked settlers assaulted Palestinians harvesting olives and severely injured US photojournalist Heidi Levine, who was covering the farmers for The Washington Post.

Levine said she was beaten for more than 10 minutes, despite wearing protective clothing identifying her as a journalist.

She suffered broken ribs and underwent surgery on her hand. Her camera, phone and passport were stolen.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters in Maryland on Saturday, urged Israel to crack down on settler pogroms and warned that President Donald Trump did not want another crisis in the West Bank.

In a statement on X on Saturday evening, the US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee described Levine’s assault as a “despicable act of terror” and demanded prosecutions.

The attacks have disrupted an olive harvest that provides income for tens of thousands of Palestinian families.

On Sunday, Israeli settlers cut down 120 olive trees on Palestinian-owned land in the village of Kisan, southeast of Bethlehem, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

Farmers have reported assaults, stolen crops, damaged trees and restrictions preventing them from reaching their land.

The United Nations humanitarian office said last week that nearly 200 settler attacks linked to this year’s harvest had caused casualties or property damage, already exceeding the 185 incidents recorded throughout last year’s season.

World.title: Tirana sees sixth day of violent protests as Albania’s PM refuses to resign
World.content:
At this moment, no one is clear on what tomorrow will bring, says Albanian journalist Lindita Karadaku.

Violent protests have rocked Albania’s capital Tirana for the sixth consecutive day as Prime Minister Edi Rama, who is serving his fourth term, ruled out resigning.

Hundreds of protesters gathered again on Sunday in front of the Ministry of Education, chanting “Rama, resign” in a tense standoff with the police, who later used rubber bullets, water cannons and tear gas to hold back the crowds.

Shops and institutions in the centre of the city have secured their doors and windows with metal shutters, while city workers removed paving stones to prevent their use by protesters.

Lindita Karadaku, a journalist for Albanian news outlet TV Klan, told Al Jazeera on Sunday that it was difficult to see how the unrest could unfold or how long it could last.

“Prime Minister Rama is determined and has made it very clear that he will not resign, but also the young people who are protesting are determined and make it clear that they will not give up so easily,” she said. “At this moment, no one is clear what tomorrow will bring.”

Rama said during a live social media stream on Sunday that “the government is not being challenged” but implied that ongoing unrest in the country might affect Albania’s path towards European Union membership.

“Albanians need to think very clearly,” Rama said. “⁠Do they want this, or do they want the EU?”



Albania is hoping to achieve membership status by 2030.

Key demands

Protesters are demanding better education, more jobs, a stop to alleged ongoing corruption, and Rama’s resignation.

According to local media reports, demonstrators in Tirana were primarily attacking government institutions and the police, including the Ministry of Education building and the area around Rama’s office.

The prime minister, who has been in office since 2013, blamed the involvement of a “foreign hand” for the surge in protests and said his government is doing its best to address corruption.

At the same time, he said that he was ready to listen to the justified demands of students and discuss the costs of education. But he insisted that those responsible for the destruction of property must be held accountable.

According to a Ministry of Health report issued on Sunday morning, 65 people were injured, of which 37 were police officers, while 12 were hospitalised. Since Tuesday, 272 people have been injured in the clashes, including 169 police officers, the ministry said.

Discontent in Albania has been growing for months. The first protests in the country this year were called the “Flamingo Revolution” and began in May. Demonstrators rebelled against the controversial project of a luxury tourist complex in the south of Albania, affiliated with Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

World.title: A timeline of West Bank attacks on Palestinians and foreign officials
World.content:
Settler pogroms have escalated, coinciding with the annual olive harvest season in the occupied West Bank.

Share A timeline of West Bank attacks on Palestinians and foreign officials on social media

European diplomats and officials were attacked on Saturday amid a surge in settler pogroms across the occupied West Bank in recent weeks, coinciding with olive harvest season.

The settler pogroms have escalated just weeks before Israel heads to the polls on October 27.

The European Union (EU) on Sunday condemned settler attacks on European diplomats and Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. A day earlier, a veteran American journalist working for the Washington Post was also brutally attacked.

But this is not the first time Israeli settlers have assaulted foreign officials or prominent Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

Here’s a timeline of some of the recent and past attacks:

October 17, 2026

Israeli settlers assaulted European diplomats, including a French mayor, near the Palestinian village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank.

The delegation was visiting Palestinian olive harvesters on Saturday when the Israeli attackers confronted the group.

In Saturday’s incident, the settlers targeted Belgium’s consul general, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives, Belgian Minister of Foreign Affairs Maxime Prevot said.

“A French mayor was assaulted and a Belgian vehicle damaged,” Prevot said, linking the incident to Israel’s “illegal settlement policy” and pledging to push for further EU sanctions.

Bernard Baudoux, the French mayor who was assaulted, told the AFP news agency the attack suggests that “there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government” towards settler violence.



Video shared by an activist at the scene, Amit Orfali, shows Baudoux leaning against a vehicle while sitting on the dusty ground. Other clips showed young masked men knocking insistently on a driver’s side window and asking for identification, while other masked men carrying sticks advanced in the distance. Orfali said the masked men “threatened to kill us”.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called on Israel to arrest the “extremist settlers” who “violently assaulted” Baudoux, and bring them to justice. “They must urgently halt this criminal violence and guarantee the safety of civilian populations, as they are compelled to do under international law,” he said in a post on X.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office has, however, appeared to question the reports of the attack on the Europeans, saying on X that they are “alleged” and require “compelling evidence”, despite acknowledging that published footage of the incident exists.

“We take positive note of statements by several Israeli representatives who condemned the attacks,” the EU said in a statement on Sunday. “But we expect full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists.”

October 16, 2026

Palestinian farmers harvesting olives and veteran American journalist Heidi Levine, 64, who freelances for the Washington Post, were brutally attacked by settlers.

Levine fell to the ground during the assault before she was set upon, witnesses said. “We looked and saw that there was a journalist … on the ground with people surrounding her, beating her, clubbing her, robbing her, pulling her up, beating her again and kicking her,” Jasper Nathaniel, an independent journalist who witnessed the attack, told Al Jazeera.

Levine later told reporters that her attackers “just kept kicking me and kicking me, like probably 50 times”.

Levine was wearing a protective vest marked “PRESS” on the front and back. Her cameras and phone were taken from her during the assault, the Washington Post reported.

Nathaniel said he and others managed to reach her when the settlers briefly backed away, but she struggled to stand. “She was in very, very bad shape. She couldn’t really get up off the ground,” he said.

As they helped Levine towards paramedics, settlers charged again, throwing more stones, he added. The journalist was eventually taken to a hospital in Ramallah.



Nathaniel said Israeli soldiers arrived after the settler assault and opened fire and used tear gas against Palestinians, shooting a man in the leg. “They do nothing to stop the settlers, and they speed into town and start firing their guns and tear-gassing, and they shoot a Palestinian man in the leg,” he said.

“They’re pointing their guns at the paramedics who are helping him, shoving journalists, including myself,” Nathaniel said, adding that the injured man was eventually taken away in an ambulance.

Wafa, the Palestinian news agency, reported that Israeli forces fired live ammunition and tear gas at Palestinians during the attack. After the soldiers left, Palestinians returned to harvesting their olives, Nathaniel added.

Netanyahu’s office has said the facts around the settler attack “remain unclear”, as it offered a conditional condemnation.

“Serious questions remain”, said a post on the official X account of the prime minister’s office, calling for an investigation to “establish the facts, including who initiated the violence”.

October 6, 2026

Israeli settlers beat Palestinian AFP news agency photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh, 58, with rifle butts near Aqraba, south of Nablus. He suffered bruises to his head and torso and was taken by ambulance to a hospital, according to witnesses, his family and fellow journalists cited by AFP.

AFP photographer John Wessels was with Ashtiyeh when the incident occurred.

The news agency reported that a quadbike had raced towards the journalists and a man had opened live fire.

“At least six other people then rushed towards the AFP journalists, firing guns,” AFP reported. “As Ashtiyeh attempted to enter a car, which was clearly marked ‘Press’, two men jumped on him and beat him repeatedly with the butts of their rifles. ‘I could hear his screams,’ said Wessels, who was also threatened at gunpoint.”

While Ashtiyeh is now conscious in a hospital in Nablus, the assailants have taken his camera equipment, according to his colleague Wessels.

The Israeli military has yet to respond to the AFP news agency.

July 11, 2026

United States Congressional Representative Ro Khanna said he and his tour group were detained by rifle-wielding Israeli settlers during a trip to Palestine.

In a post on X, Khanna had accused the Israeli army of supporting the settlers.

“When the [Israeli army] arrived, they sided with the settlers and continued our detention,” Khanna wrote.

Khanna, a Democrat who is considering running for US president in 2028, told the Reuters news agency that “hoodlums … with machine guns” had detained his group a day earlier. “They block off the road. And then they call the [Israeli military] and the [Israeli military] is on their side,” Khanna said.

He added that the settlers were armed with US-made assault rifles.

In an interview with DRM News, Khanna said his experience in the occupied West Bank and Israel was the “first time” he had “really been acutely aware of being brown”.

“I saw the arrogance in the eyes of those settlers. Twenty-one and 22-year-olds with guns, laughing that they had detained us. The arrogance of those young [Israeli army] soldiers that my tax dollars are funding. Having no respect for the fact that they were detaining Americans,” he added.



The Israeli military disputed Khanna’s version of the events, saying that it “dispersed” civilians who were blocking the road.

Israeli officials have, however, ruled out apologising to Khanna or holding the settlers accountable.

Three months after the incident, on Saturday, October 17, Khanna called Netanyahu a “liar” after his office released an October 16 statement on X saying that “serious questions remain” about “who initiated the violence” and other details of the attack on Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine.

“Netanyahu called me a liar when settlers detained me, along with a NYT photographer, in Zanuta this past July,” Khanna wrote. “Netanyahu, you are the liar with the blood of Palestinian children on your hands.”

November 2025

One Canadian and three Italian activists were injured by illegal Israeli settlers in the Ein ad-Duyuk village in the Jericho governorate in the central West Bank, local sources told the Anadolu news agency.

Anadolu reported that settlers had stormed into a Bedouin community where the activists were residing and then assaulted them. Three activists sustained moderate injuries, while one was critically wounded, the news agency said and added that their passports, phones, and belongings were also taken.

July 2025

Palestinian activist and English teacher Awdah Hathaleen, who contributed to the Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land, was shot and killed on July 28, 2025, in the occupied West Bank village of Umm al-Khair in the Masafer Yatta region.

The beloved 31-year-old activist and father of three fell to the ground as people rushed over to try to help him. Then an ambulance came out of the nearby illegal settlement of Carmel and took him away.

Footage published by Israeli human rights group B’Tselem appears to show the suspect Yinon Levi opening fire on Hathaleen during a confrontation in the village.

Despite the visual evidence and prior sanctions imposed on Levi by both the EU and the United States over past attacks on Palestinians, Israeli authorities released him to house arrest.

US President Donald Trump also removed the penalties against Levi and other settlers accused of extremist violence after assuming office in January 2025.

July 2024

Israeli settlers attacked a group of foreign volunteers helping Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank.

David Hummel, an American-German in the group, told the AFP news agency that eight mainly American volunteers were working with the farmers in an olive grove near the Palestinian village of Qusra when settlers attacked them.

“They started attacking and beating us all with sticks and metal pipes, and they were throwing rocks as well at us,” he said.

“I was attacked on my legs, on my arms and here on my jaw as well and it was … very violent,” he added.

The Israeli army condemned the violence and said its troops were deployed to the scene and had fired warning shots into the air, causing the Israeli settlers to flee the area.

World.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
World.content:
France awoke to scenes of widespread damage on Sunday after a day of riots and demonstrations, with shopfronts shattered, burnt out cars, charred bikes, and piles of glass and debris on the pavements of Paris.

Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful.

They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas.

President Emmanuel Macron was due to address the nation at 20:00 local time on Sunday after what has been described as one of the worst outbreaks of disorder in modern French history.

In Paris, protesters clashed with riot police, who turned tear gas and water cannon on the crowds. During the day, some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles. At least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons.

"It's like we had a war," Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told news agency AFP.

Another resident, Anita GrasIt, said it was "terrifying" to see groups of young people "smashing everything, with total impunity".

The looters were "proudly carrying supermarket baskets filled with goods and laughing about their thefts", Maryse, a woman living nearby who gave only her first name, told the BBC.

Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram. In Lille, a McDonalds was set on fire, police said, and an Apple store in the city was broken into and looted.

World.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
World.content:
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.

The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.

A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week.

Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing.

It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

Ukraine has struck St Petersburg before, though regions closer to Ukraine are threatened more often. The city's oil terminal was last hit in July.

Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight into Sunday.

St Petersburg's governor said 12 apartment buildings and two homes were damaged in the attacks on the city, while Pulkovo Airport was temporarily closed.

He also said mobile internet service disruption was possible.

Social network VK confirmed a drone had targeted its regional data centre, but stressed its services were available "as usual" after users reported outages in the early hours of the morning.

Ozon also confirmed its local logistics centre had been targeted by a drone, sparking a fire.

It said staff were evacuated and no one was injured, and that it was not accepting shipments from sellers at the location "as it is currently serving other operational purposes".

As well as numerous oil facilities across Russia, Ukraine has also mounted strikes aimed at disrupting the Russian economy more broadly. Earlier this month, it launched a series of attacks on Yandex, Russia's largest search engine, that led to service disruptions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have frayed since the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel in the hope of bringing down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war, ahead of the midterm elections.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Trump's decision to temporarily suspend a raft of sanctions against Russia has brought fresh criticism, including from some US Republicans.

However, on Sunday, Zelensky said on Telegram he had had conversations with Trump's top negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

He said their teams are in constant communication and preparing the next diplomatic steps.

Both Russia and Ukraine have been striking one another's energy infrastructure with increasing intensity ahead of the winter, as Moscow's full-scale invasion drags on in its fifth year.

Russia says it hits targets used by Ukraine's military, though the UN noted on Friday that the first two weeks of October had been the deadliest for Ukrainian civilians in years.

Russian strikes on energy facilities have left hundreds of thousands without power, raising concerns about civilians enduring another freezing winter.

Zelensky said on Saturday that tens of thousands of people were still without power. Russia launched nearly 2,700 drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 66 missiles in the past week, most of which were aimed at energy facilities, he said.

World.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
World.content:
Warning: This story contains descriptions of drug-taking from the start and discusses suicide

The few grains of fentanyl sit in the silver foil as a straw, held between Mike's lips, hovers above, with a cigarette lighter below. The 48-year-old army veteran is crouched low in an alleyway in Columbus, Ohio's Linden neighbourhood.

"This drug will damn near make you do anything, unfortunately," he says.

The hit he's smoking cost three or four dollars.

"You can snort too much and you can't take it back. Kind of like a gunshot. Can't call the bullet back," he says.

He burns the foil and inhales. As the opioid takes hold, he grips the fence behind him. He sways as a low moan comes from deep in his throat - he could be humming a tune.

We've spent a few days with Mike - he's been our guide through the neighbourhood's back streets. Everyone seems to know him and he's regarded fondly. He helps out at a local pawn shop and gas station, and that's how he feeds his 20-year-old opioid addiction.

Synthetic opioids are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.

Fentanyl, which is entirely man-made, is 50 to 100 times more powerful than heroin, which is cultivated from poppies. It is now often cut with synthetic tranquillisers, which make reviving overdose victims more difficult. These are homemade threats, where cocktails of synthetics can be made in American basements and bathtubs.

World.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
World.content:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys, while France decried the attack as "appalling". Both called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened, suggesting it was part of a "co-ordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".

It was also condemned by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September.

But Trump issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US national interest, prompting a backlash from US lawmakers. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Trump's order was "an important and truly historic moment", and that the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Since then, Ukraine's president declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The sanctions suspension seemed to add further fuel to the fire.

Zelensky said on Saturday morning that the sanctions "could have helped enormously" and that the law was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end".

He pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities that had caused power cuts in several regions and said: "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine â right before winter."

Zelensky said it was "important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening" on the ground.

World.title: Anti-government protesters battle with police in Albania
World.content:
Demonstrators and riot police fought pitched battles in the centre of Tirana on Saturday for the fifth day in a row.

Masked protesters, many of them high school and university students, hurled rocks and petrol bombs at riot police trying to defend the education ministry, one of the focal points of the protests.

The police responded with water cannon and volleys of tear gas, sending the crowds scattering. There are also reports that rubber bullets were used for the first time.

Protests which began in the summer have grown into a wider anti-government movement, with calls for the prime minister to resign following corruption allegations linked to his administration.

Many of the protesters in central Tirana wore gas masks or face masks, while volunteers handed out syringes of saline eyewash to reduce the pain from the tear gas which billows down the street.

The constant boom of petrol bombs could be heard exploding on Saturday.

During the afternoon, the focus of the protests shifted to the office of Prime Minister Edi Rama on the city's main boulevard.

Here the crowds swelled to far larger numbers than on previous days.

Riot police faced a steady hail of cobble stones and fireworks, and responded with barrage after barrage of tear gas, some of the canisters landing far back in the crowds, causing panic.

Incensed by the gas, the crowds waited for it to clear, then renewed their attacks.

World.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
World.content:
A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean has resumed after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days.

A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery.

The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate.

Rough seas and strong winds forced the team to remain on their research vessel for three days, until the weather cleared on Sunday.

"We are finally getting off the ship and able to land on Nikumaroro," Sirisha Bandla, a technology specialist who is part of the expedition, said in a video update from the deck of the Marin Mainiku.

The researchers arrived at the uninhabited atoll last week and began an underwater survey of the area of interest.

But the weather - powered by strong El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific - has so far prevented them from beginning a second of three phases, in which underwater objects will be probed to determine their depth and sediment will be dredged.

World.title: At least 17 dead in crush at Hindu festival event in India
World.content:
At least 17 people have been killed and many more injured in a crush at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark the Hindu festival of Durga Puja, officials say.

The incident occurred during sudden rainfall, which witnesses say prompted a surge of people to try to seek shelter.

West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and that 25 people were being treated for injuries.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the regional government was providing help to affected families.

Six of the dead have been identified, Adhikari said.

A senior police official told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining and the crowd started "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.".

Deadly crowd incidents, including during religious festivals, are not uncommon in India due to poor management and lack of adequate safety precautions.

Two years ago, 121 people were killed in Uttar Pradesh during a Hindu religious gathering.

World.title: CAF Champions League: Rangers strike late to beat MC Alger
World.content:
Rangers International secured a crucial 2-0 victory over Algerian champions MC Alger in the first leg of their CAF Champions League second preliminary-round tie at the MKO Abiola Stadium in Abeokuta on Sunday.

Despite Rangers playing with 10 men from the 13th minute, MC Alger conceded two late goals in the 84th and 87th minutes, resulting in a 2-0 victory for the Flying Antelopes.

Kenneth Igboke converted a penalty in the 84th minute before James Emo struck three minutes later to give the Nigerian champions a valuable advantage ahead of the return leg in Algeria.

The late goals rewarded Rangers’ persistence and gave the Flying Antelopes a two-goal cushion to defend when the teams meet again in Algeria on Friday, 23 October.

The result also gives the Nigerian side an opportunity to build on their continental campaign after a difficult passage through the previous round.

Rangers advanced to the second preliminary round after overcoming AS Sobemap of Benin Republic on penalties. The tie ended 1-1 after both legs before the Enugu club won 5-4 in the shootout in Lomé.

MC Alger, meanwhile, reached this stage after defeating Nigerien side ASN Nigelec 5-0 on aggregate, following a goalless first leg.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Algerian club arrived in Nigeria as a formidable opponent, having won their domestic league title, but Rangers made home advantage count with their late double strike.

The two-goal margin gives the Nigerian side a useful advantage, although they must remain disciplined in the return leg to secure qualification for the group stage.

Rangers are among Nigeria’s most successful clubs, with nine league titles, including their latest triumph in 2026. They also won the African Cup Winners’ Cup in 1977, establishing a significant place in the country’s football history.

The Flying Antelopes will now turn their attention to the return fixture in Algeria, where they must protect their lead against an MC Alger side seeking to overturn the deficit.

Victory over the two legs would secure Rangers a place in the CAF Champions League group stage and bring them closer to competing among the continent’s leading clubs.

World.title: 2027: Uba Sani targets 3 million votes in Kaduna as top El-Rufai allies defect to APC
World.content:
Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani has announced a target of three million votes for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections, following the defection of former Kaduna State Commissioner of Finance, Muhammad Bashir Sa’idu, and other prominent politicians from the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Mr Sani announced the target on Saturday at a ceremony in Zaria to receive Mr Sa’idu and other defectors into the APC.

Mr Sa’idu, a former Chief of Staff and Commissioner for Finance under ex-Governor Nasir El-Rufai, claimed that more than 200,000 ADC members and supporters had joined the APC through his political group, Kaduna De-Initiatives.

Other prominent defectors include Jafaru Sani, a former commissioner for education under Mr El-Rufai and an ADC governorship aspirant, and former Senator Suleiman Abdu Kwari, who also served as commissioner of finance during the former governor’s administration.

The defections mark a significant political realignment in Kaduna ahead of the 2027 elections, particularly as several figures associated with Mr El-Rufai’s administration move to the party led by his successor.

Uba Sani raises APC’s vote target to three million

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr Sani said the APC had raised its target in Kaduna State from two million to three million votes, citing the growing number of supporters joining the party.

He said the state has 4.6 million registered voters, claiming 96 per cent have collected their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Before now, we were promising to deliver two million votes, but we have now upgraded to three million votes, God willing. There are 4,600,000 registered voters in Kaduna State and 96% have received their voter cards,” he said.

The governor said the APC would intensify grassroots mobilisation, including door-to-door campaigns, to canvass support across the state.

“We will go to every nook and cranny of Kaduna State, go house-to-house to canvass for votes, to ensure victory for APC from top to bottom,” he said.

Mr Sani also linked the party’s electoral ambitions to the federal government’s projects and political appointments in Kaduna State, including the emergence of Tajudeen Abbas as Speaker of the House of Representatives.

“The president loves Kaduna because he has sited many projects in our dear State, he has given many citizens of the state political appointments, and so we should reciprocate by voting massively for APC in all elections,” he said.

He described Mr Sa’idu as a principled and trustworthy politician, saying he had anticipated his return to the APC.

“The decampee is a man of the people, and even when he went to ADC, we were confident that he would return home. He stands for justice. Malam Jafaru Sani is also someone who can be trusted. He is also a seasoned public servant,” Mr Sani said.

The governor further insisted that the APC offered equal opportunities to members, regardless of when they joined the party.

“I, as the Governor, House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas, the North West zonal Vice Chairman, Hon Garba Datti Babawo and all of us, none is more important than the other in our party. We are all equal, and everyone has the right to aspire to any position that he wants,” he said.

Sa’idu declares ADC dead in Kaduna

Mr Sa’idu said the ADC had lost political relevance in Kaduna after his group and other supporters left.

He said the Kaduna De-Initiatives had built the party’s structures from the ward to the state level but became dissatisfied with its leadership and candidate selection process.

“We discovered that the party was being teleguided by a family, a situation which we found unacceptable. So, we studied the situation and compared the list of ADC candidates who won the primaries with the APC candidates.

“We saw that there was no basis for comparison; the contrast between the ADC and APC candidates is very glaring,” he said.

Mr Sa’idu said the group subsequently convened an emergency steering committee meeting and resolved to return to the APC.

“So, we have returned home. And as of one month ago, about 100,000 of those who defected with us have returned. These were card-carrying members of ADC. Between then and now, over 100,000 defectors have also joined APC,” he said.

He claimed that no credible opposition remained in Kaduna State following the defections.

“The former Commissioner of Finance said that there is not a single bona fide politician remaining in ADC, adding that there is now no opposition in Kaduna State, following their defection because ‘we were the opposition’.”

He also predicted that the ADC would finish third in the state when the 2027 election results were announced.

Why Sa’idu and other El-Rufai allies left the ADC

The defections followed disagreements over the ADC’s governorship primary, in which Isah Ashiru emerged as the party’s candidate for the 2027 election.

Mr Ashiru secured 86,113 votes, while Mr Sani, who also contested the primary, came second with 29,580 votes. Mr Sani rejected the outcome, alleging irregularities.

Mr Sa’idu said his group grew dissatisfied with what it described as a small group’s influence over the party’s affairs and the quality of candidates produced during the primaries.

The dispute deepened divisions among politicians who had previously aligned with Mr El-Rufai and later joined ADC.

Mr Sa’idu, Mr Sani and Mr Kwari’s return to the APC has now brought several former associates of the ex-governor into the political camp of Mr Sani, who succeeded him in 2023.

From El-Rufai’s government to APC: Former allies change political camps

Mr Sa’idu’s defection is particularly significant given his previous position in Mr El-Rufai’s administration, where he served as Chief of Staff and Commissioner for Finance.

Mr Kwari also held the finance portfolio under the former governor, while Mr Jafaru Sani served as commissioner for education.

Their move to APC marks another shift in the political allegiances of figures who held prominent positions during Mr El-Rufai’s eight-year administration.

El-Rufai reflects on friends who abandoned him

Earlier, in a statement titled “My Relationships and the Aftermath,” Mr El-Rufai reflected on relationships with former colleagues, friends and associates, saying adversity had revealed the nature of some relationships.

Although he did not name specific individuals, his remarks came amid political realignments involving people who had served in his administration or worked closely with him.

“Over the years, I have stood by people and for causes I believed in, sometimes in difficult circumstances and at considerable personal cost. I did so not in expectation of praise, gratitude or reciprocity, but because I believed it was right,” he wrote.

Mr El-Rufai said he did not regret supporting people or causes he believed in, even though some might not reciprocate when circumstances changed.

“I have no regrets about standing by people or for causes when I believed it was right to do so, and I bear no resentment towards anyone who chooses not to do the same for me,” he said.

His continued detention amid legal proceedings has coincided with the political repositioning of several former associates, including those who have now joined Mr Sani’s APC.

It remains to be seen how much the defections will affect the political balance in Kaduna State as parties prepare for the 2027 elections.

World.title: 2027: We’ll not step down for Atiku — Kwankwaso replies ADC
World.content:
Former Kano State Governor and Vice Presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has dismissed reports suggesting that he and his presidential candidate, Peter Obi, are working for the ruling party or may withdraw from the 2027 presidential race in favour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) or any other political party.

Mr Kwankwaso, in a Facebook statement on Sunday, accused the ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) of running smear campaigns to mislead voters.

He reaffirmed that the NDC ticket—tagged the “Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) ticket”—remains fully in the race and is committed to providing a credible governance alternative for the nation.

No merger, no withdrawal

Mr Kwankwaso urged the electorate to ignore claims that the NDC is covertly working for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) or planning a last-minute withdrawal.

“Let me state clearly and unequivocally: we will not withdraw our candidature for the ADC or any other party. We remain confident in our capacity, competence, and readiness to lead Nigeria,” Kwankwaso declared.

“The OK ticket is neither working for nor acting on behalf of APC or any of its candidates. We see no possibility or reason to withdraw from the presidential race in favour of the ADC candidate or any other. These claims are unfounded and should be treated as such.”

He further charged ADC campaign team to focus on presenting its candidate’s vision rather than fabricating narratives against rival opposition figures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rising tensions between NDC and ADC

Mr Kwankwaso’s statement followed a series of political exchanges between the NDC and the ADC campaign council.

The ADC-PCC, through spokesperson Kola Ologbondiyan, recently accused Mr Kwankwaso of covertly aligning with President Bola Tinubu and APC.

ADC alleged that Mr Kwankwaso’s recent public call for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to step aside and support Peter Obi was a calculated attempt to divide the opposition vote and favour the ruling party.

ADC also claimed that Mr Kwankwaso prioritised personal ambition for future election cycles over a unified opposition front.

Vice President Shettima’s attack on Atiku

In response, Mr Kwankwaso advised the ADC to focus on addressing the ruling party’s criticism.

Vice President Kashim Shettima recently fired at ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar, mocking his repeated presidential bids and dismissing his economic proposals—such as production subsidies—as unrealistic.

Mr Shettima remarked that political ambition requires “intellectual maturity”. He quipped that Atiku’s candidacy was “more of Odinga Odinga than Abraham Lincoln,” raising questions about how Atiku planned to fund his proposed policies.

Mr Kwankwaso criticised the ruling APC’s performance while dismissing the ADC as incapable of addressing Nigeria’s pressing needs.

“The APC-led government has failed Nigerians. The ADC offers no better alternative,” he noted. “We believe the OK ticket presents a credible and viable option, backed by proven capacity, a strong track record, credibility, and broad support across both Northern and Southern Nigeria.”

He described the NDC as a “healing ticket” focused on tackling security, education, healthcare, infrastructure, and economic revitalisation.

Read the full statement below:

I have noted with deep concern the ADC campaign team’s conduct. The attacks directed at me, our presidential candidate His Excellency Peter Obi, and our party, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), are unnecessary and unhelpful.

Rather than presenting the competence, credibility, and capacity of their own candidate, as we have consistently done by putting our credentials and record of achievements before Nigerians, the ADC Presidential Campaign Council appears intent on creating mischief against our party and ticket. This includes attempts to portray us as working for the ruling party or to suggest that we may withdraw from the race in favour of ADC candidate at the last minute.

The ADC-PCC would be better served directing its energy toward rebutting the serious allegations levelled against their candidate by the Vice President, His Excellency Kashim Shettima, instead of targeting His Excellency Peter Obi and me.

We are aware that the ADC-PCC may try to mislead our supporters on the eve of the election by claiming that we intend to withdraw in their favour. Let me state clearly and unequivocally: we will not withdraw our candidature for ADC or any other party. We remain confident in our capacity, competence, and readiness to lead Nigeria.

The OK ticket is neither working for nor acting on behalf of APC or any of its candidates. We see no possibility or reason to withdraw from the presidential race in favour of the ADC candidate or any other. These claims are unfounded and should be treated as such.

The APC-led government has failed Nigerians. The ADC offers no better alternative. We believe the OK ticket presents a credible, viable option, backed by proven capacity, a strong track record, credibility, and broad support across Northern and Southern Nigeria. It is a healing ticket committed to uniting our country and tackling critical challenges in security, education, agriculture, infrastructure, healthcare, the economy, and other key sectors.

We believe NDC remains the country’s most formidable and viable opposition party. I therefore urge all our supporters and well-meaning Nigerians to keep working toward our great party’s victory.

Nigeria will be OK. – RMK

World.title: Finance Ministry faults claim that FG’s interest payments hit 124% of revenue
World.content:
The Federal Ministry of Finance has disputed a claim that the Federal Government’s interest payments reached 124 per cent of its revenue in the first half of 2026, describing the figure as misleading.

The ministry said recent analysis and public commentary, which cited the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, compared mismatched interest figures against an incomplete revenue base.

In a statement released on Sunday, the ministry said the 124 per cent interest calculation includes the debt serviced by the federal government on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states.

“Measuring this against federal revenue alone overstates the ratio, which is only meaningful when debt and revenue cover the same level of government,” the statement said.

The ministry also asserted that the reported revenue is incomplete as it excludes the independent revenue earned by government agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the treasury.

“In addition, more revenue is typically earned in the second half of the year than in the first due to the statutory timing of certain payments. This is why the ratio stood at 156% in H1 2025, while the full-year 2025 debt service-to-revenue ratio was below 60%, down from 97% before the reforms,” it stated.

The ministry explained that federal revenue rose by 72 per cent from ₦3.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to ₦6.2 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Interest payments, however, rose by 38 per cent, from ₦5.6 trillion to ₦7.7 trillion over the same period, according to the ministry.

“The interest-to-revenue ratio fell by 32 percentage points in a single year, from 156% to 124%, and the gap between interest and revenue narrowed from ₦2.0 trillion to ₦1.5 trillion,” the ministry said.

The ministry attributed the changes to the current administration’s economic reforms, arguing that revenue is growing faster than interest costs.

It argued that a six-month figure alone should not be used to evaluate the sustainability of government debt.

“Debt sustainability is assessed on a full-year basis, not over six months,” the statement said.

Citing the World Bank report, the ministry said Nigeria’s full-year 2026 debt service, covering both interest and principal, is projected at 46 per cent of revenue, and that this forecast is the appropriate benchmark for assessing the country’s debt-service burden.

The ministry noted that all borrowing falls within the limits approved by the National Assembly under the 2026 Appropriation Act and the approved borrowing plan, in compliance with the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 and the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act 2003.

“We encourage analysts and commentators to apply the same rigour they seek to hold the government to: compare like with like, read figures in context, and seek clarification where the data is unclear,” the ministry said.

World.title: Inside Tinubu’s Cross-party Campaign Council: Roles for politicians outside APC
World.content:
Three prominent opposition politicians have been handed responsibility for coordinating President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign in their respective states. This arrangement has drawn criticism over party loyalty ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister Nyesom Wike of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), and Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke of Accord are among the politicians appointed to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council.

Under the revised council list announced on 13 October, Mr Wike will coordinate the campaign in Rivers State and the FCT, Mr Soludo in Anambra and Mr Adeleke in Osun.

Opposition figures and some APC members have criticised their appointments, questioning the political implications of assigning campaign leadership roles to politicians outside the ruling party.

The controversy is particularly pronounced in Accord, whose Board of Trustees has endorsed Mr Adeleke’s support for Mr Tinubu despite an unresolved legal dispute over the party’s own presidential nomination.

The appointments come as the APC prepares for nationwide campaign activities, with the president expected to attend rallies in 12 states under a proposed itinerary running from October to January 2027.

Wike: Rivers and FCT

Mr Wike’s appointment formalises his role in Mr Tinubu’s re-election campaign, while he remains affiliated with the PDP. The former Rivers State governor supported Mr Tinubu during the political disagreements that preceded the 2023 presidential election and later joined his administration as FCT minister. His campaign responsibilities cover Rivers, where he served as governor between 2015 and 2023, and the FCT, where he currently holds a ministerial appointment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Wike has defended the cross-party coalition supporting the president and described himself as a field commander for the campaign in the FCT. The appointment extends his support for Mr Tinubu beyond public endorsements to an organisational role in two politically significant territories.

However, it remains unclear how his responsibilities will be coordinated with existing APC campaign structures in Rivers and the FCT.

Soludo: Anambra

Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo has been appointed coordinator of Mr Tinubu’s presidential campaign in the state.

Mr Soludo won a second term in November 2025 on the platform of APGA.

His inclusion places a sitting governor from another party in charge of coordinating support for the president’s re-election in Anambra.

Although the appointment shows political cooperation, it does not mean Mr Soludo has defected to the APC or that APGA has merged with the ruling party.

The arrangement also raises questions about how the governor’s campaign responsibilities will relate to existing APC officials and structures in Anambra.

Adeleke: Osun

Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has been appointed coordinator of Mr Tinubu’s re-election campaign in Osun State.

Mr Adeleke won re-election in August on the Accord platform, having previously belonged to the PDP.

His appointment has attracted particular attention because of an unresolved legal dispute over Accord’s presidential nomination.

On 5 October, the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered Accord and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election.

Justice Mohammed Garba Umar, ruling in suit FHC/ABJ/CS/1268/2026, held that the party had failed to submit Mr Olawepo-Hashim’s name despite evidence that he emerged from its presidential primary on 30 May.

Accord’s national chairman, Maxwell Mgbudem, subsequently challenged the judgement at the Court of Appeal.

Available reports indicate the judgement is under appeal, but PREMIUM TIMES has not independently obtained the appellate court filing or established whether any subsequent order has affected the judgement.

Meanwhile, Mr Adeleke’s decision to support Mr Tinubu has received backing from some officials of his party.

On 14 October, Accord’s National Assembly and State House of Assembly candidates in Osun pledged to mobilise support for the president.

Two days later, Accord’s Board of Trustees endorsed Mr Adeleke’s decision to support Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

In a statement signed by Samson Isibor on behalf of the board’s chairman, Isaac Adeniyi, the BoT defended the governor’s appointment as the president’s campaign coordinator and pledged support for Mr Tinubu.

The endorsement followed criticism from some individuals identifying themselves as Accord leaders in Lagos, who questioned Mr Adeleke’s political allegiance.

The BoT rejected their claims and challenged their authority to speak for the party.

However, the board’s endorsement does not, by itself, establish that Accord has formally withdrawn Mr Olawepo-Hashim’s candidacy or adopted Mr Tinubu as its presidential candidate.

The development leaves two separate questions: the outcome of the legal dispute over Accord’s presidential nomination and whether the party’s national organs have formally adopted the president’s re-election bid.

Other appointments and the wider structure

Mr Tinubu heads the expanded campaign council, with Vice-President Kashim Shettima and APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda among its senior officials.

Former Zamfara State Governor Abdulaziz Yari serves as director-general.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio, House of Representatives Speaker Tajudeen Abbas and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq are among the senior officials assigned leadership responsibilities.

Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma serves as secretary, while other senior APC figures have been assigned regional and mobilisation roles.

The council also includes former governors and other political figures serving in advisory capacities.

Former Gombe State Governor Ibrahim Dankwambo is among those named in published accounts of the council’s advisory structure.

The distinction between state coordinators and advisers is significant. State coordinators lead campaign mobilisation in specific territories, while advisory appointments do not necessarily carry direct operational responsibility for a state.

The precise responsibilities of all appointees should be read alongside the APC’s final official council list.

Criticism from opposition and APC members

The inclusion of politicians outside the APC has drawn criticism from opposition figures and some ruling-party members, who have questioned the appointments on grounds ranging from party loyalty to political accountability.

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, criticised the expanded campaign council in a statement issued on 14 October through his campaign’s director of strategic communication, Phrank Shaibu.

Atiku questioned the size of the council and accused Mr Tinubu of attempting to divert public attention from economic hardship and insecurity.

He also criticised the use of the Presidential Villa for the council’s inauguration, arguing that the president’s official residence should not be used for partisan political activities.

As PREMIUM TIMES previously reported, Atiku argued that the president should be judged by his administraqtion’s performance rather than the number of politicians he recruited into his campaign.

Another ADC chieftain, Dele Momodu, criticised the inclusion of Messrs Wike and Soludo and Mr Adeleke during an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time programme on 14 October.

Mr Momodu, deputy director-general of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, compared the president’s growing political influence with the concentration of power under the late military ruler Sani Abacha.

The appointments have also attracted objections from within the APC.

Polycarp Alegu, a media aide to the Ebonyi State APC chairman, questioned why politicians from other parties were given campaign leadership positions ahead of longstanding APC members.

According to The Trumpet, Mr Alegu argued that the arrangement could undermine loyal party members’ morale and expose internal campaign arrangements to politicians who had not joined the APC.

Questions about the political implications of the appointments were also raised by Paul Ibe, media adviser to Atiku.

In a 16 October opinion article published by TheCable, Mr Ibe questioned whether politicians could coordinate a rival party’s presidential re-election campaign while remaining members of parties with their own constitutions and electoral interests.

He specifically questioned Mr Adeleke’s role because Accord had its own presidential nomination.

The criticisms raise questions about the authority under which the appointments were accepted and whether the affected parties’ internal rules permit such arrangements.

However, the appointments alone do not establish that any party constitution has been breached.

Support for cross-party arrangement

Despite the criticism, politicians within the affected parties have supported the appointments.

Mr Wike has defended the arrangement as part of a broader political coalition supporting Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

Representatives of the PDP and APGA have also publicly supported the inclusion of their members in the campaign structure, according to The PUNCH.

In Accord, the endorsement has gone beyond individual expressions of support.

The party’s Board of Trustees announced its backing for Mr Adeleke’s campaign role on 16 October, following an earlier declaration of support for Mr Tinubu by Accord’s legislative candidates in Osun State.

However, the endorsement has not resolved the competing positions within the party.

Mr Olawepo-Hashim has questioned the governor’s decision to support Mr Tinubu, while Accord’s national leadership has appealed the Federal High Court judgement concerning his nomination.

The developments illustrate the distinction between political endorsements by party officials and formal decisions affecting a party’s presidential nomination.

Former House of Representatives member Sam Onuigbo has also welcomed the inclusion of politicians from outside the APC, describing the arrangement as an example of cooperation across party lines.

Tinubu to attend rallies in 12 states

The expanded council is expected to play a significant role in implementing the APC’s proposed nationwide campaign programme.

Although the party plans campaign activities across the 36 states and the FCT, Mr Tinubu is scheduled to attend rallies in only 12 states between October 2026 and January 2027.

As PREMIUM TIMES reported on 16 October, the proposed presidential appearances are expected to begin in Kaduna on 24 October.

The itinerary also lists Rivers for 7 November, Plateau for 14 November, Oyo for 21 November, Borno for 25 November, Enugu for 28 November and Bauchi for 29 November.

Other proposed stops are Sokoto on 4 December, Delta on 12 December and Kano on 17 December.

Adamawa is scheduled for 4 January 2027, with the concluding rally proposed for Lagos on 9 January.

The APC has said the itinerary remains subject to adjustment.

Of the three prominent non-APC state coordinators, Mr Wike’s assignment in Rivers coincides with a state where the president is scheduled to campaign personally.

Anambra and Osun are not among the 12 states listed for presidential appearances.

Under the proposed programme, Messrs Soludo and Adeleke would therefore coordinate campaign activities in their states without a scheduled presidential rally, unless the itinerary changes.

The arrangement places greater responsibility on state coordinators and other campaign officials to mobilise support in areas the president is not expected to visit.

Criticism of the limited campaign tour

The proposed itinerary has also attracted criticism from the ADC Presidential Campaign Council.

Its director of media and publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, accused Mr Tinubu of avoiding direct engagement with voters across much of the country.

Mr Ologbondiyan argued that a president seeking re-election should be prepared to defend his administration’s record on the economy, insecurity and the cost of living before voters across the federation.

The APC has rejected the suggestion that the limited itinerary reflects an unwillingness to campaign.

During an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time programme on 15 October, Obafemi George, a member of the campaign council’s media and strategic communications committee, said the president had assessed the country’s electoral map and decided to balance campaigning with governance.

As PREMIUM TIMES previously reported, Atiku argued that the president should be judged by his administration’s performance rather than the number of politicians he recruited into his campaign.

He said Mr Tinubu would continue promoting his administration’s policies while ensuring that government responsibilities were not neglected.

Cross-party politics ahead of 2027

The appointments reflect the political alliances developing ahead of the 2027 election.

For the APC, bringing politicians from other parties into the campaign could expand its mobilisation network in states where support for Mr Tinubu extends beyond the ruling party’s membership.

For the appointees, the arrangement creates a distinction between their existing party affiliations and the presidential candidate they have been assigned to support.

The development also comes as six opposition parties participating in the G100 initiative consult presidential candidates on possible electoral cooperation, including a proposed framework for selecting a common candidate.

While the APC is incorporating politicians from other parties into its campaign structure, G100 participants are discussing arrangements for cooperation among opposition parties.

The two processes illustrate different forms of political alignment ahead of the election.

However, the expanded council does not establish how the non-APC coordinators will work with existing state party executives, what authority they will exercise or how their campaign activities will be financed.

Those questions are particularly relevant in states where the appointed coordinator belongs to a party other than the APC.

As the APC prepares for its proposed campaign opening in Kaduna on 24 October, the expanded council provides a picture of the alliances supporting Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

How those appointments will operate alongside existing party structures, and whether the cross-party arrangements will translate into coordinated campaigns, remains to be seen.

World.title: ESDIAC secures licence to operate in Nigeria’s data market
World.content:
ESDIAC Global Systems Limited, a Nigerian technology company, says it has secured a licence to operate in Nigeria’s data market, paving the way for expansion of its telecommunications and digital communication services.Nigerian news

This is contained in a statement issued in Lagos on Friday by its founder and Chief Executive Officer, Austin Ugbebor.

Ugbebor said the licence would enable ESDIAC to provide cross-border data solutions, international connectivity, data top-ups and global eSIM services to Nigerian consumers and businesses.

He said the company aimed to make international communication more affordable and accessible for Nigerians at home and in the diaspora.

He commended President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Government for policies aimed at promoting competition and growth in Nigeria’s digital economy.

According to him, the company will leverage the licence to expand its operations, invest in local infrastructure, develop talent and extend affordable communication services to underserved communities.

He said ESDIAC operates in no fewer than 150 countries and 400 cities worldwide, offering international calling facility, global eSIMs and cross-border data solutions.

Ugbebor reaffirmed the company’s commitment to supporting Nigeria’s digital transformation agenda through innovation, investment and inclusive connectivity.

World.title: Article of Faith: The acceptable sacrifice (2), By Femi Aribisala
World.content:
You must be born again.

In the tabernacle Moses built, the inner court was reserved for consecrated priests (descendants of Aaron) to perform sacrifices. The Holy of Holies was off-limits. It was a no-go area. It was a sacred space within the Temple where the Ark of the Covenant was placed, protected by a heavy veil. Only the High Priest could enter there, once a year, on Yom Kippur. This restriction represented the high holiness required to approach God’s presence.

If any man violated these restrictions, he died on the spot. This is what happened to Nadab and Abihu when they offered strange fire in the temple. Priests entering the inner court and the holy of holies had a rope tied around their waist. If they died as a result of ritual impurity or because of sins of disobedience, they were then pulled out with the rope around their waist.

Access By Faith

However, what is impossible with man is possible with faith in God.

Jesus says:

Assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you. Matt 17:20).

Therefore, Abel could offer an acceptable sacrifice to God before the Law of Moses. He did this by faith.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts; and through it, he being dead still speaks. (Heb 11:4).

The Tabernacle of David

But by the grace of God, David, the man after God’s heart, also found a way to bypass God’s legal limitations. He was not an Aaronite, and neither was he a Levite. He was from the tribe of Judah. Nevertheless, his faith in God made a way for him to offer an acceptable sacrifice to God.

David says:

Enter into (God’s) gates with thanksgiving, and into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name. (Psa 100:4).

Rebuilding the Tabernacle of David

God sent me to pray for a man sick with cancer. But after I prayed for him, God did not heal him. His parents sent for me. They said that after I prayed for him, he became better. But then he became so much worse. Could I come back to pray for him?

God told me to go back. But I struggled with God. I told Him, “If You wanted to heal him, You could have done so the first time I prayed for him.” “Why do I have to pray a second time?” “If you want to kill him, just kill him without involving me.”

So, God said, “Don’t pray for him again.” “Just show him a video.” God said, “Go to the shelf, and I will show you which video you are to show him.”

When I got to the shelf, He asked me to stretch out my hand and take a videotape. When I did, I took one entitled, “If Satan Can’t Steal Your Joy, He Can’t Keep Your Goods.”

I watched the video and understood why it was relevant. Jesus says:

Therefore, you now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and your joy no one will take from you. (John 16:22).

I copied the video and took it to the man on his sickbed. But when I played the tape, it only played for 10 minutes. There was a power cut, so the recording stopped. Not to worry. I told him about the message in the video. “Rejoice.” Thereafter, for two hours, I sang praises to God with the sick man and his family.

Two weeks later, the man died. Then, I changed gears with God. I told Him it did not matter whether those He sent me to pray for lived or died. He can heal them, or He can kill them if He wants to. My business is to touch and pray; healing is His department.

Sacrifice of Praise

When I reached that juncture, God told me to sing a song:

“I will enter His presence with thanksgiving in my heart,

I will enter His courts with praise

I will say this is the day that the Lord has made

I will rejoice for He has made me glad.”

When I sang that song, God switched on the light. I now have perfect understanding of the matter. Indeed, I was sent to heal the sick man. But his healing was spiritual. God was taking him home to Himself. God’s message to Him was to enter His heavenly gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise.

What God required of the man was a sacrifice of praise.

“Thus says the Lord: ‘Again there shall be heard in this place — of which you say, “It is desolate, without man and without beast” — in the cities of Judah, in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without man and without inhabitant and without beast, the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who will say: “Praise the Lord of hosts, for the Lord is good, for His mercy endures forever” — and of those who will bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the Lord. For I will cause the captives of the land to return as at the first,’ says the Lord. (Jeremiah 33:10-11).

The sacrifice of praise is acceptable to God. It is offered joyfully even under the most inconvenient circumstances. God does not accept praise that is not offered joyfully.

The psalmist asks:

Why are you cast down, O my soul? And why are you disquieted within me? (Psa 43:5).

No matter the vagaries of life, God requires us to offer to Him joyful praise:

Because Your lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise You. Thus I will bless You while I live; I will lift up my hands in Your name. My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness, and my mouth shall praise You with joyful lips. (Psa 63:3-5).

My lips shall greatly rejoice when I sing to You, and my soul, which You have redeemed. (Psa 71:23).

Then I will go to the altar of God, to God my exceeding joy; and on the harp I will praise You, O God, my God. (Psa 43:4).

Women like to dance. But make sure you are dancing on the inside

Building a Temple

David resolved to build a house for God. He insisted God was too important to dwell in a tabernacle. However, God told David he could not build Him a temple because he had killed too many people and his hands were full of blood.

But God said through Isaiah that He does not desire a Temple built by fleshly men.

Thus says the Lord: “Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest? For all those things My hand has made, and all those things exist,” says the Lord. “But on this one will I look: on him who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at My word. (Isa 66:1-2).

God sent men to destroy every temple built by men.

Spiritual Houses

Jesus told the Samaritan woman:

Believe Me, the hour is coming when you will neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, worship the Father. You worship what you do not know; we know what we worship, for salvation is of the Jews. But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth. (John 4:21-24).

Temples Built Inside Men

Coming to Him as to a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God and precious, you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. (1 Pet 2:4-5).

NKJV

Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone defiles the temple of God, God will destroy him. For the temple of God is holy, which temple you are. (1 Cor 3:16-17).

Useless Sacrifices

God also cannot accept sacrifices made by sinful men. What He desires from men is love and mercy. That is the first and great commandment.

You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ (Matt 22:37).

But you cannot love God unless you are born again.

God says in Hosea:

I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. (Hos 6:6).

Jesus reiterates this:

Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance. (Matt 9:13). CONTINUED.

World.title: MOVIE REVIEW: Agbara Nla remake casts old spell on new generation
World.content:
A particular kind of fear only a classic Nollywood villain from the late 1990s can inspire: the kind that makes an audience laugh nervously, whisper prayers in fear, and still refuse to look away.
