More than three decades after he first embodied Isawuru, the veteran Christian filmmaker Mike Bamiloye returns as the terrifying antagonist of a story that once helped define an era of Nigerian gospel filmmaking.

Yet the most remarkable thing about this remake is not simply that Mr Bamiloye has revisited one of his most recognisable roles. It is that a film built around spiritual warfare, demonic oppression and the supremacy of God’s power has become one of Nollywood’s biggest non-December releases.

Directed by Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and his brother, Joshua “Jay Mikee” Bamiloye, the film opened nationwide on 1 October, Nigeria’s Independence Day. PREMIUM TIMES reported that it generated approximately ₦71.4 million from preview screenings and another ₦99.2 million during its opening weekend, bringing its opening-frame total to about ₦170.6 million. It recorded the biggest non-December opening for a Nigerian film and the strongest opening for a faith-based Nollywood production. It has grossed ₦307.2 million so far.

But does the film’s success translate into an equally convincing cinematic experience? And more importantly, what is the secret behind the film’s success? Is it just nostalgia?

From 1993

To appreciate the ambition behind Agbara Nla: The Return, it helps to understand what the original meant to Nigerian audiences.

The first ‘Agbara Nla’ premiered in 1993 as a Mount Zion Film Productions television serial written by Mike Bamiloye. Its English-language adaptation, ‘The Ultimate Power’, followed in 1994, helping the story reach audiences beyond Yoruba-speaking communities. The production became one of Mount Zion’s defining works and helped establish the ministry’s reputation for bringing Christian teachings to the screen.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The story itself had an extraordinary journey. Bamiloye has recalled that the original production idea dates to 1987, when a project initially titled ‘Agbara To Ju Agbara Lo’ was filmed but abandoned after the cameraman reportedly disappeared with the tapes. The project revived in 1993, after Mount Zion had gained filmmaking experience, and eventually reached television audiences across western Nigeria.

Plot

The village of Muwonleru lives under the oppressive influence of Isawuru, a feared occult figure whose power extends beyond ordinary fear and superstition.

Isawuru challenges Oba Adetunji, the village king, demanding that he bow to him and pay homage as his predecessors allegedly did. When the king refuses, Isawuru makes good on his threat, destroying the royal household and beheading the monarch.

Before his death, however, the king writes to his cousin, Kola, who lives in Ibadan. The letter becomes a call to take the Christian message to a community held captive by spiritual oppression.

Kola and Bose, played by Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and Aanu Kolade Abiodun, initially evade the assignment. Kola receives a promotion that transfers him to Lagos, which he sees as an escape from the daunting mission.

The responsibility eventually falls to Olaboye and his wife, Olatomi, played by Philip Olubakin and Remilekun Mosiko. The couple must leave behind the comfort of urban life to confront the forces terrorising Muwonleru.

Olaboye’s journey to the mission is strengthened by his encounter with Engineer Ojo, whose family has experienced what the film presents as a miraculous birth after more than two decades of childlessness. The encounter helps persuade Olaboye to accept the assignment.

What follows is a familiar but compelling Mount Zion confrontation between light and darkness, featuring marine spirits, forest witches, occult rituals, and a succession of encounters designed to establish the film’s central question: whose power is truly greater?

Mike Bamiloye owns the screen

The most immediately satisfying element of Agbara Nla: The Return is its central performance.

As Isawuru, Mike Bamiloye doesn’t merely reprise an iconic character; he seems to understand exactly why the character endured in the original movie. Beyond the costume’s intimidating presence, Mr Bamiloye animates the persona that gives Isawuru his well-earned reputation, giving the villain a presence that endures even when he is not the centre of the action.

There is also an unexpectedly entertaining quality to his wickedness. Isawuru seems to relish his own reputation, and Bamiloye plays that relish with a conviction that invites nervous laughter from the audience.

Aanu Kolade Abiodun also makes a strong impression as Bose. Her performance gives the character a relatable personality. Even after she is possessed following her ill-fated friendship with Paulina, she convincingly depicts both fierce horror and vulnerable pity.

Review

The plot is straightforward in its moral architecture. Evil is real, spiritual warfare has real consequences, and faith demands more than personal conviction; it requires obedience and sacrifice.

The more interesting conflict, however, is not simply between Isawuru and the Christian protagonists. It is between the desire for personal comfort and the responsibility to confront a community’s suffering. Kola’s reluctance gives the story a human side that occasionally feels more relatable than its supernatural spectacle.

The film’s production design and costumes show an understanding that remaking a classic doesn’t mean reproducing every visual limitation of the original. Isawuru’s appearance, the forest coven, the marine queen, and the redesigned Ologosodudu evoke the visual imagination of older Nigerian supernatural films while benefiting from a more ambitious production.

The film also shows an appealing willingness to retain the narrative associated with Mount Zion’s earlier productions. Rather than disguising the film’s origins, the directors build on them, preserving the heightened performances and dramatic confrontations that made the original distinctive.

The commercial success of Agbara Nla: The Return is more than a flattering statistic. It challenges assumptions about when Nigerian audiences will turn out for local films and what kinds of stories they are willing to pay to see.

For years, December has been a key period for Nollywood releases, benefiting from holiday travel, family gatherings, and increased cinema attendance. Against that backdrop, the remake’s October opening stands out.

Agbara Nla: The Return shows that nostalgia, faith, and theatrical spectacle combine to create commercial power.

However, for all its strengths, Agbara Nla: The Return is not immune to the weaknesses of the tradition from which it emerges.

Its runtime, estimated at between two hours and 40 minutes and three hours, is a substantial demand on the audience. The chapter-like structure provides some relief, but the film occasionally confuses duration with dramatic depth.

Certain sequences linger longer than necessary, particularly when the narrative pauses to underline a spiritual lesson that the preceding action has already communicated.

The film has a clear theological framework, and its resolution should be judged partly within that framework. But audiences unfamiliar with Mount Zion’s storytelling conventions may find the conclusion less dramatically persuasive than the preceding conflict.

Agbara Nla: The Return does not treat the supernatural as a metaphor to be explained away; it takes the existence of spiritual forces as a premise of its story and builds its drama around the consequences of that belief.

For audiences who share its theological assumptions, this approach may heighten their appreciation of the film. For others, some of its claims and dramatic choices may invite scepticism or discomfort. This matters because the film is not simply trying to entertain a general cinema audience. It is also engaging viewers whose religious convictions shape how they interpret the actions on screen.

These shortcomings do not erase its achievement. Agbara Nla: The Return has made an old story feel relevant again, even if it occasionally takes longer than necessary to make its point.

Overall, Agbara Nla: The Return shows that, beyond nostalgia, a good story that resonates with audiences still finds relevance when told with an understanding of the trends of the time.

Verdict: 8/10

Agbara Nla: The Return is showing in Cinemas Nationwide

World.title: 2027: Adeleke risks Accord sanctions over Tinubu campaign role — Oke
World.content:
Governor Adeleke

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The Ogun State Chairman of Accord, Hon. Michael Rotimi Oke, has said Governor Ademola Adeleke of Osun State could face disciplinary action over his reported appointment as coordinator of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 presidential campaign in Osun State, if it is established that he acted against his party’s interests.

Oke, however, cautioned against rushing to judgment, saying the appointment alone was not enough to establish anti-party activity, as Accord’s national leadership had yet to investigate the circumstances or hear from the governor.

Speaking in an interview with Vanguard, Oke said the party’s constitution provided grounds for disciplinary action against members who engaged in anti-party activities, but stressed that any decision on Adeleke’s case must be based on established facts and the position of the party’s authorised organs.

“The issue here is not just about Governor Ademola Adeleke having any form of relationship with the APC Presidential Campaign Council, but whether such relationship contravenes the constitution of the party, the political stance of Accord, or any other decision taken by the party,” he said.

Oke said the party’s national leadership learnt of the reported appointment through the media and had yet to issue an official position on the matter.

He explained that Articles 13, 14 and 20 of the party’s constitution addressed members’ obligations to comply with party decisions and provided for disciplinary action over anti-party activities and misconduct.

According to him, Adeleke’s reported role must be assessed against the nature of his involvement, particularly whether it amounts to cooperation with the President on national development or active campaigning for the APC presidential candidate against Accord’s interests.

“If the role of Governor Adeleke was that of cooperating with the President on national development, then by itself, such will not constitute anti-party actions,” Oke said.

He, however, warned that an official endorsement of Tinubu or active campaigning for the APC candidate, especially if Accord adopts a different presidential candidate, could provide grounds for disciplinary proceedings.

Oke noted that Accord had yet to produce a presidential candidate for the 2027 election, making it necessary for the party to establish its position before determining whether Adeleke’s reported appointment breached any directive or constitutional provision.

The Accord chieftain said the governor’s reported appointment also raised broader questions about the party’s political identity, members’ confidence and the prospects of its candidates contesting for elective offices in 2027.

He said uncertainty over the governor’s political alignment could create divisions within the party, with some members backing him while others demand sanctions.

On Adeleke’s relationship with Tinubu, Oke said the governor’s reported acceptance of the appointment appeared to be driven by a personal connection with the President.

“At the inauguration of the committee in Abuja, we heard Governor Adeleke refer to President Tinubu as his father. So, I can conclude that Governor Adeleke must have accepted the appointment on a personal relationship basis,” he said.

Oke, however, cautioned that the governor’s personal relationship with Tinubu should not, in itself, determine the party’s verdict on the matter.

“There is a difference between the opinion of individual party leaders and a decision taken by authorised bodies of the party,” he said.

He maintained that the national leadership had a responsibility to protect Accord’s institutional integrity while ensuring that Adeleke was not condemned without a fair assessment of the facts.

The development has attracted attention because Adeleke was re-elected Osun governor under Accord in August 2026, while Tinubu is the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 election.

Oke said the party’s ultimate decision would have implications beyond the governor, potentially shaping Accord’s cohesion, political identity and electoral strategy ahead of the general elections.

World.title: Shettima lists federal projects worth billions in Bauchi
World.content:
— BASFA puts value of interventions at ₦144bn

By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has highlighted federal government projects worth billions of naira in Bauchi State, describing them as evidence of President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructural development in the North-East.

Shettima spoke at the weekend during the inauguration of the Bauchi Shettima Forum for Asiwaju (BASFA) in Bauchi. He was represented at the event by the Minister of State for Regional Development, Uba Maigari Ahmadu.

The vice-president said several projects were being implemented through the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) to address the region’s developmental challenges, adding that more projects would be inaugurated in Bauchi and other North-East states in the coming months.

He cited the ongoing construction of the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Borno road as a major federal infrastructure project expected to improve connectivity and stimulate economic activities.

According to him, the road is being constructed with reinforced concrete to ensure durability.

“Work is currently ongoing on this project, utilising modern construction techniques. It is a high-quality road being built with reinforced concrete. We are actively working on it, and I can assure you that construction will reach Bauchi town very soon,” he said.

Shettima attributed the administration’s regional development initiatives to the establishment of the Ministry of Regional Development and five regional development commissions to address the peculiar needs of different parts of the country.

He urged Bauchi residents to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the ongoing interventions demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to the region’s development.

Earlier, the convener of BASFA, Dr Nafi’a M. Abdullahi, said the forum was established to promote awareness of the Tinubu administration’s policies and programmes and highlight its impact on the people of Bauchi State.

Abdullahi said the group would mobilise support for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket ahead of the 2027 presidential election, citing projects in healthcare, education, security and agriculture.

Healthcare, education projects

The BASFA convener listed the establishment of a diagnostic centre at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH) and the construction and renovation of eight healthcare facilities across the state among interventions attributed to the NEDC.

She also disclosed that efforts were underway to upgrade the General Hospital in Alkaleri to a Federal Medical Centre to expand access to healthcare services.

In the education sector, Abdullahi cited the completion of a student hostel at Sa’adu Zungur University, Gadau, and the ongoing construction of 1,600-bed accommodation facilities at the Federal Polytechnic, Bauchi, and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University (ATBU).

She added that the NEDC had established mega schools and renovated educational institutions across the state.

On security, Abdullahi said the Federal Government had approved the establishment of military battalions in Alkaleri and Tafawa Balewa to strengthen security and address threats facing communities.

She also said the administration had committed resources to agriculture and food production, putting the estimated value of federal projects and interventions in Bauchi at ₦144 billion.

Abdullahi said BASFA would continue to promote the administration’s programmes while identifying challenges affecting communities and working with relevant stakeholders to seek solutions.

World.title: FG ends 17-year blackout in Gombe communities
World.content:
— Begins 16MW mini-grid network across four communities

By Soni Daniel, Editor, Northern Region

The Federal Government has ended a 17-year electricity blackout in Tallasse, Balanga Local Government Area of Gombe State, with the commissioning of a one-megawatt solar mini-grid project executed through the Rural Electrification Agency (REA).

The project, commissioned on Saturday, features a 2.4-megawatt-hour battery storage system and was delivered in partnership with the Gombe State Government and a private developer.

The commissioning also marked the flag-off of a 16-megawatt network of four interconnected solar mini-grids across Dukku, Bajoga, Kumo and Kaltungo communities, aimed at providing reliable electricity to homes, farms, markets and small businesses across the state.

The Tallasse project already serves 6,028 connections and includes electricity-powered groundnut oil processing, rice milling and flour grinding facilities, as well as electric tricycles to support economic activities.

Speaking at the commissioning, the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said the projects represented a practical expression of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, noting that renewable energy initiatives were being deployed across the country, including Adamawa, Lagos, Oyo, Plateau, Kano, Kwara and Gombe states.

Tegbe said the commissioning marked a new chapter for Tallasse residents, who had endured 17 years without electricity.

“The true significance of these investments will be measured in the daily lives they improve: the farmer who can process produce closer to home, the trader who can preserve perishable goods, the artisan who can power equipment, and the young person who can build a livelihood within the community,” he said.

He added that the projects, as they become operational, could strengthen public services, reduce dependence on expensive self-generation and attract businesses to the communities.

The minister said his ministry would continue to work with the Gombe State Government, developers and host communities to ensure that the infrastructure translated into reliable electricity, productive economic activities and sustainable local prosperity.

Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, described the projects as the outcome of collaboration between the state government and the Federal Government through the REA.

He said that in an agricultural community such as Balanga, which had gone 17 years without electricity, combining reliable power with rice milling, groundnut processing, flour production and electric mobility would strengthen the entire local economy beyond household lighting.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the REA, Abba Aliyu, said the agency was shifting its focus from counting electricity connections and installed megawatts to measuring the economic impact of its projects.

Aliyu said access to electricity without reliability limited its benefits, explaining that the projects incorporated battery storage, intelligent monitoring, productive-use equipment and sustainable operating models.

According to him, the approach is designed to establish functional electricity ecosystems rather than merely install power plants.

The projects are being delivered under the Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up programme, as the Federal Government pursues multiple approaches to improving electricity supply.

The strategy includes strengthening the national grid while accelerating mini-grids, embedded generation, solar home systems and dedicated power solutions for universities, markets and agricultural clusters.

World.title: Attack on Abia Station: No arms, ammunition stolen — CP
World.content:
— Two senior policemen killed, three inspectors injured as hoodlums attack facility

— Explosives set station building, patrol van ablaze

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — The Abia State Commissioner of Police, Wilfred Afolabi, has said no arms or ammunition were stolen when armed hoodlums attacked the Uratta Police Divisional Headquarters in Aba, killing two senior police officers and injuring three inspectors.

The attackers, who stormed the facility at about 2.26am on Saturday, reportedly used explosives to set parts of the station building and a patrol van ablaze.

The injured inspectors are receiving medical attention, while parts of the station and other vehicles within the premises were reportedly damaged.

Afolabi confirmed the attack while inspecting the damaged facility alongside Governor Alex Otti on Saturday.

The police commissioner, who said he arrived at the scene at about 4am, disclosed that security operatives had launched operations to track down the perpetrators.

“The most important thing is to get the culprit, and that is what we are doing,” he said, adding that no arrests had been made as of the time of his visit.

“The assurance I can give is that wherever they are, whenever they enter the hole, we will bring them out.”

In a statement on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chinaka, said Afolabi personally led tactical teams to the area, where they combed the surrounding environment and restored calm.

She said intensified security operations and intelligence gathering were ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attack.

The commissioner condemned the incident and vowed that the perpetrators would be brought to justice.

Governor Otti also visited the injured officers at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, Aba, to assess their condition.

The police urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible information that could assist the investigation.

The attack recalls a similar incident on February 23, 2021, when gunmen attacked the same police station, killing a police sergeant identified as Okezie and setting ablaze a patrol vehicle donated by the state government.

World.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israel’s upcoming election
World.content:
US President Donald Trump (R) and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (L) speak to reporters upon Netanyahu’s arrival at Trumps Mar-a-Lago residence in Palm Beach, Florida, on December 29, 2025. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP)







US President Donald Trump on Sunday offered his “complete and total” endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the country’s October 27 elections.

“Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel. BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who is in a tight race to win a new mandate, quickly acknowledged Trump’s gesture.

“Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!” Netanyahu wrote on X.

In his post, Trump described Netanyahu as “a Great Warrior Prime Minister” and ally in the war against Iran that began in late February with a massive bombing campaign but has dragged on as Tehran has retaliated by blocking global energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump asserted that without Netanyahu as Israel’s leader, the United States would be alone in combating the threat from the Islamic regime, “with its 51 year old chant, ‘Death to Israel, Death to America! We will destroy the Little Satan and the Big Satan.'”

“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” the US president said.

“This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much,” he added.

msp/md

World.title: Tinubu’s subsidy removal most patriotic act since independence — Agbo
World.content:
— Rep says reform has boosted government revenue, capital spending

By Anayo Okoli

ENUGU — A member of the House of Representatives, Dennis Nnamdi Agbo, has described President Bola Tinubu’s removal of the petrol subsidy as the most patriotic act by a Nigerian president since independence in 1960.

Agbo said Nigeria was technically bankrupt when Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023, arguing that drastic measures were required to address the country’s economic challenges.

The lawmaker, who represents Igbo Eze North/Udenu Federal Constituency, Enugu State, and is a former consultant with the World Bank and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), spoke while delivering the 2026 Distinguished Public Lecture Series of the Department of Public Administration and Local Government at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN).

The lecture, held at the Princess Alexandra Auditorium, was titled “Three Years of Post-Subsidy Removal: Evaluating the Socio-Economic Effects of Nigeria’s Deregulated Downstream Sector.”

Agbo acknowledged that the policy was neither populist nor politically convenient but described it as a decision driven by what he called a generational outlook and patriotic zeal.

“Truth be told, if we appreciate the true workings of our national politics, it will be understood that the removal of fuel subsidy is the most patriotic act of a president since our independence,” he said.

He argued that successive administrations had avoided removing the subsidy despite its perceived inevitability, largely because of a lack of political will.

“Many, almost all the presidential candidates in the 2023 election, campaigned with a promise to remove fuel subsidy. It was clearly inevitable considering the parlous condition of our nation then,” he said.

According to him, Tinubu has remained resolute in implementing the policy despite the public backlash, adding that the decision was intended to steer the country towards economic recovery.

“For too long, we have yearned for Nigerian and African economic renaissance, but we failed to take the bold steps that unleash the benefits of our vast economic potentials, for Nigerians, for Africans.

“The removal of fuel subsidy in Nigeria is one such bold step, and it is already redefining the outlook for our continent’s economy,” Agbo said.

He also linked the policy to investment in refining capacity across Africa, citing the Dangote refinery in Nigeria and a proposed refinery investment in Kenya as examples of the continent’s changing economic outlook.

However, the figures and details of the Kenyan project cited in his remarks were not independently established in the information provided.

Agbo listed other benefits he attributed to subsidy removal as increased government revenue, the clearance of recurrent debts owed by states, funding for major state projects, economic expansion, GDP growth, increased foreign reserves, exchange-rate stability and the growing adoption of solar energy.

The lawmaker further claimed that the Federal Government had maintained capital expenditure at about 70 per cent of the budget over the past three budget cycles, compared with between 25 and 30 per cent previously.

He said the size of the capital budget had also risen to as much as ₦40 trillion annually, adding that even after accounting for currency depreciation, the amount represented a substantial increase over previous years.

On the social and economic difficulties associated with the policy, Agbo acknowledged the pressure on household welfare and the rising cost of essential services.

He said the government recognised that the reforms, although considered necessary by the administration, had imposed significant hardship, particularly on poor and vulnerable Nigerians.

“The government is prepared to stay the course of reforms, but nevertheless, committed to attending to the plight of this group whose fortunes have been most affected by inflation, rising prices and high cost of living, mainly occasioned by after effects of economic reforms,” he said.

World.title: Buhari saw Tinubu as ‘Bad News’ for Nigeria — Baba-Ahmed
World.content:
— PRP chairman says ex-president resisted pressure to back Tinubu in 2023

Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, national chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), has claimed that former President Muhammadu Buhari was reluctant to transfer power to President Bola Tinubu in 2023 because he considered him “bad news” for Nigeria.

Baba-Ahmed spoke at a summit organised by the Northern Elders Forum, in a video published on Symfoni’s YouTube channel on Saturday.

He said Nigerians should have questioned Tinubu’s presidential ambition when he declared “Emilokan”, meaning “it is my turn”, during the build-up to the 2023 general election.

“Nigerians ought to have known there was something wrong the day Tinubu said, ‘It’s my turn’. Maybe we missed it,” he said.

“We have a presidency of a country of 250 million people. My turn? To do what? To become president.”

Baba-Ahmed said Buhari was reluctant to hand over power to Tinubu after considering the implications of his presidency for the country.

“Even Buhari saw Tinubu as bad news for this country. In fairness to him, he is not around him. Buhari resisted some people who insisted it had to be Tinubu,” he said.

The PRP chairman criticised Tinubu’s administration, alleging that the country had deteriorated under his leadership.

“Now we are being depressed for having a president for three and a half years. He has dragged the country as low as it is possible to go. And it has to stop him. We cannot go below, beyond where we are,” Baba-Ahmed said.

He, however, expressed confidence in Nigerians’ ability to overcome the country’s challenges, saying the nation had survived major crises in the past.

“We are very resilient people. We have seen crises bigger than this, and we survived it. We survived it, and we will survive this one,” he said.

“We will survive the four years of abuse, neglect, and plunder that Tinubu has caused because Nigeria has to survive for our children and their children.”

‘Every index of failure shows in this administration’

Baba-Ahmed accused Tinubu of prioritising his political ambition over the welfare of Nigerians, alleging that the administration had failed across key indicators.

“We will not allow a president to fulfil an ambition that one individual alone can wreck his country, just to prove that he has the power and the money to do so,” he said.

“We are at the bottom. There is no way to go anymore. Every index of failure shows in this administration.”

He also faulted Tinubu for not personally appealing to Nigerians for another term, saying the president had instead relied on political allies to campaign on his behalf.

Baba-Ahmed further accused northern governors of failing to draw the president’s attention to economic hardship and public dissatisfaction in the region.

Opposition coalition targets 2027 election

The PRP chairman said opposition parties were working towards forming a coalition to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

He described the effort as serious, saying the parties were prepared to pool resources and set aside their differences to build a common front.

“What we have seen is an incredible willingness for politicians to come together and say, let’s put aside some of our differences and see if we can actually create a momentum strong enough to remove this Tinubu,” he said.

Baba-Ahmed said the coalition would produce a candidate to challenge the president and urged Nigerians opposed to Tinubu’s re-election bid to support whoever emerged as its flag-bearer.

“There will be a candidate that will be produced by this coalition. Vote for whoever he is,” he said.

He also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure that the 2027 general election reflected the will of voters.

“INEC must guarantee that the 2027 elections will reflect the will of the people,” he said.

“If it does, and it must, because the consequences are almost clear, Tinubu is done.”

World.title: Speaker Abbas mobilises grassroots support for Tinubu, APC candidates in Kaduna
World.content:
Tajudeen Abbas

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has urged Kaduna citizens to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates to sustain ongoing reforms and development projects in the state.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Abbas made the call on Sunday in continuation of the tour of his constituency to inaugurate projects.

Speaking during a groundbreaking ceremony for road construction and educational projects in Ikara Local Government Area, Abbas said the sacrifices associated with the Federal Government’s reforms were temporary.

He expressed optimism that Nigerians would soon begin to experience the benefits.

He urged Nigerians to give Tinubu a second term to complete the reforms, calling him a friend of Kaduna State.

The Speaker said Kaduna benefited from four federal university projects within three years under Tinubu’s administration, after decades without another federal university.

He listed the upgrade of the Federal College of Education, Zaria, to a university, the establishment of the University of Applied Sciences in Kachia and the conversion of the Kaduna petroleum institute into a university.

Abbas also said a bill he sponsored secured presidential approval to convert Kaduna Polytechnic into a Federal University of Technology. He said the development, along with other federal projects, justified Kaduna residents supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Abbas also urged residents to support Gov. Uba Sani’s re-election in 2027, citing ongoing road, water and health projects across the state.

He warned that a change of government could jeopardise the completion of ongoing projects, urging citizens to support continuity.

The Speaker commended Uba Sani for his contributions to Kaduna State’s development and support for his emergence as Speaker of the House of Representatives.

He also solicited support for the APC candidates in Kaduna, thanking the party for its support and contributions to development in the state.

In his remarks, Gov. Uba Sani, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr AbdulKadir Meyere, commended the Speaker for extending development projects to communities across the state.

Gov. Sani also solicited support for all APC candidates in the state for continuity and to sustain the dividends of democracy.

World.title: Troops Disrupt Illegal Arms-Trafficking Network in North-central, Arrest One Over Alleged Kidnapping, Sexual Assault
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian military has said that troops of the Joint Task Force, North-Central Operation Enduring Peace, have uncovered, tracked and disrupted an illegal arms-trafficking network in the North-central region, particularly in Plateau State. The troops also dismantled kidnapping networks in the state.

The Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, made this known during his weekly update on the operational activities of troops of the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) across the country.

He also revealed that troops of the Joint Task Force, North-West Operation Fansan Yamma, apprehended a suspect identified as Yusuf Iliya Sani at Maraban Kakini over his alleged involvement in kidnapping, extortion, sexual assault and killings in Birnin Gwari Local Government Area (LGA) of Kaduna State.

He said: “Troops of Operation Enduring Peace maintained operations to disrupt illegal arms trafficking, identify suspected perpetrators of violent crime and dismantle kidnapping networks in Plateau State.

“To this end, troops conducted a covert operation in Mangu and Barkin Ladi LGAs of Plateau State and arrested a suspected arms fabricator at Heipang, Barkin Ladi LGA. Three other suspects were also arrested over their alleged involvement in illegal arms trafficking. Troops recovered one locally fabricated revolver rifle, one fabricated pistol, one fabricated AK-47 barrel, one AK-47 magazine and 42 rounds of 7.62mm × 54mm rimmed ammunition.

“On 10 October 2026, troops arrested a suspect, Yusuf Suleiman, at Barkin Ladi Main Market. He was allegedly linked to the attack on Kassa community on 24 September 2026, as well as kidnapping, armed robbery and the killing of a resident, Mr Gyang, on 16 April 2026.

“Also, on 14 October 2026, troops raided a suspected kidnappers’ hideout at Ruga in Methodist Kisahyip, Agingin, Bassa LGA of Plateau State, and arrested two suspects.”

Recounting the operational activities of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma on 9 October 2026, General Onoja said troops operating around the Galadimawa area sighted three suspected terrorists fleeing with a kidnapped person.

He further explained: “Troops engaged the suspects and forced them to abandon the victim.

“On 10 October, troops responded to reports that a local resident travelling from Dogon Dawa to Takama Village in Birnin Gwari LGA of Kaduna State was under attack by an unknown armed group. On arrival, the responding troops engaged the assailants and recovered an AK-47 rifle with 15 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition.

“Following continued tracking and monitoring, troops apprehended a suspect identified as Yusuf Iliya Sani at Maraban Kakini on 10 October 2026 over his alleged involvement in kidnapping, extortion, sexual assault and killings in Birnin Gwari LGA of Kaduna State.”

Onoja said the operations conducted across all operational theatres had sustained the AFN’s efforts to ensure a safe and secure environment and restore security across the country.

The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, commended the resilience of all security personnel, urging them to maintain operational momentum, remain highly vigilant and deny criminal elements any freedom of action.

The Defence Chief also called on all security agencies to strengthen their collaborative intelligence-sharing frameworks to enhance operations against criminal elements across the country.

He said national security was a collective civic responsibility, adding that through unwavering unity and resolve, the military would secure a peaceful and prosperous future for Nigeria.

World.title: Peter Obi Media Office Faults Shettima Over ‘Diminished Obi’ Remark
World.content:
* Says political leaders should debate records, policies not personal attacks

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Peter Obi Media Office has criticised Vice-President Kashim Shettima over his description of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, as “diminished,” urging political leaders to focus on candidates’ records, policies and ideas rather than personal attacks.

In a statement issued Sunday by its spokesman, Idris Zekeri Jnr, the media office described the remark as inconsistent with the standards of political engagement expected of leaders, particularly at a time when political parties are positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 general election.

The office took exception to what it considered a contrast between Shettima’s call for northerners to respect former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, an opposition figure, and his description of Obi, another opposition leader.

“Although Shettima has the right to oppose Obi, it is difficult to understand why he would demand respect for one opposition leader while casually dismissing another,” the statement said.

It added that political disagreements should not prevent public officials from recognising the contributions and political standing of their opponents.

The media office said Obi had maintained a campaign focused on issues and had avoided abusive language against political opponents.

“As a man of great decency, our candidate has conducted his campaign professionally and decorously. He has consistently focused his remarks on issues and has neither discussed nor used abusive language against anyone,” it said.

The statement also drew attention to the records of Obi and Shettima as former governors of Anambra and Borno States, respectively, arguing that their respective performances should be assessed against verifiable evidence rather than political rhetoric.

“However, Obi’s performance in Anambra State across key areas of governance surpassed Shettima’s record in Borno State, as demonstrated by performance statistics and the awards he received,” the office said.

It cited Obi’s record in fiscal management and investments in education and healthcare as areas that, in its view, distinguished his administration.

The office, however, did not provide comparative statistics in the statement to substantiate its assessment of the two former governors’ performances.

It challenged the vice-president and other political opponents to interrogate Obi’s record using verifiable facts and figures if they disagreed with the assessment.

“If Shettima contests any aspect of Obi’s record, he should present the facts rather than resort to political name-calling,” the statement added.

The media office said the controversy raised broader questions about political civility, the treatment of opposition figures and the responsibility of public officials to sustain issue-based debate in Nigeria’s democratic process.

It also appealed to political leaders from the South-east, including those in the All Progressives Congress (APC), to distinguish political loyalty from their responsibility to uphold mutual respect among political actors.

The statement urged South-east political leaders who support the APC to reflect on the implications of the exchange, particularly where they believe that criticism of an opposition politician from their region is inconsistent with the treatment accorded other political figures.

It said disagreements over party affiliation should not become grounds for tolerating what it considers disrespectful language against fellow Nigerians.

“We urge Igbo leaders in the APC and all Nigerians to draw the appropriate lesson from this episode and note that political loyalty must never justify tolerating disrespect towards a fellow Nigerian,” the statement said.

The office maintained that political competition should provide an opportunity for candidates and their supporters to examine competing records, policy proposals and governing philosophies.

“Those who oppose Obi should scrutinise his ideas and record rather than resort to personal abuse,” it said.

“Nigeria needs a contest based on records and ideas, not selective respect and political denigration.”

The media office further argued that Obi’s political relevance should ultimately be determined by voters rather than by comments from political opponents.

“The Nigerian people, rather than Shettima’s rhetoric, will determine Peter Obi’s political relevance,” it said.

The statement, dated October 18, 2026, was signed by Zekeri on behalf of the Peter Obi Media Office.

The development comes as political parties and their leading figures intensify their positioning ahead of the 2027 general election, with the conduct of political campaigns, the credibility of candidates and the tone of public debate expected to feature prominently in the contest.

While political leaders are entitled to criticise opponents and challenge their records in office, the exchange underscores the importance of substantiating political claims with evidence and maintaining a distinction between legitimate criticism and personal disparagement.

For the NDC presidential candidate and his supporters, the central argument is that Obi’s record as a former governor should be judged on its merits. For his political opponents, the challenge is to present competing evidence and policy alternatives capable of persuading voters.

Ultimately, the debate over the records of former governors and their suitability for national leadership is likely to remain part of the broader political contest as the 2027 election approaches.

World.title: 2027: Abia Youths Declare Support for Tinubu, Deputy Speaker Kalu, Plan One-Million-Man March in Aba
World.content:
A group of youths comprising artisans and Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) owners under the umbrella of “Great Aba Men” in Abia State has declared support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu.

The declaration was made during a courtesy visit to the Deputy Speaker at his country home in Bende on Saturday.

Speaking on behalf of the group, its leader, Prince Okwudiri Uche, said Abia youths will give President Tinubu the highest number of votes in the South East in the 2027 presidential election.

He said: “From today, we have declared for Mr. President. We will support Mr. President and Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu. Asiwaju is the next President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“There is no way we will have the Deputy Speaker of this federation from Abia State, supported by Mr. President, and not return the President. It will not happen. Rt. Hon. Sir, we will make you proud because we will deliver President Tinubu. Abia youths will make it happen. He will go for a second term. Aba people will not let you down”.

The group, which congratulated the Deputy Speaker on his appointment as Director-General II (South) of the PBAT/APC Presidential Campaign Council, requested him to serve as its Grand Patron.

It also revealed plans to organize a one-million-man march for President Tinubu in Aba.

In his remarks, Kalu commended the group for declaring support for President Tinubu and himself.

He noted the President’s love for the people of the South East, particularly Abia State, stating that the President who supported a son of Abia to emerge as Deputy Speaker deserves to be repaid with gratitude.

“From today, you have become Mr. President’s foot soldiers and will take the message of Renewed Hope to every nook and cranny of Aba. I declare you the sons of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. We are starting a movement that will go beyond January 16, 2026,” Kalu said.

He promised to support the group with a campaign bus for the planned march, charging them to mobilize across the State and take the message of Renewed Hope Agenda to the hinterlands.

“Every street will come out to show that we are supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. In Bende, the President will harvest all the votes because the Deputy Speaker is from this Local Government. So, go and put up your strategy. We will show that Great Aba Men are behind the President. We must make sure the President wins in Aba. I want you to be very visible in Aba and take over Aba. Let’s comb the city to announce our presence,” he said.

World.title: FG Tasks VCs to Prioritize High-demand Degree Programmes
World.content:
* Reaffirms commitment to establishing autism centres across six geopolitical zones



Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Federal Government has called on vice-chancellors of Nigerian universities to prioritise degree programmes that address critical manpower shortages, respond to emerging societal needs and equip graduates with specialised skills for professional practice and employment.

It said such programmes should include degrees in Audiology, Occupational Therapy, Speech and Language Therapy, Clinical Psychology and Medical Social Work, noting that expanding training in these fields would help bridge gaps in specialised healthcare and social services while creating more career opportunities for young Nigerians.

Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, also reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to establishing autism centres across the six geopolitical zones to improve access to specialised care and support for persons on the autism spectrum and their families.

Alausa stressed that universities must align their academic offerings with national workforce needs and the growing demand for specialised professional services.

He noted that developing these programmes would strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to provide essential services locally, reduce gaps in specialist care and build a skilled workforce capable of meeting the needs of the population.

The planned autism centres are expected to support access to diagnosis, therapeutic services and research, while serving as regional hubs for families, healthcare professionals and educational institutions.

The initiative reflects the Federal Government’s determination to strengthen local capacity and improve support for persons with autism and related developmental conditions.

The minister assured stakeholders that the Federal Government would continue to pursue reforms that expand access to relevant education, strengthen institutional capacity and promote skills development.

Alausa commended the Chairman of the Federal Government Committee for the Advancement of Audiology, Occupational Therapy and Speech and Language Therapy, Dr. Victoria Amu, for her passion and dedication to duty.

He called on vice-vhancellors and other university administrators to work closely with the Ministerial Committee Chairman, Dr. Victoria Amu, the relevant regulatory agencies and professional bodies to facilitate the development of the proposed programmes and ensure that training meets appropriate academic and professional standards.

The minister reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to building a responsive and inclusive higher education system that equips Nigerians with relevant skills, addresses critical manpower gaps and expands access to essential specialised services.

The initiatives form part of the administration’s broader efforts to strengthen human capital development, improve service delivery and ensure that Nigeria’s education system responds effectively to national priorities and the needs of its citizens.

World.title: Birmingham, UNILAG Bring UK Postgraduate Degrees Closer to Nigerians
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Nigerian students seeking internationally recognised postgraduate qualifications will have an opportunity to study programmes offered by a United Kingdom university without relocating abroad, following a new partnership between the University of Birmingham and the University of Lagos (UNILAG).

The universities have launched two one-year postgraduate programmes in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Technologies, and Digital Media and Communications, which will be delivered in Lagos from September 2027.

The initiative, developed under a Transnational Education (TNE) arrangement in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission, is designed to expand access to international higher education while developing skills relevant to Nigeria’s growing economy.

Speaking at the launch on Thursday, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, described the partnership as crucial to Nigeria’s tertiary education development.

“Our planned collaboration and partnership with the University of Birmingham is both timely and strategic at this critical phase of Nigeria’s tertiary education advancement. It is designed to consolidate and deepen the significant gains we have made in strengthening our university system, while expanding access to world-class, high-quality education anchored in global best practices,” he said.

The MSc in AI and Data Technologies will cover machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, large language models and AI ethics, preparing graduates for opportunities in fintech, healthcare innovation and business analytics.

The MA in Digital Media and Communications will focus on digital cultures, communication, power, identity and media ethics, while equipping students with research, content creation and broadcasting skills for careers in journalism and digital communications.

The Provost of the University of Birmingham, Professor Nick Vaughan-Williams, said the programmes would support Nigeria’s educational and workforce development needs.

“We’re proud to launch these programmes with our partners at UNILAG. Together we are supporting Nigeria’s tertiary education and talent needs, which are central to its ambitions for economic growth,” he said.

Echoing the emphasis on the partnership’s long-term value, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, Professor Folasade T. Ogunsola, said the collaboration reflected the university’s broader approach to international partnerships:

“The University of Lagos-University of Birmingham TNE collaboration reflects UNILAG’s broader vision of reimagining partnerships built on mutual respect, co-creation, and shared responsibility.”

The British Council Nigeria described the arrangement as a more affordable and accessible route for Nigerian students to obtain UK postgraduate qualifications without studying abroad.

World.title: Stretford Hill Advocates Durable, Safer Infrastructure at Sustainability Series
World.content:
Vanessa Obioha

Stretford Hill Limited has stressed the need to prioritise quality, safety and durability in infrastructure development, arguing that the value of construction goes beyond the structures delivered to the benefits they provide for people, businesses and communities.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian construction and infrastructure company, Engr. Lakunle Runsewe, made this point as the company participated as a partner and exhibitor at the 10th Sustainability Table Series, held on October 15 and 16 at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos.

“The true value of infrastructure is not measured by what we build alone, but by what it makes possible for people, businesses and communities,” Runsewe said.

He added that infrastructure development required deliberate attention to planning, construction and maintenance, with safety and durability serving as priorities to ensure structures remained functional and secure over time.

The event, themed “Leading the Sustainable Development Agenda: People, Planet, and Prosperity,” brought together policymakers, business leaders and sustainability stakeholders to discuss approaches to sustainable development.

At its exhibition stand, Stretford Hill showcased its capabilities in building construction, civil and structural engineering, project management, interior fit-outs and furnishing, specialised architectural metal works, fabrication and facilities support.

The exhibition also provided an opportunity for the company to engage industry stakeholders, exchange ideas on the built environment and strengthen professional relationships.

The event underscored the importance of public-private sector collaboration in advancing sustainable development, particularly in the construction industry, where effective planning, technical expertise and adherence to quality and safety standards are essential throughout a project’s lifecycle.

Founded in 2013, Stretford Hill provides integrated construction and engineering services.

The company said its approach was guided by diligence, integrity, safety and excellence, with a commitment to delivering construction and infrastructure solutions that meet professional standards and serve the needs of businesses and communities.

World.title: Ibori Mourns Dele Cole, Hails His Contributions to Resource Control, True Federalism
World.content:
Former Delta State Governor, Chief James Ibori has mourned prominent Niger Delta leader, Patrick Dele Cole, praising his unwavering commitment to the struggle for true federalism and resource control.

Cole, who was born on August 4, 1940, in Abonnema, in the Kalabari Kingdom of present-day Rivers State, died in London at the age of 86.

In a statement issued on Sunday, titled “PDC: So Long My Leader,” Ibori described the late Cole as a steadfast advocate of the Niger Delta cause who remained loyal to his roots despite the political implications of his position.

He said Cole played a significant role in the region’s struggle for true federalism and resource control, noting that his commitment to the aspirations of the Niger Delta people remained firm even while he served as a Special Adviser in the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo.

According to Ibori, Cole’s dedication to the region demonstrated his willingness to stand with his people at a time when doing so could attract considerable political costs.

Cole’s political choices, he added, were guided by his commitment to the interests and legitimate aspirations of the Niger Delta people.

“He was a prominent leader in the Niger Delta who stood firmly with us in our struggle for True Federalism and Resource Control. Even while serving as a Special Adviser in President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, he remained committed to his people and their legitimate aspirations.

“His actions reflected deep loyalty to his roots and an unwavering commitment to the Niger Delta cause. At a time when such a stance could carry significant political costs, he chose to stand with his people,”

Ibori who enjoined the family of the late statesman to take solace in God, said his contributions to the development of Nigeria, especially the Niger Delta region will forever be cherished.

World.title: Chess Meets Art in New Festival  by Tunde Onakoya
World.content:
Vanessa Obioha

A new festival proposed by Chess in Slums Africa founder and Guinness World Record titleholder Tunde Onakoya will bring chess and art together in a celebration of Lagos’s vibrant culture.

Announcing the Lagos International Chess Festival on Saturday, October 10, at the Mikano Motors showroom in Lagos, where he celebrated his birthday, Onakoya said the festival would take chess beyond traditional tournaments and introduce the game to a wider audience.

He said the idea was inspired by his love for chess and his travels around the world to play the game. Having experienced chess in different parts of the world, he wants others to visit Lagos and experience it in a new way.

“Chess is an intellectual endeavour, but it is also a game that connects people, and my goal is to inspire everyone to play chess. It has a lot of tremendous benefits. It is a game that has opened my world. I hope this festival achieves that,” he said.

Scheduled for October 2027, the festival will bring together people from different walks of life, including artists, doctors and architects. Proposed activities include a chess and art exhibition, a large-scale tournament for children, matches between grandmasters and a celebrity chess tournament. Organisers also plan to introduce a chess and fashion event and a party celebrating Lagos.

Another proposed attraction is chess on a boat, an idea inspired by the city’s waterways and its relationship with the surrounding lagoon.

The festival’s visual identity also draws on Lagos culture. Its logo combines elements of the Eyo masquerade, a recognisable symbol of the city, with the shape of a rook, one of the principal pieces in chess. The colours are intended to reflect the vibrancy of Lagos.

World.title: Emily Ratajkowski turns heads in red gown at Academy Museum Gala – PHOTOS
World.content:
Model Emily Ratajkowski turned heads in a striking red gown as she attended the Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles. Image: Instagram @emrata

Model Emily Ratajkowski turned heads in a striking red gown as she attended the Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles with her boyfriend, French film director Romain Gavras.

The 35-year-old model joined her 45-year-old partner on the red carpet on Saturday, with the couple posing together for photographs before heading inside the star-studded event.

Ratajkowski opted for a vibrant, figure-hugging dress featuring twisted sleeves and ruched detailing around the waist, while Gavras kept his look classic in a black suit, white shirt and tie.



The appearance offered another public glimpse into the couple’s relationship, which has attracted attention since they were first romantically linked in November 2025.

Emily Ratajkowski and Romain Gavras turn heads

The couple appeared in good spirits as they posed together at the gala, with their latest outing coming weeks after they were reportedly spotted sharing affectionate moments during a trip to Rome.



Emily Ratajkowski and Gavras were first seen kissing in New York in November last year before making their relationship Instagram official in February 2026.

Their appearance at the Los Angeles event adds to a series of public outings since their romance became known.

The model’s relationship with Gavras is also her longest reported romance since her divorce from film producer Sebastian Bear-McClard in 2022.



Following the split, Ratajkowski was linked to several high-profile personalities, including Pete Davidson, Harry Styles and comedian Eric André.

Who is Romain Gavras?

Gavras is a French film director whose work includes the 2018 film The World Is Yours, which screened at the Cannes Film Festival’s Directors’ Fortnight, and Athena, which premiered at the Venice International Film Festival in 2022.

His latest film, Sacrifice, premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2026 and marks his English-language debut.



The film stars Anya Taylor-Joy in a story about a zealot who plans to sacrifice three influential people in an attempt to save the world from destruction.

Gavras has also directed music videos, including Jay-Z, Kanye West and Frank Ocean’s No Church in the Wild, which earned a Grammy nomination in 2013.

He is the son of acclaimed Greek-French filmmaker Costa-Gavras.



Gavras’ previous high-profile relationships

Before dating Emily Ratajkowski, Gavras was romantically involved with British singer Dua Lipa. Their relationship ended in 2023 after approximately eight months together.

He also previously dated singer Rita Ora. The pair were linked in 2020 and reportedly enjoyed holidays together before their relationship ended during the Covid-19 lockdown period.

For Ratajkowski and Gavras, however, their latest red-carpet appearance suggests their relationship continues to develop, with the pair increasingly appearing together at public events.

World.title: World Rugby rankings: Springboks’ lead cut by All Blacks
World.content:
The All Blacks have closed the gap on the Springboks in the latest World Rugby rankings following their Bledisloe Cup win over Australia on Saturday. Image: All Blacks website

The All Blacks have closed the gap on the Springboks in the latest World Rugby rankings following their Bledisloe Cup win over Australia on Saturday.

Dave Rennie’s New Zealanders beat the Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney on Saturday to wrap up a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup triumph, having won the first match 50-19 in Auckland.

Following their win in Australia, the All Blacks picked up 0.46 ranking points to move to 92.27 points, just 0.82 adrift of the Springboks.



Meanwhile, Australia lost 0.46 points and dropped to seventh place overall.

Rank Team Points 1 South Africa 93.09 2 New Zealand 92.27 3 Ireland 88.08 4 France 87.43 5 England 85.68 6 Scotland 84.78 7 Australia 84.43 8 Argentina 82.24 9 Japan 77.28 10 Fiji 76.81 11 Wales 76.38 12 Italy 76.30 13 Georgia 73.94 14 Portugal 69.39 15 USA 67.58 16 Chile 66.94 17 Spain 66.83 18 Uruguay 65.75 19 Tonga 65.14 20 Samoa 64.73

‘Character and courage’

Rennie said post-Test that the All Blacks have rediscovered their confidence after responding to their 3-1 series defeat to the Springboks with the two emphatic victories over Australia.

The All Blacks followed produced a strong response after losing Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series against the world champions.

New Zealand were particularly impressive in the first half, scoring six tries to establish a commanding 36-7 lead at the break.

For Rennie, the performances demonstrated the character and resilience within his squad after a difficult series against South Africa.

“That was excellent,” he said.



“A lot of stuff that we did well last week, we were able to put 40 minutes of that together.”

The coach praised his players’ physicality, ball-carrying, breakdown work and decision-making, which helped New Zealand dominate large portions of the encounter.

“I’m proud of the character and the courage,” Rennie added.

However, he felt the All Blacks could have made the margin even greater had they maintained their first-half accuracy and clinical execution after the interval.

Beauden Barrett delivers reminder of his class

Veteran fullback Beauden Barrett was among New Zealand’s standout performers, scoring two tries in Sydney after limited opportunities during the series against South Africa.

The 147-Test veteran benefited from injuries elsewhere in the squad and made the most of his opportunity, underlining the experience and quality available to Rennie.

The coach was particularly impressed with Barrett’s influence on the team.

“It just highlights how fortunate we are,” Rennie said.

“Beauden’s experience, communication, the quality of his decision-making is excellent. It’s great having him in the mix.”

Barrett’s performance provided a timely boost for New Zealand as they prepare for the next stage of their international campaign.

Injury concerns cloud All Blacks revival

Despite the back-to-back victories, New Zealand still face significant selection concerns ahead of their European fixtures next month.

The All Blacks were already without several key players for the Sydney Test, including Ardie Savea, Leroy Carter, Caleb Clarke, Ruben Love and Richie Mo’unga.

Further concerns emerged after Shannon Frizell and Samisoni Taukei’aho sustained knocks.

The extent of those injuries will influence Rennie’s selection decisions as he looks to maintain the momentum generated by the victories over Australia.

While the Wallabies results have restored confidence, New Zealand will need to demonstrate that they can sustain their improved performances against stronger opposition.

Codie Taylor explains All Blacks response

Captain Codie Taylor said the squad had taken an honest look at itself following the defeat to South Africa.

Although the 3-1 series result left the players disappointed, Taylor said they believed there were positive elements in their performances against the Springboks that could provide a foundation for improvement.

“We had an honest look at ourselves after that RGR, and you know, as always, you’re never satisfied and we probably walked away from that pretty gutted,” he said.

“But also knowing that we were playing a brand of rugby that we could be really proud of and really grow on.”

Taylor said winning the Bledisloe Cup and following it with another convincing performance in Sydney had helped restore confidence within the squad.

He also acknowledged the mental challenge of meeting the standards expected of the All Blacks.

“I thought we did that for majority of the game, so really proud of the lads,” he said.

The two victories over Australia provide New Zealand with renewed momentum after their series defeat to the Springboks.

However, their upcoming European campaign will offer another opportunity to measure their progress against international opposition.

World.title: Leanne Manas ‘forced to leave’ Morning Live? SABC responds
World.content:
The SABC has distanced itself from claims Leanne Manas is leaving Morning Live. Images via IG

A TikTok account, in Leanne Manas’s name, claims that she has been “forced” to leave her longtime position as co-anchor of the SABC breakfast show, Morning Live.

The posts have implied that racial discrimination is the motive behind her alleged exit.

SABC RESPONDS TO VIRAL LEANNE MANAS TIKTOK VIDEOS

On TikTok, an account bearing the name Leanne Manas has claimed that she was leaving the SABC breakfast show, Morning Live.



The account has over 20 000 followers and almost 300 000 likes, and is one of several unverified accounts that ar believed to be impersonating the TV anchor.

One of the posts reads: “Stop racism in South Africa. I’m being forced to resign from Morning Live”.

Another reads: “After 22 years of working for the SABC, I have decided to resign”



On its official platform, the SABC distanced its claims from the social media posts.

It shared: “SABC News wishes to clarify that reports circulating on social media regarding Morning Live Anchor Leanne Manas’ alleged resignation from the organisation are false.

“We encourage the public to refrain from sharing unverified information and to rely on credible sources and verified accounts for accurate updates. 

SABC News wishes to clarify that reports circulating on social media regarding Morning Live Anchor Leanne Manas’ alleged resignation from the organisation are false. We encourage the public to refrain from sharing unverified information and to rely on credible sources and… pic.twitter.com/oPPRkdFIAs — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 18, 2026

WHEN DID SHE JOIN THE BREAKFAST SHOW?

Leanne Manas joined Morning Live in 2004 as co-anchor alongside her late colleague, Vuyo Mbuli.

She shared on her Instagram account: “The nerves got the better of me, but as I walked onto that set, I was welcomed by the friendliest SABC crew who embraced me from the moment I arrived. Sitting next to the formidable Vuyo Mbuli, I realised I was going to be okay.



“In fact, I was better than okay; I was on top of the world. Something snapped inside of me that day, and the passion for what I do grew so strong that I knew this was what I wanted my career to be for as long as I possibly could”.

In 2024, she marked her 20th anniversary of helming the breakfast show.

“It certainly hasn’t been easy, but it has been a privilege and honour”, she added.



In June, Leanne Manas took a short break from Morning Live to recover from ankle ligament reconstruction surgery. She returned a few weeks later.

World.title: Comrades Marathon champion George Kusche shines at Amsterdam Marathon
World.content:
South Africa's George Kusche won the 2026 Comrades Marathon in record-breaking fashion on Sunday morning. Image: Comrades Marathon

South Africa’s reigning Comrades Marathon champion George Kusche delivered a star performance at the Amsterdam Marathon on Sunday, setting a new personal best of 2:10:09 over the 42.2km distance.

The Nedbank Running Club athlete finished 26th overall after taking more than three minutes off his previous marathon best in another significant milestone in his road-running career.

Kusche, who has established himself as one of South Africa’s leading ultra-distance runners, showed his ability to compete over the marathon distance with an impressive display on the international stage.



George Kusche makes major marathon breakthrough

The 2:10:09 performance represents a substantial improvement for Kusche, who has built his reputation through his achievements in South African road running.

Although best known for his success in the 2026 Comrades Marathon, the 37-year-old’s latest result in Amsterdam highlights his progress over the shorter marathon distance.

His 26th-place finish provides a clear measure of his performance against the field, while the new time marks an important benchmark for his future marathon ambitions.



From Comrades Marathon glory to international marathon racing

Kusche’s success in this year’s Comrades Marathon has made him a prominent name in South African distance running.

He covered the 85.777km in a record-setting time of 5:15:56, setting a new ‘Up’ run record between Durban and Pietermaritzburg.

Meanwhile, Kusche was not the only South African to produce an impressive performance in Amsterdam.



Cwenga Nose, representing Phantane Athletics Club, made an outstanding marathon debut, clocking 2:09:35 to finish 23rd overall, breaking the 2:10 barrier on debut.

Lemi Berhanu (Ethiopia) won the men’s race with a time of 2:03:32, narrowly missing the course record. Nicholas Kipkorir (Kenya, 2:03:38) finished second, and Patrick Mosin (Kenya, 2:03:57) took third.

World.title: Proteas vs Australia: Rain the big winner on Day 1 at St George’s Park
World.content:
Australia's Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls on a rain-shortened first day of the second Test against South Africa at St George's Park on Sunday. Image: MARCO LONGARI / AFP

Australia’s Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls on a severely rain-shortened first day of the second Test against South Africa at St George’s Park on Sunday.

South Africa, sent in to bat, were 20 for two when play was called off after two short periods of play during which only 12.2 overs were bowled.

READ | Cricket club refuses murder-accused Tristan Perez membership



Crucial blows

But it was enough for Boland to strike two crucial blows.

He dismissed Aiden Markram and David Bedingham – South Africa’s most successful batsmen in their defeat in the first Test in Durban.

Coming on as first change, Boland bowled Markram for 11 with his tenth delivery, a ball which nipped in off the pitch to crash into Markram’s middle stump off an inside edge. Then he produced a ball which seamed away to have Bedingham caught behind first ball.



Boland was making only his 20th appearance in Australia’s 50th Test since making a sensational debut when he took six for seven against England in Melbourne in December 2021.

He has had to wait his turn behind Australia’s world-class pace trio of skipper Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.

All-seam attack

Boland got his chance on Sunday, replacing off-spinner Nathan Lyon when Australia decided to field an all-seam attack on a green-tinged pitch in heavily overcast conditions.



“Scotty Boland has been incredible whenever he’s played Test cricket,” Cummins said after winning the toss.

“When there’s anything in the wicket, he gets a lot of seam movement, super accurate, and then even if it does flatten out, he brings control, experience. He’s the whole package.”

Rain started falling 10 minutes after the toss and delayed the start by two hours. Markram hit two boundaries off Starc before play was halted with South Africa on 11 for no wicket after 5.3 overs.



Boland was brought into the attack after the players returned in the afternoon and immediately struck a challenging length.

Three changes for Proteas

New cap Marques Ackerman was unbeaten on five and captain Temba Bavuma was on four when rain brought what proved to be the final stoppage of the day.

Boland for Lyon was the only change from the Australian team that won the first Test by 214 runs.



South Africa made three changes, with fast bowler Kagiso Rabada returning after recovering from a hamstring injury. He replaced left-arm spin bowler Keshav Maharaj.

Ackerman and fellow batsman Matthew Breetzke replaced Tristan Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne with Ryan Rickelton taking over from Verreynne as wicketkeeper.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: The small municipality that grew its tax base by 4 800 people in one year
World.content:
The Drakenstein Municipality has had incredible success.

The municipality is the third richest in the Western Cape after the City of Cape Town and Stellenbosch.

Unlike other Western Cape municipalities, Drakenstein’s economy is supported by a large group of middle-income taxpayers.



What’s Driving Taxpayers to this Municipality?

Between 2023 and 2024, Drakenstein added 4 862 taxpayers to its population, according to tax statistics from the South African Revenue Service (SARS).

Stellenbosch, the Western Cape’s richest municipality, added 3 195 taxpayers.

Cape Town, the second-richest municipality, added 63 611.

During that year, the taxable income in Drakenstein rose by R1.6 billion.

This means the average income among its newest residents is R341 834.

Drakenstein is also the only one of the top 3 wealthiest Western Cape municipalities to have a decrease in the average taxable income.



The average taxable income declined by R325 in the latest data.

The municipality has successfully won over the middle class.

Many of Drakenstein’s newer residents are drawn to the area for its affordable property market, excellent service delivery, and good public schools.

The average home price in Wellington was R1.7 million in 2025.

In Cape Town, the average price was R2.1 million and in Stellenbosch, R2.2 million.

Middle Class Utopia

Drakenstein Municipality is well-run.

According to recent reports, the municipality has achieved 99.1% Capital Expenditure.

It also implemented a rates cap after legal consultation and collaboration with the National Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (CoGTA).

Now, rates on a 3-bedroom home in Paarl are R500. A home in Cape Town has rates of R1 014, and in Stellenbosch R750.

The area also has the fewest poverty-stricken residents of the Western Cape’s richest municipalities.

Only 18 707 residents in the municipality receive a Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant.

In Stellenbosch, 31 020 residents receive the grant, and 310 794 get it in the City of Cape Town.

The limited reliance on government assistance is reflected in the municipality’s improved crime statistics.

Stellenbosch has a 9.9% crime rate, while Wellington has a 5.71% crime rate and Paarl a 5.96% rate.

World.title: Jacob Zuma’s TRC testimony postponed – here’s what we know
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma's testimony before the TRC Cases Inquiry has been postponed following his recent hospitalisation. The commission has yet to confirm a new date. Image: X/Gagasi FM

Former president Jacob Zuma’s appearance before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) Cases Inquiry has been postponed following his recent hospitalisation.

Zuma was scheduled to testify on Thursday, 22 October, before the judicial commission chaired by retired Constitutional Court Justice Sisi Khampepe.

According to a report, the decision followed discussions between Zuma’s legal representatives and the commission.



A new date for his appearance has not yet been confirmed.

ZUMA’S HEALTH CONCERNS DELAY TESTIMONY

The postponement comes amid concerns about the 84-year-old former president’s health, which also forced the MK Party to cancel its election manifesto launch in Mbombela, Mpumalanga.

MK Party parliamentary leader John Hlophe previously acknowledged that cancelling the event was necessary given Zuma’s condition.



Meanwhile, the Jacob Zuma Foundation has appealed for privacy, saying it would not provide minute-by-minute updates on his recovery.

Foundation spokesperson Mzwanele Manyi criticised repeated media enquiries, describing them as an invasion of Zuma’s privacy and dignity.

His health will now be a factor in determining when he can give evidence before the commission.



MBEKI NEXT TO TESTIFY BEFORE TRC INQUIRY

While Zuma’s appearance remains on hold, former president Thabo Mbeki is scheduled to testify on Monday, 19 October, and Tuesday, 20 October.

The inquiry is investigating allegations that political interference prevented the prosecution of apartheid-era crimes referred by the original Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

President Cyril Ramaphosa established the judicial commission in May 2025 to determine whether senior political figures or government officials influenced decisions to delay or abandon criminal prosecutions.



The proceedings are expected to shed light on why several cases remained unresolved decades after the end of apartheid.

ZUMA AND MBEKI’S LEGAL CHALLENGE

Both former presidents previously challenged Khampepe’s appointment as chairperson, raising concerns about her impartiality because of her earlier involvement in the original TRC and the National Prosecuting Authority.
