Nairobi sits at about 1,800 metres, so days are mild and nights are cool all year. That altitude is a draw for people who dislike tropical heat, and it spares the city much of the coast’s humidity.

The trade-off is distance and traffic. A school run or a hospital visit can take an hour each way at peak times, so many families choose a home by where the school is. Our healthcare guide explains where the private hospitals are.

2. Kilimani and Westlands: Apartments Near the Action

Kilimani and Westlands are apartment districts close to offices, shops and restaurants. They suit single professionals and couples who want to walk to dinner and keep a short commute.

Street-level crime is the main concern in dense parts of the city, and the State Department lists armed carjacking and mugging among the risks across Kenya. Choose a building with a guarded entrance, avoid walking at night and use a ride-hailing app rather than hailing a street taxi. Our Is Kenya safe for expats guide covers the precautions in detail.

3. Diani Beach: The Coast Lifestyle

Diani is a long stretch of white-sand beach in Kwale County, south of Mombasa, and the favourite coastal base for foreign residents. We did not find Kwale County among the areas the US advisory tells Americans not to visit, but the advisory does single out stretches of the coast for terrorism and kidnapping risk.

A Kenya Airways Boeing 737 at Moi International Airport, Mombasa, in August 2025. Many coastal visitors fly into Mombasa and travel on by road. Photo: Bahnfrend, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Residents and tourists in Diani have long raised concerns about insecurity, and Kenyan press reports describe new street lighting and extra patrols meant to restore night-time activity. Ask neighbours and your landlord about specific roads and the hours when they feel safe before you commit to a lease.

4. Mombasa: Port, Railway and Heat

Mombasa is Kenya’s main port and the coastal end of the Madaraka Express railway. The train takes about 4 hours 30 minutes to Nairobi, with three daily departures at 08:00, 15:00 and 22:00, and Economy fares of KSh 1,500 (about US$12) one way.

We rank Mombasa last for newcomers because of heat, humidity and fewer foreign-friendly services than Nairobi. It still suits people who work in shipping or trade, or who want a historic coastal city.

Entry and Residency: What the Rules Say

Most foreign visitors, including US citizens, must apply online for an electronic travel authorisation, known as an eTA, before they travel. Citizens of some countries and East African Community members are exempt. The official eTA portal says applications are usually processed in about three days and advises applying at least two weeks ahead.

Living or working in Kenya needs a separate permit, and landing without a visa is not permission to work. Our residency visa guide sets out the classes, and our guide to the eTA and travel insurance rule covers what visitors must buy.

What It Means for You

If you are scouting Kenya, rent for a few months in two areas before you commit to either. Visit in the dry and the rainy season, and confirm travel advice with your embassy before booking.

Kenya observes Mashujaa Day, a national holiday, on Tuesday 20 October 2026, and September inflation was 6.8%, according to the national statistics bureau. Our retirement guide, Nairobi cost of living guide and Kenya hub carry the rest.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm current rents by suburb or a crime rate for any Nairobi district, and we could not read the current State Department advisory line by line, so its wording is taken from reports of it. The ranking is therefore a judgement about services and published warnings, not a measured safety index.

Fares, entry rules and advisories change often. Check the official sources listed below before you travel or sign a lease.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best place to live in Kenya for expats?

For most American expats, Nairobi’s Karen and Gigiri area is the best base because it has the greatest concentration of international schools, embassies and UN staff. Kilimani and Westlands rank second for apartments and walkability.

Is Kenya safe for American expats?

The US State Department rates Kenya Level 2, exercise increased caution, and warns against travel to Nairobi’s Eastleigh and Kibera and to several border and north-coast areas. Most expats live in a few gated suburbs and take the precautions the embassy lists, such as avoiding night driving and sharing less about travel plans.

Do Americans need a visa to live in Kenya?

Visitors, including US citizens, apply online for an electronic travel authorisation (eTA), which the official portal says is usually processed in about three days. Living or working in Kenya needs a separate permit or residency class, covered in our Kenya residency guide.

Is Diani Beach a good place to live?

It suits people who want a beach lifestyle, and it sits in Kwale County, which we did not find among the areas the US warning tells Americans not to visit. Security has needed attention, so ask local residents and your landlord about specific roads before you sign a lease.

How do you get from Nairobi to Mombasa?

The Madaraka Express train takes about four and a half hours and runs three times a day. Reported one-way fares are KSh 1,500 (about US$12) in Economy and KSh 4,500 (about US$35) in First Class.

Why is Nairobi popular with international organisations?

The United Nations Office at Nairobi in Gigiri hosts the headquarters of the UN Environment Programme and UN-Habitat. That draws diplomats, aid workers and consultants, and it supports a large market for expat housing and schools.

Sources

World.title: Vida Loca Drug Suspect Sent to Madagascar
World.content:
A man known as “Vida Loca”, wanted over an alleged cocaine network linking Madagascar, Mauritius and Southeast Asia, was extradited from Spain to Madagascar on Friday 16 October 2026. The case matters to US readers because it touches Indian Ocean drug routes, money laundering through Asian hubs and Interpol cooperation.

Key Facts —Who. The suspect known as “Vida Loca”, a Franco-Mauritian man and naturalised French citizen, reportedly named as Maurice Vitto Laurent Jeevanji, aged 57. —What. Extradited on charges of high-risk drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal association; he is a suspect and is presumed innocent until a court rules. —Where. From Spain to Madagascar; the alleged network ran between Madagascar, Mauritius and Southeast Asia. —When. Friday 16 October 2026. —Why it matters. The case involves Indian Ocean cocaine routes, money laundering through Asian hubs and cooperation with Interpol. —Status. As of 18 October 2026, 11:00 GMT

What We Know

Spain extradited the suspect known as “Vida Loca” to Madagascar on Friday 16 October 2026, according to Newsmada and Défi Media. Spanish authorities had detained him on an international arrest warrant from Madagascar’s Pôle Anti-Corruption (PAC), the country’s anti-corruption unit, and on an Interpol Red Notice.

Défi Media has named him as Maurice Vitto Laurent Jeevanji, aged 57, in a January 2026 profile. He is a Franco-Mauritian man and a naturalised French citizen, while other outlets call him Laurent Vitto.

According to Newsmada, the charges are high-risk drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal association (“association de malfaiteurs” in French). These are accusations at this stage, and he is presumed innocent until a court rules.

Newsmada reported that the extradition followed judicial cooperation between Madagascar and Spain. The ministries of Justice, Foreign Affairs and Public Security, Interpol and Spanish authorities all took part.

An Interpol Red Notice asks police in member countries to locate a wanted person and hold them provisionally pending extradition. Spain acted on both that notice and the Madagascan warrant.

Antananarivo, Madagascar. (Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Madagascar Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Network Investigators Describe

Défi Media reported in January 2026 that investigators suspect “Vida Loca” of being the central figure and financier of an international cocaine network. The network allegedly ran between Madagascar, Mauritius and Southeast Asia, touching Bangkok, Pattaya, Antananarivo and Port Louis.

The same reporting says he allegedly financed the Appaya clan, a group named in the reporting. It also says Spain had opened its own drug investigation.

Défi Media reported that 16 kg of cocaine was seized in Madagascar in February 2025. It also says three Mauritians and five Malagasies were arrested in early 2025.

Défi Media reported that a confidential PAC report on the matter went to Mauritius’ Financial Crimes Commission (FCC). The FCC is among the Mauritian bodies investigating the case.

Défi Media further reported that an intercepted phone call in January 2025 reportedly contained instructions on transporting drugs and threats. We have not independently verified this, and none of it has been tested in court.

What Is Not Known

The date of his arrest in Spain has not been made public in the reports we reviewed. Nor is it known where he is being held in Madagascar or when he will appear in court.

No plea has been reported, and no statement from his lawyers has appeared in the coverage we saw. No official figure for the money involved has been published in those reports either.

Motives, roles and guilt are matters for the court, and we do not speculate on them. Défi Media’s account of the network rests on investigators’ suspicions, not on a verdict.

What It Means for Readers in the United States

This is a story about transit routes and money, not about a single country. Défi Media describes a network spanning the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia, touching hubs such as Bangkok and Pattaya.

The case also shows Interpol cooperation at work, with Spain acting on a Red Notice and a warrant issued in Madagascar. For compliance teams, it is a reminder that cross-border money laundering cases can involve several jurisdictions at once.

Mauritius’ Financial Crimes Commission is named in the reporting as one of the bodies investigating. Madagascar’s anti-corruption unit issued the arrest warrant that led to his detention in Spain.

For related coverage, see our reports on Madagascar Seeks 11 Chinese Convicts and Mauritius Sergeant Charged After Woman Shot. Our country pages for Mauritius and Madagascar carry further reporting.

The suspect is now in Madagascar and the charges are yet to be tested in court. Further official detail on his detention, hearing and plea would show how the case proceeds.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is “Vida Loca”?

“Vida Loca” is an alias used for a Franco-Mauritian man and naturalised French citizen. Défi Media has named him as Maurice Vitto Laurent Jeevanji, aged 57, while other outlets call him Laurent Vitto.

What is he accused of?

Newsmada reports the charges as high-risk drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal association. He is a suspect and is presumed innocent until a court rules.

When and how was he extradited?

He was extradited from Spain to Madagascar on Friday 16 October 2026. Spain had arrested him on a warrant from Madagascar’s anti-corruption unit and on an Interpol Red Notice.

What is still unknown?

The date of his arrest in Spain, his place of detention, a court date and his plea have not been reported. No statement from his lawyers has been published in the coverage we reviewed.

World.title: Brazil Court Sets Rules on Campaign Channels
World.content:
The Supreme Federal Court in Brasília, which set new liability rules for social media platforms in June 2025 (Photo: Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Sunday, 18 October, 5:58 a.m. ET · Source: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE)

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Friday 16 October, the electoral court (TSE) unanimously approved rules on when a supporters’ messaging channel counts as part of a campaign.

The trigger Conflicting rulings on “Exército do Lula”, a WhatsApp channel run by federal deputy André Janones, pushed the court to set clear criteria.

Meta order On Thursday 15 October, Judge Marco Aurélio Bellizze ordered Meta to treat both candidates equally, under a fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000) a day.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 81% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 19.5% (18 October, 5:54 a.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 80% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 20% and 21% ), as of 18 October, 12:00 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The court has not said how it will treat other supporter channels, and campaigns can still challenge individual cases.

Brazil’s electoral court entered the last week before the Brazil election 2026 runoff with new rules for online campaigning. On Friday 16 October, the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously approved a resolution on when a supporters’ channel is legally linked to a campaign.

The vote on Sunday 25 October decides who runs Latin America’s largest economy, so online disputes between the two campaigns matter beyond Brazil. The court is the body that supervises the election and rules on campaign conduct, including on social media and messaging apps.

What the New Campaign Channel Rules Say

The resolution was drafted by Judge André Mendonça and sets out objective signs that a channel is tied to a candidacy, CNN Brasil reported. They include the use of campaign money or material resources, technical support from the campaign, official promotion of the channel and campaign guidance on what it publishes.

The signs are not cumulative, and one objectively verifiable element can be enough, CNN Brasil said. A channel linked to a campaign must be registered with the electoral authorities and follow the propaganda rules for its platform.

Spontaneous support from individual voters is not enough on its own to show a link, according to ICL Notícias. The aim is to separate organised campaign operations from ordinary political speech.

Why the Court Acted After Conflicting Rulings

The resolution followed a dispute over “Exército do Lula”, a WhatsApp channel administered by federal deputy André Janones of the Rede party, Gazeta do Paraná reported. Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign had complained to the court that the channel spread disinformation.

Two TSE judges then issued opposite decisions on whether the channel could stay online, the same outlet said. On Sunday 11 October, the court’s president, Kassio Nunes Marques, suspended it, and the electoral ombudsman, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, reversed that the same day for lack of evidence.

Nunes Marques suspended it again on Tuesday 13 October unless it was registered, and the channel was back online around 14 October, according to Folha de Pernambuco.

Meta Ordered to Treat Both Candidates Equally

A day earlier, on Thursday 15 October, Judge Marco Aurélio Bellizze ordered Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, not to restrict the reach of presidential candidates unequally, Bahia Notícias reported. The order carries a fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000 at 5.07 reais per dollar) for each day of non-compliance.

Lula’s campaign had told the court that Meta’s artificial intelligence tool refused to generate images of the president while accepting requests about Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the same report. The judge found signs of a failure in Meta’s control system but said the evidence did not show deliberate or systematic misconduct.

What It Means for US Readers

Brazil’s court is now setting the online ground rules for a vote that moves Brazilian stocks, the real and trade ties with Washington. US-listed Brazilian shares can swing on court rulings as much as on polls in the final days.

The Meta order also shows a foreign platform facing daily fines from a Brazilian court during an election. Expect more rulings of this kind before 25 October, and read each as a decision on one case rather than a signal about the outcome.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro an 81.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 19.5% (18 October, 5:54 a.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$187 million in total bets, and our Brazil election odds page tracks them.

The court has not said whether other supporter channels will be reviewed or whether the new criteria will be applied to channels already online. It is also not known how Meta will respond to the order or whether the fine will ever be enforced.

Neither ruling measures any effect on voters, and polls remain the guide to the race. Our Brazil election polls tracker lists every survey.

On Friday 16 October, the TSE unanimously approved criteria for when a supporters’ messaging channel counts as part of a campaign. One objectively verifiable sign, such as campaign funding or guidance, can be enough.

Why did the court act now?

Judges had issued conflicting rulings on the WhatsApp channel “Exército do Lula”. The runoff is on Sunday 25 October, so the court wanted clear rules for the final week.

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened Vox Brasil, a Brazilian polling institute, published a runoff survey that puts Lula narrowly ahead in a technical tie.

The numbers Lula has 51% of valid votes and Flávio Bolsonaro 49%, while raw totals read 46.4% to 44.6%.

Margin of error 2.15 percentage points at 95% confidence, so the 1.8-point raw gap is inside the margin.

Still open Most other recent surveys, including Datafolha and Quaest, have Flávio ahead by the same 51% to 49% margin.

Vox Brasil, a Brazilian polling institute, put Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, at 51% and Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, at 49% of valid votes in a runoff survey reported from 11:01 p.m. ET on Saturday 17 October. The result keeps the Brazil election 2026 race a technical tie.

The vote on Sunday 25 October decides who runs Latin America’s largest economy, which matters for Brazilian stocks, the real and trade with Washington. What the Vox Brasil Poll Found

Vox Brasil Opinião e Pesquisas interviewed 2,100 voters aged 16 or older from 15 to 17 October, with a 2.15-point margin of error and a 95% confidence level, Metrópoles and tmc.com.br reported. The survey is registered with the electoral court under number BR-04332/2026.

Lula has 46.4% and Flávio Bolsonaro 44.6% of all answers, with 5% blank, null or for neither and 3.9% undecided, according to Metrópoles. Once those answers are set aside, the split is 51% to 49% in Lula’s favour.

Voters were also asked whom they would never back, and 45.3% named Lula and 45.3% named Flávio, Metrópoles reported. Rejection is a measure of how many voters a candidate cannot win over.

If you hold Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, polls that disagree on the leader can mean price swings until the result is known. A single survey does not settle the race, and the 2-point gaps in most polls sit inside their margins of error.

If you follow US politics or trade, the winner will set Brazil’s course with Washington for the next four years. Read the average of all polls, not one survey, and treat each result as a snapshot of the days of the interviews.

World.title: Help needed to recover bag with passport, US cash and visa left at Western Border
World.content:
Help needed to recover bag with passport, US cash and visa left at Western Border

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A San Ignacio family is asking the public for help to recover a bag left behind at the Belize Western Border.

According to the family, a woman forgot her black Michael Kors tote bag on a bench outside the money exchange booth near the taxi stand on the night of Monday, October 12, while waiting for her ride.

The bag contained US cash, her passport with an American visa, a credit card and other personal belongings.

The family says video footage appears to show a woman in red shorts and a black blouse picking up the bag and getting into a red car.

They are asking anyone who can help identify the person or vehicle to come forward. A reward is being offered.

If you have information, please call or WhatsApp 610 8117.

World.title: 24 live rounds and suspected cocaine found hidden under cement block in Orange Walk
World.content:
24 live rounds and suspected cocaine found hidden under cement block in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Orange Walk police have recovered live ammunition and suspected cocaine hidden in an empty lot in Orange Walk Town.

Police say that around 8:00pm on Friday, October 16, officers from the Orange Walk GI3 Unit acted on information that someone had hidden something in a bushy lot at the corner of Chips Alley and Cabbage Street.

During checks, an officer found a green plastic bag tucked under a cement block.

Inside were 24 live 9mm rounds, 13 Luger brand and 11 S&B brand, along with a small plastic bag of white powder suspected to be cocaine.

The suspected cocaine weighed 7.3 grams.

No one was in the area at the time, and both the ammunition and drugs were sealed and logged as found property.

World.title: Teen reports being beaten with belt by stepfather in Orange Walk
World.content:
Teen reports being beaten with belt by stepfather in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 13 year old boy from Orange Walk District has reported to police that he was struck with a belt by his stepfather.

The boy visited the Orange Walk Police Station on Friday, October 16, accompanied by his biological father.

He told police that earlier that afternoon, his stepfather became upset after seeing his younger sibling walking with some boys the teen knew from school. He said his stepfather then lashed him with a belt on his hand and lower back.

According to the report, the boy was then told to pack his belongings and leave to stay with relatives. He later made his way to his father’s home, and his father took him to the police station.

A medico legal form was issued. The boy has been placed in the care of his father, and both parents have been instructed to report to the Human Services Department on Monday, October 19, for a follow up.

World.title: ATM Cave and Barton Creek closed as river levels rise
World.content:
ATM Cave and Barton Creek closed as river levels rise

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Actun Tunichil Muknal (ATM) and Barton Creek Archaeological Reserves are closed to visitors today because of elevated river levels.

The Institute of Archaeology of the National Institute of Culture and History (IA/NICH) made the announcement early Sunday morning, October 18.

All water related tour activities have also been suspended at the Nohoch Che’en Archaeological Reserve, a popular cave tubing destination.

All other archaeological reserves remain open for visitors.

The IA/NICH says it is monitoring conditions and will provide updates as necessary.

The closures come after days of heavy rain across the country, with an excessive rainfall warning issued by the National Meteorological Service.

World.title: Swerving Toyota stop ends with taxi driver arrested and car impounded
World.content:
Swerving Toyota stop ends with taxi driver arrested and car impounded

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 51 year old taxi driver of Savannah Street, Orange Walk Town, has been charged with failing to provide a specimen.

He is Jaime Gomez.

Police say officers on burglary patrol on San Antonio Road around 10:50pm on Thursday, October 15, saw a white Toyota Corolla swerving from side to side on Savannah Street.

When officers stopped the car, Gomez allegedly got out of the driver’s side staggering, leaving the engine running and headlights on. Officers say they smelled a strong odour of alcohol on his breath.

He was arrested for driving under the influence and taken to the Orange Walk Police Station, where he was asked for a urine specimen. Police say he refused three times.

He was then taken to the Northern Regional Hospital, where, in the presence of a doctor, he again refused to give a urine or blood sample.

Gomez was charged on Friday morning and granted bail to appear in the Orange Walk Magistrate’s Court on Monday, October 19. His car was impounded.

World.content:

Showers and periods of light rain are affecting most areas this morning, but the activity is expected to decrease somewhat by the afternoon. Tonight, a few showers and some light rain will affect mainly the coast, with isolated thunderstorms possible.

Coastal areas will reach a high of 86°F (30°C) with a low of 79°F (26°C). Inland areas will hit 90°F (32°C), cooling to 73°F (23°C). The hills will see a high of 79°F (26°C) and a low of 68°F (20°C).

World.title: NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops
World.content:
NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops

By Zoila Palma: NASA satellites are tracking signs of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean, including rising sea surface temperatures and changes in ocean levels and colour.

According to NASA, one of the first indicators appeared in January 2026, when a wave of warm water known as a Kelvin wave was detected near Micronesia in the western Pacific. By early April, the waves had reached the eastern Pacific, contributing to warmer ocean temperatures and rising sea levels in some areas.

Kelvin waves transport heat across the Pacific Ocean, helping trigger a chain reaction that weakens the trade winds and allows warm water to accumulate farther east. NASA reported that sea levels in parts of the eastern Pacific rose by approximately 1 to 1.3 feet, while levels around Indonesia and northern Australia were 6 to 8 inches below normal.

NASA data also show that sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific are approximately 3 degrees Fahrenheit, or 1.7 degrees Celsius, above the long-term average, with the possibility of further warming in the coming months. These temperature changes are significant because ocean heat influences atmospheric conditions, affecting rainfall and weather patterns around the world.

Another sign of El Niño is a change in the ocean’s colour as populations of microscopic marine plants known as phytoplankton decline in some equatorial Pacific waters.

NASA says that its scientists will continue monitoring El Niño through its fleet of Earth-observing satellites to better understand the phenomenon and its potential effects.

World.title: INSIDE THE SLIGOVILLE STAND-OFF
World.content:
Police are seen on the road leading to the house off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine where three men were killed in an alleged shoot-out with members of the security forces last Friday morning.

“POLICE, we a go pull the door, just wait nuh. Mi nuh waan dead enuh!”

One of the children inside the ill-fated house in the Five Miles area off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine shouted these words as she and two other occupants of the premises seemingly negotiated with law enforcers to cease their gunfire so they could exit the house last Friday amid a stand-off with alleged gunmen inside the building.

A video recording seen by the Jamaica Observer captured some of what was happening inside the house while law enforcers were outside. The 18-minute 25-second video was captured during a WhatsApp video call with relatives during Friday morning’s daring gun battle. The video cuts out for much of the recording, with an onscreen notification saying “video paused”, but the audio can still be heard.

The child, who the Sunday Observer has been told is the 10-year-old girl who was injured in the incident, is heard appealing to one of the occupants of the house to open the door.
