World.title: From spreadsheets to autonomous tractors: AI's growing role in farming
World.content:
Artificial intelligence primarily helps farmers process data in their daily operations, but autonomous agricultural robots and drones are no longer the stuff of science fiction either.

According to Airika Verrev, crop and livestock production manager and consultant at Pajo Ranch, AI's capabilities have improved significantly even in the short time she has been using it. This spring, the food producer tried using AI to compile data in Excel, but the technology was not yet up to the task. By the grain harvest season, however, that had changed.

"These days, I no longer create a single Excel spreadsheet myself. I tell AI what I want and what it should look like, and that's it," Verrev said.

She also uses AI to analyze data and find relevant provisions in legislation. Nevertheless, she said the information it provides must be constantly checked.

Marten Madissoo, assistant professor of agricultural engineering at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, confirmed that the technology does not relieve farmers of the responsibility to evaluate its answers.

"We have to bear in mind that AI is simply a useful tool that allows us to make decisions faster, but we still need to be experts ourselves," he said.

More broadly, Madissoo sees significant potential for machine learning and artificial intelligence in the agricultural sector. Potential applications include logistics, organizing the storage and processing of agricultural products and analyzing fields. However, he said there is no one-size-fits-all solution as the potential applications depend largely on the problem being addressed.

One possibility is to make better use of data that farmers already collect for field records, registers and reports.

"We have the advantage of having data spanning several years. By bringing this data together and developing a model to analyze it, we can achieve those gains," Madissoo said.

At the same time, he reiterated the need to combine agricultural and technical expertise. The relevant indicators must be assessed by people familiar with the fields who can define what they want to learn from the data.

From chat bots to field drones

However, chatbots are just the tip of the iceberg. Marten Madissoo coordinates the work of the AI and Robotics Center AIRE at the Estonian University of Life Sciences. The center focuses on opportunities to improve the competitiveness of industrial companies through artificial intelligence and robotics.

As an example of AI's industrial applications, Madissoo pointed to an AIRE demonstration project at meat producer Nõo Lihatööstus, which tested the use of AI for quality control of packaged products moving along a conveyor belt. The system was designed to detect problems such as poorly attached labels, incorrect dates or defects in a product's appearance.

Researchers at the University of Tartu have also used artificial intelligence to identify field islands in aerial photographs and sort grain. Novaator has previously reported on the Estonian University of Life Sciences' experiments with autonomous agricultural machinery.

The AgXeed AgBot autonomous tractor, jointly tested by the Estonian University of Life Sciences and Baltic Agro. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

New solutions involving agricultural drones could soon emerge. An amendment to the Plant Protection Act is currently being considered by the Riigikogu that would allow plant protection products to be sprayed from unmanned aircraft under certain conditions.

According to Madissoo, several autonomous solutions already exist, but their deployment is hindered by both legal restrictions and the need to ensure safety. For example, he said the Estonian University of Life Sciences' field robot is still firmly in the testing phase. The machine needs to be taught the boundaries of fields and where it can operate.

"It's not exactly science fiction, but it will still take some time before we can put all these technologies and capabilities to use," he said.

In his assessment, repetitive tasks with clearly defined procedures are particularly well suited to automation as machine learning can make them more efficient.

Trust but verify

Airika Verrev believes that, in the future, combining data with the help of AI will make farming significantly more precise. For example, AI could analyze aerial and drone photographs to help determine how much fertilizer or plant protection products need to be ordered for the upcoming season. This could help avoid unnecessary spending.

"The savings could actually be quite substantial. Right now, though, we're still estimating how much to order," she said.

According to Verrev, many producers currently use AI primarily as a more advanced search engine. However, she said a lack of time makes it difficult to keep up with new developments.

Madissoo said businesses' willingness to adopt new technology depends primarily on whether the benefits are clear and the investment is justified.

"How much do I need to invest and how quickly will that investment pay for itself?" he said, summing up the key question facing producers.

However, Madissoo believes that an initial experiment does not have to be expensive. Farmers can start with a chatbot and a specific question, then try analyzing their own data and testing the resulting recommendations on a smaller field, for example. For more complex ideas, he recommends seeking support from universities or AIRE.

"At one conference, someone gave a good example of AI adoption: Horses are still around today, but they have absolutely no significance in the transportation sector. It's the same with AI. You can manage without it, but you'll simply fall behind the mainstream. So I encourage people to use it: Trust, but verify," Madissoo said.

World.title: People increasingly not paying hospital fees
World.content:
Since patient visit fees increased last year, more and more people have been falling behind on payments to hospitals. Patients with outstanding debts can no longer see a specialist.

A year and a half ago, the cost of visiting a doctor quadrupled, with patient visit fees rising from €5 to €20 and daily hospital bed fees doubling from €2.50 to €5. Since then, the number of patients owing money to North Estonia Medical Center (PERH) has doubled, while the total amount owed has tripled.

"Daily hospital bed fees account for about 70 percent of the debt, while visit fees, mainly for emergency department visits, account for the remaining 30 percent," said Anneli Habicht, PERH's head of customer service.

According to Habicht, in about half of cases patients simply forget to pay, while the other half have no intention of paying. Before turning to a debt collection agency, the hospital spends a couple of months trying to recover the money itself.

"When we look at which groups are more likely to owe us money, it seems to be older people approaching retirement age, as well as very young adults. In terms of gender, men tend to be more likely to fall behind on payments," Habicht said.

Last year, nearly 2,200 people owed money to Narva Hospital. The amounts involved are generally small and are usually paid after a reminder.

"In the first nine months of this year, the number of debtors has increased by about 25 percent. At the same time, we haven't seen any behavior that would require us to take aggressive action through debt collection agencies or any signs that people are deliberately trying to avoid their obligations," said Narva Hospital CEO Üllar Lanno.

Tartu University Hospital has not experienced the same problems as its counterparts in northern Estonia.

"The hospital still receives most of its revenue for medical treatment through its contract with the Estonian Health Insurance Fund. Patients' out-of-pocket payments account for less than 3 percent of that. We have half a million outpatient visits a year and perhaps 200 to 400 patients need to be sent payment reminders," said Joel Starkopf, a member of Tartu University Hospital's management board.

According to debt collection agency Julianus Inkasso, the number of claims submitted by hospitals has increased by a few percentage points, although some medical institutions have submitted 10 percent more claims.

"When the visit fee was €5, it was a little easier to pay. If you're in a difficult financial situation, €20 is harder to afford. And if you forget to pay on time, finding that extra money later can be more difficult when you're working with a tight household budget," said Merle Laurimäe, CEO of Julianus Inkasso.

More than half of debtors settle their debts within a year of receiving a letter from the collection agency. However, they must also cover late-payment interest and collection fees of up to €30.

"I think the total could rise to around €55 at most, provided you act in time," Laurimäe said.

World.title: Reform Party unveils campaign slogan as PM touts economic growth
World.content:
Prime Minister and Reform Party chair Kristen Michal says Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average, as Reform pledges a clear course in the 2027 elections.

Speaking at the party's council meeting in Tartu on Saturday, Michal said the largest income tax cut in Estonia's history had doubled economic growth.

"Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average," he said, also citing rising wages, consumption, exports and manufacturing, alongside lower unemployment and easing inflation.

"The Reform Party can say with confidence: our plan is working," the prime minister emphasized. "Estonia has been led through a major test and is now on a solid growth path, moving forward even in the face of headwinds."

He noted that wages are rising, with consumer confidence up and people taking home an average of 10 percent more money this year. Defense spending of 5 percent GDP, he added, is also strengthening security and giving families and businesses confidence to plan for the future.

Even the opposition is starting to see that the Reform Party's plan is working, Michal said, accusing Isamaa and the Center Party of already making plans to form a coalition — potentially joined by the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE).

"The Reform Party is their main enemy for a reason: they can only steal Estonia's prosperity and growth if we're out of the picture," the party chair said, emphasizing that the key issue in the March 2027 elections will be whether this prosperity will continue to grow or be taken away from them.

Michal said that incomes must rise faster than prices, as a wealthier Estonia can invest more in education, healthcare, a cleaner environment and a better quality of life.

"No other party in Estonia stands as firmly for the economy, national defense, liberal principles, Estonian-language education and culture, and European values," he said. "These are the foundations of Estonia's future."

'A clear course for the future'

The Reform Party also unveiled its campaign slogan: "A clear course for the future."

Tartu mayor and party council chair Urmas Klaas said it reflects the party's focus on security, economic growth and opportunities for families and businesses.

He recalled that Reform's "Blue, black and white plan" for Estonia, unveiled in March, centers on building a stronger middle class, bolstering security and making greater use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the economy and government.



"We're running for election to ensure that robust security can give families confidence, people's work and knowledge can create prosperity and technology can help businesses grow and the state operate more efficiently," Klaas said.

MP and Reform Party secretary general Kristo Enn Vaga said the slogan emphasizes that Estonia's future is up to its own choices.

"We in the Reform Party want Estonia to be secure and the economy to grow, because that gives people and businesses more opportunities to carry out their plans," Vaga said. "This is the future we want to build."

World.title: Gallery: Public bomb shelter in Tallinn hidden behind woodland mural
World.content:
A street-level public civil defense shelter in the heart of downtown Tallinn has been transformed with a mural featuring Estonian trees and wildlife.

Located next to Kalev Sports Hall in Tiigiveski Park, the modular concrete shelter cannot withstand a direct missile hit, but it can protect around 20 people from blast waves, shrapnel and debris from an explosion as close as 50 meters away.

Similar shelters are already widely used in Ukraine, including in Kramatorsk.

The concrete module, donated by security company Citysec, is also now fully wrapped in a woodland mural by Colorees Art's Helena Hanni and Vahur Agar, featuring a wild hare, a bear family, an owl in flight and a wolf.

While usually kept closed in peacetime, the shelter was open to visitors on Friday, when officials were on hand to explain its features to the public.

Tallinn unveiled a new street-level civil defense shelter on Juhkentali tänav. October 2026. Source: Ellen Rudi/Tallinn Strategic Management Office

City weighs dozens more shelters

Citysec CEO Eduard Rikkas said the module was developed on a 50-50 basis with partners in Ukraine, where the design has already been in use for years.

Deputy Mayor Tiit Terik (Center) said the shelter door can be opened remotely during an emergency, and will unlock automatically if power or communications fail.

The shelter door, he added, will be kept locked in peacetime.

Tallinn has mapped 40 to 50 potential sites for similar shelters, with public procurement to follow if the city decides to order more.

According to the manufacturer, the shelter model installed on Juhkentali tänav costs up to €70,000.

World.title: US lifts restrictions on Iraqi exchange firms
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed on Sunday that the US Treasury Department has lifted restrictions on several Iraqi exchange companies.

The CBI said in a statement that the US Treasury Department removed the restrictions after verifying that these companies met the standards it established, enabling them to resume the sale of US dollars to travelers.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen compliance with regulatory controls and organize the sale of foreign currency in accordance with approved frameworks, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

In late September, the spokesperson for the Iraqi government confirmed that Iraq received a new shipment of US dollars from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

Al-Aboudi explained that the step comes within the framework of bilateral understandings reached between Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and US officials during his recent visit to the United States.

The United States halted physical dollar supplies to Iraq in April 2026, including a huge cargo worth $500 million, to force Baghdad to limit the influence of Iran-backed armed groups and minimize illegal financial flow.

Washington decided to keep the supplies going in response to the Iraqi government’s efforts to tighten monitoring on dollar distribution, reduce currency abuse, expand electronic payments, and phase out the traditional currency auction system.

The revenues Iraq generates from international oil exports are officially stored in a designated account under the custody of the Federal Reserve Bank, giving Washington significant structural power over Baghdad’s access to physical cash.

The new funds will be used largely for travel-related activities and foreign transfers approved by the CBI.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister and UK National Security Adviser review security and economic ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi received British National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell in Baghdad on Sunday, October 18, 2026, to discuss expanding bilateral relations between Iraq and the United Kingdom, focusing particularly on defense coordination, intelligence sharing, and economic partnerships.

According to an official communique released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Powell extended congratulations to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi on the parliamentary confirmation and completion of his ministerial lineup.

The British envoy commended Baghdad’s ongoing anti-corruption campaign and structural economic reform agenda, affirming the United Kingdom’s backing for the Iraqi government’s institutional modernization and fiscal stabilization policies.

The discussions also addressed shifting geopolitical dynamics across the Middle East, with both sides underscoring the necessity of close multilateral coordination to de-escalate cross-border frictions.

The meeting emphasized joint diplomatic engagement to resolve underlying causes of regional instability, protect critical supply corridors, and anchor long-term security in the region.

World.title: Iraq’s oil output hits 4.4 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Eco Iraq, a digital platform that analyzes economic, energy, and environmental data in the country, revealed on Saturday that oil production during September reached its highest daily average since the beginning of 2026, at 4.39 million barrels per day.

According to the observatory, Iraq’s oil output stayed at normal levels in January and February, averaging more than 4.1 million barrels per day, before falling drastically in March as a result of the military conflict in the Middle East.

Oil output fell to its lowest point in May before gradually recovering in the months that followed.

Iraq’s average daily oil output was 4.09 million barrels in January and 4.14 million barrels in February before falling to 1.9 million barrels in March and 1.63 million in April.

In May, the country’s oil production fell to 1.4 million barrels per day before rising to 1.52 million in June.

The improvement in oil output continued until the third quarter of the year. According to figures from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), average output increased to 2.9 million barrels per day in July, 3.74 million barrels per day in August, and 4.39 million barrels per day in September.

Iraq’s oil production in September reached its highest daily rate since the beginning of 2026, signaling a gradual recovery in output following the sharp decline experienced during the months of war in the region.

World.title: Iraq to appoint Al Halbousi and Al Fayyadh as vice presidents
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi political factions within the governing State Administration Coalition have reached a preliminary agreement to reactivate the long-dormant positions of Vice President of the Republic, an informed political source revealed on Sunday, October 18, 2026.

Under the emerging cross-party consensus, the leadership posts are slated to be assigned to Taqaddum Party leader and former Parliament Speaker Mohammed Al-Halbousi alongside Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh.

According to the source, the prospective appointments will mirror the financial compensation model adopted for deputy prime ministers, restricting allocations solely to nominal salary entitlements without authorizing supplementary office operational budgets or creating new civil service staff quotas.

The financial restraint is designed to forestall public criticism and prevent administrative expansion within executive payrolls while accommodating broad-based political power-sharing requirements across key coalition partners.

The source noted that restoring the two vice-presidential slots has featured prominently across bilateral consultations and plenary coalition assemblies as a stabilizing mechanism for the current parliamentary cycle.

The political maneuvering follows action taken by the Council of Representatives on Thursday, October 15, when lawmakers ratified three deputy prime ministers and filled eleven ministerial portfolios—including vacant and newly established ministries—within Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s cabinet, while deferring a vote on the Ministry of Migration and Displaced.

World.title: Central Bank of Iraq raises housing loan allocations to 3 trillion dinars
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) announced on Sunday, October 18, 2026, an expansion of its financial allocations supporting the national housing sector, increasing the designated lending portfolio to three trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $1.97 billion).

The initiative is aimed directly at addressing the high volume of citizen applications seeking to purchase apartments and residential units inside organized housing complexes across Iraqi governorates.

According to an official administrative directive issued by the Central Bank, the decision is enacted pursuant to the provisions of CBI Law No. 56 of 2004, as amended.

The measure triples the previous funding ceiling specified in a prior regulatory directive dated August 22, 2024, raising the aggregate financing cap from one trillion dinars to three trillion dinars while retaining the existing operational terms, repayment criteria, and credit conditions.

The directive instructed the Director General of the relevant specialized lending institution to visit the Central Bank’s headquarters in Baghdad to formally sign the contractual annex required for the allocation increase and finalize administrative protocols.

The liquidity injection expands mortgage-backed real estate credit, stimulates the domestic construction industry, and bridges the acute housing deficit by enabling middle-income citizens to secure homeownership inside modern investment residential compounds.

World.title: PMF’s ammunition depot explodes in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered investigation into the circumstances surrounding an explosion at an ammunition depot in a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) base in the capital, Baghdad, according to the Iraqi Security Media Cell (ISMC).

Al-Zaidi stressed the need to expedite the investigation to find out the specific reasons for the incident and implement all essential safety measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.

The PMF announced on Saturday that five of its members had been wounded following an explosion at an ammunition depot located at one of its bases in eastern Baghdad.

The PMF confirmed in a statement that a fire—triggered by the explosion of a stockpile of damaged ammunition at one of its headquarters in eastern Baghdad—has been brought under control.

The statement indicated that the explosion caused minor injuries to five personnel. Specialized committees have initiated an investigation into the incident’s causes, and the findings will be announced upon the investigation’s conclusion.

During the early stages of the military conflict in the Middle East, which has spilled over into Iraq, several PMF headquarters were targeted in devastating bombings carried out by the United States.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt discuss electricity interconnection project through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed on Saturday approaches to expedite the electricity interconnection project between Egypt, Iraq, and Jordan.

According to a statement released by the Egyptian Foreign Ministry, the meeting took place during Abdelatty’s visit for the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers and ahead of al-Zaidi’s scheduled trip to Egypt on November 23.

The meeting addressed measures to improve bilateral cooperation, as well as attempts to de-escalate tensions in the region and promote security and stability.

The two sides discussed the activation of the three countries’ trilateral cooperation mechanism and strategies to advance collaborative projects, notably in electricity interconnection and oil, to promote economic integration and serve the three nations’ common interests.

Abdelatty emphasized the necessity of boosting economic, commercial, and investment relations with Iraq, notably by increasing Egyptian firms’ participation in infrastructure, reconstruction, and development projects.

The Egyptian foreign minister emphasized the possibilities for utilizing Egyptian experience in construction, transportation, energy, agriculture, and pharmaceutical industries.

Abdelatty highlighted the importance of increasing bilateral commerce and facilitating Egyptian products’ access to the Iraqi market.

Additionally, Abdelatty underlined Egypt’s unwavering support for Iraq’s unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, opposing foreign involvement in its internal affairs.

The Egyptian foreign minister also praised the Iraqi government’s efforts to improve national security and reinforce state authority and institutions, including bringing arms under state control.

World.title: Iraqi Interior Ministry Kickboxing Team bags seven medals at world championship
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Interior kickboxing team delivered an impressive performance at the World Kickboxing Championship in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, capturing seven podium medals amidst intense global competition. Running from October 12 to 20, 2026, the international championship brought together 3,043 elite fighters representing 53 participating nations.

According to a ministerial statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the institutional sports delegation was led by Colonel Muayyad Abdul Ridha Abdul Sada, with Colonel Haider Hamid Abdul serving as head coach.

The athletic lineup featured fighters Ammar Ali Kadhim, Hussam Aziz Qate’, Yousef Abdul Nabi Mowzan, Salah Haider Hamid, and Hassan Makki Abdul Kadhim, all of whom mounted deep runs in their respective weight classes.

Ammar Ali Kadhim clinched a gold medal in the 74-kilogram category alongside a silver medal in ring-style competition. In the 63-kilogram division, Hussam Aziz Qate’ secured a gold medal, while Salah Haider Hamid claimed bronze in the 69-kilogram tatami (mat) discipline.

Hassan Makki Abdul Kadhim collected a pair of bronze medals across both the 84-kilogram and 89-kilogram brackets. Meanwhile, Yousef Abdul Nabi Mowzan advanced to the semifinals after defeating his Indian opponent in the opening bout and overcoming an Uzbek contender in the second round, guaranteeing further podium contention for the squad.

World.title: Bimol Akoijam willing to contest Manipur Assembly polls if Congress offers ticket
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam on Sunday said he was willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong constituency if the party offered him a ticket, as he faces a sexual harassment case and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).

Speaking at an event, the Inner Manipur MP said his decision to enter the electoral contest would be guided by the future of the state.

"I am ready to fight elections from Keishamthong (in Imphal West district). If the party offers me a ticket, I will contest the Keisamthong assembly constituency. This decision is for the future of the state," Akoijam said, according to news agency PTI.

The Manipur Assembly elections are due next year.

His remarks come amid an ongoing police investigation into sexual harassment allegations against him and his dismissal from JNU, where he was a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.

JNU dismissal and police investigation

Akoijam was dismissed from the university on October 9 following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment. He has denied the charges and described the university's action as a "witch hunt", claiming he was not given an opportunity to respond to the inquiry committee's findings.





Delhi Police booked him on October 11 following a complaint by JNU's chief security officer. He recently appeared before investigators at the Vasant Kunj North Police Station in New Delhi in connection with the case.

At least 11 female students submitted complaints against Akoijam in May. They alleged that he invited students to his campus residence on the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to harass them.

Some students also alleged that he made obscene and inappropriate remarks in class.

After appearing before investigators, Akoijam said he intended to challenge his dismissal legally.

Speaking to reporters in Imphal on Friday, he said his lawyers were preparing the case and that he would file it within a day or two.

He also said he had cooperated with the police and would continue to do so, while requesting adequate notice for any further questioning because of his responsibilities as an MP.

Akoijam says Manipur's wider crisis needs attention

During his remarks to the media, Akoijam also urged greater attention to the wider situation in Manipur, including the plight of internally displaced people, lawlessness and issues surrounding buffer zones.

"Thousands of people are languishing in relief camps. I donât think my pain is anything greater than the pain of these people," he said, while alleging that the action against him was an attempt to silence his voice.

The MP had earlier said, "Justice will be done," before travelling to New Delhi to join the police investigation.

The allegations have also triggered political reactions in the state. BJP workers staged a protest outside Congress Bhavan in Imphal, demanding Akoijam's resignation and accusing him of bringing disrepute to Manipur. Police prevented the protesters from entering the premises.

Congress spokesperson Hareshwar Goshwami described the protest as a diversionary tactic and accused the ruling party of deflecting attention from killings and the crisis in the state.

Akoijam has maintained that the allegations against him are false and has challenged the process that led to his dismissal. The sexual harassment allegations remain under investigation.

World.title: Global uranium production to dip by 50% by 2040 as demand set to double, says IAEA report; forecast could pinch India too
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Global uranium supply constraints would witness mining production drop by at least 50% by 2040 even as demand is set to double, according to the latest International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) report.

This IAEA forecast on global uranium supply crunch is likely to affect Indiaâs goal to increase its nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047.

According to publication âUranium 2024: Resources, Production and Demandâ, also known as the âRed Bookâ, jointly prepared by Nuclear Energy Agency of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the Agency, global uranium requirements are projected to increase to 90,045 tonnes of uranium (tU) in the low-case scenario and up to 1,42,631 tU in the high-case scenario by 2050, which represents a 50% to 144% increase from todayâs requirements of approximately 60,000 tU.

In contrast to future doubling of uranium requirements, uranium production from existing mines is forecast to decrease by at least 50% by 2040, the report said. âConversion capacity is already insufficient and is projected to fall further behind demand through 2040, highlighting the need for substantial new investment and facility expansions. While global enrichment capacity currently exceeds demand, it remains unevenly distributed geographically,â it said.





The report suggested new mines and expansion or life extension of existing mines, as well as reopening of idled mines, saying these steps will be required for assurance of supply in the future.

Amid the gloomy scenario predicted by IAEA, India has initiated steps to increase nuclear power capacity from current 8,180 MW to 22,480 MW by 2031-32. The expansion includes construction and commissioning of 10 reactors, totalling 8,000 MW, across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Karnataka, and MP.

Additionally, pre-project activities for 10 more reactors have commenced, with plans for progressive completion by 2031-32.

Further, the Modi govt accorded in-principle approval to set up 6 x 1208 MW nuclear power plant in cooperation with the USA at Kovvada in Srikakulam district in Andhra Pradesh.

India procures uranium from a combination of domestic mining and international suppliers: Domestic uranium is mined by Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) from deposits in Jharkhand, Andhra and Karnataka.

It relies primarily on natural uranium for its pressurised heavy water reactors and is gradually shifting toward a closed fuel cycle using plutonium-fuelled fast breeder reactors (FBRs) and eventually thorium.

To supplement limited domestic reserves and back its expansion targets under HANTI Act, 2025, India imports and has active supply arrangements with Kazakhstan, Russia, Canada, Australia (finalised arrangements under a nuclear cooperation deal), Uzbekistan and France.

However, the IAEA prediction of uranium shortfall if drastic steps not taken could pinch India too.

Over the next decade, nuclear fuel production will face increasing demand across all nuclear fuel-related segments due to increasing construction programmes in both established and embarking countries, necessitating the development of new fuel types, including for small modular reactors and advanced reactors, it said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âAn increase in uranium production will require sustained investment with positive market conditions, and the discovery of new deposits will require sustained long-term exploration efforts, bearing in mind that the development of new uranium mines takes 10â15 years on average, from deposit discovery to the start of mining operations,â it said.

In addition, significant and timely investment in exploration and mining/processing technology will be required, including cost-effective uranium extraction techniques for exploiting unconventional deposit types (for example uranium from phosphate and black shale deposits), some of which may become economic if there is a sustained increase in market prices, it suggested.

World.title: Centre issues advisory to Meta, asks it to overhaul content promotion system on Facebook, Instagram
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives.

"

"Ensure that recommendation systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives, and endeavour to provide appropriate diversity of relevant and credible information," an advisory issued by the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), dated October 10, stated, PTI reported.

"Also strengthen mechanisms for rapid identification, review and escalation of content, which is gaining significant reach through recommendation systems and has the potential to cause widespread public confusion, apprehension, violence or disturbance of public order," it added.

While the advisory does not cite any specific incident that led to its issuance, it comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

MeitY also asked Meta to cooperate with law enforcement and other authorised government agencies by providing information or assistance within the timelines prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021.





The ministry noted that certain content relating to "ongoing public events" was being "prominently displayed and recommended to users" on Meta platforms.

Citing the Information Technology Act, 2000, the advisory highlighted the companyâs obligation to exercise due diligence under the IT Rules, 2021, which require intermediaries to inform users about prohibited content, including material likely to cause public disorder or incite a cognisable offence.

MeitY also flagged content presenting old or selectively edited visuals as current events, misleading claims about emergencies, restrictions or police action, and audio-visual material depicting law-and-order situations without adequate context. It also raised concerns over content likely to incite violence and misleading material receiving disproportionate amplification.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The advisory outlined six requirements for Meta, including measures to identify and address prohibited content and review recommendation and ranking systems to ensure misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not "disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users".

MeitY emphasised that the advisory seeks to promote responsible information dissemination while respecting lawful expression and public discourse.

"Meta is advised to ensure that any action taken pursuant to this advisory is consistent with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the IT Rules, 2021, and other applicable laws," the ministry added.

World.title: Shots fired at Tiger Shroff, actor's driver hurt; Bishnoi gang claims responsibility - top developments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Unknown gunmen opened fire at actor

on Sunday, injuring his driver and another person, an autorickshaw driver. The incident took place near Mumbai's Pushpa Park, within the limits of Juhu police station in the western suburb.

According to police, the actor escaped unhurt, while his driver, identified as Firdaus, sustained an injury to his left hand.

"The chain of events leading to the incident is being pieced together," a police official said.

"Shroff is safe and has not sustained any injuries in the firing incident. His driver, identified as Firdaus, and another driver of the autorickshaw, identified only as Chauhan, were injured in the shooting and were rushed for medical treatment," the official added.

Shroff and his driver were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Doctors said the actor had sustained a few abrasions but no bullet wounds.

The third person was taken to Cooper Hospital after sustaining bullet injuries to his chest.

Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibility

Meanwhile, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the attack.

"Ram Ram to all the brothers. Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu take responsibility for what happened to Tiger Shroff today.





We had called him and tried to explain things to him, but he did not understand. So today, we made him understand properly," Anil Pandit said in a Facebook post.

"Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch.

"Note: And those dogs from other groups who think they can gain fame by using our name - we will soon kill them and make them famous.

"Salute to the martyrs," he added.

The authenticity of the claims and their alleged link to the firing had yet to be independently established. Police are investigating the incident and examining the available evidence to determine the motive behind the shooting.

Police launch massive manhunt

Meanwhile, Mumbai Police has launched a manhunt to nab those involved in the incident. Specialised teams are examining CCTV footage from the area for leads.

"The incident occurred while Tiger Shroff was returning in his car.

He was not hit by any bullets and is completely safe. Mumbai Police has formed multiple teams and initiated further action. The forensic team has begun its preliminary analysis, with approximately 15 teams currently working on the case," DCP Mohit Garg said.

"Further information will be shared as it becomes available. As I mentioned, the forensic team is carrying out its investigation. At this stage, it would not be appropriate to disclose specific details regarding the number of rounds fired," he added.

Fadnavis directs Mumbai Police to expedite probe

Meanwhile, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis called the Mumbai Police commissioner to seek details about the firing incident.

He directed the commissioner to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible.

Fadnavis also called Tiger Shroff and spoke with him.

He assured him, saying, âWe are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.â

Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also condemned the incident and said Mumbai Police has formed several teams to track down those who opened fire.

He added that the accused will be given a response in their own language.

"Tiger Shroffâs vehicle was targeted. This incident is deeply concerning and condemnable; I condemn it in the strongest possible terms. I have spoken with the Police Commissioner, and I have also spoken with Tiger Shroff. The Mumbai Police Commissioner has formed several teams to track down those who opened fireâthey will be apprehended and given a response in their own language.

Our current priority is to keep Mumbai and its citizens safe.

Whether it is a celebrity or an ordinary citizen, ensuring their safety is the responsibility of the police and the government, and there will be no negligence in this regard," Shinde said.

"No gang will be spared; we will not let them get away with this. We have seen large-scale gang wars like this before, back in the 1990s. Even then, the Mumbai Police effectively handled the situationâthey dealt with the perpetrators in their own language, ensuring that law and order were maintained.

So, any gang attempting to spread terror here should think twice. This is Mumbai; this is Maharashtra," he added.

Rohit Shetty, Salman Khan among film personalities targeted

Several personalities from the film industry have been targeted in shooting incidents in recent years.

In February this year, five rounds were fired outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing.

World.title: Tiruchendur residents flag water shortage, allege inadequate supply to residential areas
World.content:
Tiruchendur residents have raised concerns over inadequate supply of municipal water to residential areas, further alleging that several lodges and hotels in the region received regular water supply and are able to provide 24x7 water access to their guests, while local residents faced shortages.

Tiruchendur Municipality, which comprises 27 wards has been facing severe water scarcity for the past six months. Residents allege that the majority of the wards receive water only once a fortnight, and water supplied is salty for consumption.

Tamilselvan, a resident of ward 23 said, “The residents of Tiruchendur municipality have been struggling with severe water scarcity for the past six months, and residents are planning to launch a protest in this regard in the coming weeks.”

Explaining the water sources of Tiruchendur municipality, including Kurangani water project and Kaanam water project by Municipal Administration and Water Supply department (MAWS) and Authoor Combined Water Supply Scheme (CWSS) operated by Tamil Nadu Water Supply and Drainage Board, he noted that Kurangani and Kaanam projects had come into halt due to reduced water flow in Tamirabarani river. Consequently, Tiruchendur municipality currently depends on water supplied through Authoor CWSS.

Mr. Tamilselvan added that around 10 lakh litres of water per day had been allotted to the municipality through Authoor CWSS, but the actual supply was less than five lakh litres a day. He said water was currently drawn from Ellappanayakkankulam to meet the deficit, but the water was reportedly salty.

He urged the authorities to take immediate measures to address the drinking water needs of Tiruchendur municipality.

Vasumathi, another resident from Govidhammal Colony alleged that water meant for residential areas was also being supplied to lodges in the region, further aggravating the shortage faced by local residents. She added that a peace committee meeting was held in the first week of October in the presence of Revenue Divisional Officer and other senior officials but no concrete measures had been taken to resolve the issue.

She added that the number of devotees visiting Tiruchendur had been increasing steadily. While acknowledging the need to ensure adequate water supply to Tiruchendur temple to meet the needs of devotees, she said the authorities should also ensure a regular supply of adequate quantities of potable water to residential areas.

Speaking to The Hindu, Thoothukudi District Collector Vishu Mahajan said Tiruchendur’s daily drinking water requirement, based on its population, was 4.34 MLD (Million Litres per Day). However, owing to the poor southwest monsoon and other water shortages, only 3.34 MLD is supplied once in two days.

He added that the influx of devotees had increased the town’s floating population, placing additional pressure on its water resources.

Mr. Mahajan said that three long term measures have been planned to meet the drinking water needs of Tiruchendur, including 3 new wells in Kurangani water source, TWAD’s new pipeline from Authoor pumping station for 2.86 MLD pumping and desalination plant for Tiruchendur temple requirement. As a temporary measure, 8 water lorries are deployed for wards with low supply.

Regarding the supply to lodges and hotels, the Collector noted that the municipality was duty bound to ensure water supply to all residential areas, as well as registered hotels and lodges within its jurisdiction.

World.title: Two-year-old boy dies of suspected malnutrition in Alappuzha
World.content:
A two-year-old boy was found dead at his home here on Sunday in a suspected case of malnutrition, the police said.

An officer of Trikkunnapuzha police station said that according to doctors, the toddler was “acutely anaemic” and appeared malnourished as his weight was 7.6 kg, whereas the normal weight for his age would be closer to 12 kg.

“A histopathology test will confirm whether the toddler’s condition and death were caused due to some illness or malnourishment,” the officer said.

Five other children

He said a case for unnatural death has been registered, and following the results of the histopathology test, the future course of action will be decided. The officer said that the child’s father was an autorickshaw driver living with his wife in Karthikappally and they have five other children, including a newborn. One of their children had died earlier, he added.

The wife was admitted to the government medical college hospital at Vandanam on Saturday to give birth, and the children were at home with the father.

Child welfare committee

On Sunday morning, the father found that the two-year-old boy had died. The child welfare committee took the remaining children into their care, the officer said.

The officer further said that the couple and their children were earlier moved to a shelter home, Gandhibhavan, in view of their poor living conditions. “However, they created problems there and returned to their home here,” he said.

World.title: Why does India need a trained workforce for elderly care?
World.content:
Every day Sreeni wakes up at 4.30 am and checks on his mother. If she is unsteady on waking up, he will assist her to the raised toilet and wait outside as she independently uses it, assuring her that help is just outside. There is a schedule of medicines, clearly sorted and kept by her bedside. The BP monitor and the glucometer reassure him that everything is in the range for her age. He learnt it all by himself, one emergency visit after another to the hospital. Hip pain was ignored till it became a debilitating fracture, a sudden loss of consciousness detected as low sodium — each crisis was a hard lesson in the trial-and-error reality of informal caregiving. Every day millions like Sreeni wake up and perform their respective self-taught routines to take care of their parents or dependants.

As our country’s population ages over the next two decades, the topic of caregiving and the need for formal training for the task will assume larger dimensions, and this is precisely what the Budget 2026-27 has highlighted in a timely manner with the announcement of training of 1.5 lakh caregivers aligned to the National Skills Qualifications Framework.

The NITI Aayog’s August 2026 report “Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047” frames caregiving as an economic activity rather than just welfare work, and this is the first time that such an intention is explicitly articulated by the Government at a national policy level, which indicates that the urgency has been acknowledged by policymakers.

Also Read: India’s growing elderly population needs an integrated care system, says report

To put it in perspective, India’s 60-plus population, estimated at approximately 149 million in 2022, is projected to touch 347 million by 2050, forming roughly 20.8% of the total population. Assuming NITI Aayog’s estimate that 10% of the population today is engaged in caregiving while being untrained and unpaid, the current total works out to about 146 million.

The planned 1.5 lakh formally trained workforce is just a drop in the ocean even by today’s requirements. The caregiving ecosystem will be at a serious juncture if we don’t plan now.

Gender parity in caregiving

For most of its history, India never needed a long-term care system because it had one: the joint family. Three generations under one roof was an insurance contract written in spirit and practised willingly. In the present scenario, with micro family units, most of the time, it is the housewives who take upon themselves the additional task of caregiving, having no formal training, learning by trial and sometimes serious error. Combined with the need to manage their own household chores, such situations increase household stress considerably. The aged who need assistance and the differently abled, about 26.8 million, are surviving, thanks to the love, care and affection of these unpaid, informal care givers.

An NSO survey has worked out that women, on average, spend 299 minutes per day on unpaid domestic work and caregiving, whereas for men it is only 97 minutes. What is required is an appreciation of the situation and the demands of caregiving being shouldered by both genders. A formal training programme, designed exclusively around caregiving, covering the detection of age-related events needing attention in the elderly, assessment of needs, continuous monitoring protocols, emergency care and psychological interventions, ideally attended by at least two family members, would improve the sharing of the duties and responsibilities.

Skilling and upskilling

If we need to have a large number of skilled, formally trained caregivers in a few years’ time, we need to start in earnest.

Two structures are functioning in India, albeit on a small scale and untested. Kudumbashree is a State mission based in Kerala that runs a network of self-help groups. It launched the K4 Care training programme in February 2024 under which its members qualify as certified geriatric/patient/disability care executives. Recent data shows that only 838 have completed the course, a rather slow progress. We can incentivise and accelerate the programme.

The other group is the ASHA workers for whom the NHSRC (National Health Systems Resource Centre) has prepared a Training Manual on Elderly Care, with training delivered via Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres. However, granular details as to the number of ASHA workers who have completed this training are not available publicly. A meaningful intervention here can have a positive impact.

Informal caregiving is not always physical, like mobility assistance or medicine management. Age-related cognitive decline — as seen in Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease — involves several emotional challenges as well. Any national curriculum must factor in geriatric mental health and behavioural management along with physical care protocols.

The way forward

There are millions of informal, unpaid family caregivers. We need to validate and upskill them into recognised caregivers.

Kudumbashree and ASHA workers who are formally trained, can serve as trainers to train more people, allowing the chain to continue. The National Caregiver Council (NCC), as envisaged in the NITI Aayog report, can act as an apex body. It can set benchmarks and supervise skill development, update training modules, standardise curricula, come out with useful FAQs and regulate and manage a national caregiver portal with a list of certified caregivers.

Transforming India’s care economy is an economic strategy waiting to be unlocked. By creating such a robust ecosystem, India can turn informal dedication into professional expertise with great economic value. For millions like Sreeni, being recognised as a caregiver for the elderly and being trained formally to deal with the associated challenges bring dignity to the relationship.

Just as India is recognised the world over for its healthcare nursing professionals, its approach to managing the challenges of elderly care too could be adopted as the compassionate alternative to the many models being practised globally. The fact that this has been announced as a Budget item is just the seed, and operationalising it at the ground level is where the final success lies.

(T.C. Suseel Kumar a former Managing Director and R. Sudhakar is a former Executive Director, LIC. Views expressed are personal.)

World.title: Actor Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt in Juhu firing incident; suspect detained
World.content:
Actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after a shooting incident in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday (October 18, 2026) evening; two individuals, including his driver, sustained injuries in the attack. The police have detained one suspect in connection with the incident.

According to Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg, the incident occurred around 7 p.m. as Mr. Shroff was leaving the place after work. His driver, Firdaus, suffered an injury to his left hand, while another bystander, Mr. Chauhan, was also injured and taken to a local hospital for treatment.

Also read | How undercover agents and informants helped the FBI unravel Lawrence Bishnoi’s gang | Explained

Mr. Garg declined to comment on a social media post by a gang claiming responsibility for the attack.

Chief Minister and State Home Minister Devendra Fadnavis called Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and directed him to probe the case swiftly and take strict action against the perpetrators.

“Our priority is to keep Mumbai’s citizens safe. We will not spare anyone trying to threaten our film industry. It is time we respond to them in their own language. In the 1990s, Mumbai saw the gang war era. The Mumbai Police stopped it. We will not tolerate such gangs. This incident is unfortunate,” Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde told The Hindu.

The Mumbai Police and forensic teams arrived at the scene on Sunday (October 18, 2026) night to gather evidence and review CCTV footage.

Mr. Fadnavis and Mr. Shinde spoke with the actor and assured him of strict action in the matter. Meanwhile, the opposition hit out at the government, questioning whether lawbreakers faced any fear of the law in the State.

“It is a matter of concern. This is the second such firing incident in recent months. Just a few months ago, there was firing at Rohit Shetty’s bungalow, which is only two lanes away from where the firing took place today. Today’s incident happened at a playground near a school frequented by children, elders, and celebrities,” filmmaker Ashoke Pandit told The Hindu.

On behalf of my industry, we condemn this act. We all stand by the Shroff family. We pray that his driver makes a safe recovery. There is a sense of fear and insecurity. Tomorrow, anybody can shoot anybody on the streets. We urge the Chief Minister to do something about it. Otherwise, the old days will return, when our industry was living under fear,” Mr. Pandit added.

World.title: St. Petersburg oil facilities ablaze as Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia
World.content:
Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday (October 18, 2026) as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war.

The strikes came amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticising Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and the prospect of further U.S. sanctions against Moscow still uncertain.

One person was killed, and five others were wounded in the St. Petersburg attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, local Gov. Alexander Beglov said. A logistics centre belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data centre operated by Russian tech giant VK were also targeted, the companies confirmed.

Russia's Defence Ministry said Sunday (October 18, 2026) that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency Tass that Kyiv was “resisting” Moscow's invasion but could not “change the current course of events.”

Future of U.S. sanctions still unclear

The strikes came after Mr. Trump told reporters that they did not know what his decision on further sanctions against Russia would be, despite signing an executive order Friday night (October 16, 2026) waiving planned restrictions, citing U.S. national interests.

Speaking on NBC's “Meet the Press” on Sunday (October 18, 2026), Mr. Zelenskyy said waiving sanctions against Russia would strengthen Mr. Putin's war effort. He also said U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after being “blocked for some period of time.”

Mr. Zelenskyy said that while he trusted Mr. Trump, siding with Moscow would be a tragedy and a “historic mistake” for Washington.

“People want to forget what's going on. But we can't give this possibility to forget, or to change reality, or to change the truth,” Mr. Zelenskyy said. “We can't compare Putin and Putin. He's an aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He's a terrorist. And that's why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position.”

A woman was killed, and a 6-year-old girl was among at least two other people wounded in two Russian attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said Sunday. Two apartment buildings, 18 cars and an educational institution were damaged in the attacks, Mykhailo Semikin, head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, said.

World.title: Comparing SIR 2002-04 and 2025-26
World.content:
There have been renewed protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Former Election Commissioners and Supreme Court judges have also questioned the exercise in its current form. As a counter, there have also been former judges and bureaucrats who have supported the current SIR process.

Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (RP Act) authorises the Election Commission of India (ECI) to carry out a special revision of the electoral roll for ‘any’ constituency or part of a constituency in such manner as it may think fit.

World.title: Minister launches desilting of Pichaikaranpallam stream in Erode
World.content:
Minister for Handlooms, Textiles and Khadi M. Vijay Balaji on Saturday (October 17, 2026) launched desilting works in the Pichaikaranpallam stream at Annai Sathya Nagar (Ward 15) on Bhavani Road. The works are being undertaken jointly by the Erode Corporation and Sri Shyam Bhakt Mandal. Erode Collector S. Kandasamy was present.

The Minister said Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had directed officials to take precautionary measures ahead of the northeast monsoon, including desilting stormwater drains and identifying areas vulnerable to rain-related damage to ensure that remedial measures were taken promptly.

Erode Corporation has 16 stormwater streams stretching a total of 45.44 km. Desilting works are being carried out at an estimated cost of ₹53.90 lakh as part of the preparations for the monsoon.

Works on five of the 16 streams have been completed at a cost of ₹16 lakh. These are at Ondikaranpalayam (2.50 km), Karuvilparai Valasu (0.60 km), Shastri Road (1.60 km), Kollampalayam Kattabomman Street (2 km), and the stretch of Mosikeeranar Street stream connecting to the river (3.65 km).

The remaining 11 streams are being desilted at an estimated cost of ₹37.90 lakh through a joint initiative involving the Corporation, Sri Shyam Bhakt Mandal and Olirum Erode. The streams are Pichaikaranpallam (1.50 km), the stream near Perumal Malai (3.50 km), Sunnambu Odai (6 km), Pichaikaranpallam from Soolai to Sathy Road (2.44 km), Kalingarayan Baby Canal (5.80 km), Pudhu Colony (1 km), Nalliyampalayam (0.80 km), Balaji Garden (0.95 km), Muthampalayam (1.10 km), Senapathipalayam (1.20 km) and Kasipalayam (0.80 km).

Later, the Minister witnessed a mock disaster-response exercise near the Soleeswarar Temple on the Cauvery riverbank in Ward 15. The Revenue Department, Fire and Rescue Services Department and Traffic Police jointly conducted the exercise to familiarise the public with safety measures during the northeast monsoon and other natural disasters, including ways to protect themselves and others during floods.

World.title: Bilawal says KP governor's rule could end if opposition engages with Centre on counterterrorism policy
World.content:
PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Sunday that if the opposition was willing to fight against terrorism and engage with the Centre on a plan, governor’s rule and emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could end.

He made these remarks while speaking to the media in Karachi, where he was visiting the Karsaz Monument on the 19th anniversary of the Karsaz bombing.

His statement comes a week after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI, which was in power in KP and in opposition in the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

“If they really want to fight terrorists, and if they want that emergency and governor’s rule in KP to end, they should engage with the federal government and politicians and discuss a united policy regarding the fight against terrorism,” Bilawal said on Sunday, referring to the PTI-led opposition.

He added that if the opposition was ready to fight terrorism and “we agree on a plan” to do so, the emergency and governor’s rule in KP could end.

“If the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister (Sohail Afridi) is a coward, if he is not ready to defend his homeland, if he is not ready to fight those terrorists, then the PPP is ready to fight them,” Bilawal said.

“That is why we supported the government’s decision to impose governor’s rule in KP.”

He stressed that the party would “join forces with everyone to fight these terrorists”.

In his media talk, the Bhutto scion said the country had reached a point where “terrorist attacks are taking place from Khyber to Khuzdar”.

He regretted that when the Taliban came to power in Kabul in 2021, the Pakistani government at that time “also decided to invite the terrorists who were in Afghanistan to come back and live in our Swat, our Malakand, our former tribal areas”. He was seemingly referring to then-prime minister Imran’s plans to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan in the country.

Bilawal went on to say that terrorists who were in jail in Pakistan were also freed. “Today, Pakistan is suffering the losses from these wrong decisions,” he lamented.

He added that the country had now once again reached the point where “some forces want to take down Pakistan’s flag in Swat” and there was a fight against terrorism ongoing across the entire country, while security forces, law enforcers and the public were being targeted.

However, he claimed, in the province where the highest number of terrorist incidents were taking place — KP — its chief minister had pledged that he would not face the terrorists.

In response to a question about the Karsaz bombing, the PPP chairman remarked that the greatest loss was caused when terrorist incidents were not taken seriously.

He said that the PPP had “prepared entire society” to fight terrorism by creating an environment for counterterrorism operations in 2008, when the party was in power. After that, he said, when the National Action Plan was introduced, the PPP adopted a holistic approach towards bringing changes in institutions to assist with combatting terrorism.

He emphasised that success was achieved when “every citizen” of Pakistan joined the fight against terrorism, saying, “Today as well, we will make efforts to create an environment where we are all united, and will fight the terrorists together.”

Answering further questions, he said Pakistan was facing a “historic economic crisis”.

“It appears that the situation will worsen. Our priority is to address this economic crisis, and to do that, we will have to fight terrorism as well,” he added.

He said efforts should also be made to improve the democratic and electoral system in Pakistan.

For this reason, he said, the PPP had highlighted the need for a new NAP and consensus on the fight against terrorism, while also extending an invitation to the opposition to play a part in this.

He said the PPP also made an effort to improve the democratic system by pushing for electoral reforms. To this end, the federal government had decided to establish an electoral reforms committee in the National Assembly, adding that he had invited the opposition to play their part in that committee as well.

“If they say that democracy is weak in this country, they should help us to strengthen it,” the PPP chairman said.

He added, “If we can create such an environment, we will be in a better position to fight terrorists.”

Bilawal also said KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had been nominated by the PPP for the office of governor, but “constitutionally, he is now a representative of the federal government”.

He said Kundi reported to the federal government, but “I will keep talking to him and keep advising him; in principle, though, he is now working together with the federal government”.

Responding to a question regarding a potential “compromise” with the opposition, Bilawal said, “You say ‘compromise’ like it’s a bad word […] Compromise and politics go hand in hand.”

He stressed that ex-PM Benazir had always strived for compromises during her political career, adding that she knew that one could reach “extremes” if they remained a revolutionary or an activist who only protested rather than working for their cause.

“We had to solve our issues and lift the public and our workers out of difficulty,” Bilawal said about the PPP’s past tenures in government. He asserted that it was the result of the PPP’s “compromises” that led to the end of Gen Pervez Musharraf’s dictatorship, as well as the passage of the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment.

“We (the PPP) are not in the federal government. Nor do we have a majority in Parliament,” he said. “But [we have to see] how we can conduct politics in the space we have.”

New provinces

Answering a question regarding the creation of new provinces, Bilawal stated that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi knew “clearly” what the PPP and President Asif Ali Zardari’s policy was regarding new provinces or administrative units, and that this was “not possible without the president’s signature”.

Naqvi’s July remarks calling for new provinces and reforms in the current governance system had ignited an animated debate across the country. The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any possible division of the province.

Bilawal stressed that the PPP’s position was clear: that they could be created in accordance with the Constitution and law if the provincial assembly agreed. The Sindh Assembly, amid a boycott by the opposition, adopted a resolution last month rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units.

“Where there is consensus and it is not a political stunt, if there is no other purpose behind it … why aren’t provinces being made there?” the PPP chairman said, giving the example of Gilgit-Baltistan.

“If we really want this to be implemented, it must only be implemented where the provinces want this,” he stressed, noting that the entire GB Legislative Assembly had passed a resolution with consensus for the region’s constitutional rights.

Bilawal requested politicians, whether on the treasury or opposition benches, not to politicise the issue of terrorism or create controversy out of steps taken to combat it, but rather to play their role in fighting it.

Bilawal also spoke about Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, saying he had the right to criticise the government’s policies, and that there should certainly be room for difference of opinion in the country.

He said the PPP had always imposed emergency through constitutional and legal means.

“In fact, during the 2008–2013 government, when emergency rule was imposed in Balochistan, it was also because of the terrorism situation, and governor’s rule was imposed there against the PPP’s own government.

“If the PPP thought only of itself, how would it have removed its own government?“

He said Fazl’s party has also been affected by terrorist attacks, so he hoped the JUI-F chief would criticise the PPP politically as much as he wished, but also condemn the terrorists.

Bilawal added that if Fazl made an effort, harmony between the government and the opposition could be achieved.

World.title: Two moments of madness cost Sri Lanka as Pakistan win tri-series opener after Salman Ali Agha century
World.content:
Sri Lanka were cruising.

Only 53 runs stood between them and a flying start in the One-day International tri-series opener against Pakistan after Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage’s 119-run stand.

The dew that made the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium outfield relentlessly slick had also deprived Pakistan’s pacers of the chance to extract reverse swing from the old ball.

Then came two moments of madness. Liyanage, who had looked composed throughout his innings, chipped Haris Rauf casually to Babar Azam at long-on before Dasun Shanaka, who had threatened to take the game away from Pakistan, heaved Shaheen Shah Afridi to the same fielder in the same position. In the space of four balls, Sri Lanka unravelled.

Naseem Shah then had Sachindu Colombage caught behind, Eshan Malinga was run out after a mix-up, and Haris cleaned up Asitha Fernando to seal a 37-run win for Pakistan, who had earlier posted 305 thanks to Salman Ali Agha’s third ODI century.

Salman celebrated his return to the Pakistan side after his unceremonious axing from the Test team two months ago with a composed 107 off 90 balls, including 10 fours and a six.

Pakistan’s innings, however, finished with a flourish from Sri Lanka’s bowlers, who conceded only 36 runs while taking five wickets in the last five overs. Eshan Malinga led the charge with figures of 4-46.

After openers Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub fell to Dilshan Madushanka, Babar Azam and Saad Baig steadied the innings with a 74-run partnership for the third wicket.

Malinga broke through by bouncing out Babar for 45 and Saad for 39, bringing Salman and Hasan Nawaz together.

The pair added 97, with Salman gradually increasing the tempo after initially settling in. He brought up his half-century in the 35th over, rotating the strike and punishing loose deliveries.

Hasan supplied the acceleration with two sixes off Sachindu Colombage, including a powerful slog sweep over cow corner.

Salman then took charge, pulling Dasun Shanaka through the leg side before launching Malinga’s slower delivery over long-off for six.

He reached three figures in the 45th over, finding the boundary through deep midwicket before edging a full delivery past the infield to third man.

Hasan fell for 37, caught by Pavan Rathnayake at short midwicket off Asitha Fernando, who also removed Arafat Minhas for 18.

Salman departed for 107 at 279-6, mistiming a lofted shot to Shanaka at long-on, and Sri Lanka seized control.

Malinga dismissed Faheem Ashraf and trapped Naseem Shah lbw in the next over, while accurate yorkers restricted Pakistan’s lower order. Haris was run out for a duck in the final over, leaving Pakistan all out for 305 in 49.5 overs.

Sri Lanka’s reply began poorly. Shaheen and Naseem made early inroads, reducing the visitors to 91-4 and leaving the chase in need of repair.

But as the ball and outfield grew wetter, Pakistan’s bowlers struggled to make the ball grip, allowing Rathnayake and Liyanage to rebuild with patience and calculated aggression.

Rathnayake initially played watchfully before cutting Arafat Minhas late through deep point and pulling Saim Ayub to the deep midwicket boundary.

He raised his maiden ODI half-century with a single off Arafat in the 31st over, then pulled two short balls from Shaheen over square leg in successive deliveries.

Liyanage offered stability at the other end, rotating the strike and punishing anything loose. He drove Naseem through the gap between mid-off and extra cover before dancing down the track to hammer Arafat straight down the ground.

Their running between the wickets kept the scoreboard moving as Pakistan struggled to find a breakthrough.

Faheem finally ended the partnership in the 38th over, when Rathnayake, having faced 74 deliveries, pushed a length ball straight to Salman at short cover.

But the wicket did little to ease Pakistan’s anxiety. Shanaka attacked immediately, pulling Faheem for four and driving through extra cover before launching Arafat over square leg for six.

Liyanage brought up his half-century with a fierce drive down the ground, and Sri Lanka remained firmly in the contest.

With 82 needed from the final 10 overs, the visitors had a genuine chance of pulling off the chase.

Then Liyanage’s loose chip and Shanaka’s reckless heave turned a promising pursuit into a collapse. From there, Pakistan needed only to keep their nerve.

Salman’s century had given Pakistan the platform; Malinga’s late burst had kept the total within reach. But Sri Lanka’s two costly shots ultimately decided the opener, handing Pakistan a winning start to the tri-series.

World.title: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen
World.content:
Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday.

Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said two officers were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the rebel group claimed it shot the aircraft down.

The coalition blamed a “technical malfunction” for the helicopter crash, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running conflict with the Houthis reignited in July.

The incident comes a week after strikes by the Houthis killed 13 people at Riyadh’s international airport, the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.

An AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter belonging to the Saudi Ministry of National Guard crashed “inside Saudi territory in Najran Region due to a technical malfunction”, coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said, according to the official Saudi Press Agency.

“The accident resulted in the martyrdom of its aircrew, consisting of two officers.”

Late on Saturday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group had “downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy” in the same area.

Egypt ready to give ‘all necessary and possible forms of support’

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the region’s largest and most powerful, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support.

“Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites,” the Egyptian presidency said in a statement on Sunday.

It followed a meeting of Egypt’s National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief.

A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorising the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said.

Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who visited Sisi on Sept 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited.

Dar, Egypt FM condemn Houthi attacks

On the diplomatic front, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a telephone conversation with Egypt’s FM Dr Badr Abdelatty, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

“The two leaders exchanged views on recent regional developments and strongly condemned the Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their full solidarity with the Kingdom and support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.”

They also discussed cooperation under the R-4 (Pakistan, Egypt, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia) framework and looked forward to the next meeting of the R-4 soon to further strengthen mutual ties and to coordinate on the regional issues, the statement added.

The foreign ministers of the four countries last met on Sept 21 in New York, where they had reaffirmed their support for Riyadh’s sovereignty and supported its right to self-defence.

Pakistan, which has signed two defence agreements with Riyadh, has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

The first one, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA), was signed in Sept 2025, under which the two countries pledged that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

The two countries are also parties to the Makkah Defence Alliance, which also includes Turkiye. The pact was signed on August 7 and provides that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all.

Yemen fighting

After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen’s conflict has surged back to life, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia in July.

The conflict intensified when Houthis captured territory around the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf’s Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have also hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport.
